name: Bell-Ringing Greatclub
entries: This Greatclub is fashioned from the clapper of a giant's bell. When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} with this Greatclub, you can choose for the target to have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn instead of dealing the extra damage from the {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}.

name: Bellhop Topper
entries: This deep purple top hat is ringed with a velvet ribbon and secured with leather straps and belts. The hat has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. You can use an action to expend 1 of the hat's charges and speak its command word, tossing it onto the ground in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. When you do, the hat magically flattens and expands into a purple, circular disk 3 feet in diameter and 1 inch thick. The disk duplicates the effect of the {@spell tenser's floating disk|PHB|floating disk} spell, except that the disk is opaque and remains within 10 feet of you, instead of 20. You can end the spell early using an action to speak the hat's command word again. When the spell ends, the disk transforms back into the hat.

name: Belt of the Berserker
reqAttune: by a Barbarian with the Reckless Attack Class Feature
entries: While wearing this wolf-hide belt, you can choose to use the following feature each time you activate your Rage class feature:

entries.name: Foolhardy Rage
entries: While you are Raging, you gain an extra {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} each turn that you can only use to extend your Rage or to take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. If you use it to take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action, you cannot take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action again on that turn. In addition, you gain a +1 Bonus to your Rage Damage. Finally, you must use your Reckless Attack Class feature on each of your turns during your Rage, or your Rage ends.

name: Belt of the Hell Hound
entries: When you wear this belt, you can feel the fires of the lower planes burn inside you. While wearing the belt, when you make a melee attack against a creature and have advantage on the attack, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} fire damage from the attack on a hit.

In addition, while wearing this belt, you can use an action to release a hellish howl. When you do, you exhale a plume of flames from your mouth in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 6d6} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The fire ignites flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Curse
entries: Once you wear this belt, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by the {@spell remove curse|PHB} spell or similar magic. While wearing the belt, you must eat twice the normal amount of food each day (a minimum of 2 pounds) to avoid {@condition exhaustion}. In addition, while wearing the belt, there is a cumulative {@chance 10|10 percent} chance when you die and again at the end of each hour you remain dead that you immediately immolate and turn to ash.

name: Belt of the Raid Leader
entries: This thick leather belt is reinforced with large rivets and secured with a heavy iron skull buckle. While wearing the belt, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to let loose a powerful war cry that inspires you and up to five allies of your choice within 60 feet of you that can hear you. An inspired creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls until the start of your next turn. When you use this property of the belt, you can make one attack using a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Belt of the Weald
entries: This thin chain belt appears to be made of metal, yet closer inspection reveals it to be made up of links of highly polished wood. While wearing this belt, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on {@skill Survival} skill checks while in a forest environment.
You ignore {@quickref difficult terrain||3} while moving through forests.
You can cast the {@spell longstrider} spell once, targeting yourself. This property of the belt can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Berserker's Mead
entries: For 1 minute after you consume this potion, you are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the first 40 points of damage you take.

name: Bicycle
entries: These First Age vehicles have become increasingly popular over the years as recreations started being crafted out of Yatamon. Both the recreations and the originals have a speed of 60 feet while being ridden.

name: Bird of a Feather (Common)
entries: This small, stuffed roc toy is filled with enchanted down. While holding the toy, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 20 feet for 1 minute or until your {@status Concentration|XPHB} ends. The stuffed toy's weak magic can carry up to 200 pounds. If you take any damage while flying in this way, you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the effect and immediately start falling.
When the effect ends, the toy becomes nonmagical.

name: Bird of a Feather (Uncommon)
entries: This small, stuffed roc toy is filled with enchanted down. While holding the toy, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 20 feet for 1 minute or until your {@status Concentration|XPHB} ends. The stuffed toy's weak magic can carry up to 200 pounds. If you take any damage while flying in this way, you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the effect and immediately start falling.

When the effect ends, the toy becomes nonmagical. If the toy is of Uncommon rarity, it instead can't be used again for {@dice 1d4} hours after the effect ends. It gives a happy little chirp once its magic can be used again.

name: Birdcage of Innocuousness
entries: This silver birdcage, sized for giants, features figures of songbirds giving the impression they fly around its exterior.

When a creature with a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} enters the birdcage, it must make a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw, becoming docile on a failure until it leaves the cage (on a success it can open the cage from the inside and escape). A creature outside the cage can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to open or close it. A creature outside the cage also can use an action to speak a command word to either create an illusion of a harmless songbird in place of the creature inside or revert the illusion to the caged creature's true appearance. When a creature exits the birdcage, it returns to its true appearance.

name: Black Candle
entries: This broad, black tallow candle is engraved with arcane symbols. When lit, its smoke is greasy and pungent, and its flame is pale gray, but it never burns down. The candle has the following properties.

entries.name: Word of Flame and Darkness
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can light or extinguish the candle by speaking a command word while within 60 feet of it. It sheds {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius.

entries.name: Witchlight
entries: While you are in the candle's light, you can cast a level 1 or 2 spell without expending a spell slot. When you cast a spell in this way, you can't cast that spell using the candle again for 24 hours, and you must succeed on a DC 0 Constitution saving throw or take Fire damage equal to {@dice 2d6} times the spell's level.

entries.name: Cursed Candle
entries: After you succeed or fail on the saving throw of the Witchlight property, its save DC increases by 2. This increase can't happen again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When the DC is 10 or higher, you also have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

name: Blackthorn Spear of the Moonless Hunter
entries: This spiny, black bone spear is a favorite among nocturnal hunting tribes. While attuned to the spear, you can always see the faint outline of it, even in total darkness. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

This spear contains a fragment of the moonless hunter, an ancient spirit that can be channeled to assume some of its powers. While holding the spear, you can use a bonus action to call forth and assume the spirit of the moonless hunter. While assuming the spirit, your eyes become pure white, and you gain the following benefits:

items: You ignore the effects of {@condition exhaustion}.
You can't sleep or be put to sleep by magical means, and you can't take or benefit from finishing a long rest.
You have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks.
You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, out to a range of 60 feet.
You can use a bonus action to cause the spear to fly back to your empty hand or land at your feet (your choice), provided that the spear is within 60 feet of you.
Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

entries: You can assume the spirit in this way for up to 8 hours. The effect ends early if you release the spirit as a bonus action or if you're farther than 60 feet away from the spear for more than 1 minute. The spirit returns to the spear when you are no longer assuming it, at which point you gain 1 level of {@condition exhaustion} for every 2 hours you assumed the spirit (minimum 1 level). {@condition Exhaustion} gained in this way can only be reduced by finishing a long rest.

name: Blade of Forlorn Hope
entries: Gifted to vanguard Kitseth by the elder primordial of fire, this wide-bladed scimitar helps its wielder protect others, but with a disregard for self-preservation.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When you hit a creature with the sword, it flares with a burning corona. You can either deal an extra {@damage 2d6} radiant damage to the target, or you can choose one ally you can see within 30 feet of the target to gain {@dice 2d6} temporary hit points.

entries.name: Immolating Surge
entries: Immediately after attacking a creature on your turn with the sword, you can take one additional action. At the end of this turn, you take {@damage 6d8} radiant damage. If this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, you die and your remains burn to nothing. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Blast Disk (Common)
entries: A Blast Disk holds destructive arcane power. A typical Blast Disk is about nine inches in diameter and one inch thick, made from layers of different metal; dragonshards are embedded in the surface of the disk and arcane symbols are engraved in its surface. Anyone studying the surface of the disk can make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check corresponding to the save DC of the disk. On a success, they identify the spell effect contained within the disk.
There are three elements to a Blast Disk: the trigger, the payload, and the charge. Each effect is selected at the time it is created.

entries.name: Trigger
entries: A spellcaster touching a Blast Disk can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to activate it. However, generally you don't want to be holding a Blast Disk when it goes off. A Blast Disk can be created with one of the following triggers, or with a more complex trigger of the creator's choosing (e.g. to detonate when a certain word is spoken, when a specific object comes within range, etc.):

items.name: Time
entries: When the disk is activated, the user can set a time delay of up to 10 minutes before it releases its effect.

items.name: Proximity
entries: 30 seconds after the disk is activated, it can trigger when someone comes within a certain distance of the disk or when someone first makes contact with the disk, then breaks that contact.

items.name: Impact
entries: The activated disk can be set to detonate on impact, then used by throwing or dropping it.

entries.name: Payload
entries: When the Blast Disk is triggered, it produces one of the following magical effects, chosen when it was manufactured:

items.name: Explosive
entries: This creates an explosion in a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on the disk. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 11 ({@damage 2d10}) damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. An explosive Blast Disk deals triple damage to objects or structures. The damage type is set when the disk is created.

items.name: Spell Effect
entries: The disk produces a spell effect when triggered. The effect must target either a single creature—whoever triggers the disk—or an area of effect centered on the disk. The level of the spell in the disk determines the saving throw DC and attack bonus, as well as the item's rarity, as shown on the Blast Disk Power table.

items.name: Charge
entries: A typical Blast Disk holds a single charge, the dragonshards shattering when the effect is triggered. However, more advanced Blast Disks recharge at dawn; this increases the rarity of the disk by one category.

items.name: Disarming a Disk
entries: When used on the battlefield, Blast Disks are typically buried or hidden. Finding the disk requires a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check, with a DC equal to the ability check that was used when it was hidden, such as Wisdom ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) or Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}). To disarm a Blast Disk, a character with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} must succeed on a Dexterity check using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, with a DC equal to the save DC of the disk. If the check is failed by 5 or more, the disk detonates as if it were triggered. Successfully disarming a Blast Disk expends one charge, meaning most Blast Disks will be rendered inert after disarming.

To disarm a Blast Disk, a character with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} must succeed on a Dexterity check using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, with a DC equal to the save DC of the disk. If the check is failed by 5 or more, the disk detonates as if it were triggered. Successfully disarming a Blast Disk expends one charge, meaning most Blast Disks will be rendered inert after disarming.

name: Blast Disk (Uncommon)
entries: A Blast Disk holds destructive arcane power. A typical Blast Disk is about nine inches in diameter and one inch thick, made from layers of different metal; dragonshards are embedded in the surface of the disk and arcane symbols are engraved in its surface. Anyone studying the surface of the disk can make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check corresponding to the save DC of the disk. On a success, they identify the spell effect contained within the disk.
There are three elements to a Blast Disk: the trigger, the payload, and the charge. Each effect is selected at the time it is created.

entries.name: Trigger
entries: A spellcaster touching a Blast Disk can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to activate it. However, generally you don't want to be holding a Blast Disk when it goes off. A Blast Disk can be created with one of the following triggers, or with a more complex trigger of the creator's choosing (e.g. to detonate when a certain word is spoken, when a specific object comes within range, etc.):

items.name: Time
entries: When the disk is activated, the user can set a time delay of up to 10 minutes before it releases its effect.

items.name: Proximity
entries: 30 seconds after the disk is activated, it can trigger when someone comes within a certain distance of the disk or when someone first makes contact with the disk, then breaks that contact.

items.name: Impact
entries: The activated disk can be set to detonate on impact, then used by throwing or dropping it.

entries.name: Payload
entries: When the Blast Disk is triggered, it produces one of the following magical effects, chosen when it was manufactured:

items.name: Explosive
entries: This creates an explosion in a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on the disk. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 11 ({@damage 2d10}) damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. An explosive Blast Disk deals triple damage to objects or structures. The damage type is set when the disk is created.

items.name: Spell Effect
entries: The disk produces a spell effect when triggered. The effect must target either a single creature—whoever triggers the disk—or an area of effect centered on the disk. The level of the spell in the disk determines the saving throw DC and attack bonus, as well as the item's rarity, as shown on the Blast Disk Power table.

items.name: Charge
entries: A typical Blast Disk holds a single charge, the dragonshards shattering when the effect is triggered. However, more advanced Blast Disks recharge at dawn; this increases the rarity of the disk by one category.

items.name: Disarming a Disk
entries: When used on the battlefield, Blast Disks are typically buried or hidden. Finding the disk requires a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check, with a DC equal to the ability check that was used when it was hidden, such as Wisdom ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) or Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}). To disarm a Blast Disk, a character with proficiency in {@skill Arcana|XPHB} must succeed on a Dexterity check using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, with a DC equal to the save DC of the disk. If the check is failed by 5 or more, the disk detonates as if it were triggered. Successfully disarming a Blast Disk expends one charge, meaning most Blast Disks will be rendered inert after disarming.

name: Blessed Reliquary
entries: This small wooden or ivory box holds a piece of a saint. While it is on your person, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws caused by Undead creatures.
You can use each of your Channel Divinity class features one additional time.

When you use Turn Undead, you may choose for the targets to have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on their saving throws. This can be used once. You regain its use after a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Blessed Stake
entries: A Blessed Stake is a necessary tool in the arsenal of vampire hunters everywhere. This wooden spike, roughly a foot in length, has been blessed by a servant of an Arch Seraph in a special ceremony.

As an {@action Attack|XPHB} action, a wielder can make a melee attack using Strength. Against most foes, this deals {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage. Against a Vampire that has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} or {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, a successful attack with the Blessed Stake kills the Vampire.

If the Vampire is CR 10 or lower, the Vampire instantly crumbles to dust. If the Vampire is more powerful, its form remains whole for one year before crumbling to dust. If the Blessed Stake is removed before then, the Vampire rises with 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}.

name: Blessing of the Moon Spirit
entries: After drinking this potion, which glows like a full moon, you gain a strange and wondrous affinity for the moon's light. This potion's effects are {@b permanent}.
While moonlight touches you, you can use a bonus action to expend three hit dice. You can use this ability once per long rest.
When you first consume this potion, your hit point maximum is increased by {@dice 2d10}. This doesn't count against the number of potions you can have affecting you at once.
{@font {@style 55|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Bliss
entries: The magical drug comes in the form of a small, round pellet of white powder. If ingested by a Humanoid, that creature is filled with feelings of calm and happiness.
Upon ingestion, you have the following effects for {@dice 1d4} hours:

items: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.
You gain {@dice 3d10} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.
Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 15 feet.
You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests}.
If you cause another creature to make a saving throw, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on that save.

entries: After the effects wear off, you must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw, or you gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.

name: Blizzard Sphere
entries: This glass sphere contains a raging blizzard inside. It's cold to the touch and vibrates with the gusts of wind trapped within. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can throw the orb at a creature or object you can see within 30 feet of you, shattering it on impact. When the orb shatters, the blizzard erupts from the glass in a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of swirling ice and snow originating from the target. When a creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d8} Cold damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

The blizzard remains for {@dice 1d4} rounds or until targeted by {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} (as if the effect were a level 5 spell). Any surface within the area is covered in slick ice and sleet, turning the ground within the sphere into {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} that remains for the effect's duration. While the blizzard persists, the area is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB}.

name: Blood Capsule
entries: This cylindrical flask is etched with arcane runes.
Humanoid blood stored in the blood capsule remains fresh for up to one year. The flask stores enough blood to sustain a vampire for one day.

name: Blood Moon Blade
entries: This fine blade is crafted from a strange black metal and bears a hole above the hilt that seems to draw in blood. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When you hit a Small or larger living creature with this weapon, that creature takes an extra {@damage 2d4} necrotic damage and you regain hit points equal to half the amount of necrotic damage dealt in this way. Constructs, plants, and undead creatures are immune to this necrotic damage.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This sword is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the sword, keeping it within reach at all times. You also have disadvantage on attack rolls with weapons other than this one, unless no foe is within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear. In addition, while you remain cursed, the number of hit points you regain when healed by magical means (other than the sword's effect) is halved.

name: Blood Pact Pendants
entries: These iron pendants come in pairs and are connected by a powerful bond of self-sacrifice. In order to create this bond, you and an ally with whom you are close perform a brief, 1-minute ritual to connect your destinies and forge a blood pact. When you create this blood pact, you must each agree on a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to permanently sacrifice, reducing your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum by that amount (minimum 1). Once a pact has been forged, trickles of the bound creatures' blood are absorbed into the normally clear gems adorning the faces of these pendants. While the gem is filled in this way, it seems to gently swirl and pulse in time with your heartbeat.

While the bound creatures are wearing their respective pendants and are on the same plane of existence, they're protected by this pact as long as one of the creatures is still conscious. When a bound creature dies, it's immediately revived with {@dice 2d10} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} plus twice the number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} it had sacrificed. When a creature is revived in this way, the other bound creature immediately drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, ending the blood pact and restoring both creatures' {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximums to normal; this property ignores any effect that would normally prevent a creature from being reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Once the pact is ended in this way, the gems and pendants crack and are no longer magical.

name: Bloodhound Amulet
entries: While wearing this pendant, you have advantage on any ability check that relies on smell. In addition, you can use an action to focus on a particular scent. When you do, you perceive that smell visually as a cloud of red vapor for up to 1 hour. Once this property of the amulet has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Bloodmage Dagger
entries: This roughly hewn obsidian {@item Dagger|XPHB} is razor sharp and can be used as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}. Its handle is covered in small holes that drink in whatever blood runs down the blade. There's a small reservoir for blood at the {@item Dagger|XPHB}'s pommel that seems to never completely fill. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The {@item Dagger|XPHB} has 5 charges and regains {@dice 1d3 + 2} expended charges daily at dusk. While holding the {@item Dagger|XPHB}, you can expend 1 charge as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to make a melee spell attack, using your spell attack bonus, against a living creature you can see within 5 feet of you. When you do, an illusory crimson dagger sweeps out toward the creature. On a hit, the target takes Necrotic damage equal to {@dice 3d6} plus your spellcasting ability modifier, and you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Necrotic damage dealt. If the target is a Construct, Plant, or Undead creature, you don't regain any {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in this way.

Alternatively, while holding the {@item Dagger|XPHB}, you can expend 1 or more charges when you cast a spell using a level 1, 2, or 3 spell slot that targets either yourself or a single creature. The spell slot you use to cast this spell counts as one level higher for each charge you expend in this way. You can't increase a spell slot level beyond level 5 in this way. When you use this property of the {@item Dagger|XPHB}, you also expend 1 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die} for each charge you expend in this way. Roll a number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} equal to the number of expended charges and take Necrotic damage equal to the total. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}. If expending charges in this way causes you to drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the spell fails and you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition.

name: Bloodmire Phiale
entries: This shallow, ceramic drinking bowl is enchanted to repurpose spilled blood into new life. The bowl holds up to 8 ounces of blood. Once filled, the blood begins to slowly swirl on its own. If left to sit for 1 hour without spilling, the blood in the bowl becomes a gruesome tonic that pulses with a faint, internal glow.

Drinking the entire bowl of still blood causes one of two effects. Roll a {@dice d12}. On a 12, you take 12 necrotic damage. If this damage reduces you to 0 hit points, you are stable. On a roll of 11 or lower, you instead regain a number of hit points equal 4 + the number rolled. The blood is thick and sweet, but leaves a bitter aftertaste.
The blood's magic fades if it's poured from the bowl without being drunk. Once the bowl has been used in this way, it can't be used again until {@dice 1d4} days have passed.

name: Bloodmire Rod of the Witch Doctor
reqAttune: by a cleric, druid, paladin, or warlock
entries: This gnarled wooden scepter from the Bloodmire is set with a strange, cracked opal at its head and can be used as a spellcasting focus. The rod has 6 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 2} expended charges daily at dusk.

While holding the rod, you can expend 1 of its charges as an action to create a magical tether of light between the rod and another creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The tether's color and effects depend on what kind of tether you create. You can only have one of each tether at a time.

entries.name: Empowering Tether
entries: This tether is a brilliant white. A creature affected by this tether regains {@dice 2d10} hit points when it's first affected by it, and while it's connected to the tether, it deals an extra {@damage 1d10} damage of the weapon's type to the first target it hits with a melee weapon attack on each of its turns. In addition, on each of your following turns while you maintain the tether, you can expend 1 of the rod's charges as a bonus action to send a surge of healing magic through the tether and cause the target to regain {@dice 2d10} hit points.

entries.name: Withering Tether
entries: This tether is a sickly red. A creature affected by this tether must make a Constitution saving throw when it's first affected by it, using your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d10} necrotic damage, and on each of your following turns while you maintain the tether, you can use a bonus action to deal {@damage 1d10} necrotic damage to the target automatically. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much necrotic damage, and the tether immediately ends.

The tether ends after 1 minute. It ends early if you sever the tether (no action required), are no longer holding the rod, the target ends its turn more than 30 feet away from you, the target has total cover from you, or if you or the target fall {@condition unconscious}.

name: Bloodmire Soulflame Lantern
entries: This iron lantern is surrounded by six glass panels and has a sharp spike in its center where a wick would normally be. When you attune to the lantern, it suddenly springs to life with a crimson flame at the top of the spike, shedding bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. The flame is magical and can't be extinguished by any means while it burns within the lantern. While the lantern is on your person, you can use a bonus action to mentally expand or reduce the lantern's light, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet each. As part of this bonus action, you can also cause the lantern's glass panels to magically turn black or clear, allowing you to choose whether the lantern's light is shed in a radius, a cone, or entirely hidden by the darkened glass.
While the lantern is on your person, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight.
You have resistance to necrotic damage and are immune to disease.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can use your reaction to spend one Hit Die to heal yourself. Roll the die, add your Constitution modifier, and regain a number of hit points equal to the total (minimum of 1). This property can't be used again for {@dice 1d12} hours.
When a creature within the lantern's light (including you) reduces a living target to 0 hit points, that creature gains {@dice 1d8} temporary hit points.
You see anything within the lantern's bright light as if you had {@sense truesight}.

Any fiend or undead creature within the lantern's bright light doesn't gain the benefits of any damage resistances it may have, and if it has an ability that would normally take effect when the creature is reduced to 0 hit points, it doesn't.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This lantern is cursed, and attuning to it extends that curse to you. You remain cursed as long as you remain attuned to the lantern, which can only be ended with a {@spell wish|PHB} spell or by the touch of a powerful fey creature. Even if you die, your attunement to the lantern doesn't end until 7 days have passed.

As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the lantern, keeping it within reach at all times. In addition, you must continuously feed the lantern's flame using your own vitality. Whenever you gain or spend any number of Hit Dice, you must also sacrifice one Hit Die to the lantern (if you have any). Alternatively, you can use an action to open the lantern's door and hold your hand over the flame, sacrificing one of your Hit Dice when you do. If the lantern isn't given any Hit Dice for 24 hours, you die, and the flame goes out until the lantern is attuned to by another creature or you return to life while still attuned to it.

name: Bloodsbane
entries: This oil is deceptively clear and smells faintly like parchment, dried ink, and a touch of sulfur. To unlock the oil's power, an additional component must be mixed in (as shown in the Bloodsbane Effects table); this component may have already been added, or the oil's user can acquire an unmixed oil and add the component as part of a short or long rest. These components are difficult to sense once diluted in the oil, and identifying this oil may require a keen nose or additional research.

The oil can coat one slashing or piercing weapon or up to 5 pieces of slashing or piercing ammunition. Applying the oil in this way takes 1 minute, during which time a willing creature must offer one drop of their blood, mixing it into the oil to activate its magic.

A creature hit with a weapon or ammunition coated in this oil must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or suffer an effect depending on the oil's special component added. In addition, if the creature fails the saving throw and the blood in the oil came from an illrigger, the creature has a seal placed on them by that illrigger. This seal doesn't count against the number of seals granted by the illrigger's Baleful Interdict feature.

entries.caption: Bloodsbane Effects
rows: The target is under the effects of the {@spell zone of truth} spell for 10 minutes.
The target is {@condition paralyzed} for 1 minute.
The creature who offered their blood to the oil knows the direction and distance to the target for 24 hours.
The target is under the effect of the {@spell charm person} spell for 1 hour. The creature they are {@condition charmed} by is the creature who offered their blood to the oil.

name: Bloodscryer Oculus
entries: These red goggles have a second set of lenses that magically adjust their distance from your eyes to magnify and focus on targets. While you're attuned to the goggles, you are unaffected by visual obscurity, such as fog or smoke, and can see normally in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}—both magical and nonmagical—within 60 feet of yourself. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, wearing the goggles increases its range by 60 feet. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight.

These lenses are also imbued with several innate spells. While wearing the goggles, you can cast one of the following spells from them, using your spell save DC, but can only target creatures whose blood you can see: {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} (level 3 version), {@spell Locate Creature|XPHB}, or {@spell Scrying|XPHB}. Casting a spell in this way doesn't require your {@status Concentration|XPHB}. Once the goggles are used to cast a spell in this way, they can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

name: Bloodshard Trident
entries: This magic trident has grooves in its obsidian surface that are used to channel blood in rituals of self-sacrifice. While holding the trident, you can use a bonus action to make a blood offering. When you do, choose a number of hit points to sacrifice. You take necrotic damage equal to the amount you sacrifice, which can't be reduced or prevented in any way. For every 5 hit points you sacrifice, the trident creates 1 shard of magic obsidian, which floats alongside the trident's three prongs for 1 minute. You can have up to 3 shards in this way at a time. The trident deals an extra {@damage 1d4} piercing damage to any target it hits for each floating shard it has.
When you throw the trident while it has at least 1 floating shard, the weapon flies back to your hand immediately after the attack.

name: Bloodthirster Scimitar
entries: This carefully carved bone scimitar belonged to a cult of vicious monks whose extraordinary bloodlust and strength have been all but entirely erased from history. While you hold this magic sword, you have resistance to necrotic damage.

When you take the {@action Attack} action while holding this sword, you can choose to forgo one of your attacks to sacrifice your own blood. When you do, you take {@damage 1d6 + 3} piercing damage from the sacrifice. This damage ignores resistance and immunity. This self-inflicted harm empowers the sword, granting you a cumulative +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon that lasts for 1 minute, up to a maximum bonus of +3. While the sword is empowered in this way, it deals an extra {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage to any target it hits.

name: Bloodthirsty Bistoury
entries: This elegant, dark dagger is never bloodstained and effortlessly pierces flesh. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
When this dagger is used by an evil-aligned creature, any creature hit by it doesn't bleed from the attack or the wound it leaves behind for 10 minutes.

name: Bloody Fiddle
entries: This scarlet-lacquered fiddle is warm to the touch, like the heat of fresh blood. Though it looks like it has seen better days, its sound is clear and strong.
While you hold the fiddle, you gain a +2 bonus to Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Song of Stirred Blood
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can play a lively or stirring tune on the fiddle. Up to six creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d10} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and if you have {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|XPHB|1} dice, you can expend and roll one to add it to the total. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Sanguine Curse
entries: The first time that you play the fiddle after finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you take 1 Slashing damage that ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}. When you use the Song of Stirred Blood property, this Slashing damage increases by 1.

name: Bloody Marilith (Common)
entries: The typical {@item bloody marilith|GriffonsSaddlebag2}, a common potion, is a specialty alcoholic beverage that fills your body with reactive energy. For 1 minute after drinking this potion, you can use a reaction even if you've already taken one since the end of your last turn. Once you take this reaction, the potion's effect ends. The potion is a deep crimson color with a thick consistency that vibrates softly within its bottle, sending ripples along its surface. It smells and tastes of freshly ground pepper, hot spices, and faintly sour tomato juice. Due to its magical nature, the alcohol within this potion affects a creature twice as much as the alcohol within a nonmagical beverage.

Drinking additional {@item bloody marilith|GriffonsSaddlebag2|bloody mariliths} before you finish a long rest leaves your body feeling worn. When the potion's effect ends, you can't move or take actions until after your next turn, as a wave of lethargy sweeps over you.

name: Bloody Marilith
entries: Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

items: {@item Bloody Marilith (Common)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Bloody Marilith (Very Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}

name: Bloody Marilith (Very Rare)
entries: The following {@item bloody marilith|GriffonsSaddlebag2} is a very rare variant with more powerful properties. It uses blood from a fiendish marilith, instead of a magical substitute, and pleasantly burns your tongue when drinking it. It also tastes better.

When you drink this potion, you can take one reaction on every turn in a combat for 1 minute. Unlike its {@item Bloody Marilith (Common)|GriffonsSaddlebag2|common} variant, this potion's effect does not end when you use an additional reaction.

Drinking additional {@item bloody marilith|GriffonsSaddlebag2|bloody mariliths} before you finish a long rest leaves your body feeling worn. When the potion's effect ends, you can't move or take actions until after your next turn, as a wave of lethargy sweeps over you.

name: Blunderbuss of the Grinning Sinner (Legendary)
entries: This dark, ornate blunderbuss has a brass barrel and a wooden handle etched with arcane symbols. It was the Grinning Sinner's weapon of choice, who imbued it with the power to shoot jinxes and hexes.

The blunderbuss functions as a {@item Musket|XPHB} that ignores {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading}, and it can make its own ammunition that deals Necrotic damage on a hit. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it determined by the blunderbuss's rarity. While holding the blunderbuss, you can use the blunderbuss as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Jinxshot (Rare+)
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a blast from the blunderbuss that forces each creature within a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} to make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the blunderbuss's bonus), taking {@damage 2d4} Necrotic damage (Rare) or {@damage 3d6} Necrotic damage (Very Rare+) on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Sinner's Jinx (Very Rare+)
entries: Once during your turn when you damage a creature with the blunderbuss, the target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC = 16 + the blunderbuss's bonus) or be cursed for 1 minute. When it makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} while cursed, it subtracts {@dice 1d4} from the total. The curse ends if this property is used on another creature.

entries.name: Luck Taker (Legendary)
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you that is cursed by this weapon makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} and rolls a 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to mimic their luck. The next time you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} within 1 minute, change the number you roll on the {@dice d20} to the triggering number.

name: Blunderbuss of the Grinning Sinner (Rare)
entries: This dark, ornate blunderbuss has a brass barrel and a wooden handle etched with arcane symbols. It was the Grinning Sinner's weapon of choice, who imbued it with the power to shoot jinxes and hexes.

The blunderbuss functions as a {@item Musket|XPHB} that ignores {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading}, and it can make its own ammunition that deals Necrotic damage on a hit. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it determined by the blunderbuss's rarity. While holding the blunderbuss, you can use the blunderbuss as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Jinxshot (Rare+)
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a blast from the blunderbuss that forces each creature within a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} to make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the blunderbuss's bonus), taking {@damage 2d4} Necrotic damage (Rare) or {@damage 3d6} Necrotic damage (Very Rare+) on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Blunderbuss of the Grinning Sinner (Very Rare)
entries: This dark, ornate blunderbuss has a brass barrel and a wooden handle etched with arcane symbols. It was the Grinning Sinner's weapon of choice, who imbued it with the power to shoot jinxes and hexes.

The blunderbuss functions as a {@item Musket|XPHB} that ignores {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading}, and it can make its own ammunition that deals Necrotic damage on a hit. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it determined by the blunderbuss's rarity. While holding the blunderbuss, you can use the blunderbuss as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Jinxshot (Rare+)
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with a blast from the blunderbuss that forces each creature within a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} to make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the blunderbuss's bonus), taking {@damage 2d4} Necrotic damage (Rare) or {@damage 3d6} Necrotic damage (Very Rare+) on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Sinner's Jinx (Very Rare+)
entries: Once during your turn when you damage a creature with the blunderbuss, the target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC = 16 + the blunderbuss's bonus) or be cursed for 1 minute. When it makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} while cursed, it subtracts {@dice 1d4} from the total. The curse ends if this property is used on another creature.

name: Bolt
entries: This {@item Heavy Crossbow|XPHB} is made of metal and fires small bolts of electricity instead of normal ammunition. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you pull the string back to load the crossbow, the string crackles with energy and loads a small bolt of lightning ammunition instead. Attacks made with this crossbow deal {@damage 1d12} Lightning damage instead of {@dice 1d10} Piercing. In addition, whenever you make a ranged attack with this weapon against a metal target or a creature wearing metal armor, you make the attack roll with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

This crossbow acts as a small lightning rod. If another creature within 10 feet of you takes Lightning damage while you're holding the crossbow, you take {@damage 1d6} Lightning damage for every 10 Lightning damage the other creature took.

name: Bolt, Acid
entries: Alchemical Ammunition carries an alchemical payload. Rather than hurling a vial, you fire Alchemical Ammunition from a Ranged weapon, using your normal attack bonus with that weapon.
Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

entries.name: {@item Acid|XPHB}
entries: When one of these pieces of Alchemical Ammunition hits, it deals the ammunition's normal damage, then applies the effect of the listed item to the target. No saving throw is allowed against this effect.

name: Bolt, Alchemist's Fire
entries: Alchemical Ammunition carries an alchemical payload. Rather than hurling a vial, you fire Alchemical Ammunition from a Ranged weapon, using your normal attack bonus with that weapon.
Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

entries.name: {@item Alchemist's Fire|XPHB}
entries: When one of these pieces of Alchemical Ammunition hits, it deals the ammunition's normal damage, then applies the effect of the listed item to the target. No saving throw is allowed against this effect.

name: Bolt, Armor-Piercing
entries: This ammunition works like an {@itemProperty AP|GrimHollowPG24|Armor-Piercing} Melee weapon, but you fire the ammunition as a projectile from a Ranged weapon.

name: Bolt, Blessed
entries: When you hit with Blessed ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Radiant. Also, if the target is Fiend, Fey, or Undead, that creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn.

name: Bolt, Bludgeoning
entries: Advanced Ammunition named after a damage type deals that damage type. Arrows and bolts can have wide heads that deal Slashing damage or blunt tips that deal Bludgeoning damage. A sling bullet can have facets that deal Piercing damage. All such ammo is heavier than normal; the weapon's maximum range while using it is halved.

name: Bolt, Brutal
entries: Designed to open wide wounds, such as with a broad-bladed arrowhead, Brutal ammunition works like a {@itemMastery Brutal|GrimHollowPG24} Melee weapon.

name: Bolt, Desecrated
entries: When you hit with Desecrated ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Necrotic. Also, if the target is Celestial, Humanoid, or Plant, that creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn.

name: Bolt, Holy Water
entries: Alchemical Ammunition carries an alchemical payload. Rather than hurling a vial, you fire Alchemical Ammunition from a Ranged weapon, using your normal attack bonus with that weapon.
Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

entries.name: {@item Holy Water|XPHB}
entries: When one of these pieces of Alchemical Ammunition hits, it deals the ammunition's normal damage, then applies the effect of the listed item to the target. No saving throw is allowed against this effect.

name: Bolt, Incendiary
entries: When you hit with Incendiary ammunition, the target takes an additional {@damage 1d4} Fire damage.

name: Bolt, Ranging
entries: Advanced Ammunition that has the Ranging property is lighter and better made than common counterparts. When you fire Ranging ammo, you can increase your weapon's normal range by 50 percent.

name: Bolt, Slashing
entries: Advanced Ammunition named after a damage type deals that damage type. Arrows and bolts can have wide heads that deal Slashing damage or blunt tips that deal Bludgeoning damage. A sling bullet can have facets that deal Piercing damage. All such ammo is heavier than normal; the weapon's maximum range while using it is halved.

name: Bolt, War Oil
entries: Alchemical Ammunition carries an alchemical payload. Rather than hurling a vial, you fire Alchemical Ammunition from a Ranged weapon, using your normal attack bonus with that weapon.
Alchemical Ammunition is heavier than normal; the weapon's normal and long ranges are halved. The Alchemical Ammunition is destroyed once used, whether the attack hits or misses.

entries.name: War Oil
entries: A target hit by a piece of Alchemical Ammunition packed with War Oil takes damage as normal for the ammunition, then becomes coated in War Oil for up to 1 minute. Alternatively, you can target a point, such as the ground or a wall, and on an attack roll against AC 10, cause the War Oil to spill out of the ammunition, creating a circular patch of the viscous substance with a 10-foot radius.

War Oil is slick and highly flammable. An area coated in War Oil counts as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, and a creature that starting its turn in a coated area or enters the coated area for the first time on a turn must succeed a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or gain the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0 until the end of its turn. Additionally, if a creature or area coated with War

Oil is exposed to an open flame or some other source of Fire damage, the oil ignites. The ignited oil burns for two rounds, dealing {@damage 2d4} Fire damage to any creature or object who comes in contact with it, and an additional {@damage 2d4} Fire damage to any creature that ends its turn while in contact with it. An ignited creature can douse the flames by using an action.
After burning for two rounds, being doused, or remaining unlit for 1 minute, War Oil dries up and ceases to be slippery or flammable.

name: Bolt, Whistling
entries: Ammunition with the Whistling property creates a high-pitched sound after firing. This sound is audible out to 300 feet from the ammo as it flies. Whistling ammo isn't heavier, but it catches the air with intricate baffles to create its sound, so its maximum range is half normal. Whistling ammo deals Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Upkeep
entries: When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wooden Ammunition
entries: Wooden ammunition is destroyed after hitting or missing a target.

name: Bomboozler (rare)
entries: Within this sturdy, corrosion-resistant polyhedron is a {@i phial of ooze acid}; a caustic substance with remarkable powers of biological alteration.

entries.name: Caustic Calamity
entries: As an action, you can press a button on the polyhedron, crushing the phial, and then toss the device up to {@b 60 feet} away. The resulting chemical reaction produces an explosion of acid in a {@b 20-foot} radius. Each creature in the area must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d6} acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, the reaction produces unpredictable biomantic effects on a failed saving throw. Roll a d10 and consult the table below to determine the effect. If a creature comes under an effect lasting 1 minute, it can make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

rows: The acid stops regeneration and healing. The creature can't regain hit points for 1 minute.
The acid coats creatures, dissolving them. The creature takes {@damage 2d6} acid damage at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute.
Parts of creatures' bodies meld together. The creature has disadvantage on attack rolls for 1 minute.
The acid fuses feet and footwear to the ground. The creature is {@condition restrained} until the end of your next turn.
The acid fuses the eyelids shut. The creature is {@condition blinded} until the end of your next turn.
The acid causes creatures' skin to become phosphorescent. The creature is under the effect of the {@spell faerie fire} spell for 1 minute.
The acid causes growths to appear and disappear on creatures' bodies, hindering their actions. The creature is under the effect of the {@spell bane} spell for 1 minute.
The acid causes creatures to shrink. The creature is under the reduce effect of the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell for 1 minute.
The acid fuses mouths shut. The creature is under the effect of the {@spell zippit!|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} spell for 1 minute.
Roll twice on the table, rerolling any further 10s and duplicate results.

entries: Once this property of the item has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn and a new {@i phial of ooze acid} has been installed in the device.

name: Bomboozler (very rare)
entries: Within this sturdy, corrosion-resistant polyhedron is a {@i phial of ooze acid}; a caustic substance with remarkable powers of biological alteration.

entries.name: Caustic Calamity
entries: As an action, you can press a button on the polyhedron, crushing the phial, and then toss the device up to {@b 60 feet} away. The resulting chemical reaction produces an explosion of acid in a {@b 20-foot} radius. Each creature in the area must make a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d6} acid damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, the reaction produces unpredictable biomantic effects on a failed saving throw. You can roll twice on the table below to determine the effects, ignoring any duplicate results. If a creature comes under an effect lasting 1 minute, it can make a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

rows: The acid stops regeneration and healing. The creature can't regain hit points for 1 minute.
The acid coats creatures, dissolving them. The creature takes {@damage 2d6} acid damage at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute.
Parts of creatures' bodies meld together. The creature has disadvantage on attack rolls for 1 minute.
The acid fuses feet and footwear to the ground. The creature is {@condition restrained} until the end of your next turn.
The acid fuses the eyelids shut. The creature is {@condition blinded} until the end of your next turn.
The acid causes creatures' skin to become phosphorescent. The creature is under the effect of the {@spell faerie fire} spell for 1 minute.
The acid causes growths to appear and disappear on creatures' bodies, hindering their actions. The creature is under the effect of the {@spell bane} spell for 1 minute.
The acid causes creatures to shrink. The creature is under the reduce effect of the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell for 1 minute.
The acid fuses mouths shut. The creature is under the effect of the {@spell zippit!|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} spell for 1 minute.
Roll twice on the table, rerolling any further 10s and duplicate results.

entries: Once this property of the item has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn and a new {@i phial of ooze acid} has been installed in the device.

entries.name: Trigger Warning
entries: Instead of throwing the bomb, you can use an action to plant it on a surface and set it to detonate in a specific situation. As an action, a creature can disarm a bomb set to explode in this way with a successful {@dc 16} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|PHB}) check. On a failed check, the bomb goes off and the creature that made the check automatically fails the saving throw. Choose one of the following detonation options:

items.name: Proximity Trigger
entries: Choose a range between 0 and {@b 20 feet}. The first Small or larger creature to move within that distance of the bomb after you leave the area sets it off. A creature that succeeds on a {@dc 16} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|PHB}) check can approach the bomb without triggering it.

items.name: Time Bomb
entries: Choose an amount of time ranging from 1 to 100 rounds. On initiative count 20 of the round you choose, the bomb explodes.

name: Bone Painted Stone
entries: {#itemEntry Painted Stone|TalesFromTheShadows}
For 1 minute, each time you damage a creature with a weapon or spell attack, you regain an amount of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.

name: Bonebreakers
entries: These unremarkable brass knuckles appear well used if not well loved. They are covered in dings and scratches accompanied by the odd stain.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a creature with this weapon, you can attempt to maim them. When you do so, the creature must succeed on a DC 19 Constitution saving throw or be maimed in one of the following ways of your choice. The creature remains maimed until it is targeted by a {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} spell or similar magic. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Broken Arm
entries: The creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.

entries.name: Broken Leg
entries: The creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved.

entries.name: Broken Ribs
entries: The creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength and Dexterity ability checks and saving throws.

entries.name: Broken Skull
entries: The creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Intelligence and Wisdom ability checks and saving throws.

name: Bonfire Charm
entries: This fiery glass sculpture is 4 inches tall and has a small, magical ember inside. When placed on a burning campfire or torch, the charm and ember enchant the fire with a faint, healing radiance. If you or any friendly creatures within the fire's light regain hit points at the end of a short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures treats a Hit Die roll of 1 as a 2.

name: Bonfire Seed
entries: When thrown, this illusion seed turns into a roaring bonfire about 5 feet across, complete with large and small timbers and hot coals. If thrown into a space where a creature is standing, you must make a ranged attack. If the attack misses, the creature knocks the seed into any neighboring space. If it hits, the bonfire does {@damage 2d6} fire damage to any creature standing in it at the start of its turn. The bonfire burns out normally in {@dice 1d4} hours, depending on rain and other conditions.

entries.name: Illusion Seeds
entries: Illusion seeds are wondrous items first created in the Shadow Realm and reliant on a supply of shadow matter to power their effects—each such seed generates an illusion and those illusions can take quite powerful forms. While illusion seeds are fairly permanent in the Shadow Realm, where there is shadow matter to empower and sustain the illusions, they are notably less permanent anywhere else. In the mortal world and on other planes, the effects of illusion seeds last for {@dice 2d12} hours and then crumble away in a small burst of glittering light and shadows.

To use an illusion seed, its owner merely needs to throw it 5 feet or more from themselves (to avoid being caught in the magical effect). Once expended, their effects are permanent (in the Shadow Realm), though they can be unraveled using {@spell dispel magic} (DC 13).

name: Boog's Ball
entries: This magic stone sphere is incredibly dense, has a 3-inch radius, and grows when thrown. As an action, you can throw the ball at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. If you throw the ball 30 feet or less away from you, the ball grows to a 5-foot radius. If you throw the ball farther than 30 feet, it grows to a 10-foot radius. Each creature in the ball's area when it reaches that point must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 14 ({@damage 4d6}) bludgeoning damage. The ball then shrinks back to its 3-inch radius and teleports either into your open hand or into a pack or pouch you wear (your choice).

name: Book of Clothier's Croquis
entries: This magic book has only the basic outline of a humanoid drawn on each of its pages. When found, the book has {@dice 2d6 + 8} remaining pages inside. If you spend at least 10 minutes drawing a detailed set of clothes on the outlined humanoid, the page becomes charged with magic. A creature holding a torn-out sheet of charged paper can use its action to speak the book's command phrase, causing the drawn clothes to either magically appear on its body or transform any similar, overlapping garment it's already wearing to match the new appearance. The sheet of paper then turns to dust and is destroyed. If the creature isn't humanoid, the clothes fit as best they can as determined by the GM.

A transformed garment loses any magical or nonmagical property it may have until it returns to its normal form, unless that garment's function is completely unchanged by the new appearance. For example, a set of {@item plate armor|PHB} that's transformed into a leather vest would no longer grant any benefit to AC, but a {@item chain shirt|PHB} that's been transformed to match the ones worn by the royal guard still would.

The drawn clothes and transformed garments remain for up to 4 hours but magically disappear or return to their normal form if you remove them or use an action to speak the command phrase again. The drawn clothes are physical but offer no benefits to AC. Although the drawn clothes and transformed garments can duplicate the appearance of other magic clothes, they don't gain their magical properties.

name: Book of Dzyan
reqAttune: by a DC 20 Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} check)
entries: This strange tome is reputed to have been originally penned by the first human civilization that long ago disappeared beneath the rising seas. It grants its bearer insights needed to peer into secretive realms, at the cost of a growing suspicion of others.

entries.name: Language:
entries: {@language Celestial|XPHB}.

entries.name: Attunement Check:
entries: Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) DC 20. To end your attunement to the Book of Dzyan, a demon or devil must cast {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} on you. The book then disappears in a flash of light.

entries.name: Benefits:
entries: While attuned to the Book of Dzyan, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can see {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creatures and objects within 30 feet of you.
You can read and write {@language Abyssal|XPHB} and {@language Infernal|XPHB}.

If you can cast spells, you always have {@spell Guidance|XPHB}, {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}, {@spell Locate Object|XPHB}, {@spell Fly|XPHB}, {@spell Divination|XPHB}, {@spell Contact Deity|CthulhuTorchlight}, and {@spell Call Deity|CthulhuTorchlight} prepared.
Simply touching a wall or object allows you to detect secret doors or similar hidden compartments built into that object within 5 feet of you.

You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks. If your check result is a 20 or higher, you learn a secret about a creature. This benefit applies only once for a given creature.
The save DC of your spells gains a +1 bonus.

entries.name: Drawbacks:
entries: When you encounter a creature you have never seen before, roll a {@dice d20} at the start of each of your turns. On a 10 or higher, you can only use your action that turn to {@action Study|XPHB} it and learn about it. Once you do so, you no longer need to make this roll when that creature is present. This drawback applies to a general type of creature. If you encountered a {@creature Hydra|XMM} this drawback would apply, but it would not affect you when encountering different {@creature Hydra|XMM|Hydras} in the future.

entries.name: Insight-Insatiable Curiosity (+15):
entries: You cannot bear to think that there are secrets out there that are beyond your grasp. A closed door, a parchment covered with strange runes, or anything else that holds a secret is an irresistible lure to you.

entries.name: Lore:
entries: The Book of Dzyan allows you to automatically succeed all DC 25 or lower checks made to learn about creatures of the planes.

name: Book of Ebon Tides
entries: This strange twilight-hued tome was written on pages of pure shadow weave, bound in traditional birchboard covers, wrapped with shadow goblin hide, and imbued with the memories of forests in the Shadow Realm. Its covers often dance with shadows as if it were resting in a forest grove, and some owners swear that a goblin face appears on them now and again. The sturdy lock on one side opens only for wizards, elves, and shadow fey.

The book has 15 charges, and it regains {@dice 2d6 + 3} expended charges daily in the twilight before dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the book retains its Ebon Tides and Shadow Lore properties but loses its Spells property.

entries.name: Ebon Tides
entries: If you spend 100 hours over a period of 30 days or more studying the volume, you can perform a magical ritual to shift the structure of the Shadow Realm in particular ways. At any point after your study completes, you can expend 5 of the book's charges while spending 1 minute {@status concentration||concentrating} and performing invocations to transform the terrain near you. You don't need to repeat the study to use this property again. When the magic ritual completes, make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check and consult the table below for the appropriate DCs. You can change the terrain in any one way listed at your result or lower. For example, if your result was 17, you could turn a small forest up to 30 feet across into a grassland, create a grove of trees up to 240 feet across, create a 6-foot-wide flowing stream, overgrow 1,500 feet of an existing road, or other similar option. Only natural terrain you can see can be affected. Built structures, such as homes or castles, remain untouched, though roads and trails can be overgrown or hidden. On a failure, the terrain is unchanged. On a 1, an overshadow (see Tome of Beasts 2 or substitute with {@creature ghost}) also appears and attacks you. On a 20, you can choose two options.

Deities, fey lords and ladies, archdevils, demon lords, and other powerful rulers in the Shadow Realm can prevent these terrain modifications from happening in their presence or anywhere within their respective domains.

entries.name: Shadow Lore
entries: If you spend 10 minutes referencing this book while researching the Shadow Realm or its creatures, you double your proficiency bonus on {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, and {@skill Religion} checks to recall lore about such subjects for the next 24 hours. If you don't have proficiency in these skills, you instead gain proficiency in them for the next 24 hours, but you are only proficient when recalling information about the subjects of your research. This research can be done during a short rest.

entries.name: Spells
entries: While holding the book, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC and spellcasting ability: {@spell cloak of shadow|bookOfEbonTides}* (1 charge), {@spell darkness} (2 charges), {@spell mirror image} (2 charges), {@spell phantasmal killer} (4 charges), {@spell see invisibility} (2 charges), {@spell seeming} (5 charges), {@spell shadow gateway|bookOfEbonTides}* (5 charges), {@spell shadow step|bookOfEbonTides}* (4 charges), or {@spell slither|bookOfEbonTides}* (2 charges). You can also use an action to cast the {@spell douse light|bookOfEbonTides}* or {@spell minor illusion} cantrips from the book without using any charges. (Spells marked with an asterisk are from Deep Magic.)

entries.name: Retributive Shadows
entries: You can use an action to speak a special command word and rip the book in half. The book is destroyed and releases its remaining magic in a wave of shadow magic. Four 10-foot cubes of shadow move outward from the book in the cardinal directions, and each cube moves up to 20 feet each round, away from the point where the book was destroyed. This effect works like the creeping darkness (see Deep Magic) spell, except it creates four cubes instead of three, and the necrotic damage dealt by the spell increases by {@dice 1d6} for each charge remaining in the book. At the GM's discretion, this effect can work like the {@spell incendiary cloud} spell instead of the creeping {@spell darkness} spell, except the cloud is a cloud of shadow that deals necrotic damage instead of fire damage, is centered on you, and the damage dealt by the spell increases by {@dice 1d4} for each charge remaining in the book.

rows: Obscure a path and remove all signs of passage (30 feet per point over 7).
Create a grove of trees (30 feet across per point over 9).
Create or dry up a lake or pond (1 foot wide per point over 11).
Create a flowing stream (1 foot wide per point over 11).
Overgrow an existing road with brush or trees (300 feet per point over 12).
Shift a river to a new course (300 feet per point over 13).
Move a forest (300 feet per point over 14).
Create a small hill, riverbank, or cliff (10 feet tall per point over 15).
Turn a small forest into grassland or clearing or vice versa (30 feet across per point over 16).
Create a new river (10 feet wide per point over 17).
Turn a large forest into grassland or vice versa (300 feet across per point over 19).
Create a new mountain (1,000 feet high per point over 19).
Shrink an existing hill or mountain (reducing 1,000 feet per point over 21).

entries: Ebon Tides In Midgard

Written by an elven princess at the Court of Silver Words, this volume encodes her understanding and mastery of shadow. Whimsical illusions suffuse every page, animating its illuminated capital letters and ornamental figures. The book is a famous work among the sable elves of the Shadow Realm, and it opens to the touch of any elfmarked or sable elf character.

name: Book of Instant Copying
entries: This book has a glass cover and is typically found with {@dice 2d10 + 30} blank pages. As an action, you can place a piece of paper or similar object (such as a leaf or patterned fabric) between the book's glass and the page below it and speak the book's command word. When you do, the book magically inscribes an image of the placed object in black ink as it appears pressed against the glass on the first blank page of the book.

Copied magic scrolls or spellbooks appear as nonsensical glyphs when copied in this way. When the last page of the book has been used, you can rebind it with 50 blank new pages using 50 gp of fine materials and 8 hours of work.

name: Book of Secrets
entries: This book contains Xorannox's collection of dirty secrets about other people: intrigues between nobles, unfaithful leaders, infernal contracts between devils and clergy of good-aligned temples, and similar misdeeds.

If you study the book for 1 uninterrupted hour, you find a piece of secret information about an important public figure of your choice. You only find information if the GM determines that person has a hidden secret. If you reveal you know the secret to the figure, you gain a +5 bonus on Charisma checks to influence them for 24 hours. After the book reveals ten secrets in this way, it holds no more secrets of use.

name: Boots of Dancing
entries: These boots make your every movement smoother, stealthier, and more elegant. You can leap up to 10 feet vertically without effort, and land safely, taking no damage, from falls up to 30 feet—merely landing in a rather dramatic manner.
When combined with a ring of dancing, you gain advantage on all Charisma ability checks.

name: Boots of Dendallen
entries: These dark, fleshy boots grant marvelous powers and enhance your normal movement. While wearing the boots, you gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hover. You can hover up to 20 feet off the ground in this way, leaving behind a thin trail of shadow when you move. In addition, when you take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action while wearing the boots, you can move an extra 10 feet.

The boots have 4 charges and regain {@dice 1d3 + 1} expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the boots, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to cast either the Expeditious Retreat or {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} spell from them. When you cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} in this way, the silvery mist that surrounds you is instead dark and ominous.

entries.name: Curse
entries: When you pull these cursed boots over your feet for the first time, make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately remove the boots before they extend the curse to you. On a failed save, you become cursed, and the boots' muscly sinews dig into your legs and feet, interlocking with your own flesh; you take {@damage 4d8} Necrotic damage, and you can't remove the boots unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

While wearing the boots, your feet sometimes move in unexpected ways. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) checks and Dexterity saving throws, and when you have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, it costs you an extra 10 feet of movement to right yourself. When you remove the boots after being cursed by them, you take another {@damage 4d8} Necrotic damage as they painfully tear themselves from your body.

name: Boots of Haste
entries: While you wear these boots, you can click your heels together to cast the {@spell haste} spell on yourself as a bonus action. You don't suffer from lethargy when the spell ends when cast using these boots. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until next dawn.

name: Boots of Shadow Walking
entries: Your movement is enhanced on shadow roads and across long distances. Your travel pace is double the normal rate, though your speed in combat is not affected.

name: Boots of Soft Landing
entries: A pair of brown, fur-lined boots that have been finely crafted. The boots are quilted, and have ceramic soles that emit a colourful magical energy.
While wearing these boots, you always land on your feet and cannot be knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}. Additionally, your fall speed is capped at 60 ft per round, and you take no damage from falling.

name: Boots of the Cloud Jumper
entries: While wearing these boots, you can jump while in the air as if you'd leapt from solid ground. You can't jump farther than your remaining movement would allow, and you treat all jumps made in this way as if they were standing jumps. When you make a midair jump, faint clouds fly out from under your feet. The boots allow you to jump in this way once before they need to make contact with a solid surface again. {@variantrule Jumping|XPHB} in this way while falling before landing on solid ground allows you to subtract up to 20 feet when calculating damage from the fall.

name: Boots of the Stampede
entries: While wearing these boots, you can move an additional 15 feet whenever you take the {@action Dash} action.

name: Boots of the Vigilant
entries: While you wear these boots, you can sense impending danger. After you roll initiative, you can choose to roll a {@dice d8} and add it to your initiative roll. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Borboss' Joyous Wand of Color
entries: This crystalline, prismatic wand can channel the illustrative intent of its wielder. While holding the wand, you can magically create a stroke of color in the air, allowing you to draw in midair or on any surface the wand touches. The effect is illusory, visibly magical, radiates {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 5-foot radius, and dissipates after 1 hour.
If you attempt to draw on an object that is being worn or carried by an unwilling creature, that creature must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw in order to avoid it.

name: Boreal Pendant
entries: This enlarged, floating snowflake is magically held in place and changes its shape as temperatures fluctuate. While attuned to the pendant you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage and give off an aura of cheeriness. The snowflake has 8 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing it, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 15) from it: {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Color Spray|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Hypnotic Pattern|XPHB} (3 charges), or {@spell Ice Storm|XPHB} (4 charges).
If you expend the last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the snowflake melts into a puddle of water. After 1 year, the pendant reforms around the magical golden brackets that hold it in place.

name: Borealus
entries: This legendary artifact was created by a powerful wizard, crafted from the finger of a towering, ancient elemental aspect of frost. It is so cold to the touch that it numbs any skin it comes into contact with, although an attuned character is immune to this effect.

entries.name: Gifts of the Rime
entries: As long as you are attuned to the Borealus, you gain the following benefits:
