entries: This adamantine helm is fashioned in the likeness of a triceratops and decorated with painted designs. You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while you wear this helmet. If you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a target immediately before hitting it with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} using the helmet, the target takes Piercing damage equal to {@dice 3d4} plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage for your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. If you hit and the target is no more than one size larger than you, it must also succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

In addition, while wearing the helmet, you can cast the {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} spell from it, transforming yourself into a {@creature Triceratops|XMM}. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed.

name: Chain Devil Gloves
entries: These leather gloves are fashioned from the hands of a slain chain devil. While wearing these gloves, an ethereal chain attaches itself to any weapon you throw that has the thrown property. The chain has a reach of 60 feet and breaks its connection to the weapon if the weapon is held by a creature or if you are ever more than 60 feet away from it. You can have up to 4 of these chains at any time.

As an action, you can cause these chains to suddenly retract and pull any attached weapons with them. Any creature within the path of one or more of these weapons must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes force damage equal to the damage die of the thrown weapon. A solid object or wall blocks the path of the retracted chain and weapon.
A retracted weapon lands harmlessly at your feet or in an open hand once it reaches you.

name: Champion's Greatbow
entries: This large bow is wrought from the boughs of an old, resilient tree. Its wooden frame is exceptionally sturdy but difficult to draw. You must have a Strength score of 13 or higher to wield this bow. This bow's damage die is a {@dice d10}, and when you make a ranged attack with this bow, you score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

Once on each of your turns when you make a ranged attack with this weapon, you can use the bow to fire a {@item javelin|PHB} or {@item spear|PHB}, instead of an arrow, without affecting the bow's damage die. When you do, the bow's normal and long ranges are halved for the attack. If the attack hits, the target takes extra piercing damage equal to your Strength modifier.

name: Chancellor's Crest
entries: While wearing this amulet, you can read all writing, and speak and understand any language.

You can use an action to cast one of the following spells: {@spell detect thoughts}, {@spell sending}, or {@spell Rary's telepathic bond}. Once the amulet has been used to cast one of these spells, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn. You can choose your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score as the spellcasting ability for casting these spells, and use your proficiency bonus to determine their attack bonus and saving throw DC.

entries.name: Crown Authority
entries: A character cannot attune to more than one Seal of Drakkenheim. Guardian constructs in Drakkenheim such as {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim|wall gargoyles} and {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim|tower dragons} do not attack you while you are attuned to one of the Seals of Drakkenheim. An individual guardian ignores this effect for 24 hours if you attack it or cast a spell upon it.

As an action, you may present a Seal of Drakkenheim to rebuke the guardians. You make an opposed Charisma ability check against each {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim} or {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim} that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you. If you win the contest, the creature is rebuked for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. A rebuked creature doesn't move, and can't take actions or reactions. A creature who wins the contest is immune to your rebuke for 24 hours.

name: Charged Gauntlets
entries: These light gauntlets are made from cloth woven from the hair of a fiend and reinforced with the scales of a dragon. The gauntlets are washed with an alchemical formula made from elemental fluid and undead dust. They are then powered with a rare animus collected from an aberration.

Each time you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} while attuned to these magic gauntlets they gain one charge. The gauntlets can have up to 10 charges. Any unexpended charges disappear when you take a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} or roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}.
While the gauntlets have at least one charge, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal Lightning damage instead of its normal damage type.

While the gauntlets have 5 or more charges, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal an additional {@damage 2d6} Lightning damage and push the target 10 feet away from you on a hit.
You can expend 2 charges from the gauntlets to cast the {@spell Shield|XPHB} spell.
You can expend 10 charges from the gauntlets to cast {@spell Destructive Wave|XPHB} or {@spell Wall of Force|XPHB}, using your monk's focus saving throw DC.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating Charged Gauntlets requires a Very Rare Workshop and the following Very Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Aberrant Animus

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Undead Dust

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Elemental Fluid

items.name: [Hair]
entries: Hair from a Fiend

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Scales from a Blue or Bronze Dragon

name: Charged Rapier
entries: This blade snaps and crackles with electrical power as it's waved through the air. While holding the rapier, you have resistance to lightning damage. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it deals an extra {@damage 1d4} lightning damage to any target it hits.

entries.name: Electric Charge
entries: If you are proficient with this weapon, when you move at least 20 feet in a straight line on your turn while holding this rapier, you can speak its command word as a bonus action to briefly disappear and transform into a bolt of lightning. When you do, choose an unoccupied space you can see within 20 feet of you that's along the same straight line and in the same direction in which you're moving. You form a 5-foot-wide line of lightning originating from yourself that extends to the unoccupied space. You reappear in that space as the bolt of lightning passes through anything in its path.

If there are any creatures in the line of lightning, roll a {@dice d20} and add 9 to the roll. If the total of the roll meets or exceeds the AC of any creature in the line, that creature takes {@damage 1d4 + 1} lightning damage as you pierce through it as the bolt of lightning.

name: Charlatan's Gloves
entries: While wearing these gloves, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to produce an illusory image that fits in the palm of your hand. The image lasts for 1 minute or until your {@status Concentration|XPHB} ends (as if you were {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on a spell). The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, because things can pass through it.

If a creature takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check contested by your Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

name: Charlatan's Wardrobe
entries: This set of plain clothes is exceptionally comfortable and easy to wear. They are always clean and smell freshly washed and lightly perfumed. You can change the appearance of the clothes as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action by twirling in place and using a command word. The clothes' changed appearance is illusory. Physical interaction with the clothes reveals their changed appearance to be an illusion, since things can pass through it. A creature that takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the clothes can determine that their changed appearance is an illusion with a successful DC 13 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. Regardless of their appearance, the clothes offer no additional protection from the elements, and can only appear to be clothes.

name: Charm of Swarms
entries: This charm resembles a large gnat. It is made of the spores of dead mushrooms; the mandibles of an insectoid creature are placed upon it. The charm is coated in an acidic bile and held together by dried mucus. It smells of bugs and rot.

When an enemy within 5 feet of you scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on an attack made against you, you can cause the enemy to become {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} ({@dice 2d6} Necrotic). While the target is {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} in this way, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks against the target.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Charm of Swarms requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Acidic Bile

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Mucus

items.name: [Natural Weapon]
entries: Spores

items.name: [Natural Weapon]
entries: Mandibles

name: Chi-Balancing Tea
entries: This potion is specially brewed by the monks of Durheim using a unique leaf found only in their gardens. The tea remains magically warm while inside its traditional porcelain bottle. The potion's flavor is deep and smoky, and leaves a sour aftertaste like the air after a storm.

When you drink this potion, it cures any short-term madness afflicting you, and if you are {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}, it ends those conditions. In addition, if you have 2 or more levels in the monk class, you regain {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended ki points.

name: Chicken Chaser
entries: When you drink this potion, your hair turns dark red (if you have any), and you gain the ability to speak with chickens permanently, as if by the {@spell Speak with Animals} spell. Additionally, you can crow a sacred and thunderous cackle that summons 100 chickens in a 20-foot radius centered on you. These chickens appear running from a distance, digging out from the ground below, and falling from the sky in a veritable tsunami of flapping, clucking poultry. Each creature in the area (excluding you) must make a DC 19 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 30d6} slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once you've summoned the chickens in this way, you can't do so again. This doesn't count against the number of potions you can have affecting your body at once.
{@font {@style 59|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Chillspike
entries: This cold steel weapon from the Everglacier is topped with a menacing ice spike that never melts. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 1d10} Cold damage on a hit. In addition, this weapon's properties and attacks with it ignore {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.

When you reduce a Large or smaller creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} using this weapon, you can choose to encase that creature in ice. An encased creature can't gain the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and is held in place by a shell of ice for 1 minute. The creature doesn't make {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws} while it's encased in the ice. The ice has AC 12, HP 20, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire damage. If a spell or other magical effect restores {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to the encased creature or the ice is destroyed, the ice crumbles and releases the creature.

entries.name: Everglacier's Fury
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can plunge the {@item Pike|XPHB} into the ground at your feet. When you do, the blade of the {@item Pike|XPHB} magically vanishes into the earth and summons up to three icy spikes from the ground nearby. Choose up to three different targets on the ground you can see within 20 feet of you. An affected target must succeed on a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d8} Cold damage as a frozen spike erupts from the ground beneath it. The spikes immediately recede into the ground after the effect, and the icy blade of the {@item Pike|XPHB} reappears.

name: Chimeric Collar
entries: This magic collar has three sections of sculpted metal bound by a strip of leather, with each section representing the head of a dragon, lion, and ram. You can place the collar on a willing Medium or smaller creature using an action. If the creature is a friendly beast companion or familiar (such as one summoned by the {@spell find familiar|PHB} spell), you can speak the collar's command word as part of this action to create a magical bond between you and the creature. The bond remains until the collar is removed.

You can use a bonus action to speak the collar's command word while you can see the bonded creature within 30 feet of you. When you do, the creature grows in size to become Large, provided there's enough space. When it becomes enlarged, the creature gains {@dice 2d10 + 4} temporary hit points, can understand {@language Draconic} (but can't speak it), and magically grows a second, identical head next to its own that lasts for the duration of the effect. Whenever the enlarged creature takes the {@action Attack} action, it can make two attacks, or it can take the Multiattack action instead if it has that action. The creature remains enlarged for up to 1 minute, until it drops to 0 hit points, or until you end the effect using a bonus action. Once this property of the collar has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

If the beast or familiar wearing the collar is a transformed humanoid or other creature, such as by the {@spell polymorph|PHB} spell or similar magic, the bond fails when you speak the command word and the collar has no effect. If the bonded creature is a familiar summoned by the {@spell find familiar|PHB} spell, the collar and familiar disappear into a pocket dimension together whenever you temporarily dismiss it. If the bonded familiar is dismissed forever or drops to 0 hit points, it leaves the collar behind. A creature can only gain the benefits of one magical collar at a time.

name: Chip
entries: Delerium is a magical mineral left behind by the meteor that landed in Drakkenheim. It appears in geode clusters of translucent, sharp-edged crystals which reflect octarine light. The eldritch stones softly hum in dissonant tones, and glow brightly at night or when exposed to magic. Deposits are found throughout Drakkenheim, often fused into stone streets and buildings like crystalline moss.
A typical delerium fragment is about the size of a finger. Crystals may be fist-sized or slightly larger, and geodes may be as big as a pumpkin. Massive clusters might grow taller than a human.

entries.name: Delerium Properties
entries: All delerium samples have the following traits regardless of size:

items: {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage; as well as Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from non-magical weapons.
{@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistant} to Acid, Cold, Fire, and Lightning damage; as well as Slashing and Piercing damage from magical weapons.
{@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerable} to Bludgeoning damage from magical weapons.

Unless contained within an {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}, delerium shatters and crumbles into worthless ash when reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. However, delerium geodes release a random {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} when destroyed.

entries.name: Delerium Hazards
entries: When a humanoid creature touches delerium without protective gear for the first time on their turn, or ends their turn in bodily contact with delerium, they must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage and gain one level of {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.

entries.name: Delerium Harvesting
entries: Delerium found in Drakkenheim is usually fused into the ground or stone buildings. It is carefully extracted using handheld mining equipment such as shovels, picks, hammers, and chisels. Consult the table to determine how long it takes characters to extract delerium. Lacking proper equipment, extraction takes ten times as long. Massive clusters are impossible to extract without heavy equipment or powerful magic.

entries.name: Uses for Delerium
entries: Delerium has vast arcane potential. Beyond trade, crystals are used for several purposes:

entries.name: Spell Component
entries: Delerium may be used as an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} or material component for any spell on the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list. When casting a spell which requires a costly material component, a spellcaster may instead use delerium of equivalent or greater value to the required cost.

entries.name: Magic Items
entries: Delerium is an exceptional material for creating magical items of all kinds. Any existing magic item described in the Basic Rules could be made with delerium. Fragments, shards, crystals, and geodes may be used to make uncommon, rare, very rare, and legendary items respectively. At the GM's discretion, characters who can cast level 5 spells or higher may learn techniques to craft magic items of their own during their downtime.

entries.name: Stable Delerium
entries: The process for crafting magic items with delerium renders the crystals stable. Unless otherwise specified, characters do not take damage nor risk {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} when they touch or handle stable delerium. Stable delerium is damaged and destroyed in the same manner as a normal magic item of its kind.

entries.name: Delerium Dust
entries: Delerium dust is made by grinding the crystals against one another to create a fine powder. This milling process is extraordinarily hazardous unless performed within an {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}. Delerium dust can be used in alchemy, as a spell component, a reagent for brewing potions, or mixed into inks used to scribe spell scrolls. {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB} & Ammunition. Delerium fragments may be used as ammunition for a {@item Sling|XPHB} or fashioned into a makeshift {@item Club|XPHB}. Such weapons and ammunition deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage, and humanoid creatures struck must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}. Delerium used as ammunition in this way is destroyed.

name: Chitinous Club of c'Naazo
entries: Once a tentacle of the monstrosity {@creature c'Naazo|TalesFromTheShadows}, this massive club made of segmented chitin is suffused with glowing, phosphorescent green magic and emits an unpleasant odor when wielded.
You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Venomous Spray
entries: As an action, you point the weapon at your enemies and spray forth a noxious cone of poison. Each creature in a 15-foot cone must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 10 ({@damage 3d6}) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Chromacloth
entries: This silken cloth is enchanted with a unique blend of Abjuration and Evocation magic, allowing it to be used for a number of purposes. It can be one of four colors: red, yellow, green, or blue. While wearing or holding the Chromacloth, you can change its color to another one as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action.

The first time you take damage of the type associated with the Chromacloth's color while wearing it as a headband or wrap, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage. Once the cloth reduces damage in this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

Alternatively, the cloth can be fashioned to be an effective {@item Sling|XPHB}. Ammunition fired from it while using it as a {@item Sling|XPHB} deals damage of the type associated with the cloth's color instead of Bludgeoning.
Refer to the table below for a reference of the Chromacloth's associated colors and damage types:

name: Chromatic Obsidian Greataxe
entries: This prismatic greataxe is made using chromatic obsidian, a dazzling type of stone found where several Elemental Planes meet. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this magic weapon, the target must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. A target takes {@damage 1d6} cold damage, {@damage 1d6} fire damage, {@damage 1d6} lightning damage, and {@damage 1d6} radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Roll the damage dice separately, recording any 6 you roll. For each 6 you roll in this way, use the table below to determine which of the following effects apply.

rows: The target's speed is halved until the end of your next turn.
The target takes an extra 6 fire damage at the end of its next turn.
The target can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.
The next attack roll made against the target before the end of your next turn has advantage.

name: Chronal Sphere
entries: This brass sphere is roughly fist-sized and weighs 1 pound. It vibrates gently while you hold it as tiny mechanisms whir inside. While holding the sphere, you can use a bonus action to speak its command word, causing spectral clock hands to appear on its curved surface and indicate the current time. The hands remain on the surface of the sphere until you speak the command word again. This property only functions on the Material Plane.

entries.name: Spells
entries: While holding the sphere, you can use an action to cast either the {@spell haste|PHB} or {@spell slow|PHB} spell (save DC 18, no concentration required) from it. Once the sphere has been used to cast a spell in this way, it can't be used to cast that spell again. When the sphere has been used to cast both of these spells, it loses this property.

name: Chronicle of Fools
entries: A poorly bound leather journal, the chronicle of fools is filled with stories from countless adventurers and chroniclers, spanning centuries. The back of the book perpetually has blank pages that hunger for more stories. The cover is indestructible, and if the pages are damaged or removed, they will re-form a few minutes later. The writing on the pages can't be obscured, smudged, or altered in any way. Only those attuned to the book can write in it. As an action, you can consult the stories within to grant yourself or a creature who can hear you advantage on any ability check. The target also adds double their proficiency bonus to this check, unless they already have expertise in the skill.

entries.name: Curse
entries: Attuning to the book curses you. You are reluctant to part with the chronicle for as long as you remain attuned to it and are compelled to keep the journal on you at all times. Some force inside the book urges you to write detailed entries about anything that happens in your life, including intimate details about you, your friends, and anything of note you may have come across. The book compels you to write in total honesty and to divulge vulnerabilities, flaws, and even damaging secrets in your entries.

name: Chronomancer's Eyepiece
entries: This singular lens lets you faintly see and command the flow of time around a target. The eyepiece has 5 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the eyepiece, you can expend 1 charge as a reaction at the end of another creature's turn to speak either of the eyepiece's two command words to warp the flow of time around that creature. You must be able to see the target, and it must be within 60 feet of you.

entries.name: Past
entries: If the target is willing, it is teleported back to the space it was at the beginning of its turn. If another creature or object is occupying the space, the target is teleported to nearest unoccupied space instead. An unwilling target must succeed on a DC 16 Charisma saving throw or be teleported in this way against its will.

entries.name: Future
entries: If the target is willing, it can immediately choose to move again, up to half its speed, without provoking opportunity attacks. After a target moves in this way, its speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

name: Chunk of Oozing Fungus
entries: This fist-sized fungal growth is a pallid color, is oozy and lumpy, and frequently fills the air with spores. The fungus has the following properties.

entries.name: Spore Cloud
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can throw the fungus up to 30 feet. The fungus is destroyed and explodes into a cloud of spores in a 30-foot {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point. Each creature other than you in the area must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 3d8} Poison damage and has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. A creature that fails this save by 5 or more also has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. On a successful save, a target takes half damage only.

entries.name: Regrow
entries: You can grow another Chunk of Oozing Fungus by coughing green-black spores into your hand as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. When you do so, you must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum decreases by 5.

entries.name: Fungal Curse
entries: You have a -1 penalty to Constitution saving throws. This penalty increases by 1 immediately after you succeed or fail on the saving throw from the Regrow property.

name: Cinder Coat
entries: This floor-length leather duster is the color of dying embers. You have a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while wearing this armor.

The coat has 3 charges. When you hit a creature with a melee attack, and that creature is not at its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra {@damage 1d10} Fire damage to the target. The coat regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn.

name: Cinder Coat
entries: This floor-length leather duster is the color of dying embers. You have a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor.

The coat has 3 charges. When you hit a creature with an attack, and that creature is not at maximum hit points, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra {@damage 1d10} fire damage to the target. The coat regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn.
The breastplate and shoulder protectors of this armor are made of leather that has been stiffened by being boiled in oil. The rest of the armor is made of softer and more flexible materials.

name: Cinderskin
entries: When you drink this bubbling, black potion, your skin becomes encrusted with charcoal. For 1 hour, you have resistance to fire damage.
{@font {@style 29|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Cinnabar Rapier
entries: This magic {@item Rapier|XPHB}'s blade is alchemically coated in a thin but toxic layer of cinnabar. The weapon has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d8 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a creature with this weapon, you can expend 1 or more charges to cause its poison to leech into the target, dealing an extra {@damage 1d4} Poison damage for each charge expended in this way.

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When the Circlet of Barbed Vision reaches an awakened state, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to poison damage, and you are immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition.
Your ability to gain a bonus to an attack roll can be used twice between rests.

name: Circlet of Barbed Vision (Dormant)
reqAttune: by a creature of non-good alignment
entries: When you don this circlet of gnarled onyx, black barbs dig into your head, imparting power to you as the circlet twists your appearance to amuse {@deity The Spider Queen|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}. The current resting place of the Circlet of Barbed Vision is unknown, but rumor has it that a spectral assassin known as {@creature Jourrael, the Caedogeist|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|the Inevitable End} seeks this relic.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: While the Circlet of Barbed Vision is in a dormant state, you have {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|advantage} on initiative rolls while you wear it, but your Charisma score decreases by 2. Your Charisma score returns to normal if you remove the circlet, but you take {@damage 4d6} psychic damage when you do so.

Additionally, when you make an attack roll, you can use your reaction to gain a +5 bonus to the roll. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the GM says whether the attack hits or misses. You can't use this property again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When the Circlet of Barbed Vision reaches an exalted state, you gain the following benefits:

items: You are immune to poison damage.
You have {@sense truesight} out to a range of 60 feet.
Your ability to gain a bonus to an attack roll can be used three times between rests.

name: Circlet of the Huntsman's Third Eye
entries: This barbed metal circlet features a grotesque yet ornately preserved eye hanging from its center. The eye rests on the forehead of the creature wearing it. While wearing the circlet, its latent cunning guides your hand, granting you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks.

The circlet has 5 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the circlet, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to cast the {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} spell from it. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws made to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on this spell. In addition, you can expend 1 charge as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or 1 additional charge when casting Hunter's Mark in this way, to magically gain {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet for 1 minute.

entries.name: Curse
entries: Attuning to the circlet curses you until you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic; removing the circlet fails to end the curse. While cursed, whenever you roll a 1 on an attack roll or ability check, you take {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage as the eye's intense frustration and scorn pierce your psyche.

name: Circlet of the Sharpened Mind
reqAttune: by a creature with an Intelligence score of 17 or higher
entries: This iron circlet has a magical pearl at its center and can hold up to 4 gemstones. When found, the circlet has 2 gemstones. A gemstone worth at least 5,000 gp can be added to the circlet over the course of 1 minute as it's magically drawn and fastened into place. While wearing the circlet, you can take a special {@action Attack} action on your turn to summon a number of floating, spectral swords equal to the number of gemstones in the circlet and make one melee spell attack with each of them against a target within 10 feet of you. You are proficient with these attacks and use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for them. On a hit, the target takes force damage equal to {@damage 1d8} + your Intelligence modifier. The swords appear at your side and remain there until you dismiss them as a bonus action or until you fall {@condition unconscious} or remove the circlet. While the swords are summoned, you can take this special {@action Attack} action once on each of your turns. The spectral swords shed bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet.

You can replace one of these melee spell attacks with a weapon attack as part of this special Attack action. If you're able to make multiple attacks when you take the {@action Attack} action, you can instead replace a number of these spell attacks up to the number of weapon attacks that you can normally make as part of the {@action Attack} action.

When a hostile creature's movement provokes an opportunity attack from you, you can use your reaction to make one melee spell attack with one of the summoned swords against the creature, rather than making an opportunity attack.

name: Circlet of Valor
entries: This steel circlet is forged from a construct and set with a gemstone animus containing a fiend. After being cleansed in the fires of a dragon's breath, this holy circlet glimmers with radiant energy.
When you cast a spell of level 1 or higher that restores {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to a creature, that creature gains Valor ({@dice 1d4}) until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Circlet of Valor requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Animus from a Fiend

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Any Dust

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Plates from a Construct

items.name: [Organ]
entries: Glands from a Dragon

name: Circlet of Wisdom
entries: {@note Worn by {@creature Keyleth, Voice of the Tempest|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, increases her Wisdom score by +2.}

name: Claws of Corruption (uncommon)
entries: These rough, menacing gauntlets, constructed from the razor-sharp claws of the pygmy rakshasa, thrum with the power of its hellish essence. The pointed tips of the claws easily dig into rock and metal alike, letting their wearer climb the roughest surfaces with feline agility.
The claws have {@b 4 charges} and regain all expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Rakshasa's Corruption
entries: Blows from this weapon can cause a target's magical energy to turn foul and consume it from within. When you hit a creature with an attack using one of these claws, you can expend {@b 1 charge} to attempt to curse it (no action required). The target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or be cursed for {@b 1 minute}. When a cursed creature starts its turn while under the effect of a spell or while concentrating on a spell, it takes {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage.

entries.name: Catclimb
entries: While wearing a pair of these claws, you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.

name: Claws of Corruption (very rare)
entries: These rough, menacing gauntlets, constructed from the razor-sharp claws of the pygmy rakshasa, thrum with the power of its hellish essence. The pointed tips of the claws easily dig into rock and metal alike, letting their wearer climb the roughest surfaces with feline agility.
The claws have {@b 5 charges} and regain all expended charges daily at dawn.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Rakshasa's Corruption
entries: Blows from this weapon can cause a target's magical energy to turn foul and consume it from within. When you hit a creature with an attack using one of these claws, you can expend {@b 1 charge} to attempt to curse it (no action required). The target must succeed on a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw or be cursed for {@b 1 minute}. When a cursed creature starts its turn while under the effect of a spell or while concentrating on a spell, it takes {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage.

entries.name: Catclimb
entries: While wearing a pair of these claws, you gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed.

name: Claws of the Crab King
entries: Your hands turn into a handsome set of powerful crab claws. For 1 minute, your unarmed strikes using the claws deal double damage to objects and structures, and you make grapple checks using them with advantage. The claws can't wield weapons or shields or do anything that requires manual precision, such as using tools or magic items or performing the somatic components of a spell.
{@font {@style 24|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Claymore of the Great Badger
entries: This weighty blade carries with it the strength of the mighty badger. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The sword has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a Large or smaller creature with this weapon, you can expend 1 charge from it to push that creature 5 feet away from you.

name: Cleaning Cube
entries: This Tiny, sentient piece of an enchanted gelatinous cube is harmlessly soapy, instead of acidic, and enjoys cleaning the surfaces it travels across. When found, the {@i cleaning cube} is a dehydrated, 2-inch cube. While dehydrated, the cube is inanimate and its weight is negligible. You can place the dehydrated cube in 1 or more gallons of water as an action, causing it to animate and grow in size to become a 1-foot cube that weighs 6 pounds. The rehydrated cube moves slowly while animated in this way, methodically cleaning objects and surfaces it comes into contact with. The cube remains hydrated for up to 8 hours, but can be squeezed as an action (as if it were a sponge) to dehydrate it again early.

The {@i cleaning cube} is considered a magical object and is not a creature. It has a speed of 1 foot and can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check. It has AC 10, 10 hit points, and resistance to all damage. The cube dehydrates when it drops to 0 hit points, but regains all its hit points when hydrated again.

entries.name: Sentience
entries: The cleaning cube is a sentient unaligned item with an Intelligence of 1, a Wisdom of 6, and a Charisma of 1. It has hearing and {@sense blindsight} out to a range of 60 feet. It can't speak or read, but obeys your commands as best as it can understand them.

entries.name: Personality
entries: The cleaning cube is happiest finding and dissolving dirt and other grime, and enjoys the feeling of moving across clean, polished surfaces. It doesn't concern itself with combat, preferring to continue its cleaning instead of involving itself in confrontation. If the cube finds a stray coin, gemstone, or other similar small item out of place while it cleans, it will absorb and clean the item until it's removed by a creature as an action or until it becomes dehydrated once again.

name: Cloak of Passage

items: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Passage|EFA}}

additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Cape of the Mountebank|XDMG}}

name: Cloak of Shadows
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}

name: Cloak of Spines
entries: This garment is made of large, soft quills that harden while worn. When wearing this cloak, your AC becomes 14 + your Dexterity modifier if you aren't wearing any armor.

If you are hit by a melee attack while wearing the cloak, you can use your reaction to cause the cloak to block the attack and retaliate against the attacker. Reduce the damage of an attack blocked in this way by {@dice 2d4}, and you deal {@dice 2d4} points of magical piercing damage to the attacker. A hedge who uses the cloak to block a melee attack instead reduces the attack's damage by {@dice 4d4} and deals {@dice 4d4} points of magical piercing damage to the attacker. Once used, this property of the cloak can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Cloak of Splendor
entries: This cloak is made of fine ermine and often embellished with fasteners or trimmed with gold or embroidered orange candles, suns, or similar symbols. While wearing this cloak, you can grip its edges and generate a {@spell sunbeam} spell once per day. If you release the cloak's edges from your grasp, the light fades, and you cannot generate further lines of radiance.

In addition, while wearing the cloak, you can use your action to generate a set of 10 magical lights once per day, each as bright as a lantern and shedding full sunlight in a 20-foot radius. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move any or all the lights up to 60 feet to a new spot within range. A light must be within 30 feet of another light created by this cloak, and a light winks out if travels more than 100 feet from you.

name: Cloak of the Boundless Spirit
entries: This swirling, translucent cloak bolsters the fighting spirits of nearby allies. The cloak has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When an ally you can see within 15 feet of you takes damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to reduce that damage by {@dice 2d6}.

In addition, when an ally within 15 feet of you rolls a 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20} for a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}, it regains 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, and you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to grant them {@dice 2d6} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. Once an ally regains 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} by rolling a 19 on a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} in this way, they can't do so again until they finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Cloak of the Listener
entries: This is a cloak made of ears that were once part of a swarm of ears. It pulses gently and oozes yellow fluid from its many holes. While wearing this cloak, you can take an action to create one of two effects:

entries.name: Ooze
entries: You tug the cloak to create a puddle of waxy goo that covers the ground in a 10-foot square centered on a point within 30 feet of you. A creature that enters or starts its turn in the area must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 15}). This wax remains for 1 minute. Once this effect is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Hide
entries: You completely conceal your head with the cloak. You have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition, you have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet, and you can hear all speech within 120 feet regardless of obstructions. These effects last for 1 minute.
Once this effect is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Cloak of the Mausgeist
entries: This fine garment is made of mausgeist fur with a silk lining. While wearing it, you gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Heightened Senses
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on hearing.

entries.name: Magic Protection
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Charm
entries: You can take an action to cast the {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell (save {@dc 13}). Once used, this property of the cloak can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Cloak of the Raven
entries: While wearing this cloak, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks. In an area of {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} or sunlight, you can grip the edges of the cloak with both hands and use it to fly at a speed of 30 feet. If you release the cloak's edges from your grasp while flying in this way or if you are no longer in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} or sunlight, you lose this flying speed.

While wearing the cloak in an area of {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} or sunlight, you can use your action to cast {@spell daylight} as a readied action. You may then fly or carry the {@spell daylight} spell into any area of darkness. The cloak can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

name: Cloak of the Stygian Bat
entries: This cloak is made from stygian bat hides and bristles with coarse black hair. While wearing the cloak, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on hearing.

In addition, you can take an action to gain a  {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet for one minute. While this effect is active, you also have blindsight with a range of 120 feet, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws while in the air. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Cloak of the Stygian Bat
entries: This cloak is made from the hide of stygian bats, bristling with coarse black hairs. While wearing the cloak, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on hearing.

In addition, you can activate the cloak to gain a fly speed of 30 feet for one minute. While it is active, you also have {@sense blindsight} (out to a range of 120 feet) and have advantage on Dexterity saving throws while in the air. The cloak cannot be activated again until you finish a long rest.

name: Cloak of Therianthropy
entries: This spotted grey cloak is made of styrkvisnar hide. While wearing it, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) checks.

Additionally, you can take an action to transform into a wolf, eagle, or seal for up to 1 hour. The transformation otherwise functions as the {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} spell, but you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to revert to your normal form. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Cloak of Wide-Ranging
entries: While wearing this wolf-skin cloak, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws to avoid levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} after traveling for more than 8 hours in a day.

name: Cloche of Surprise Treats
entries: This magic silver cloche covers a large dinner platter. You can use an action to speak the cloche's command word and remove it from the platter. When you do, use the table below to determine what kind of meal appears.

rows: A delicious meal appears on the platter large enough for one creature and provides as much nourishment as 1 day of {@item rations (1 day)|PHB|rations}.

A number of decadent, perfectly ripe mixed berries equal to twice the number rolled on the {@dice d12} appear on the platter. Eating one of these berries duplicates the effect of eating a berry from the {@spell goodberry} spell. These berries remain potent for up to 10 days.
The cloche magically conjures a great feast, as if by the {@spell heroes' feast|PHB} spell. This version of the spell can feed a number of creatures equal to the number rolled on the {@dice d12}.

entries: Once the cloche has been used to conjure a meal in this way, it can't be used again until a number of days have passed equal to the number rolled on the {@dice d12}.

name: Clockwork Colony Toolbox
entries: This trim bronze toolbox rattles softly with the sound of bolts, screws, and other tools inside. The box weighs 3 pounds and is 3 feet long, 1 foot wide, and 1 foot deep. Inside the toolbox are four empty, resizable bins with nothing inside. Any metal object left inside the closed toolbox for 1 hour becomes meticulously clean and polished.

Similarly, any small machine (such as a compass or {@item hunting trap|PHB}) left inside the closed toolbox for 1 hour is magically repaired. Any magical item with "clockwork" in its name regains all its hit points when left in the toolbox in this way. If the magical item has charges or additional magical properties, it regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges and the ability to use those properties again. Once an item or object has been restored in this way, it can't be restored by the toolbox again for 24 hours.

name: Clockwork Earwig
entries: This 1-inch-long, copper mechanism magically coils around and clasps to the side of your ear, fitting as a functional ear cuff. It can be worn or removed using an action. When worn in this way, the mechanism can magically process any sound you hear, granting you the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks you make that rely on hearing.

You can tap the earwig twice to record up to 1 minute of sound, tapping it twice again to stop recording early. You can tap the earwig once to replay the recording in your ear, tapping it a second time to stop it early. Pressing and holding your finger to the earwig while it's replaying the recording will pause the recording until you release your finger from it. Creating a new recording in this way erases any previous one stored.

You can speak the earwig's command word as an action to cast the {@spell comprehend languages|PHB} spell from it. The spell ends early if you remove the earwig. This property of the earwig can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Clockwork Faefly
entries: This brass clockwork mechanism is 2 inches long and whirs with the hum of tiny gears inside. You can tap the head of the faefly twice as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. When you do, it magically begins to flutter 5 feet in the air until a creature grasps it or it is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The faefly has AC 10, HP 10, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage, and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all other damage. If you move more than 60 away feet from the hovering faefly, it follows you until it is within 60 feet of you. It takes the shortest route to do so. If prevented from moving, the faefly sinks gently to the ground and becomes inactive, and its light fades out. While it's flying, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and use a command word to cause it to move up to 20 feet.

If you are within 60 feet of the faefly, you can use another command word as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cause it to emit light as if targeted by the {@spell Light|XPHB} spell or cast {@spell Faerie Fire|XPHB} (save DC 13), affecting a 20-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} originating from the faefly. Faerie Fire doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB} when cast in this way, but it ends early if the faefly drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Once the {@spell Faerie Fire|XPHB} spell is cast from the faefly, it can't be cast in this way again until the next dawn.

The faefly is a magical object, not a creature. If the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell is cast on it while it has at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, it regains {@dice 2d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If the faefly drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed, at which point it regains all its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

name: Clockwork Healerbee
entries: This pill-shaped magical mechanism is 2 inches long and made of brass and glass. It has a pair of tiny wings that silently keep it aloft. It hovers up to 5 feet in the air and does its best to stay at your side within your space. The bee can pass through another creature's space and doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

The bee has 8 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn. While the bee is within your space, you can use a command word as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend up to 3 charges to send the bee to magically heal a creature you can see within 20 feet of you. The bee flies out and touches its stinger to the target, causing the target to regain {@dice 1d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} for each expended charge and emitting an instantaneous burst of {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} that fills the target's space. The bee then returns to your space.

The bee is a magical object, not a creature. It has AC 15, HP 10, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage, and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all other damage. If the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell is cast on the bee while it has at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}, it regains {@dice 2d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If the bee drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it can't be used again for 24 hours, at which point it regains all its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

name: Clockwork Inkbeetle
entries: This minuscule, mechanical beetle is 1 inch long and quietly whirs with a mix of magical and mechanical forces. Placing the beetle on a piece of parchment you're holding or carrying causes it to spring to life and begin tracking your travels. As you move, so does the beetle, leaving behind a small line of ink. The ink immediately dries and doesn't dissolve in water. In addition, the beetle's small frame allows it to move even while enclosed in a book or similar enclosure without losing its sense of movement or direction.

The beetle mirrors your movement to create a to-scale map of your journey, drawing 1 inch of ink in your choice of the following scales: 20 feet per inch, 200 feet per inch, 2 miles per inch, or 20 miles per inch. You can rotate the dial on the beetle's underside to change the scale as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. The beetle is immune to magical effects that would otherwise alter its sense of direction.

The beetle always knows which way is magnetic north. When placed on a piece of parchment for the first time, it crouches down to stamp a small compass rose on the sheet before it begins to move. If the beetle runs out of space on the parchment to travel, it stops moving in that direction and emits a clicking sound that can be heard by creatures within 5 feet of it.

Attaching one Band of the Found and Lost to the beetle while you wear the other allows the beetle to move and trace your movements in this way from afar as long as you are both on the same plane of existence.

name: Clockwork Mend-A-Pillar
entries: This segmented mechanical caterpillar is 5 inches long, weighs 1 pound, and is made of copper. It has several tiny copper legs that give it a 5-foot walking speed. Within it are multiple containers filled with silk filaments, spools of thread, dyes, and an incredibly strong adhesive. Each of these materials is expelled through a tube in its mouth, and it is equipped with a transmutation lens in its head that allows it to change the adhesive to various kinds of wood, metal, stone, or crystal.

As an action, you can speak the caterpillar's command phrase to cause it to repair a broken or torn object or area that it's set upon. As long as the break or tear is no larger than 1 foot across in more than 1 dimension, the caterpillar can create the material to repair it. The caterpillar then begins crawling over and repairing the object or area, taking 10 minutes for every cubic foot it repairs (minimum of 1 minute). The caterpillar can physically repair a magic item or construct, but can't restore magic to such an object. After the caterpillar finishes repairing an object or area, it stops moving and makes a soft chirping sound audible out to 30 feet. Once the caterpillar repairs 10 cubic feet of material, it can't be used again until 24 hours have passed.

The caterpillar is considered a magical object and is not a creature. It has AC 10, 15 hit points, and has resistance to all damage types. If the {@spell mending|PHB} spell is cast on the caterpillar while it has at least 1 hit point, it regains {@dice 2d6} hit points. If the caterpillar drops to 0 hit points, it can't be used again for 24 hours, at which point it regains all its hit points.

name: Cloud-Touched Boomerang
entries: You can choose to activate this boomerang's swirling vortex whenever you attack with it. On a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or fall {@condition prone}.

entries.name: Special
entries: When thrown, the boomerang returns to an unoccupied space adjacent to you. As a reaction, you can choose to catch it.

name: Club of Dancing
entries: This metallic club emits prismatic flashes of light whenever it hits a target. While you're holding this weapon, you can use an action to cast the dancing lights spell from it. In addition, the club has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dusk. When you hit with an attack using this weapon, you can expend 1 of its charges to deal an extra {@damage 1d6} thunder damage. If the target is a creature, it must also make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, that creature's speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn, and it spends its action on its next turn dancing in place: shuffling, tapping its feet, and capering.

name: Club of the Forest Drake
entries: This wooden club's head has been naturally formed into the shape of a dragon's maw. As an action, you can speak the club's command word and strike the ground with it to cause a wave of thorns and thrashing vines to spring up from the ground in a 15-foot cone in front of you. Each creature in the area must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d6} slashing damage and be {@condition grappled} by the thorns and vines for up to 1 minute. A {@condition grappled} creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength or Dexterity check, freeing itself on a success. At the end of each of its turns, a {@condition grappled} creature takes {@damage 1d6} piercing damage as it's constricted by the thorny vines. Once this property of the club has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Club of the Rook
entries: This club is a magic weapon and has a weighty stone tower at its end. While holding the weapon, you can use an action to move up to 30 feet in a line to an unoccupied space you can see on the ground, barreling through creatures no more than one size larger than you and objects that weigh no more than 400 pounds in the line. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks and ignores {@quickref difficult terrain||3}. Each target in the line you barrel through must make a DC 13 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 3d4} bludgeoning damage and is knocked {@condition prone}. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage and isn't knocked {@condition prone}. If a target in the line is a structure or is too large or heavy to barrel through, it automatically succeeds on the saving throw and your movement ends early. Your movement also ends early if you attempt to move over a space in which you normally can't, such as over a gorge or up a wall.
The club's property can't be used again until the next dawn. In the meantime, the club can still be used as a magic weapon.

name: Coat of Lies
entries: This coat is made from the tongues of a harvester of lies' victims. While you wear it, you gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) checks.

The cloak has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 charge while wearing the cloak to enhance the next spell you cast before the start of your next turn, allowing that spell to be cast without any Verbal or Somatic components.

name: Coat of Lies
entries: This coat made of the severed tongues of a {@creature Harvester of Lies|GrimHollowLairsEtharis|harvester}'s victims provides a +1 bonus to your AC, and you have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Deception}) checks.

Additionally, as a bonus action three times per day, you can activate the magic of the cloak. If you do, the next spell you cast before the start of your next turn can be cast without any somatic or verbal components.

name: Coat of Many Eyes (Rare)
entries: This armor is a creation of the daelkyr Belashyrra, the Lord of Eyes. Made from a tough, leathery material, the coat is warm to the touch and covered with eyes—eyes of many different types of creatures, constantly glancing around as it studies your surroundings. When you attune to the armor, it binds itself to your flesh and shares its insight, granting the following benefits:

items.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.

items.name: Eyes Everywhere
entries: The armor lets you see in all directions, and you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight.

items.name: Gifts of the All-Seer
entries: All Coats of Many Eyes are linked to Belashyrra, and while wearing one you may receive visions—flashes of things the Lord of Eyes wishes to see through you. If you follow through with these tasks, your armor can evolve, gaining additional powers and increasing its effective rarity.

items.name: Rare
entries: A rare coat also grants you a +1 bonus to AC and allows you to see {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creatures and objects within 120 feet.

items.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

name: Coat of Many Eyes (Uncommon)
entries: This armor is a creation of the daelkyr Belashyrra, the Lord of Eyes. Made from a tough, leathery material, the coat is warm to the touch and covered with eyes—eyes of many different types of creatures, constantly glancing around as it studies your surroundings. When you attune to the armor, it binds itself to your flesh and shares its insight, granting the following benefits:

items.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.

items.name: Eyes Everywhere
entries: The armor lets you see in all directions, and you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight.

items.name: Gifts of the All-Seer
entries: All Coats of Many Eyes are linked to Belashyrra, and while wearing one you may receive visions—flashes of things the Lord of Eyes wishes to see through you. If you follow through with these tasks, your armor can evolve, gaining additional powers and increasing its effective rarity.

items.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

name: Coat of Many Eyes (Very Rare)
entries: This armor is a creation of the daelkyr Belashyrra, the Lord of Eyes. Made from a tough, leathery material, the coat is warm to the touch and covered with eyes—eyes of many different types of creatures, constantly glancing around as it studies your surroundings. When you attune to the armor, it binds itself to your flesh and shares its insight, granting the following benefits:

items.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.

items.name: Eyes Everywhere
entries: The armor lets you see in all directions, and you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight.

items.name: Gifts of the All-Seer
entries: All Coats of Many Eyes are linked to Belashyrra, and while wearing one you may receive visions—flashes of things the Lord of Eyes wishes to see through you. If you follow through with these tasks, your armor can evolve, gaining additional powers and increasing its effective rarity.

items.name: Very Rare
entries: A very rare coat also grants you a +1 bonus to AC and allows you to see {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creatures and objects within 120 feet. Additionally, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast {@spell Arcane Eye|XPHB} with it. Once you cast the spell in this manner, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

name: Coat of the Crest
entries: This exquisite brocade coat is cut in a long, high-collared style popular among nobles of the Clovis Concord—a nation on the west coast of {@book Wildemount|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Wildemount} whose stylish fashion is often mimicked in Tal'Dorei. Its shimmering lining hints at its magical properties. You gain a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this coat, which can be worn over light armor.

Additionally, the coat has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. When you are the target of an attack while wearing this coat, you can spend 1 charge as a reaction to gain resistance to one type of damage from the triggering attack. This resistance is effective against the triggering attack and lasts until the start of your next turn.

name: Coconut of Alacrity
entries: {@i Component: beast (horse) bone}

The original concept for this bizarre item is said to come from a faraway land where horses are so rare that buying one is more expensive than producing low-end magical paraphernalia. When both halves of this coconut are clapped together, they produce the sound of a trotting mount and increase one's velocity to match that of an unladen swallow.

entries.name: Mighty Gallop
entries: This item can be socketed on mounts. When hung from a Small or larger creature that is serving as a mount, that creature can take the Dash action as a bonus action on its turn. Once this property of the item has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Swallow's Velocity
entries: Using two hands, you can hold each coconut half and clap them together repeatedly to increase your travel pace over long distances. For as long as you continue to do this, you and up to 6 friendly creatures of your choice that can hear the clapping can travel 3 miles per hour at a slow pace (27 miles per day), 4 miles per hour at a normal pace (32 miles per day), or 6 miles per hour at a fast pace (45 miles per day). The sound of the clip-clopping coconuts can be heard up to 100 feet away; other creatures within this area that can hear are alerted to the sound and can't be surprised by creatures benefitting from this magic item while it is in use.

name: Cogwork Wings
entries: These wings are a strange device made by a mapach tinkerer. Two wings, made of brass and cloth, are attached to a box containing an intricate array of gears and cogs. Leather straps allow it to be worn on the back. It has two levers, one on either side of the central mechanism. Before donning the wings, you can pull the left lever to extend the wings and the right lever to set them into motion. Pushing the right lever causes the wings to stop flapping, and pushing the left lever causes them to retract, but you can't reach these levers while wearing the wings.

While wearing the contraption with the wings in motion, you have a fly speed as shown on the table below. You can use the device to fly for up to 1 hour, all at once, or in several shorter flights. The length of a flight is rounded up to the nearest minute. If you are flying when the hour expires, the wings stop moving and you drop to the ground, taking falling damage.

As a reaction while falling, you can press a button on the front of the center buckle of the straps to cause the wings to set into a fixed position, allowing you to glide. While gliding, you descend at a rate of feet per round determined by your combined weight until you land, moving forward and descending at the same speed.

If you press the gliding button, there is a {@chance 50} chance the device will fail and the wings will become stuck in a fixed gliding position. If this occurs, the device will become completely useless after you have landed, and nothing can cause the wings to retract or flap until they become unstuck after {@dice 2d12} hours.
The speed of your flight and glide is determined by your combined weight along with your gear (worn and carried). The cogwork wings themselves weigh 20 pounds and are included in the total weight.
The wings regain 10 minutes of flight for every 4 hours they aren't in use.

name: Coil Crook
entries: This smooth, red staff is actually made from a rigid length of decorative silken rope. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and use a command word to cause it to magically loosen and turn into a 10-foot length of Rope. You can repeat the command word as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to cause the Rope to untangle itself and become the solid staff once more. It can be used as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} in either of these forms.
While holding the staff, you can cast the {@spell Rope Trick|XPHB} spell from it, using it as the rope required for the spell. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Coin of Easy Living
entries: This Gold Piece appears mundane but, when flipped, always lands on the side you call while it is in the air. Additionally, you can summon it to your palm at will as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

name: Coin of War and Fear
entries: This dark metal coin is a token of heretical dogma that claims Empyreus and Beleth are one and the same. One side bears the Empyreus's icon, while the other shows Beleth's leering face.

While holding this coin, you can take an action to flip it. Roll a {@dice d6}. The icon of Empyreus shows on an even number, granting you the Boon of Empyreus. On an odd number, Beleth shows and confers the Boon of Beleth.

entries.name: Boon of Empyreus
entries: For one minute, you gain a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}, and you add {@dice 1d4} to the first attack roll you make each of your turns. If you would receive this boon again before the next dawn, you instead take {@damage 3d6} Radiant damage and the boon is not applied.

entries.name: Boon of Beleth
entries: For one minute, an aura radiates from you in a 10-foot radius. When an enemy ends its turn in the area, it must succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. While the aura lasts, you deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage whenever you hit a {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature with a weapon attack. If you would receive this boon again before the next dawn, you instead take {@damage 3d6} Necrotic damage and the boon is not applied.

name: Coin's Edge
entries: This magical coin has the symbol of a dagger on it. When the coin is flipped into the air, it transforms into a mundane dagger. Once this property is used, it can't be undone.

name: Cold Snap Circlet
entries: This icy circlet is made from {@condition frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} contaminated ichor, kept in a state of permafrost by the heart of a naturally cold creature, and lined with {@condition frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} bones of undead, all powered by the animus of an elemental. Even in its permanently {@condition frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} state, it is comfortable to wear.

Once per turn, when you cast a spell that deals Cold damage using a spell slot, you can choose one target that was dealt Cold damage by the spell to gain the {@condition Frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition. The escape DC equals your spell save DC.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Cold Snap Circlet requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Animus from an Elemental

items.name: [Bones]
entries: Ribs from an Undead

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Contaminated Ichor

items.name: [Organ]
entries: Heart from a White Dragon, Silver Dragon, Winter Troll, or any monster {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Cold damage.

name: Coldfire Anvil
entries: This cold, iron anvil weighs 50 pounds and is 1 and a half feet long. It has three magic runes on its side from the Everglacier that magically enchant any item sharpened, forged, or otherwise smithed using this anvil. Over the course of a full workday, or half as long if you're proficient with {@item smith's tools|PHB}, you can use the anvil to turn a nonmagical metal weapon into a coldfire one. A coldfire weapon is magical and deals an extra {@damage 1d6} cold damage to any target it hits, but is made fragile like ice. When you make an attack roll using a coldfire weapon and roll a 1, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 9 or lower, the weapon shatters and is destroyed, releasing a biting burst of icy air that deals {@damage 2d6} cold damage to all creatures within 10 feet of the weapon. After 7 days, a coldfire weapon loses the enchantment and becomes nonmagical again.
Once the anvil has been used to enchant a weapon in this way, it can't do so again for {@dice 1d6 + 1} days.

name: Coldrazor
entries: This infamous axe is wielded by the memori lich known as Runa Banasár. It appears to be made of ice, carved with runes and studded with various tiny, glittering gems.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. On a hit, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 4d6} Cold damage. If a single attack with Coldrazor deals more than 20 points of Cold damage, the target must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.
Immediately after hitting or missing with a ranged attack made with this weapon, it flies back to your hand.

name: Coldsnap
entries: You have a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Cold damage on a hit.

The {@item Whip|XPHB} has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a creature that doesn't have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage with this weapon, you can expend 1 charge to force the target to make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0 until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is instead halved for the same duration.
Once you attune to this weapon, its normally frigid handle feels warm to the touch.

name: Collapsible Mountain
entries: This small statuette of a snow-topped, forested mountain seems remarkably detailed, yet it stands only about 4 inches tall. Stories tell that it was a gift from the bearfolk to the shadow fey priests of Hecate when they first came to the Shadow Realm and that it was once merely a collapsible hill. Over time, its power has grown as it travels from one owner to another. The priests of Hecate say no one can retain it for more than a year.

When you hold the collapsible mountain, you may take an action to speak its command word to instantaneously create a pine-covered mountain, fully 2,500 feet tall. You may choose to either have the mountain rise under you or to have the mountain rise under another creature you can see at least 120 feet away. In the first case, other creatures nearby may wind up hundreds of feet below you (and combat ends between any two non-adjacent creatures). Groups of creatures move roughly {@dice 2d6 × 100} feet apart. If you have the mountain rise under another creature, you and adjacent creatures see the mountain grow rapidly nearby, but you remain at the altitude you started at. A small spring or brook usually appears nearby in this instance.
Each day, the mountain's land and streams provide simple food and fresh, cold water sufficient to nourish 15 humanoids or five steeds.

Speaking the command word again collapses the mountain. Any creature standing on it is not harmed (the descent is swift but not dangerous). Creatures who enter combat unaware of the nature of the collapsible mountain are treated as if {@status surprised} by the sudden change.

name: Collar of the Cat
entries: While socketed on armour, clothing, a focus, or a weapon, you have a preternatural ability to land on your feet. You have advantage on checks made to maintain your footing and you can subtract up to 20 feet from the fall when calculating falling damage.

name: Collar of the Undead
entries: Some people have no qualms about exploiting any opportunity for profit, including the sorrow caused by the loss of a loved one. Such people would appreciate the Collar of the Undead, whether as con artists looking for bereaved individuals to fleece, or as dark sorcerers in need of souls.

As an action, you can place this collar around the neck of a Humanoid creature of Large size or smaller that has died within the last 10 days. The creature returns to life with 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}. The creature uses its normal game statistics, except that its creature type becomes Undead and it doesn't need to eat, sleep, or breathe. If its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are reduced to 0, the creature is utterly destroyed, turning into dust.

Each dawn, the creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} Maximum decreases by {@dice 1d4} as its soul slowly slips away. When the creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} Maximum reaches 0, or its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are reduced to 0, it falls apart into a heap of dust and is destroyed.

On each of your turns, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to mentally command the creature if it is within 60 feet of you, and it follows your orders to the best of your ability. If you issue no commands, the creature takes the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action and moves only to avoid harm. Once given an order, the creature continues to follow it until its task is complete.
If the collar is removed, the creature is immediately reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

name: Combined Mirror Shards
entries: If all five mirror shards are held together so they are stacked front to back, front to back, they have the following powers:

items: Wielder can cast {@spell sacred flame} three times per day as if by an 11th-level caster

Instead of the above, the wielder can opt to cast a single robust {@spell sacred flame} spell once per day. This causes maximum (24) damage, and any target creature with vulnerability to radiant damage rolls its saving throw with disadvantage

entries: Anyone can use the five mirror shards in this way, even non‑spellcasters.

Although the shards' edges are certainly sharp, reasonably careful PCs should be in no danger of cutting themselves when using the shards in this way. A clever PC might even bind the five shards together with strong cord, wire, or rope to keep them together and make it easier to use them.
Each mirror shard is as wide as a man's fist and just under an inch in thickness. Although apparently made of normal glass, they are extremely difficult to break.

Because the shards have {@creature the Dusk Queen|TalesFromTheShadows}'s essence within them, they possess a spark of quasi‑intelligence. The mirror shards' primary goal is to be rejoined with the Dusk Queen's mirror. A shard continually urges any PC possessing it to take it to the Queen's Tower. If a PC attempts to damage a mirror shard, remove it from the forest, or do anything else contrary to the shard's goal, it attempts to force the PC into compliance (DC 11 Wisdom saving throw to resist).
A mirror shard has: AC 13; hp 5 ({@dice 2d4}); damage threshold 20; INT 4 (-3), WIS 20 (+5), CHA 21 (+5) (as long as {@creature the Dusk Queen|TalesFromTheShadows} is alive)

name: Comet Ballista
entries: This crossbow is partially covered in cold shards of stone and metal and uses {@item sling bullet|PHB|sling bullets} as ammunition instead of {@item crossbow bolt|PHB|crossbow bolts}. When you fire a sling bullet from this magic crossbow, it flashes with blue light and leaves behind a brief, glimmering trail of cold, sparkling dust. Ranged attacks with this weapon deal bludgeoning damage, instead of piercing damage, and any target hit by it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} cold damage. In addition, the first time you hit a target on each of your turns with a ranged attack using this weapon, each creature within 10 feet of the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} cold damage.

entries.name: Hailing Comets
entries: You can use an action to fire the crossbow into the air and speak its command word, choosing a point that you can see within 120 feet of you when you do.
