name: Essence of the River Spirit
entries: This small, stoppered vial contains a clear liquid that shimmers with a faint blue light. When the vial is opened, you can pour the liquid into a small pool of water, such as a bath or hot spring, transforming it into a healing pool. A creature that soaks in the pool for at least 10 minutes regains {@dice 4d4 + 4} hit points. The pool loses its magic after 1 hour or once six creatures have benefited from this effect.
{@font {@style 33|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Essence of Umami
entries: This potion makes everything taste amazing. When you pour it on any food, no matter if it's a hunk of tofu or a slab of slow-roasted brisket, essence of umami makes it glow with magic. When the food is tasted, it magically gives the taster their own personal version of the ultimate culinary experience.
{@font {@style 5|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Eternal Chalk
entries: A stick of Eternal Chalk never breaks or wears down with normal use. When using this chalk, you can choose the color of its marks and whether they emit a faint glow. Any marks you make with this chalk can't be erased for 7 days by anyone except you.

name: Ether Spear
entries: This {@item Spear|XPHB} can slip through the Ethereal Plane to reach its destination. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals Force damage instead of Piercing. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action while holding the {@item Spear|XPHB}, you can choose a space you can see within 20 feet of you. The tip of the {@item Spear|XPHB} vanishes and reappears in that space, allowing you to make melee attack rolls with the {@item Spear|XPHB} against a target within 5 feet of that space until the end of the turn. These attacks ignore {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} and treat {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover} as if it were {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} instead.

entries.name: Ethereal Sight
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane while on the Material Plane and vice versa. This effect lasts for 1 minute. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Everfull Stein
entries: This large ceramic stein is decorated with dwarven glyphs and topped with a brass lid that can be opened by thumb lever. While the lid is closed and the stein is empty, you can name a nonmagical ale, beer, or mead as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and the stein fills with that liquid.

name: Everglacier Prosthesis
reqAttune: by a creature missing a hand, arm, or leg
entries: When found, this item appears to be a roughly hewn length of ice with runes etched into its side. To attune to this item, you must attach it to the end of your missing arm or leg, at which point the ice magically attaches to you and forms an icy copy of the appendage it's replacing. The prosthetic is a fully capable part of your body and can't be removed against your will as long as you're attuned to it.
While the prosthetic is attached, you have resistance to cold damage, and your unarmed strikes with the limb deal cold damage instead of bludgeoning damage.

In addition, the prosthesis has 6 icy spikes protruding from its surface. You can use an action while the prosthetic is attached to launch up to 3 of the spikes at one or more targets within 30 feet of you. Make a ranged spell attack for each spike, using an attack bonus of +7. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 2d6} cold damage. {@dice 1d4 + 2} launched spikes regrow daily at dawn.

name: Everhot Stew Pot
entries: This cauldron is made using the plated iron from a construct infused with the ash of an elemental. The animus used must be from a dragon which adds both control and potency to the latent elemental magics. The spoon used to stir the cauldron is carved from the bone of a magical creature. This cauldron can heat to boiling temperatures without requiring fire simply by being filled and stirred, and the stews and soups it produces are always delicious and hearty.

During a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can cook enough stew to feed up to three creatures. All creatures who eat a stew from this pot gain 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. While a creature has these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, they gain {@condition Valor|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} ({@dice 1d4}).

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating an Everhot Stew Pot requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Animus from a Dragon

items.name: [Bones]
entries: Ribs from a Monstrosity

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Elemental Dust

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Plates

name: Everice Box
entries: This large wooden box weighs 25 pounds and is 3 feet long, 2 feet deep, and 2 feet tall. It has rugged ropes on its left and right sides as well as on the top of its lid. The left and right sides of the box are covered by enchanted slabs of stone that magically keep the contents on the inside of the box at a consistent 40 degrees Fahrenheit. The box can hold up to 24 Rations (or an equivalent amount of food). For a creature stuck inside the box to escape, it or a creature within 5 feet of the box must make a DC 10 Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, freeing the trapped creature on a success.

While the box's lid is closed and its latch is shut, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and use a command word to shrink it and its contents down to a more portable size. The weight of the box and anything inside it is halved while it's shrunk in this way, and the box measures a mere 1 foot long by 8 inches deep and tall. You can repeat the command word to return the box to its normal size. Opening the latch, whether by choice or by force, immediately returns the box and its contents to their full size and weight. A living creature can't be shrunk in this way, and the lid and latch are forced open if the box becomes too small for it.

name: Everlasting Sugarbomb
entries: This large sugarbomb is roughly two inches in diameter. Its flavors are a mix of bitter, salty, savory, spicy, sour, and sweet, but also refreshing. The sugarbomb is solid and slowly dissolves in your mouth, changing in flavor each time you reach a new layer. An Everlasting Sugarbomb provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day after 1 minute of letting it dissolve in your mouth. The sugarbomb fully dissolves after 30 uses. You can bite through to the center of the sugarbomb with a successful DC 25 Strength or Constitution check (your choice). If you succeed, make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute and suffer from painful nausea.

name: Evoker's Exchange
entries: While wearing this amulet, you can choose to convert the damage from one form of raw energy to another. You can use this amulet as a spellcasting focus when you cast a spell of 1st-level or higher that deals only fire or lightning damage and doesn't require concentration. When you do, you can choose to have the spell deal lightning damage if it originally dealt fire, or fire damage if it originally dealt lightning.

If a spell that deals fire damage would normally ignite flammable objects that aren't being worn or carried, it does not if it's converted to lightning damage in this way. However, a spell that deals lightning damage does ignite such objects if it's converted to deal fire damage instead.

name: Eye Kite
entries: These unique kites can be shaped like an octopus, crane, or dragon. As an action, while flying the kite, you can see through it as if it were a pair of eyes looking down from the sky. While looking through the kite, you gain all the visual benefits you would normally have and can see in all directions facing downward.

name: Eye of Dendallen
entries: While you're attuned to this item, you can cast the {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB} spell from it at will.

entries.name: Curse
entries: The Eye of Dendallen is cursed. When you attune to it, you must make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw as you're suddenly overcome with the urge to see what it sees. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately end your attunement to the eye before it extends the curse to you. On a failed save or if you choose not to end your attunement to it, you are cursed until you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic. When you become cursed, you forcefully tear out one of your own eyes, taking {@damage 4d10} Necrotic damage, and allow the Eye of Dendallen to crawl into the now vacant socket. If you're already missing an eye, you simply let the eye crawl into that socket without taking the Necrotic damage.

You can see normally through the Eye of Dendallen while it's in your socket. In addition, you have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. If you already had {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, the eye increases its range by 30 feet. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can focus on looking through the eye to see through magical {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} for 1 minute as if it were nonmagical {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

If your attunement to the eye ends after being cursed by it, it pulls itself out of your socket and tries to escape. The eye uses the Spider stat block except its creature type is Undead; it has HP 5; and it doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep. Slaying the eye while it isn't attuned to a creature destroys the item.

entries.name: Dendallen Familiar
entries: The eye also doubles as a gruesome companion while you're attuned to it. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can command the eye to crawl out of your socket and move independently of you. You control the eye as if you summoned it with the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell, using the statistics above. If the eye drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or you dismiss it, it reappears inside your open socket with a sickly sound. If it does so as a result of dropping to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it turns pitch black, and none of its magical properties can be used until the next dusk.

name: Eye of Starsight
entries: This black bronze amulet is made of intricate cogwork and has a single polished glass orb the size of an eye set tightly in its center. This item has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} charges each night at dusk.

entries.name: Cosmic Insight
entries: When you wear this amulet, the orb inside grants you supernatural awareness of your surroundings. When you make a skill check, attack roll, or saving throw, you can spend your reaction and expend a charge to re-roll the result. You must do this after your first die has been rolled, but before the outcome has been determined. You must take the result of the new roll.

entries.name: Stellar Eye
entries: Speaking a command word causes the cogwork around the glass orb to open slightly, allowing the orb to be removed. Speaking the command word again closes it. While the amulet is open, you can use your bonus action to command the orb to float out of its setting, or return to a resting state. While the orb is floating, you can spend an action to move it up to 30 feet in any direction, and you can expend a single charge to mentally receive visual information from the orb for 10 minutes. The orb has {@sense truesight} out to 30 feet and is blind beyond this radius. It can see in all directions at once. There is no limit to how far away from you the orb can move, but it can't enter a different plane of existence from you. The orb's movement can be blocked by a solid barrier, but it can pass through an opening as small as 1 inch in diameter. While the orb is outside of the amulet, you cannot benefit from its other property.

name: Eye of Sunrise
entries: A crimson gemstone glitters on the back of this black iron gauntlet. While wearing the gauntlet, you can use a bonus action to cause the stone to shed bright red light in a 10-foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 10 feet. You can use another bonus action to extinguish the light.

Additionally, you can use an action to raise the gauntlet and emit a fiery explosion in a 30-foot cone. The explosion can be heard 300 feet away. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 5d6} fire damage plus {@damage 5d6} force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Each structure and mundane object in the area that isn't being worn or carried takes {@damage 10d6} fire damage plus {@damage 10d6} force damage. Once this action is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Eye of the Bookwurm
entries: This small, glass sphere is enchanted with weak Divination magics to help you find specific words or phrases in writing. It has a stylized iris etched into the glass.

You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to use a command word and then speak the word or phrase you're searching for. The word or phrase magically appears and floats within the sphere. By holding the eye in a free hand, your vision becomes magically enhanced to subconsciously highlight the word or phrase you searched for in a green light wherever you see it. Once you've used the eye's ability for the first time, you can change the word or phrase as many times as you like for the next hour, after which the item can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Eye of the Tiger (uncommon)
entries: The tiger's eye gemstone at the centre of this ring gleams with the devious malice peculiar to the fiendish pygmy rakshasa. Spinning slowly in its socket, it studies its wearer and surroundings, almost as if waiting for a time to pounce.
The ring has {@b 5 charges} and regains all expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Arcane Interference
entries: While wearing the ring, whenever you are the target of a spell or make a saving throw against a spell's area of effect, you can use your reaction to tug at the Weave, consuming {@b 1 charge} and attempting to unravel the spell's magic. If the spell is of 2nd level or lower, roll a d4 and consult the table below to determine the effect, which occurs immediately before the spell's effect. If the spell is 3rd level or higher, this property has no effect.

rows: The caster of the spell must make a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw, taking force damage equal to {@damage 1d6} plus an additional {@damage 1d6} for each level of the spell on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
The spell's potency is diminished. If the spell requires an attack roll, the roll is made with disadvantage. If it requires you to make a saving throw, you have advantage on it.

You absorb a portion of the spell's energy, gaining temporary hit points equal to {@dice 1d6} plus an additional {@dice 1d6} for each level of the spell. These temporary hit points last for {@b 1 minute}.
You are unaffected by the spell.

name: Eye of the Tiger (very rare)
entries: The tiger's eye gemstone at the centre of this ring gleams with the devious malice peculiar to the fiendish pygmy rakshasa. Spinning slowly in its socket, it studies its wearer and surroundings, almost as if waiting for a time to pounce.
The ring has {@b 6 charges} and regains all expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Arcane Interference
entries: While wearing the ring, whenever you are the target of a spell or make a saving throw against a spell's area of effect, you can use your reaction to tug at the Weave, consuming {@b 1 charge} and attempting to unravel the spell's magic. If the spell is of 5th level or lower, roll a d4 and consult the table below to determine the effect, which occurs immediately before the spell's effect. If the spell is 6th level or higher, this property has no effect.

rows: The caster of the spell must make a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw, taking force damage equal to {@damage 1d6} plus an additional {@damage 1d6} for each level of the spell on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
The spell's potency is diminished. If the spell requires an attack roll, the roll is made with disadvantage. If it requires you to make a saving throw, you have advantage on it.

You absorb a portion of the spell's energy, gaining temporary hit points equal to {@dice 1d6} plus an additional {@dice 1d6} for each level of the spell. These temporary hit points last for {@b 1 minute}.
You are unaffected by the spell.

name: Eye of the White Worm (Legendary)
entries: This fist-sized eyeball is cold and clammy to the touch. It is milky-white with purple veins, and its pupil constantly searches for something.

While holding the eye, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the eye's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Thought Scour (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the eye's bonus) from the eye. When you probe deeper into a creature's mind, it takes {@damage 3d8} Psychic damage unless it is a willing target. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Mnemonic Siphon (Very Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the eye's bonus) from the eye. When you do, you gain a version of the affected memory as if you experienced it yourself, though you still know the memory isn't yours. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Violation of the Real (Very Rare+)
entries: When you cast a Conjuration spell using a spell slot that deals damage, or that summons a creature that can deal damage, the spell or creature deals an extra {@damage 1d10} Psychic damage to one target the first time it deals damage during a turn.

entries.name: Enduring Violation (Legendary)
entries: When you cast a Conjuration spell with a duration of 1 hour or more, you can extend the duration to 24 hours, and the spell no longer requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Eye of the White Worm (Rare)
entries: This fist-sized eyeball is cold and clammy to the touch. It is milky-white with purple veins, and its pupil constantly searches for something.

While holding the eye, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the eye's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Thought Scour (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the eye's bonus) from the eye. When you probe deeper into a creature's mind, it takes {@damage 3d8} Psychic damage unless it is a willing target. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Eye of the White Worm (Very Rare)
entries: This fist-sized eyeball is cold and clammy to the touch. It is milky-white with purple veins, and its pupil constantly searches for something.

While holding the eye, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the eye's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Thought Scour (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the eye's bonus) from the eye. When you probe deeper into a creature's mind, it takes {@damage 3d8} Psychic damage unless it is a willing target. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Mnemonic Siphon (Very Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the eye's bonus) from the eye. When you do, you gain a version of the affected memory as if you experienced it yourself, though you still know the memory isn't yours. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Violation of the Real (Very Rare+)
entries: When you cast a Conjuration spell using a spell slot that deals damage, or that summons a creature that can deal damage, the spell or creature deals an extra {@damage 1d10} Psychic damage to one target the first time it deals damage during a turn.

name: Eyedrops of Clarity
entries: This eyedropper is stoppered with a cork at the opening of its spherical top, which is designed in the likeness of an eye. When found, the eyedropper contains {@dice 1d4 + 2} doses of magical solution. When uncorked, the solution inside begins to drip from the eyedropper. A creature can use its action to uncork and apply 1 dose of the eyedrops to itself or another willing creature that it can see within reach, stoppering the eyedropper again once finished. A {@condition blinded} creature that has eyes and receives a dose of the eyedrops ceases to be {@condition blinded}. In addition, that creature gains {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 30 feet and has advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight for 1 hour. If the creature already has {@sense darkvision}, its range increases by 30 feet for the duration.

name: Eyes of Akibu
entries: When this potion is poured over your eyes, your long-range vision enhances. For 4 hours, you can see up to 300 feet away as if looking at something one-tenth as far away from you.
{@font {@style 8|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Eyes of Googly
entries: Firm, and always slightly moist to the touch, this pair of eyes wanders of their own accord. When placed on a single object that can fit inside a {@b 5-foot} cube, the object becomes sentient. It can't speak, and has statistics the GM deems appropriate.

name: Eyes of the Beheld
entries: These button-sized metal trinkets typically come in sets of two and resemble the fearsome visage of a one-eyed monster. As an action, you can place one firmly on a solid surface—such as a wall, table, or boot—where it remains until destroyed. While you're within 5 feet of one, you can use a bonus action to speak the command word to cause its eye to open. The opening is about the size of a keyhole, and by peering through it, you can open and see through another eye's opening of your choice. You choose which eye to look through the first time you peer into the hole and can change it again using a bonus action.

The eyes you can choose to see through in this way must be a part of the set, be placed on a solid surface, and be on the same plane of existence as the one you're looking through. You can only see through one eye at a time, which operates both ways, and nothing can pass through the hole. If another eye attempts to look through one you're already using, the connection between the first two ends and is replaced by the new one. An eye closes when it's no longer being looked through.

Each eye has AC 10 and 5 hit points. If it drops to 0 hit points, the eye is destroyed. If a target or area is immune to divination magic or can't be perceived through {@spell scrying|PHB} sensors, it doesn't appear through the hole. If you find another eye of the beheld, you can connect it to an existing set by holding it against another eye from the set for 1 minute.

name: Eyes of the Dragonne

items: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA}}

additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Eyes of the Eagle|XDMG}}

name: Fable's End
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll made with Fable's End against a Large or smaller creature, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be banished to a harmless demiplane. At the end of its next turn, the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. If you make an attack roll against a Fey with this weapon, you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} and force the save against being banished on a roll of 19 or 20; Fey creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this save. When a creature is banished in this way, the weapon's center emits a brilliant magenta flash of light.

name: Face of Fugari
entries: Fugari is a figure of legend, a dragon frog who would glower at his subjects, filling them with dread at being swallowed whole. Drinking this potion gives you a grim, bullfroggish demeanor which strikes fear into those who view you. For the next minute, you have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks.
{@font {@style 14|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Faeflame Torch
entries: This magic torch was harvested from a tree in the Safire Wood, one of the most beautiful and deadly fey forests. While holding the torch, you can use a bonus action to speak its first command word, causing eerie blue flames to appear above the head of the torch. The flames shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. The flames are not extinguished when immersed in water and last until you use a bonus action to speak the command word again or until you stow the torch.

You can use an action while holding the lit torch to speak its second or third command word. Speaking the second command word causes any illusion within the torch's bright light to be outlined in blue, green, or violet (your choice) for 1 minute. The torch can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

Speaking the third command word causes the flame to fly from the torch and erupt at a point you can see within 60 feet of you, creating an explosion of blue flames and duplicating the effect of the {@spell faerie fire|PHB} spell (save DC 15, no concentration required) in a 20-foot radius sphere centered on that point. A creature also takes {@damage 3d6} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. You can choose to end the effect early as a bonus action. When the effect ends, the flame reappears above the torch. The torch can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

name: Faerie Crown
entries: This crown is woven of aromatic flowers. When you first don the crown after attuning to it, {@dice 1d6 + 3} butterflies begin fluttering around it.
When you are hit by a melee attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to release one of the butterflies. The attack misses you and destroys the butterfly instead.
Once all butterflies are destroyed, the crown withers and crumbles to dust.

name: Failed Purity Spear
entries: The grayed unicorn horn that rests at the top of this sickly spear is fractured and slowly leaks a silver, corrupting fluid. A {@i failed purity spear} is the rare version of a {@item purity spear|tgs1}, a legendary weapon, that was made by a creature other than an elder fey. Its magic is a sad reminder that while unicorns are paragons of good, even their magic can become toxic when mistreated.

entries.name: Corruption
entries: This magic spear has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dusk. You can expend 1 charge when you hit a creature with the spear to cause it to inject the target with its corrupting fluid. When you do, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 point of corruption, which last for 1 minute. A creature takes {@damage 1d4} poison damage at the start of each of its turns for each point of corruption it has, up to a maximum of {@damage 3d4} poison damage. This poison damage ignores resistance and immunity. A creature with at least 1 point of corruption can make another DC 15 Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a success, it removes 1 point of corruption. A creature is {@condition poisoned} while it has 3 or more points of corruption.
If you expend the spear's last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the tip of the spear shatters, and the spear becomes a nonmagical {@item quarterstaff|PHB}.

entries.name: Charge
entries: If you move at least 20 feet straight toward a target and then hit it with the spear on the same turn, the target takes an extra {@dice 1d6} piercing damage.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This spear is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the spear, keeping it within reach at all times. You also have disadvantage on attack rolls with weapons other than this one, unless no foe is within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear. While you're cursed, you have disadvantage on any saving throw against poison. However, while you are poisoned, you gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

name: Familiar Figurine
entries: Once per day as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can use this finely-carved figurine to cast {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB}.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Familiar Figurine requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any

items.name: [Bones]
entries: Bones from a Giant

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Dust from an Elemental or Fey

name: Familiar's Collar
entries: While worn by a friendly beast you can activate the {@spell Control Animal|ObojimaTallGrass} spell at will, targeting only the creature wearing the collar.

name: Fangs of Guile
entries: This rare necklace was created by supplicants of {@deity Kren|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting}, who obtained knowledge of their craft in a ritual exchange. The necklace imbues its wearer with equal parts guile and ferocity.
While you wear the necklace, you have advantage on {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, and {@skill Persuasion} skill checks.

The necklace has 3 charges. It regains {@dice 1d3} charges nightly, at dusk. You can spend an action to expend 1 to 3 charges and cause a large red spectral maw to bite a creature you can see within 5 feet of you. The spectral jaws make an attack roll with a {@hit 7} bonus. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 3d6} magical piercing damage for each charge spent. You gain an amount of temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt.
If the necklace has no charges at dusk, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a 1 the fangs yellow and dull, and the necklace loses its magic forever.

name: Feather Token (Raven)
entries: You can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to throw this black token into the air. You can see and hear through the token for one hour. The token disappears afterwards or if the distance between you and it exceeds 1 mile. The bird has the statistics of a {@creature Raven|XMM}.

name: Feather Token (Snowy Owl)
entries: You can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to wave this white and grey feather across a creature's face. For {@b 1 hour}, that creature can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action without the usual requirements of being Obscured or behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB}, as long as it is against snowy terrain.

name: Feathered Helm
entries: The helm itself is simple leather, hide, scale, or plate, but the magic imbued into it comes from the feather. The birdfolk races of Humblewood consider the giving of a feather to be one of the highest honors one can bestow, and it represents an eternal bond or deep appreciation.
The helm has 3 charges that, while wearing it, you can use to activate its abilities. The helm has different properties based on the race of the birdfolk who gifted the feather.

entries.name: Corvum
entries: You can use a charge to cast {@spell Tasha's hideous laughter} (save {@dc 16}) and two charges to cast {@spell detect thoughts} (save {@dc 16}).

entries.name: Gallus
entries: You can use a charge to cast {@spell bless} and two charges to cast {@spell aid}.

entries.name: Luma
entries: You can use a charge to cast a random 1st-level spell from the {@filter sorcerer spell list|spells|level=1|class=sorcerer}, then roll a {@dice d20}. On a roll of 20, you may use this ability again without expending a charge. On a roll of 1, the spell also targets you, unless you are its only target, in which case the spell fizzles to no effect. Any spell cast using this helm that requires a saving throw has a save DC of 16.

entries.name: Raptor
entries: You can use a charge to cast {@spell hunter's mark} and two charges to cast {@spell magic weapon}.

entries.name: Strig
entries: You can use a charge to cast {@spell divine favor} and two charges to cast {@spell pass without trace}.
The helm regains {@dice 1d3} charges each day at dawn.

entries.name: A True Gift
entries: Whether you are playing through the Humblewood adventure, or playing your own campaign in the Wood, look for organic relationships between a character and the races of birdfolk. If one stands out, use that to decide what type of feather is offered to the player in this helm.

Additionally, a player whose character is a birdfolk may want to make this gift themselves. Make sure to create a narrative bond between this character and who they share a feather with—the gift of a feather is not something which should be given lightly.

name: Felinobelix (legendary)
entries: This foot-high, black, stone cat statue has {@b 6 charges} and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. Whenever you roll a die, you can expend {@b 1 charge} to roll another die of the same size (no action required). You can then choose which of the die rolls to use. You can choose to spend the charge after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. As a reaction when another creature you can see within {@b 30 feet} of you rolls a die, you can expend {@b 1 charge} to cause it to roll a second die of the same size; you choose which of the dice to use.
If the result of the re-rolled die is a 1, a devil is summoned. Consult the chart below to determine which devil.

The devil is always the same individual, who has progressed further in the infernal hierarchy with each visitation. It is hostile towards all creatures, but is especially hateful towards you, as it believes you are stealing its luck.

name: Felinobelix (rare)
entries: This foot-high, black, stone cat statue has {@b 3 charges} and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. Whenever you roll a die, you can expend {@b 1 charge} to roll another die of the same size (no action required). You can then choose which of the die rolls to use. You can choose to spend the charge after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined.
If the result of the re-rolled die is a 1, a devil is summoned. Consult the chart below to determine which devil.

The devil is always the same individual, who has progressed further in the infernal hierarchy with each visitation. It is hostile towards all creatures, but is especially hateful towards you, as it believes you are stealing its luck.

name: Fell-Rider Chariot
entries: This Large, dark iron chariot weighs 300 pounds and can fit up to four Medium or smaller creatures. While you're in the chariot, you have resistance to fire damage. Two sets of floating, flaming reins appear when you stand in the chariot, which are harmless to you. As an action, you can crack the reins downward to summon two armored {@creature nightmare|MM|nightmares} that are hitched to the front of the chariot. The nightmares have a +1 bonus to AC and exist until they drop to 0 hit points. You can use an action to dismiss them, which works only if you are standing on the chariot. The nightmares are friendly to you, fight only to protect themselves, and can't be unhitched from the chariot. The nightmares' hitches prevent them from being ridden.

The {@creature nightmare|MM|nightmares} regain all lost hit points when they are dismissed for 24 hours. When a nightmare drops to 0 hit points, it can't be summoned again until {@dice 1d4 + 1} days have passed. If the second nightmare drops to 0 hit points while the first one can't be summoned in this way, the second nightmare reappears at the same time as the first.

The chariot is drawn where the {@creature nightmare|MM|nightmares} pull it, which you control by holding the reins. If you have a good alignment, there is a {@chance 20|20 percent} chance each turn you move the chariot that the nightmares ignore your command and stop in their tracks. While both nightmares are pulling the chariot, it shares their average movement speeds and stays upright when flying. While only one nightmare is pulling the chariot, the nightmare's speed is halved, and it has a flying speed of 0.

While both {@creature nightmare|MM|nightmares} exist, you can use an action while holding the reins to cause the nightmares, the chariot, and any creatures or objects inside it to magically enter the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa.

name: Felling Greataxe
entries: This large axe has felled thousands of trees since its creation, giving it a ring-like pattern on its blade and a unique enchantment. As an action, you can speak the axe's command word and swing it to cause a large, spectral tree to fall down in a line 60 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes {@damage 3d6} bludgeoning damage and is knocked {@condition prone}. On a success, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked {@condition prone}. The spectral tree vanishes immediately after the effect. This property can't be used again until the next dawn. In the meantime, the axe can still be used as a magic weapon.
In addition, you have advantage on any ability check you make to cut down a tree when you're using the axe to chop it down.

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When Fenthras reaches an awakened state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The weapon's bonus to attack and damage rolls increases to +2. Additionally, when you hit with an attack using this weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} lightning damage.

When you hit with an attack using this weapon, you can declare it a bramble shot. The attack deals an extra {@damage 3d8} piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} or become {@condition restrained} by steely brambles that burst from the arrow. A {@condition restrained} target can repeat the {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.

name: Fenthras (Dormant)
entries: This gorgeous {@item longbow|phb} made of everbark from the Fey Realm flexes and shifts like a living entity. It is said to have been wielded by the legendary ranger {@creature Vex'ahlia|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} against great evils.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: While Fenthras is in a dormant state, you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When you make an attack with Fenthras, you can declare it an oracle shot, allowing you to experience the area around the arrow using your normal senses for 10 minutes. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.

Additionally, when a creature is killed by an attack using this weapon, a six-foot-tall tree rapidly grows out of the corpse over the next minute. The tree is rooted in the ground to make the body difficult to move, but does not permanently damage the corpse or its organs.

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When Fenthras reaches an exalted state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The weapon's bonus to attack and damage rolls increases to +3.
The extra lightning damage dealt by attacks using the bow increases to {@damage 1d6}.
You can declare a bramble shot twice between rests, and the {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} DC increases to 17.

name: Ferguson's Talons
entries: Legend has it these hand claws were crafted from the talons of a fabled feline. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: While you are holding this magic weapon, you have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Feline Form
entries: While you are holding this magic weapon, you can cast {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} from it. When you do, the spell targets only yourself and the only form you can take is a Cat.

entries.name: Nine Lives
entries: The weapon has 9 charges. While holding it, when you fail a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} you can expend 1 charge (no action required) to succeed on it instead. The weapon loses this property if it has no charges.

name: Ferryman's Take
entries: These tarnished copper coins are always found in pairs and bear the portrait of a horned man on one side (heads) and a rowboat on the other (tails).

You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to place the coins over the eyes of a Humanoid that is dead, willing, or has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. When you do, the coins create an effect based on which side is facing up. You can remove one or both of them from the creature's eyes as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to end the effect early. If the coins aren't facing the same direction, they have no effect.

entries.name: Heads
entries: While the coins are heads up over the eyes of a creature that has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, that creature is {@variantrule Stable|XPHB}. If placed over the eyes of a conscious creature, it enters a physical and mental state indistinguishable from death for 1 hour or until the coins are removed, and it has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Psychic damage for the duration. Once a living creature leaves this state, it can't enter it again for 24 hours.

entries.name: Tails
entries: While the coins are tails up over the eyes of a dead creature, that creature is under the effect of the {@spell Gentle Repose|XPHB} spell. Its body can't be detected through magical means, and the soul of the creature can't be contacted.

name: Festerwood Buckler
entries: This festerwood Shield is riddled with amber pustules that glow with a low, yellow light. While holding this magic Shield, the pustules emit {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 5-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 5 feet. In addition, while you're holding the Shield, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature that you can see within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack roll to attempt to bash that creature with the Shield. When you do, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d4 + 1} Acid damage.

name: Festerwood Claymore
entries: This heavy, dark wood is incredibly strong and forms part of the symbiotic relationship it shares with destructive beetles that live inside. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll made with this weapon, some of the sword's beetles leave the weapon and latch onto the target, biting and hindering it for its next {@dice 1d4} turns. While affected by the beetles in this way, the target takes {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage at the start of each of its turns and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved. The target or a creature within 5 feet of it can take an action to swat away the beetles, removing them and ending the effect early. If the target is a plant, a Plant creature, or an object made of wood, this effect deals maximum damage to it at the start of each of its turns and lasts for 4 turns unless ended early by a creature.

name: Festerwood Fungal Stave
reqAttune: by a Cleric, Druid, or Sorcerer
entries: This fungal staff has 25 charges and regains {@dice 1d10 + 15} expended charges daily at dusk. While holding the staff, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend 1 or more charges to cause clusters of noxious mushrooms to magically appear in a number of unoccupied spaces equal to the number of charges you expend. The spaces must be on solid ground within 60 feet of you. Each space becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for the duration of the effect. When a creature moves into or within an area covered by these mushrooms, it takes {@damage 2d4} Poison damage for every 5 feet it travels. The mushrooms live for 1 minute or until you dismiss them as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

In addition, while holding the staff, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it (regardless of the spell's normal casting time), using your spell save DC: {@spell Cloudkill|XPHB} (5 charges), {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Insect Plague|XPHB} (5 charges), or {@spell Stinking Cloud|XPHB} (3 charges). A spell cast in this way doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}, but it ends at the end of your next turn and must target a point adjacent to a space occupied by your mushrooms.

If you expend the last charge from the staff, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the fungi on the staff begin to overgrow, destroying the staff and forcing you to drop it in an unoccupied space adjacent to you. A {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} Violet Fungus grows in its place.

name: Festerwood Logger
entries: This magic axe is a favorite among lumberjacks. The axe is made entirely of the magically hardened festerwood and sharpened to a menacing edge. The weapon's glimmering yellow pustules leech acid with each attack, causing any target hit by it to take an extra {@damage 1d4} Acid damage. This Acid damage is maximized if the target is a plant, a Plant creature, or an object made of wood.

name: Festerwood Vizard
entries: This dark wooden mask is strangely insect-like and magically conforms to fit your face. While wearing the mask, you have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 10 feet.

In addition, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cause beetles to fly out of the mask's mouth, which use the Swarm of Insects ({@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}) stat block. The swarm doesn't take its own turns, but you can command it to move and make one attack as part of the action to summon it and then again on each of your subsequent turns as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, using its statistics. If you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, the swarm takes the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action and uses its movement to avoid danger. The swarm disappears when it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If it goes 10 minutes without attacking a creature, it disperses harmlessly to seek food elsewhere. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Festerwood's Light
entries: This festerwood {@item Rapier|XPHB}'s blade is inlaid with scrapings from the Lightspore, the radiant mushroom growing at the center of the Festerwood. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, attuned to the {@item Rapier|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks made to find locations within the Festerwood, and you are immune to magical contagions. While holding the sword, it sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 10 feet.

You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to raise the blade overhead and use a command word. When you do, all other creatures within 30 feet of you are dusted with a sudden wave of magical spores. An ally affected by the spores is suddenly invigorated, allowing it to immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to either make one attack roll using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or move up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. An enemy affected by the spores must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.
The {@item Rapier|XPHB} has 5 charges for the following properties. It regains {@dice 1d3 + 2} expended charges daily at dusk.

entries.name: Spells
entries: While holding the {@item Rapier|XPHB}, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17, +9 attack bonus) from it: {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} (level 4 version), {@spell Compulsion|XPHB}, {@spell Confusion|XPHB}, {@spell Contagion|XPHB}, {@spell Faerie Fire|XPHB}, {@spell Locate Animals or Plants|XPHB}, or {@spell Moonbeam|XPHB} (level 4 version). In addition, you can cast the {@spell Dancing Lights|XPHB} cantrip while holding the {@item Rapier|XPHB}.

entries.name: Spore Cleansing
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can touch a willing creature with the {@item Rapier|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to remove 1 Spore Counter from that creature.

name: Feywatch Shield
entries: This metal shield of elven make is a classic gift to allies of the fey. While holding it, you gain a +5 bonus to ability checks made to identify or perceive illusions and on saving throws against becoming {@condition charmed}.

name: Feywood Ivy
reqAttune: by a druid, ranger, or fey creature
entries: This tiny seed has a glowing rune on its shell. While holding the seed against a weapon or similar held object, you can speak its first command word as an action to cause the seed to sprout and cover the object with green and purple vines. The vines form a comfortable grip with which to hold the object and also create a protective cover for it, such as a sheath or carrying case, that automatically stows the object while it isn't being held, unless you decide for it not to. You can use an action to speak the first command word again to cause the vines to retreat from the object and return to the seed.
While an object is covered by the vines, you can't be disarmed of that object unless you are {@condition incapacitated}. In addition, the object can be used as a spellcasting focus for you.

While the vine-covered object is on your person, you can use a bonus action to speak the vines' second command word to cause them to lash out at a Medium or smaller target that you can see within 5 feet of you. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition grappled} for 1 minute. While {@condition grappled}, the target is {@condition restrained} and can use an action on each of its turns to make a DC 13 Strength or Dexterity check (its choice), freeing itself and ending the effect on a success. The effect ends early and frees the target if you move more than 5 feet away from it. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Field Cauldron
entries: This miniature cauldron is used by adventuring witches to brew potions out on the road and stretch their ingredients even further. When used alongside {@item Alchemist's Supplies|PHB|alchemy supplies} to brew an {@filter uncommon potion or rarer|items|source=ObojimaTallGrass|type=potion|rarity=uncommon;rare}, you also brew a {@filter random common potion|items|source=ObojimaTallGrass|type=potion|rarity=common}.

name: Fife of Dragonsong
entries: This magical fife can be played as an instrument or wielded as a deadly weapon. You are proficient with the Fife of Dragonsong as both an instrument and {@item Blowgun|XPHB} while you're attuned to it. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Thunder damage on a hit.

entries.name: Dragonsong
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to play a powerful note that repels foes and empowers allies. The note is audible out to 100 feet. Enemies within a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d6} Thunder damage and is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

Allies within the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} that can hear the note are bolstered by it instead. Each ally affected by the note gains {@dice 2d6} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

name: Figurine of Wondrous Power, Byeshk Worg Pack
entries: This set of four miniature worg statuettes is made from byeshk, a metal that is anathema to Aberrations. Each statuette is small enough to fit in a pocket. If you use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to speak the command word and throw one of the figurines to a point on the ground within 60 feet of you, the figurine becomes a living Worg for up to 1 hour. You can use one figurine or multiple simultaneously. If the space where a worg would appear is occupied by other creatures or objects, or if there isn't enough space for the worg, the figurine doesn't become a worg.
The worgs are Immune to Psychic damage, cannot be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, and their Bite attack deals an additional {@damage 2d6} damage against Aberrations.
The worgs are friendly to you and your companions. They understand your languages and obey your spoken commands. If you issue no commands, the worgs defend themselves but take no other actions.

At the end of the duration, the worgs revert to their figurine forms. A worg reverts to a figurine early if it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or if you use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to speak the command word again while touching it. When a worg becomes a figurine again, its property can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

name: Fin Symbiote
entries: This tendril of flesh, harvested from an Aberration, melds with the body of its host. If you are a Humanoid, you can attune to this item by stitching it into your skin during the {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} process. At the end of this time, the fin burrows into your body and bonds with your muscular system. Non-Humanoids cannot attune to the Fin Symbiote.
While attuned to the symbiote, you gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Symbiotic Health
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.

entries.name: Immovable
entries: When you would be moved against your will, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to subtract 10 feet from that movement.

entries.name: Aberrant Power
entries: If you have achieved at least Stage 1 of the {@charoption Aberrant Horror|GrimHollowPG24|Aberrant Horror Transformation}, add +2 to the DC of save DCs for your Aberrant Horror Boons.

entries.name: Symbiote Link
entries: You cannot voluntarily end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to this magic item. If it is physically removed from your body, it regrows in {@dice 1d4} hours unless you receive a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell before it grows back (which also ends your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}).

name: Final Messenger
entries: {@note Requires Use by a {@race Warforged|EFA}}

A delicate winged creature, this homunculus was designed to facilitate communication between warforged soldiers during the Last War. A {@creature Final Messenger|ExploringEberron24} is a Tiny Construct with an AC of 20, 6 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet. It has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage and Psychic damage, and all conditions other than {@condition Unconscious|XPHB|Unconsciousness}. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, treat all its ability scores as 10 (+0). It has {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. It has no limbs and the only action it can take on its turn is the {@action Dash|XPHB} action.

If you are a warforged, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to integrate a Final Messenger into your body. While it is part of your body, the messenger cannot be targeted by any attack. You can only have one messenger attached to your body at a time. A messenger can only remain active for 8 hours after it detaches from a warforged body, after which time its energy dissipates and it gains the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. An {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} messenger must complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} while attached to a warforged, after which it regains its energy, as well as regaining all lost {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

A Final Messenger holds four pieces of data, accessible only to the warforged it is attached to. While the messenger is attached to you, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to review the data currently stored within the messenger, and if you choose to, change any or all of these data points.

items: A destination for the messenger. This can be very specific (a particular apartment in Sharn) or more general (an open marketplace).
A target individual. This could be a specific person or a category ("Any Karrnathi warforged").
A single image recorded through the eyes of a warforged attached to the messenger.
A message of up to 25 words.

entries: You can release the messenger as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, at which point it flies to its destination by the most direct route possible. Once it reaches the destination it seeks the target individual; if no target has been set, it approaches the nearest warforged.

If you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} while a Final Messenger is attached to you, it immediately detaches and seeks out its target. It retains its stored message, but replaces its stored image with the last thing you saw before dropping to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

name: Finding Channeling Wand
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Finding Dragonmark Channel
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Finding Dragonmark Reservoir
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Fingerprint Kit

items.name: Ability:
entries: Intelligence

items.name: Utilize:
entries: Reveal the fingerprint left behind on an object and sketch a copy (DC 20), or match a copied fingerprint against a humanoid creature's (DC 15).
This item allows you to capture the details of a fingerprint that has been left on an object and match them against another creature. It consists of an inkpad, parchment, and talcum powder.

name: Fire Bomb
entries: You can throw a Fire Bomb by using an {@action Attack|XPHB} action. Target one space you can see within 20 feet. A creature in this space must make on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature in that space takes {@damage 2d6} Slashing damage and {@damage 4d6} Fire damage and starts {@hazard Burning|XPHB}. Creatures adjacent to the attacked space take half that damage and are not {@hazard Burning|XPHB}.

name: Fire Dervish Cloak
entries: This breathable cloak sounds like a crackling fire as it billows behind you and can create a small, fiery cyclone around you as you twirl in it. The cloak has 5 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. Once on each of your turns, you can expend 1, 2, or 3 charges from the cloak (no action required) and reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 10, 20, or 30 feet, respectively, until the end of the turn in order to spin in place instead. When you do, each creature within 5 feet of you must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 1d8} Fire damage for each charge you expended, and it can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you until the end of the turn.

name: Fire Fire!
entries: This hollow metal crossbow was created by a team of kobolds and contains an enchanted ember at its core. The crossbow has 3 charges. While the crossbow has at least 1 charge, the inner ember burns brightly when you hold the weapon. While it burns, the crossbow emits {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet, and any nonmagical Bolt fired from the crossbow catches fire and deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Fire damage on a hit.

You can also expend 1 charge as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cause the ember to spew forth devastating flames, sending out a wave of fire in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d6} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried start burning.

The crossbow regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the magical ember inside the crossbow dies out, and the weapon becomes nonmagical.

name: Fire Shield
entries: This potion burns like a hot tamale when you drink it and fills you with fiery strength. The next time you would take fire damage, you take no damage and instead regain a number of hit points equal to half the damage you would have taken. The effects of this potion last for 24 hours or until you regain hit points in this way.
{@font {@style 35|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Fire Wand of the Unbroken Circle
entries: This wooden wand is carved out of ash and is always faintly warm to the touch. Whenever you grip the wand's handle and later look at your palm, it's strangely covered in a fine layer of charcoal. This wand has 7 charges.

While holding the wand, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast either {@spell Flame Blade|XPHB} (2 charges) or {@spell Produce Flame|XPHB} (0 charges, or 1 charge to cast at level 5) from it, using an attack bonus of +5. When you cast the {@spell Flame Blade|XPHB} spell using this wand, the sword's fiery blade appears above the wand's haft instead of in a free hand.

Whenever you would fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a {@spell Flame Blade|XPHB} spell cast in this way, you can expend 1 charge as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to succeed on the save instead. You can only take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} if you're holding the wand.
The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Firecracker Crystals
entries: These multicolored crystals are usually purchased in small bags at festivals and holiday events. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can throw one of the 1-inch crystals against a solid surface within 20 feet of you to crack it apart. When a crystal breaks, it releases the magic inside. The magic ends at the end of your turn and is entirely sensory.

A bag of Firecracker Crystals comes with {@dice 1d4 + 8} crystals inside. Roll {@dice 1d8} for each crystal in the bag and record each number rolled. Use these numbers to determine the kinds of crystals found in the bag, as shown on the table below.

rows: Releases a small flash of {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 5-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 5 feet, followed by the smell of spices and citrus
Releases small spiraling motes of energy that fizz and fly about in a 5-foot radius
Releases a cloud of bright, verdant smoke that fills a 5-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} and smells both foul and sickly sweet
Releases a series of comically large bubbles that float outward from the point of impact in a 5-foot radius
Releases the sound of music; the song is random, and plays only enough to make it recognizable as music
Releases a dazzling display of sparkling glitter in a 5-foot radius
Releases a mystery effect; when used, roll on this table again to determine the effect, rerolling until you don't roll an 8

name: Firelance Venom
entries: This poison is harvested from the venom sac of a dead or {@condition incapacitated} {@creature firelance|HumblewoodTales}. A creature subjected to this poison must make a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw, taking 14 ({@damage 4d6}) poison damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. If the poison damage reduces a creature to 0 hit points, it is {@condition poisoned} for 1 hour, even after regaining hit points. A single dose of this poison costs 300 gold pieces.

name: Fireweaver Gloves
entries: While wearing these fine golden gloves, you can cast the {@spell Produce Flame|XPHB} cantrip from them (+5 to hit). You can hold this flame and other small nonmagical ones (such as that from a Candle or Torch) as if they were tangible objects and can sculpt them like clay. Once sculpted, a flame retains its form for 1 minute before returning to normal. A nonmagical flame carried in this way burns for 1 hour before dying. If you drop or throw a nonmagical flame, it immediately burns out.

When you cast {@spell Produce Flame|XPHB} using the gloves, the spell has a duration of 1 hour, instead of 10 minutes. In addition, you can place the spell's conjured flame on the ground at your feet (no action required). The placed flame is harmless and burns out after 1 minute, ending the spell, unless you take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to pick it back up while within 5 feet of it. Until you pick up the flame, you can't hurl fire as described in the spell unless you cast it again.
In addition, when you take Fire damage while wearing these gloves, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8 + 2}, provided you have a free hand.

name: Fisherman's Spear
entries: This well-crafted spear has a worn oak haft that magically springs forward at the call of its wielder. When you make a melee attack with the spear, you can cause it to magically extend, targeting a creature up to 15 feet away from you. For every 5 feet the spear extends beyond its normal reach, you take a -1 penalty to the attack roll.

name: Fists of the Guiding Star
entries: Stars and celestial bodies glimmer through these hand wrappings. While wearing these wraps over your hands, you can use a bonus action to spend 1 ki point to cause small motes of starlight to guide a creature you can see within 30 feet of you, giving it advantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of your next turn. If that creature's next attack hits, the attack deals extra radiant damage equal to your Martial Arts die + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).
In addition, you can use an action to cast the {@spell light|PHB} cantrip while wearing these wraps.

name: Flame Lance
entries: This weapon is a long metal lance with a small flame that burns at its end. It has a hose coming from the hilt that connects to a metal tank that you wear on your back.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon.

The tank has 5 charges. You can use an action and expend one or more charges from the tank to cast {@spell burning hands} (Save {@dc 15}). For 1 charge, you cast the 1st-level version of the spell. You can increase the spell slot level by one for each additional charge you expend.
Once per day, you can pour a vial of alchemist's fire into the tank. When you do, it regains all expended charges. It otherwise does not regain charges on its own.
You have disadvantage when you use a lance to attack a target within 5 feet of you. Also, a lance requires two hands to wield when you aren't mounted.

name: Flame of Ingenuity
reqAttune: by a bard, sorcerer, or wizard
entries: This wooden lantern contains a small flame within and represents the true power of fire's gift when properly harnessed. The creation of the first flame of ingenuity is said to have been divinely inspired by {@deity Gesme|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} herself.

entries.name: Light of Revelation
entries: The mystical flame inside this wooden lantern never goes out and can only be quenched inside an {@spell antimagic field}. It sheds {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} in a 30-foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 30 feet. {@condition Invisible} creatures and objects become visible so long as they are in the lantern's {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light}, and illusions in the {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} are immediately revealed, appearing as spectral forms rather than solid matter. You can use a bonus action to speak a command word to reduce the flame's light to {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} in a 5-foot radius.

entries.name: Stroke of Ingenuity
entries: When you roll a 1 or 2 on an Intelligence check while you are attuned to the lantern, you can reroll the die and must use the new result.

entries.name: Arcane Rekindling
entries: By spending 1 minute meditating on the flame within the lantern, you can regain up to 5 levels worth of spell slots, divided as you choose. For example, you could regain one 5th level spell slot, or one 3rd level and one 2nd level spell slot. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Flamebreather Staff
entries: This red, hollow quarterstaff releases a plume of fire when spun. When you hit with an attack using this magic weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} fire damage.

In addition, while holding the quarterstaff, you can speak its command word as an action to cause it to release a gout of flame from its end, duplicating the effect of the {@spell burning hands|PHB} spell (save DC 13). This property of the quarterstaff can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Flamefriend Lantern
entries: This wrought-iron lantern holds a small fire elemental spirit. To attune to this item, you must also succeed on a {@dc 10} Charisma check to bond with the spirit inside the lantern.

entries.name: Light and Flame
entries: While attuned to the lantern, you can verbally ask the elemental to glow (no action required), causing the lantern to cast bright light in a radius of your choice up to 60 feet and dim light for the same distance beyond that. You can also cast the {@spell produce flame} cantrip from the lantern at will. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

entries.name: Elemental Essence
entries: The fire elemental spirit in the lantern can grant you a small fragment of its power. As an action, you gain one of the following benefits of your choice for 1 hour:

items: You have resistance to fire damage.
Whenever a creature hits you with a melee attack, that creature takes fire damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

You can cast the {@spell burning hands} spell (spell save {@dc 15}) from the lantern at 3rd level. Once you cast the spell, you can't do so again until the next time you use this property of the lantern.

entries: Once the elemental has shared its power with you in this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Willful Attunement
entries: Your {@quickref attunement|DMG|1|0} to the lantern lasts until you choose to end it, or until you anger the elemental (by dousing the lantern in water, attacking another nonhostile elemental being, and so forth). You can attempt to attune to the lantern again and repeat the check to bond with the elemental during a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}, but you make this check with {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage} until you have made amends to the spirit, as the GM determines.

name: Flammable Tincture
entries: This swirling mixture of red and white liquid is formed from the remains of a coldfire ooze. As an action, the vial of Flammable Tincture can be hurled up to 30 feet at a target, which must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw or be covered with the liquid. For 1 minute, the creature loses its {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} or {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage and has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire damage instead.

name: Flammable Tincture
entries: This swirling mixture of red and white liquid is formed from the remains of a coldfire ooze. As an action, the vial of flammable tincture can be hurled up to 30 feet at a target, which must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or be covered with the liquid. For 1 minute, the creature is vulnerable to fire damage. This overrides any previous immunity or resistance.

name: Flashdraw Wand
entries: This delicate Wand hums with bound potential, and seems drawn to your fingers. While attuned to it, you cannot be {@status Surprised|XPHB}. Additionally, whenever you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} you can choose to immediately draw this wand (no action required). If you do so, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the total to your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} score, and all creatures within 5 feet of you take 1 Lightning damage.

name: Flesh of Dendallen
entries: This patchwork shirt is made of enchanted pieces of stitched-together flesh. The shirt has 6 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 2} expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the shirt, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to cast the {@spell False Life|XPHB} spell. In addition, while you're {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d4} plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1) at the start of each of your turns. You don't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in this way if you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition or have taken Fire or Radiant damage since the start of your last turn.

entries.name: Curse
entries: When you put on this cursed shirt for the first time, make a DC 20 Strength saving throw as the fleshy fabric begins to bubble, hiss, and fuse to your skin. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately remove the shirt before it extends the curse to you.On a failed save, you become cursed, and the shirt attaches to your flesh; you can't remove the shirt unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic. Any nonmagical clothing you were wearing under the shirt is destroyed, and magical objects worn beneath it rise to the surface as it seeps through them to attach to your skin.

As long as you remain cursed, you have the Undead creature type in addition to any other creature type you already have, and you have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Radiant damage. When you remove the shirt after being cursed by it, you take {@damage 4d10} Necrotic damage as the shirt is peeled from your skin.

name: Flip and Skip
entries: This blue potion sparkles and fizzes when opened and makes your tongue tingle when imbibed. For the next hour, you gain a +3 bonus to Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks.
{@font {@style 2|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Flood Pauldron
entries: This jewel-encrusted pauldron has the distinct appearance of a large conch shell. While wearing this pauldron, you can breathe underwater, and you have a swimming speed of 30 feet.

While worn, the pauldron releases a thin veil of illusory water, creating a small, watery cape behind you. While wearing it, you can use an action to speak its command word to cause the water to become real. When you do, the water pours from the shell in a flooding torrent that extends from you to form a 10-footradius, 20-foot-high cylinder of water that moves with you and remains centered on the ground beneath you. The cylinder lasts as long as you concentrate (as if concentrating on a spell), up to 10 minutes. However, if you move in such a way that causes you to leave the cylinder, such as by swimming upward and climbing out of it, the effect ends.

Any creature other than you in the cylinder when it appears must make a DC 13 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} bludgeoning damage and is pushed away from you to the nearest unoccupied space outside of the cylinder. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't pushed.
Once this property of the pauldron has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Flooze (uncommon)
entries: The versatility of the magically-enhanced ooze used to craft this flail can't be overstated. Its high tensile strength allows its 'chain' to stretch in response to its wearer's thoughts, while the flail's head boasts a hardness and density comparable to steel.
This magic flail deals an extra {@damage 1d6} acid damage to the first target it hits on each of your turns. The flail has {@b 8 charges} and regains {@dice 1d4 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Reachier
entries: While holding the flail, you can expend up to 4 charges (no action required) to increase your reach with this weapon by 5 feet for each charge expended until the end of your turn.

name: Flooze (very rare)
entries: The versatility of the magically-enhanced ooze used to craft this flail can't be overstated. Its high tensile strength allows its 'chain' to stretch in response to its wearer's thoughts, while the flail's head boasts a hardness and density comparable to steel.
This magic flail deals an extra {@damage 1d8} acid damage to any target it hits. The flail has {@b 8 charges} and regains {@dice 1d4 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Reachier
entries: While holding the flail, you can expend up to 4 charges (no action required) to increase your reach with this weapon by 5 feet for each charge expended until the end of your turn.

entries.name: Sticky Fingers
