On a successful save, a creature takes half as much fire damage and isn't bound by the chains. A bound creature's speed is halved, and it takes {@damage 1d12} fire damage at the start of each of its turns for up to 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Heart of the Sleeveless
entries: This vest is made from a luxurious, silky material that seems to always make the wearer appear more fit. The clothing gently hugs the wearer, redistributing weight and muscle to flatter and accentuate their physique. It seems to deflate sadly once taken off.

While worn, the fabric's color changes with the wearer's mood or flash of emotion. Refer to the table below for the vest's colors when affected by different emotions. While unworn, the fabric's color becomes a muted blue.

name: Hearthfire Breastplate (Adept)
entries: The Hearthfire Breastplate has been profoundly transformed by its corruption. Once it was emblazoned with a golden sun and radiated light. Now its surface is black and distorted, wriggling as if the metal were alive.

entries.name: Aspirant
entries: At this tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following benefits while wearing the Hearthfire Breastplate:

items: You can cast the {@spell Shield|XPHB} spell a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You gain a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} and saving throws.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Though the breastplate isn't heavy, it feels burdensome, even when you aren't wearing it. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws.

entries.name: Adept
entries: At the Adept tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following additional benefits while wearing the Hearthfire Breastplate:

items: Take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to choose up to six creatures you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature gains {@dice 1d4 + 5} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. You can use this property a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Creatures other than you have a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while they have {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} provided by the breastplate.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: You feel the pain of the companions you try to protect. When an ally within 60 feet takes damage that reduces their {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you take Psychic damage equal to half the number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} lost. This damage can't be reduced or avoided in any way.

name: Hearthfire Breastplate (Aspirant)
entries: The Hearthfire Breastplate has been profoundly transformed by its corruption. Once it was emblazoned with a golden sun and radiated light. Now its surface is black and distorted, wriggling as if the metal were alive.

entries.name: Aspirant
entries: At this tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following benefits while wearing the Hearthfire Breastplate:

items: You can cast the {@spell Shield|XPHB} spell a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You gain a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} and saving throws.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Though the breastplate isn't heavy, it feels burdensome, even when you aren't wearing it. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws.

name: Hearthfire Breastplate (Master)
entries: The Hearthfire Breastplate has been profoundly transformed by its corruption. Once it was emblazoned with a golden sun and radiated light. Now its surface is black and distorted, wriggling as if the metal were alive.

entries.name: Aspirant
entries: At this tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following benefits while wearing the Hearthfire Breastplate:

items: You can cast the {@spell Shield|XPHB} spell a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You gain a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} and saving throws.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Though the breastplate isn't heavy, it feels burdensome, even when you aren't wearing it. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws.

entries: At the Adept tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following additional benefits while wearing the Hearthfire Breastplate:

items: Take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to choose up to six creatures you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature gains {@dice 1d4 + 5} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. You can use this property a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Creatures other than you have a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while they have {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} provided by the breastplate.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: You feel the pain of the companions you try to protect. When an ally within 60 feet takes damage that reduces their {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you take Psychic damage equal to half the number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} lost. This damage can't be reduced or avoided in any way.

entries.name: Master
entries: While at the Master tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following additional benefit while wearing the Hearthfire Breastplate:

items: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to ward that creature. It has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering damage. You can use this property once, regaining the ability to do so after you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Seeing your companions fall fills you with dreadful guilt. When an ally that you can see drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. If the creature dies, you have the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition instead. At the end of each of your turns, you can make a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw, ending the condition on a success.

name: Heartless Cage Pendant
entries: This metal ribcage pendant has 12 pairs of ribs that contain a single, roughly hewn ruby that rattles around inside. The pendant has {@dice 1d4 + 8} charges when found. When a charge is expended, a pair of the pendant's ribs magically rust.

While wearing this pendant, you can use your reaction to expend 1 of the pendant's charges when a hostile creature that you can see within 30 feet of you is reduced to 0 hit points, causing the target to immediately die before any magical effects or traits can either restore it to life or prevent it from falling to 0 hit points. When you do, you gain {@dice 2d6 + 25} temporary hit points, and that creature can't be restored to life by any spell of 5th level or lower. A creature is immune to this effect if it has legendary actions.

When you expend the pendant's last charge, the ribcage shatters and releases the ruby inside. When it does, the ruby crackles with necrotic energy and summons 12 {@creature skeleton|MM|skeletons} that appear in unoccupied spaces that you can see within 60 feet of you. The summoned skeletons are friendly to you and your companions. Roll initiative for the summoned creatures as a group, which have their own turns. They obey any verbal commands that you issue to them (no action required by you). If you don't issue any commands to them, they defend themselves from hostile creatures, but otherwise take no actions. The GM has the skeletons' statistics.
A {@creature skeleton|MM} disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or after 24 hours.
Once the ribcage shatters and the ruby summons the {@creature skeleton|MM|skeletons}, the pendant and gemstone crumble into ashes and are destroyed.

name: Heaven's Edge
entries: This ornate dagger is made of multiple pieces that magically hover together, but move as if they were solidly connected. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 2d4} radiant damage to any creature it hits. This extra damage increases to {@damage 4d4} radiant damage if the creature is a fiend or undead.

When you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this weapon against a fiend, the target must make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is banished, as if by the {@spell banishment} spell. This version of the spell doesn't require concentration but ends early if you become {@condition incapacitated} or die within the next minute. On a successful save, the creature is {@condition blinded} until the start of your next turn and isn't banished.

name: Heaven's Gavel
reqAttune: by a creature of good alignment
entries: This platinum weapon was a gift from a divine dragon to one of her loyal knights and has been passed down for generations. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit an evil-aligned creature with the weapon, that creature takes an extra {@damage 1d6} radiant damage.

The maul has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a creature no more than one size larger than you with the maul, you can expend up to 3 of its charges as part of the attack. When you do, the target must make a DC 17 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is launched 10 feet away from you for each expended charge, or half as far on a successful one. If the target hits a solid object by being launched in this way, it takes {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it had left to travel from the impact. If the solid object is a creature, that creature takes the same amount of bludgeoning damage from the impact as the target of the attack.

name: Heaven's Herald
entries: This golden trumpet is never dulled by rust or dirt. As an action, you can blow the trumpet to create a rousing battle call that can be heard up to {@b 600 feet} away.

When you use the trumpet, choose up to 12 willing creatures within {@b 600 feet} to become emboldened. An emboldened creature has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition and {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom saving throws. In addition, its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by {@dice 2d10} and it regains the same number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. These benefits last for 8 hours.
If you are a Fiend or Undead creature, you take {@damage 8d6} Radiant damage when you blow the trumpet.
Once you use Heaven's Herald, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

name: Heavenkiller Chronicles
entries: Spicule's vast tome contains secrets concerning celestials and how to use them to fuel dark magic. You must spend 50 hours studying this tome to gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Intelligence checks to determine the vulnerabilities and weaknesses of Celestials.
You deal an extra 9 ({@damage 2d8}) damage to Celestials when you hit them with an attack.

You know how to harvest parts of Celestials and use them to fuel dark magic. You can harvest a heart, eye, or other useful organ from a Celestial's corpse with a successful DC 16 Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check. You can use a harvested Celestial organ in place of one material component that would normally be consumed by the spell, up to a cost of 2,500 gp.

name: Heavenly Chalice
entries: This golden goblet is ornamented with 4 glimmering gems and stripes of jet and ivory. It weighs 2 pounds and can hold the contents of one potion. When a {@item Potion of Healing (*)|DMG|potion of healing} (of any rarity) is poured into the cup, a cleric, paladin, or other creature with a magical connection to a celestial can spend 1 minute reciting a prayer over it. At the end of the prayer, the potion becomes sanctified and begins to glow with a calming blue light. When a {@item Potion of Healing (*)|DMG|potion of healing} becomes sanctified, it creates a pool of hit points equal to the maximum number of potential regained hit points possible for that potion.

When a creature drinks from a sanctified {@item Potion of Healing (*)|DMG|potion of healing}, that creature can restore a number of hit points of its choice, up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool. When the pool is reduced to 0 hit points, the potion is gone.
A potion remains sanctified for 24 hours or until it's spilled or poured into another vessel. Once this property of the goblet has been used, it can't be used again for 24 hours.

name: Heavy Golem Armor
entries: This heavy set of plate mail is 5½ feet tall, weighs 100 pounds, and is reconfigured from the pieces of an iron golem. Despite the armor's larger size, a series of clever harnesses inside its chest piece comfortably support you inside it. While wearing this armor, your Strength score is 19, unless it's already higher, and you are considered to be a Medium creature. Magic currents run through the inside of the armor and connect to you, allowing you to control the metal limbs as if they were your own. This magical connection causes you to still take any damage you receive while wearing the armor.

While wearing this armor, you can use a bonus action to speak its command word to force the armor to move more rapidly. When it does, you gain the effect of the {@spell haste} spell (no concentration required), and the armor's joints creak and groan from the increased strain. At the end of each of your turns while you're under this effect, there is a cumulative {@chance 20|20 percent} chance that the armor overheats. When it does, you take {@damage 1d10} fire damage from the armor, and the effect ends. Once this property of the armor has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Hecate's Dagger
entries: This adamantine dagger has a blue leather hilt wrapped with gold wire, a star opal as its pommel. Its blade is etched with the phases of the moon and a triangle similar to Hecate's holy symbol. It is said to be one of the daggers the goddess used when she parted and shaped raw shadow to create the Shadow Realm for her devoted followers. Several such daggers may exist.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It has the following additional properties.

entries.name: Counterspell
entries: When you speak Hecate's name while wielding the dagger, your {@spell counterspell} rolls are all made with advantage.

entries.name: Geas
entries: Once per day, you may cast the {@spell geas} spell on any cleric, paladin, or devout follower of Hecate.

entries.name: Control Shadows
entries: Once per day, you may cast either the {@spell ebon tide|BookOfEbonTides} spell or the {@spell dimension door} spell.

name: Hecate's Lantern
entries: Hecate's lantern is said to have been used to divide darkness and light during the creation of the Shadow Realm. It is made of gold and mithral with panes of amber and clear crystal, and it can be held by an ornate loop at its top. A single ever-burning candle shines within, though the panes of the lantern often make it appear as three candles.

You must be brandishing the lantern to use it. This lantern has 12 charges for the following properties. It regains {@dice 1d12 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the lantern's last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the lantern vanishes and returns to a high priestess of Hecate or to the goddess herself.

entries.name: Create Mire
entries: As an action, you can expend 5 charges to create shadow mire (see Chapter 5 of Book of Ebon Tides) with a 40-foot radius centered on you.

entries.name: Force Shift
entries: As an action, you can expend 3 charges to force any shapeshifter you can see within 120 feet to shift their form. If unwilling, the target gains a DC 13 Charisma saving throw to negate the effect.

entries.name: Spells
entries: As an action, you can cast the {@spell moonbeam} spell (2 charges) with a range encompassing any point you can see or the {@spell child of light and darkness|BookOfEbonTides} spell (8 charges).

name: Hedgewitch's Gardening Cane
entries: This wooden walking stick has a silver flower at either end. The flower is blooming on the handle, but merely a bud towards the bottom. While holding the cane, you can use an action to tap it against the ground and mentally command the bottom portion to magically transform into a broom, a hoe, a rake, a shovel, or back into a normal cane.

name: Hedonic Motivator
entries: This magic whip once belonged to an especially controlling succubus or incubus. The whip has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dusk. While holding the whip, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 of its charges to lash out with it against a friendly creature within 10 feet of you. That creature gains one of the following benefits of your choice:

items: The creature gains {@dice 2d4 + 4} temporary hit points, which last for 1 minute.
The creature can add {@dice 1d4 + 2} to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

name: Hel's Coin
entries: While carrying this blackened silver coin, if you fail a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}, you treat the save as a success instead. Then the coin crumbles into dust.

If you carry more than one Hel's Coin, you gain the following curse instead. If you succeed on a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}, you treat the success as a failure. Then one Hel's Coin crumbles to dust. This curse remains until there is only one coin left in your possession, whereupon that coin's normal effect resumes. You can freely divest yourself of extra coins.

name: Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting (uncommon)
entries: Full of useful knowledge and heavy enough to crush a skull, Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting is nothing if not handy. The personalised quotes from Heliana, Peeper's deft proofing and editing, and the numerous ink stains and spilled watercolours give this hefty tome a homemade feel.

entries.name: Fantastic Phalanges and Where to Find Them
entries: As an action, you can open this book and stare intently at its pages, which turn of their own accord to settle on an anatomical diagram of the corpse nearest to the book. You immediately learn all the harvestable parts of the corpse, as well as their Component DCs.

entries.name: Know Thy Enemy
entries: As an action, you can place an object that belonged to a creature—such as its scat, scales, or clothing— between the pages of this book. One minute later, the book tells you one piece of information about the creature. At the GM's discretion, this may be: its saving throw proficiencies, damage resistances, immunities, and vulnerabilities; condition immunities; creature's type; one of its traits; or one of the clues acquired during a hunt. Placing more objects that belonged to that creature (or a creature with the same statblock) yields no further results.

entries.name: Weapon of the Learned
entries: This book can be used as a simple melee weapon that deals {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on a hit. If you are proficient in {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}, you are proficient with this weapon.

name: Heliana's Guide to Monster Hunting (very rare)
entries: The deluxe, leatherbound version of this book imparts some of Heliana's own wisdom to those that read it regularly; it has the Anatomiser property and Know Thy Enemy reveals two pieces of information.

entries.name: Fantastic Phalanges and Where to Find Them
entries: As an action, you can open this book and stare intently at its pages, which turn of their own accord to settle on an anatomical diagram of the corpse nearest to the book. You immediately learn all the harvestable parts of the corpse, as well as their Component DCs.

entries.name: Know Thy Enemy
entries: As an action, you can place an object that belonged to a creature—such as its scat, scales, or clothing— between the pages of this book. One minute later, the book tells you two pieces of information about the creature. At the GM's discretion, this may be: its saving throw proficiencies, damage resistances, immunities, and vulnerabilities; condition immunities; creature's type; one of its traits; or one of the clues acquired during a hunt. Placing more objects that belonged to that creature (or a creature with the same statblock) yields no further results.

entries.name: Weapon of the Learned
entries: This book can be used as a simple melee weapon that deals {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on a hit. If you are proficient in {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}, you are proficient with this weapon.

entries.name: Anatomiser
entries: If you read this book for {@b 1 hour}, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice for the next 24 hours: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Investigation}, {@skill Nature}, {@skill Medicine}, {@skill Religion}, or {@skill Survival}. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again for 24 hours.

name: Hellfire Pitchfork
entries: This menacing, black iron {@item Trident|XPHB} is warm to the touch, weighs 10 pounds, and has the {@itemProperty H|XPHB|Heavy} property. As a result of its weight, the {@item Trident|XPHB} has a normal throwing range of 15 feet and a long range of 45 feet. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 1d8} Radiant damage on a hit. While the {@item Trident|XPHB} is within 60 feet of you, you can use a command word as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically cause it to disappear in a puff of smoke and reappear in one of your open hands. If you use the command word immediately after making a ranged attack roll with the {@item Trident|XPHB}, it erupts in a 5-foot-high pillar of flame, instead of smoke, before it reappears in your hand. Any creature in the {@item Trident|XPHB}'s space when it erupts in this way must succeed on a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d8} Fire damage.

name: Helm of Burning Rage
entries: This helm is forged in fires ignited with elemental dust, using plates from a construct and the heart of a red dragon. The plates are then soaked in elemental fluid before having an animus gem installed that contains the energy of a Fire Giant.

While your Rage is active, you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage. In addition, once per turn, while you are Raging, when you hit a target with a Melee weapon that benefitted from your Reckless Attack feature, the target becomes {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} ({@dice 2d4} Fire).

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Helm of Burning Rage requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Animus from a Fire Giant

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Elemental Dust

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Elemental Fluid

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Plates

items.name: [Organ]
entries: Heart from a Red Dragon

name: Helm of Heroes
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} if you're wearing no armor while wearing this helmet. You can still use a Shield and gain this benefit. In addition, while you aren't wearing armor, the helm becomes suffused with glory and glimmers for 1 minute whenever you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll. While the helm is glimmering in this way, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of each of your turns equal to half your level (round down), and you and your allies within 10 feet of you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

name: Helm of Patron Saints
entries: While wearing this helm, you can see invisible creatures and objects within 60 feet of you. In addition, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls, and increase your spell saving throw DC by 2.

entries.name: Relics of Saint Vitruvio
entries: These holy relics of the Sacred Flame were wielded by Saint Vitruvio and are kept in several religious sites throughout Drakkenheim. The Knights of the Silver Order and the Followers of the Falling Fire now seek these relics. Not only do both factions revere Saint Vitruvio, both wish to use these relics to help advance their goals in Drakkenheim.

A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio may cast the {@spell heal} spell three times per day, after which they must finish a long rest before they may do so again. In addition, that character gains the ability to attune to two additional magic items so long as those magic items are both Relics of Saint Vitruvio.

name: Helm of the Broken Dragon
entries: This helmet is made of harsh, angular shapes that come together into the shape of an aberrant dragon skull. Your scales twist into strange, fractal-like patterns tinged with otherworldly colors when you attune to this item. While wearing the helmet, you have resistance to psychic damage, and creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks against you. In addition, your breath weapon changes to be a plume of unearthly psionic energy, dealing psychic damage instead of its normal damage type. A creature in the area must make a Wisdom saving throw, instead of your breath weapon's normal save. On a failed save, a creature is also affected as by the {@spell bane} spell for 1 minute as maddening whispers fill its mind. The creature can make a Wisdom saving throw against your breath weapon DC at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This helmet is cursed with gnawing insecurity and self-doubt. Attuning to the helmet curses you until you are targeted by the remove curse spell or similar magic. While cursed, you are unwilling to remove the helm, and you gain the following flaw: "Whatever course of action I take, there is a voice in my head that screams at me to do the opposite. The voice is never silent."

name: Helm of the Chromatic Dragon
reqAttune: by a dragonborn of evil alignment
entries: This iridescent helmet has been blessed by a powerful, evil dragon. While wearing this helmet, your breath weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of its type, and you can choose whether it deals acid, cold, fire, lightning or poison damage. You can also choose if your breath weapon affects a 15-foot cone or 5-by-30-foot line, and if creatures affected by it must make a Dexterity or Constitution saving throw.
In addition, when you use your breath weapon, roll a {@dice d6}. On a 5 or 6, you gain an additional use of your breath weapon before you need to finish a short or long rest.

name: Helm of the Justicars
entries: This helm once belonged to Grand Mage-Arbiter Elodie Scolian, the preeminent leader of the surviving Justicar order. Designed to eliminate the threat that all mages pose to the nonmagical populace, the wearer of this helmet has an uncanny resilience against spells of all kinds. While wearing this helmet, you gain a +1 bonus to AC, you have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects, and spell attacks have disadvantage against you.

In addition, the helm has 12 charges and regains {@dice 2d6} expended charges daily at dawn. Whenever you're affected by a spell while wearing this helmet, you can use your reaction to learn the level of the spell and expend any number of charges from the helm (minimum 1 charge). If the number of charges is equal to or greater than the level of the triggering spell, you are unaffected by it. A cantrip is considered to be a 1st-level spell for the purposes of this property.

name: Helm of the Platinum Dragon
reqAttune: by a dragonborn of good alignment
entries: This magical platinum helmet has been blessed by a powerful, holy dragon. While wearing this helmet, you gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws, and when you use your breath weapon, you can choose to exhale a holy blue plume of healing energy instead. When you do, this breath weapon deals radiant damage, evil-aligned hostile creatures within the area have disadvantage on the saving throw, and any friendly creatures in the area regain a number of hit points equal to your breath weapon's damage dice instead. This property of the helm can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Helm of the Ruby Dragon
reqAttune: by a dragonborn of neutral alignment
entries: This magic gold and ruby helm has been blessed by a powerful, psychic dragon. While wearing this helmet, you have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks, as well as Intelligence checks made to glean information from an observation or bit of lore. In addition, you can speak telepathically to any creature within 30 feet of you. The creature understands you only if the two of you share a language. You can speak telepathically in this way to one creature at a time.

When you use your breath weapon while wearing this helmet, you can choose to exhale a blast of pure, concussive force. When you do, your breath weapon deals force damage, instead of its normal damage type, and any creature that fails the saving throw takes an extra {@damage 2d6} psychic damage and is {@condition stunned} until the end of your next turn. This property of the helm can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Helm of the Sentinel
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA}
entries: This helm has 3 charges. While wearing it, you can use any of its properties. It regains all expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Counterspell
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to expend 1 charge and establish a defensive ward with a contingent {@spell Counterspell|XPHB}. The next time you can see an unfriendly creature within 60 feet of you casting any spell that either targets you or causes you to make a saving throw, the {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} immediately takes effect whether or not you want it to, as if you had cast it using your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell. The ward ends immediately after {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} takes effect or at the next dawn.

entries.name: Protection
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to expend 1 charge and cast {@spell Protection from Energy|XPHB} on yourself.

entries.name: Deflection Field
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to expend 1 charge and cast {@spell Shield of Faith|XPHB} on yourself.

name: Helmsman's Shelter
entries: This magic Shield offers a degree of control over the seas. While holding this Shield, you have a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC. While attuned to the Shield, you have a +1 bonus to any ability check you make to control a waterborne vehicle.

The Shield has 5 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the Shield, you can expend 3 charges to cast the {@spell Control Water|XPHB} spell (save DC 15) from it. Alternatively, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend 1 charge to take control of a water vehicle you can see within 300 feet of you that has a rudder. If the vehicle has a creature currently controlling its rudder, it must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you wrestle control away from the creature and can alter the direction of the vehicle by up to 90 degrees. You maintain control of the vehicle until the start of your next turn.

name: Herbalist's Aid
entries: Drinking this highly sought-after potion grants you a unique sense helpful for detecting ingredients. For the next hour, you gain a +3 bonus to all ability checks made to locate an ingredient.
{@font {@style 19|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Hero's Blade
entries: When poured over a weapon, this heroic elixir stains it blue and causes it to shimmer as if it were a gemstone reflecting light. For the next minute, the weapon gains a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls. Until this effect ends, creatures hit by this weapon don't benefit from any damage immunities or resistances they have, if any, for 1 minute.
{@font {@style 58|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Heroism
entries: When you drink this glowing red elixir, you gain advantage on the next attack roll you make within the next 24 hours.
{@font {@style 17|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Heron's Eye Ring
entries: While wearing this ring you gain a +3 bonus to Wisdom ({@skill Insight} and {@skill Perception}) checks. Spells. The ring has 6 charges. While wearing it, you can use an action to expend some of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it:

items: {@spell Dispel Magic} (3 charges)
{@spell Find Traps} (2 charges)
{@spell See Invisibility} (2 charges)
{@spell Shared Vision|ObojimaTallGrass} (2 charges)
{@spell Spell Signature|ObojimaTallGrass} (2 charges)

entries: The ring regains {@dice 1d4 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn.

name: Hexaxe
entries: This {@item Handaxe|XPHB} amplifies curses bestowed on its enemies. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon against creatures under the effects of a Warlock spell you cast that requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

The weapon has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dusk. When you're forced to make a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a Warlock spell while you're holding the axe, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to add your Charisma modifier (minimum +1) to the save.

name: Hidden Hand
entries: When consumed, this grainy potion heightens your senses and gives you a sunken feeling of untapped strength. For the next 24 hours, you gain telekinetic powers as if you were under the effects of the {@spell Telekinesis} spell.
{@font {@style 52|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Hide of the Brimstone Behemoth (Legendary)
entries: This cloak was made from the hide of a reptilian magma Fiend, incomparable in its destructive power. Flame now shies away from it, for one who has mastered such a titanic creature can master its element.
While wearing this cloak, you gain a +3 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} and Constitution saving throws determined by the cloak's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Deep-Dweller (Rare+)
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage and a {@variantrule Burrow Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. Once during your turn when you emerge from burrowing, each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the hide's bonus), taking {@damage 2d8} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Infernal Roar (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Fear|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the hide's bonus) from the cloak. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Hellfire Maw (Very Rare+)
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can exhale hellfire in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the hide's bonus). On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} Fire damage and {@damage 4d6} Necrotic damage, and it can't regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half damage only. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Pernicious Fire Immunity (Legendary)
entries: Fire actively avoids you. You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Fire damage. When you are the target of an attack that deals Fire damage, the attack randomly targets another creature within the attack's range, which can include the attacker. When you make a saving throw against an effect that deals Fire damage, you must choose one other creature that is also making the saving throw against that effect. It has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the save.

name: Hide of the Brimstone Behemoth (Rare)
entries: This cloak was made from the hide of a reptilian magma Fiend, incomparable in its destructive power. Flame now shies away from it, for one who has mastered such a titanic creature can master its element.

name: Hideaway Vase
entries: This durable, ceramic vase is 3 feet tall and weighs 15 pounds. You can use an action to remove the vase's lid. When you do, you must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma saving throw or be shunted onto a harmless demiplane inside the vase. A Large or larger creature automatically succeeds on the saving throw, but a willing Medium or smaller creature can choose to fail it. If a creature is already on the demiplane when you remove the lid, that creature reappears in the nearest unoccupied space, and you automatically succeed on the saving throw. Immediately after opening the vase in this way, the lid flies back and reseals the vase.

While on this demiplane, you can't move and are {@condition blinded}, but can hear everything outside of the vase as if you were standing in its space. You can leave this demiplane using an action to reappear in the nearest unoccupied space. When you attempt to leave the demiplane, a creature outside the vase can use its reaction to hold the vase's lid shut and make a DC 25 Strength check, preventing you from leaving on a success.

The vase has AC 12, 30 hit points, and is vulnerable to bludgeoning damage. The vase is destroyed if it drops to 0 hit points. If the vase is destroyed while a creature is on its demiplane, that creature is forced into the nearest unoccupied space. Once a creature leaves the demiplane, the vase's lid can't be removed again for 24 hours.

You can remain on the demiplane for up to 8 hours or until the vase is placed inside an extradimensional space created by a {@item bag of holding}, {@item portable hole}, or similar item, at which time you are forcefully shunted out of it. If the lid is successfully held in place when you would be forcefully shunted from the demiplane in this way, the vase shatters and is destroyed.

While holding the vase, you can use an action to change the style, color, and apparent quality of the vessel. The vase's weight doesn't change. Regardless of its appearance, the vase can't be anything but a vase.

name: Hindsight
entries: A well-known potion amongst investigators and merchants, this thick brew acquires special insight on an object when poured over it. The only downside is that you must then lick the brew off the object to obtain any of this information. When poured and then licked off, the potion reveals a minor but useful bit of information about the object.
{@font {@style 16|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Hjartarydi's Belt
entries: Touching this blood-red leather belt fills you with a sense of comfort. While you have the belt equipped, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions.

name: Hoarder's Haul
entries: Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

items: {@item Hoarder's Haul (Uncommon)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Hoarder's Haul (Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Hoarder's Haul (Very Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}

name: Hoarder's Haul (Rare)
entries: This magical cart is made from the large, hollow horn of a fallen dragon. While all {@i hoarder's hauls} are made from the horns of dragons, their true magic stems from the strength of the dragon's greed. Uncommon and rare carts have handles and a single wheel at their front and must be physically moved. Very rare versions have a flying speed of 10 feet, can hover up to 20 feet off the ground, and move according to your spoken directions, provided that you are within 30 feet of the cart.

The cart has two command words. The first command word can be spoken using an action and causes the cart to shrink or enlarge, becoming as small as 1 foot long and 7 inches across or as large as 5 feet long and 3 feet across. Regardless of its size, the cart always weighs 5 pounds without anything inside it. Anything contained by the cart does not resize to fit its new size, potentially spilling onto the ground if the cart becomes too small.

When you place a nonliving object in the cart, you can speak the cart's second command word as an action to cause the object to become locked in place. A locked object can't be removed or interacted with against your will, unless the cart becomes too small to contain it. A creature that attempts to remove an object locked in this way must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition frightened} of the cart for 1 minute. A {@condition frightened} creature is unwilling to move toward the cart or interact with it for the duration. If the cart is a rare or very rare version, the creature also takes psychic damage on a failed saving throw. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to this effect for 24 hours. You can speak the second command word as an action again to unlock any number of objects within the cart.

The cart's properties depend on the item's rarity. The uncommon variant has a carrying capacity of 500 lb., and a save DC of 15. Creatures that fail the saving throw take {@damage 3d6} psychic damage.

entries: This magical cart is made from the large, hollow horn of a fallen dragon. The cart's properties depend on the item's rarity. The uncommon variant has a carrying capacity of 250 lb., and a save DC of 13.

The cart's properties depend on the item's rarity. The uncommon variant has a carrying capacity of 750 lb., and a save DC of 16. Creatures that fail the saving throw take {@damage 6d6} psychic damage.

name: Hogs' Wash
entries: This foul-tasting tea is brewed from the powdered tusks of doom boars. When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell.
Hogs' Wash can also be used as a component in removing a Shadowsteel curse (see "{@book Shadowsteel Curses|GrimHollowPG24|7|Shadowsteel Curses}").

name: Hollow Eye
entries: This small wooden talisman is shaped like a large eyeball with an empty void in place of the pupil. While holding the eye, as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 1 of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} to drip a small quantity of your own blood into the eye and cast either the {@spell Arcane Eye|XPHB} spell or the {@spell Divination|XPHB} spell. Once you use the eye once, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Homegrown
entries: When poured over a surface that is at least a 50-foot square area and isn't obstructed by obstacles (such as trees or boulders), this pungent liquid begins to quickly foam and expand. After 1 minute, a newly formed and furnished home of grand size appears in the space.
{@font {@style 51|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Homeroot
entries: This piece of gnarled root has several bulbous openings along its twisted length. Enchanted by powerful druids, this root has a tiny door and a small, chimney-like protrusion from its larger end. While holding it, a tiny plume of illusory smoke emanates from the chimney.

You can bury and plant this root in soil over the course of 1 minute. If the root remains buried for 1 hour, it then immediately grows underground to create a comfortable, wooden dwelling (provided that there's enough room to grow), and a stump appears from the ground where the root was buried. The stump has a simple round door carved into it that is large enough for a Medium or smaller creature to enter. The door appears and opens only at your command, which you can speak as a bonus action. It is immune to the {@spell knock|PHB} spell and similar magic, such as that of a {@item chime of opening|DMG}. The door opens to reveal a tunnel 15 feet deep and lined with ladder-like rungs made of twisting roots. At the bottom of the tunnel is a large, circular room that's 30 feet in diameter with 10-foot-high ceilings. The room is brightly lit by bioluminescent fungi that grow along its wooden walls and ceiling. You can magically control the light in the room by touching the luminous fungi, allowing you to fill the room with total darkness, dim light, or bright light.

A single hallway leads away from the room. Four doors line the hallway, which each lead to a room that's 10 feet in diameter with a 10-foot-high ceiling. Every room is decorated with various pieces of wooden furniture made from coiled roots and other magically occurring plant growth, such as tables, chairs, or a bed, depending on the needs of the creature who planted the root.

At the end of the hallway hangs a single red root. You can use a bonus action to pull the root to cause the hallway to extend upward into a tunnel, complete with a root-like ladder, and create a second, temporary entrance to the dwelling in an unoccupied space 60 feet away from the entrance stump. The temporary entrance is well-hidden, noticeable only with a successful DC 15 Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, and remains until the start of your next turn.

A creature that casts the {@spell plant growth} spell as an action can redesign the appearance and furniture in one of the dwelling's rooms. If the spell is cast over the course of 8 hours, the creature can redesign the appearance and furniture of the entire dwelling instead, except for the location of the entrance stump. A conscious druid or ranger inside the dwelling is aware of any Small or larger creature that comes within 60 feet of the dwelling's entrance, and magically knows only the creature's size and gait, such as the gallop of a horse or walk of a humanoid.

The entrance stump has 100 hit points, immunity to damage from nonmagical weapons excluding siege weapons, and resistance to all other damage. Only a {@spell plant growth} spell cast on the stump can repair it, with each casting restoring 10 hit points to it, or all its hit points if cast over the course of 8 hours. If the stump is destroyed, the dwelling collapses and magically shunts anything inside it (other than the furniture) to the nearest unoccupied space next to where the root was buried. When this happens, the earth magically returns to the way it was before the root was buried.

name: Homeward Boots
entries: These well-worn boots have an ever-changing arcane circle ingrained into their heels. While wearing the boots, you can use an action to speak their first command word to create an arcane circle, as per the {@spell teleportation circle|PHB} spell, on the ground below you. The circle appears as a trail of dirt or similar muck from the bottom of the shoe, and is treated as a permanent one for the purposes of this spell. Speaking the first command word again destroys the first circle, magically cleaning the surface it was placed on, before creating a new one at your location.

You can speak the boots' second command word as an action while wearing them to cast the {@spell teleportation circle|PHB} spell, except that this circle is only 5 feet in diameter. This circle's sigil sequence matches the one created by the first command word and links to its location. When it's created, the circle appears under your feet, centered on your location, and you immediately teleport through it. Only a circle created in this way can connect to the permanent one created by the boots' first command word. If the permanent circle is washed away or otherwise cleaned or destroyed before you speak the second command word, the spell fails and the circle isn't created.
Once you use the boots to teleport in this way, they can't do so again until {@dice 1d3} days have passed. In the meantime, you can still speak the boots' first command word.

name: Homeward Tonic
entries: This fiery red elixir smells of home and drinking it gives a sensation of comfort when consumed. For the next 24 hours, you always know the direction of the place you consider home, provided it is on the same plane of existence.
{@font {@style 20|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Honey of Robust Health
entries: When you consume this honey as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can reroll any result of 1 or 2 on {@variantrule Hit Dice|XPHB} spent to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} during that rest. You must use the new roll. The honey has a deep red tinge and a rich flavor, and it warms the stomach.

name: Honey of the Hearth Fire
entries: When you consume this honey, you end the {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions on yourself.

name: Honey of the Hive Warden
entries: When you consume this honey, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison for {@b 1 hour}. Once during the duration, you may cast {@spell Insect Plague|XPHB} ({@dc 15}). Instead of locusts dealing Piercing damage, the spell creates bees that deal Poison damage.

name: Honey of the Norn-Blessed
entries: When you consume this honey, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws for {@b 1 hour}. Once during the duration, you may cast {@spell Augury|XPHB}.

name: Honey of the Sacred Bear
entries: When you consume this honey, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks for {@b 1 hour}. Once during the duration, you may cast {@spell Heroism|XPHB} on yourself, requiring no {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

name: Honey of the Skald's Tongue
entries: When you consume this honey, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Performance|XPHB} and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} checks for {@b 1 hour}. Once during the duration, you may cast {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} ({@dc 15}).

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When Honor's Last Stand reaches an awakened state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The shield's bonus to AC increases to +2.
If you successfully {@action shove} a creature while holding this shield, that creature takes {@damage 2d6} force damage.
When a creature within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack, you can attempt to {@action shove} that creature as a reaction.

name: Honor's Last Stand (Dormant)
reqAttune: by a creature of non-evil alignment
entries: This massive silvered shield bears the crest of {@deity The Platinum Dragon|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} and never tarnishes. Its metal is always warm to the touch.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: While Honor's Last Stand is in a dormant state, you gain a +1 bonus to AC while holding the shield. This bonus is in addition to the shield's normal bonus to AC. You also can't be knocked {@condition prone} while bearing this shield.

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When Honor's Last Stand reaches an exalted state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The shield's bonus to AC increases to +3.
When you successfully {@action shove} a creature while holding this shield, you can move it up to 15 feet away from you.
As a bonus action, you can protect an ally within 5 feet of you, granting that ally a +3 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn or until they are no longer within 5 feet of you.

name: Hook of the Tall Man (Legendary)
entries: This hook is made from a single huge claw attached to a large bleached fingerbone mounted on a haft of ash. The tip of the claw gives off an eerie glow. The finger and claw were cut from the hand of the Tall Man.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon determined by the hook's rarity. While holding the hook, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Snare (Rare+)
entries: When you hit a creature with the hook, you can activate the {@itemMastery Topple|XPHB} mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you're using with it.

entries.name: Fey Haunt's Stride (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} from the hook, and when you do so, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your next Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check made before the end of your next turn. This property can be used twice, regaining all expended uses when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}.

entries.name: Strike from Shadows (Very Rare+)
entries: When you start your turn with the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the first attack you make on your turn, even if the condition ends before you make the attack. If that attack hits, it deals an extra {@damage 2d6} Piercing damage.

entries.name: Hunter's Hook (Legendary)
entries: When you hit with an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} made with the hook, the target takes an extra {@damage 2d6} Psychic damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 until the end of the turn.

entries.name: Terrifying Stride (Legendary)
entries: Immediately after you use the Fey Haunt's Stride property, you can choose a creature within 20 feet of you. It must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. While {@condition Frightened|XPHB} in this way, the creature can't take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

entries: This hook is made from a single huge claw attached to a large bleached fingerbone mounted on a haft of ash. The tip of the claw gives off an eerie glow. The finger and claw were cut from the hand of the Tall Man.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon determined by the hook's rarity. While holding the hook, you can use the following properties.

entries: When you hit a creature with the hook, you can activate the {@itemMastery Topple|XPHB} mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you're using with it.

entries: You can cast {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} from the hook, and when you do so, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your next Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check made before the end of your next turn. This property can be used twice, regaining all expended uses when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}.

entries: This hook is made from a single huge claw attached to a large bleached fingerbone mounted on a haft of ash. The tip of the claw gives off an eerie glow. The finger and claw were cut from the hand of the Tall Man.
