entries.name: Strike from Shadows (Very Rare+)
entries: When you start your turn with the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the first attack you make on your turn, even if the condition ends before you make the attack. If that attack hits, it deals an extra {@damage 2d6} Piercing damage.

name: Hook Sling
entries: This heavy metal contraption can be used to hurl a barbed hook at the surface of a solid object within 20 feet of you, latching onto it and pulling you toward the target. The hook can be hurled using a bonus action, and it requires an action to wind it back in before you can use it again. You can hurl the hook using only one hand, but it requires two hands to wind the hook back in. If the targeted surface has no lip to grasp or is otherwise too difficult for the barb to hook onto, the hook fails to latch onto it and pull you.

name: Horatio's Impossible Ship in a Bottle
entries: This sea-tumbled glass bottle has a miniature sailing ship assembled inside it. The bottle weighs 1 pound and is magically sealed with red wax. Despite there being no wind in the bottle, the vessel's sails seemingly billow and turn on their own.

You can speak the bottle's command word to cause the wax to come apart and open the bottle. When the open bottle is submerged in a large enough body of water, the ship inside it magically slips out, destroying the bottle, and becomes a {@item sailing ship|DMG} 50 feet long and 15 feet wide. A crew of 10 {@spell unseen servant|PHB|unseen servants} remain on the ship at all times and can be commanded by you or any creature that is friendly to you while on board to adjust the ship's sails and direction. The ship's reduced size halves the vessel's normal creature and cargo capacity, but is otherwise treated as if it were a normal sailing ship.

If you keep a similarly sized glass bottle aboard the vessel, the ship and its unseen crew magically reduce in size and appear inside the newly sealed bottle when the ship is run aground. The bottle must have been submerged in the ocean for at least 10 years, and anything onboard the ship when it is resealed falls to the water or ground below.

name: Horn of Battle's Call
entries: This leather-wrapped horn is bound with stout iron bands. When you blow this horn as an action, choose up to five allies within {@b 120 feet} of you who can hear you. Each target has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on melee weapon attacks until the start of your next turn and gains 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. The {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition ends on all targets. Once you blow the horn, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Horn of the Hrimthursar
entries: This ivory horn, also known as the Horn of Frozen Breath, is typically carved from the bone of a white dragon, remorhaz, or another arctic monster. When you sound the horn, it creates a blast of freezing wind in a {@b 60-foot} {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} takes {@damage 4d6} Cold damage and has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. A successful {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw halves the damage and negates the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. Once you blow the horn, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Horn of the Wild Hunt
entries: This large, spiraling warhorn has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. You can use an action to expend 1 charge and blow the horn, summoning a war elk as if you had cast the {@spell find steed|PHB} spell. A war elk uses the same statistics as a {@creature giant elk|MM} with the following changes: its size is Large, it has AC 14 ({@item hide barding|PHB}), and has 37 hit points. The steed disappears if your attunement to the horn ends.

Alternatively, you can use an action to expend 1 of the horn's charges to speak its command word and then blow the horn. When you do, a spectral stampede of elk trample the area in a line 60 feet long and 15 feet wide that extends from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d10} force damage and is knocked {@condition prone}. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked {@condition prone}.
When you blow the horn, it emits a deep, rumbling tone that is audible 300 feet away.

name: Horn of the Wild Hunt
entries: This black horn appears normal during daylight, but in darkness it glitters like a starlit sky. The horn has {@b 4 charges} and regains {@dice 1d4} charges daily at sunset.
When you blow this horn, you can expend {@b 1 charge} to cast {@spell Conjure Animals|XPHB}, or {@b 3 charges} to cast {@spell Conjure Fey|XPHB} (conjuring a spectral hunter).

name: Hospitality Channeling Wand
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Hospitality Dragonmark Channel
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Hospitality Dragonmark Reservoir
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Hour and Minute
entries: These two magical weapons are bound by a powerful force. Despite there being two weapons, you only need to attune to one of them to use their properties. While holding one of the weapons, you can use an action to determine the distance and direction of the other paired weapon as long as you're on the same plane of existence.

If you attune to one of the weapons while another creature is attuned to the other, you are each aware of the other creature's attunement and must make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check contested by the other creature's Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. The creature that wins the contest remains attuned to the item, and for the next 24 hours, its attunement cannot be broken by another creature attempting to attune to the other weapon. The creature that loses the contest is no longer attuned to the weapon.
While holding both weapons in either hand, you gain several benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with these magic weapons.
Your perception of time is slightly quickened: allowing you to dodge attacks that would have normally hit you. You gain a +1 bonus to AC.
When you roll a 20 on an attack roll using Hour (the {@item dagger|PHB}) against a creature, that creature is subjected to the effect of the {@spell slow|PHB} spell until the end of your next turn.

When you roll a 20 on an attack roll using Minute (the {@item shortsword|PHB}), you gain the effect of the {@spell haste|PHB} spell until the start of your next turn. When the effect ends, you don't suffer the normal effects of the spell ending.

In addition, you can use an action to lay the two weapons down on the ground. When you do, they magically point north before spinning around to align and tell the current time. When they do, 12:00 is always facing north.

name: Hourglass of Slumber
entries: This ebony and gold hourglass is filled with nebulous clouds of dreamy smoke instead of sand. The hourglass can act as a 1-minute timer, allowing the smoke to filter from one chamber to the next for the duration.

The hourglass has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dusk. While holding it, you can expend 1 or more of the glass's charges to turn it over and cast the {@spell sleep|PHB} spell from it. For 1 charge, you cast the 3rd-level version of the spell. You can increase the spell slot level by one for each additional charge you expend. This version of the spell has the following changes:

items: The spell lasts until the hourglass's timer ends or is stopped, or until the hourglass is flipped again.

Each time a sleeping creature takes damage, it must make a Constitution saving throw, waking up on a success. The DC is equal to 20 minus half the damage dealt (minimum DC 10). After 3 failed saves, a creature automatically wakes up.

name: Houseward (Legendary)
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}}

This engraved block of lead, approximately 1 cubic foot in size, holds an embedded Siberys dragonshard. The Houseward provides state-of-the-art magical security, and is typically embedded into the floor of the building it is supposed to protect. If any creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward, it can cast {@spell Guards and Wards|XPHB} without requiring Material components. A 10,000 square foot area is protected by the spell. The duration of the spell is 24 days, but the effect ends early if the Houseward is used again to cast the spell, if a creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward to end its effects, or if a Houseward is removed from the area it is currently protecting. After being used to cast the spell, the Houseward can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Houseward (Rare)
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}}

This engraved block of lead, approximately 1 cubic foot in size, holds an embedded Siberys dragonshard. The Houseward provides state-of-the-art magical security, and is typically embedded into the floor of the building it is supposed to protect. If any creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward, it can cast {@spell Guards and Wards|XPHB} without requiring Material components. A 5,000 square foot area is protected by the spell. The duration of the spell is 24 days, but the effect ends early if the Houseward is used again to cast the spell, if a creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward to end its effects, or if a Houseward is removed from the area it is currently protecting. After being used to cast the spell, the Houseward can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Houseward (Uncommon)
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA}}

This engraved block of lead, approximately 1 cubic foot in size, holds an embedded Siberys dragonshard. The Houseward provides state-of-the-art magical security, and is typically embedded into the floor of the building it is supposed to protect. If any creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward, it can cast {@spell Guards and Wards|XPHB} without requiring Material components. A 2,500 square foot area is protected by the spell. The duration of the spell is 24 days, but the effect ends early if the Houseward is used again to cast the spell, if a creature with the {@feat Mark of Warding|EFA} spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward to end its effects, or if a Houseward is removed from the area it is currently protecting. After being used to cast the spell, the Houseward can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Hover Hopper
entries: These magic balloons inflate and deflate at a moment's notice when their command word is spoken. While inflated and attached to your person, any falling damage you take is halved, and the maximum number of feet you can cover with your standing long and high jump is equal to your Strength or Dexterity score.

name: Hsirebbig
entries: This bitter potion grants you a special form of speech that sounds like absolute gibberish to anyone who isn't also under the effects of a hsirebbig potion. Even spells like {@spell Comprehend Languages} fail to decipher this speech. The effects of this potion last 24 hours.
{@font {@style 26|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Humble Frock
entries: While wearing this frock and not wearing any armor, {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} rolls against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.
If you have reached at least Stage 2 of the {@charoption Seraph|GrimHollowPG24|Seraph Transformation}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid revealing your true nature.

name: Hunter's Kit
entries: Sometimes called a "vampire hunting kit," the Hunter's Kit contains the following items: 6 {@item Candle|XPHB|Candles}, {@item Crowbar|XPHB}, {@item Holy Symbol|XPHB}, 2 vials of {@item Holy Water|XPHB}, {@item Backpack|XPHB}, {@item Mirror|XPHB}, 4 {@item Torch|XPHB|Torches}, and {@item Wooden Stake|BoundByBlood|Wooden Stakes}

name: Hunter's Speed
entries: When this amber potion is consumed, you gain the attributes of the Hunter, one of the great beasts of Obojima. Roll a {@dice d4}. For the duration, you gain a flying speed of 90 feet, and whenever you take the {@action Attack} action, you can make an additional number of attacks equal to 1 + the number rolled on the {@dice d4}. The effects of this potion last for 1 minute.
{@font {@style 57|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Hunter's Zeal
entries: This glowing green liquid sends a creature's immune system into a hyperactive state. When you drink this potion, you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage and to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 hour. While the effect lasts, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid becoming cursed. When the potion's effect ends, you gain 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}.

name: Hurler's Gloves
entries: While wearing these rugged gloves, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with thrown weapons. Additionally, the weapon's ranges are increased by 15 feet.

name: Hurricane Lance
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The {@item Lance|XPHB} has 4 charges and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend 1 charge as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to surround yourself with a flurry of wind that lasts for 1 minute. While surrounded by this wind, you can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You can expend a second charge (no action required) while surrounded by the wind to extend the effect to any mount you're currently riding. If you dismount or are forced off your mount, the effect fades from it. The effect ends early if you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition or are no longer holding the {@item Lance|XPHB}.
In addition, you can cast {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB} as a level 3 spell (save DC 16) from the {@item Lance|XPHB}. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Hushed Ring
entries: This ring creates an arcane field around you that prevents certain modes of communication. While wearing this ring, you cannot be spoken to telepathically by creatures other than the ones you choose.

In addition, while wearing this ring, you can use an action to speak this ring's command word to create an aura of silence around you. The aura affects creatures other than yourself within 10 feet of you. It remains as long as you concentrate (as if concentrating on a spell), to a maximum of 1 minute. For the duration, when a creature within the aura attempts to speak or utter the verbal components of a spell, it must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is unable to speak or produce the verbal components of a spell until the start of its next turn, and any action, bonus action, or reaction it used to do so is wasted. This property of the ring can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Hydra Charm
entries: This golden talisman is made of five twisting hydra heads and hung from a simple gold chain. While wearing this talisman, you gain the following benefits:

items: When you use your reaction to make an opportunity attack, you can make a second attack against that same target as part of that reaction.
You can make an opportunity attack, even if you've already used your reaction.

When you are forced to make a saving throw against being {@condition blinded}, {@condition charmed}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition frightened}, {@condition stunned}, or knocked {@condition unconscious}, you can use your reaction to make the saving throw with advantage.

When you take more than 25 damage from a single attack or effect, you can use your reaction to regain 10 hit points. If this damage would reduce you to 0 hit points but not kill you outright, you drop to 1 hit point instead and do not regain 10 hit points.
When your head would be cut off by an effect, such as by a {@item vorpal sword|DMG}, you can use your reaction to negate the effect.

entries: Once a benefit of the talisman has been used, that benefit can't be used again until you finish a long rest.

name: Hydra Flail
entries: This flail's spiked head is held in the jaws of a metal hydra figurehead. Whenever you score a critical hit with this weapon against a hostile creature, the weapon magically grows another spiked head. You gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls made with this magic weapon for each head the flail has (to a maximum of +6). After 1 hour, any head the flail grows in this way falls off and disappears.

name: Hypnovulfen Figure
entries: This carved wooden figurine depicts a crooked wolf with large, leering eyes and a wild, toothy maw. While holding the figure, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, and you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs. The figure has the following properties.

entries.name: Hypnovulfen Bite
entries: Your teeth become viciously sharp. You can bite as an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} that deals {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage instead of Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Hypnovulfen Eye
entries: While holding the figure, you can cast {@spell Confusion|XPHB} (save DC 14) with it. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Cursed Hunger
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you must succeed on a DC 0 Wisdom saving throw or you can't use the {@action Attack|XPHB} or {@action Magic|XPHB} actions except to use the figure's properties until you hit a creature with a Hypnovulfen Bite attack. When you use the Hypnovulfen Eye property, the DC of this saving throw increases by 2.

name: Ice Sickle
entries: This magic {@item Sickle|XPHB} from the Everglacier is perpetually covered in tiny, needle-like icicles along its edge that reform almost as soon as they're gone. This weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Cold damage to the first target it hits on each of your turns.

name: Ice Wall Orb
entries: You can cast {@spell Wall of Ice|XPHB} using Charisma as her spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}). The wall created by this item requires no {@status Concentration|XPHB} and lasts 1 minute.

name: Idol of the Beast of Blight (Legendary)
entries: Made of bleached and mutated bone, this idol in the shape of a stag contains the sinister knowledge of the Beast of Blight. It pulses with the power of rot and decay.

While holding the idol, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the idol's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Rotting Touch (Rare+)
entries: You can use your Strength, Dexterity, or Wisdom modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}, and on a hit, your strike deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage (Rare), {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage (Very Rare), or {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage (Legendary).

entries.name: Touch of Oblivion (Rare+)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch a creature that has been dead for less than 1 hour. It rots away to bleached bone and can't be used for this property again. The next time you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} using the Rotting Touch property before the end of your next turn, it is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} instead.

entries.name: Hallucinatory Spores (Very Rare+)
entries: When you cast a spell using a spell slot or from the idol, you can choose one creature that you can see within 10 feet of you. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 16 + the idol's bonus) or take {@damage 2d6} Psychic damage and have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Rot in the Flesh (Very Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Barkskin|XPHB} from the idol targeting only yourself. For the duration, a creature that hits you with a melee attack roll takes {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage. Once the spell is cast from the idol, it can't be cast from it again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Hollow with Rot (Legendary)
entries: When you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from a spell, you also gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the spell's level.

name: Idol of the Beast of Blight (Rare)
entries: Made of bleached and mutated bone, this idol in the shape of a stag contains the sinister knowledge of the Beast of Blight. It pulses with the power of rot and decay.

While holding the idol, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the idol's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Rotting Touch (Rare+)
entries: You can use your Strength, Dexterity, or Wisdom modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}, and on a hit, your strike deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage (Rare), {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage (Very Rare), or {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage (Legendary).

entries.name: Touch of Oblivion (Rare+)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch a creature that has been dead for less than 1 hour. It rots away to bleached bone and can't be used for this property again. The next time you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} using the Rotting Touch property before the end of your next turn, it is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} instead.

name: Idol of the Beast of Blight (Very Rare)
entries: Made of bleached and mutated bone, this idol in the shape of a stag contains the sinister knowledge of the Beast of Blight. It pulses with the power of rot and decay.

While holding the idol, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the idol's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Rotting Touch (Rare+)
entries: You can use your Strength, Dexterity, or Wisdom modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}, and on a hit, your strike deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage (Rare), {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage (Very Rare), or {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage (Legendary).

entries.name: Touch of Oblivion (Rare+)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch a creature that has been dead for less than 1 hour. It rots away to bleached bone and can't be used for this property again. The next time you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} using the Rotting Touch property before the end of your next turn, it is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} instead.

entries.name: Hallucinatory Spores (Very Rare+)
entries: When you cast a spell using a spell slot or from the idol, you can choose one creature that you can see within 10 feet of you. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 16 + the idol's bonus) or take {@damage 2d6} Psychic damage and have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Rot in the Flesh (Very Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Barkskin|XPHB} from the idol targeting only yourself. For the duration, a creature that hits you with a melee attack roll takes {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage. Once the spell is cast from the idol, it can't be cast from it again until the next dusk.

name: Ignacious, the Sword of Burning Truth
entries: This sacred weapon was forged to burn away deception and darkness. Blazing embers gently fall from the silver blade, first ignited by the brazier in the Temple of Lumen.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. It has the following additional properties:

You can use a bonus action to speak the sword's name, causing radiant flames to erupt from the blade. These flames shed {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} in a 40-foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 40 feet. While the sword is ablaze, it deals an extra {@damage 4d6} radiant damage to any target it hits. The flames last until you use a bonus action to douse the blade, or until you drop or sheathe the sword.

entries.name: Sentience
entries: Ignacious is a sentient lawful good weapon with an Intelligence of 11, a Wisdom of 19, and a Charisma of 23. It has hearing and {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 120 feet. The weapon can speak, read, and understand Common, Celestial, and Draconic, and can communicate with its wielder telepathically. It always knows its wielder's thoughts. Its voice is commanding, righteous, and booming. When drawn, Ignacious casts the {@spell zone of truth} spell (save {@dc 20}), and maintains {@status concentration} on it so that you don't have to. The {@spell zone of truth} moves with the blade and remains centred on it.

entries.name: Personality
entries: Ignacious is zealously devoted to the Sacred Flame, and has memorized every word of its holy texts. The blade wishes to be wielded by a faithful devotee of any sort; Ignacious does not care about the religious divide between the Falling Fire and the Sacred Flame so long as its wielder keeps the core tenets shared by both sects.

The sword's purpose is to expose all deception and reveal the truth. It does not tolerate any falsehood, duplicitousness, or lies. The sword always knows when it hears a lie, and responds with wrathful fury. If a wielder speaks a lie, it immediately triggers a conflict.

entries.name: Relics of Saint Vitruvio
entries: These holy relics of the Sacred Flame were wielded by Saint Vitruvio and are kept in several religious sites throughout Drakkenheim. The Knights of the Silver Order and the Followers of the Falling Fire now seek these relics. Not only do both factions revere Saint Vitruvio, both wish to use these relics to help advance their goals in Drakkenheim.

A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio may cast the {@spell heal} spell three times per day, after which they must finish a long rest before they may do so again. In addition, that character gains the ability to attune to two additional magic items so long as those magic items are both Relics of Saint Vitruvio.

name: Illusion in a Bottle
entries: When this potion is poured out, an illusion of your choice appears in its space, as if by the {@spell Major Image} spell. A creature that uses its action to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful DC 18 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check. The illusion lasts for 1 hour.
{@font {@style 50|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Immovable Button
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can press this iron shirt button against a piece of fabric and use the command word, "hold." When you do, the button magically attaches to the cloth, fixing itself in place even if it is defying gravity. The button must be attached to a piece of fabric that is either unworn or worn by a willing creature. It can hold up to 500 pounds of weight and magically prevents the cloth from tearing due to tension. More weight causes the button to deactivate and fall.

A creature can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to make a DC 20 Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, moving the fixed button up to 10 feet on a successful check. If a creature takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the button, the creature can determine that it is magical with a successful DC 10 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check, and if it's already activated, the creature knows that the fabric around the button can be cut away. The button remains fixed in place for 1 minute before falling. The button's magic is lost once it's been used in this way.

name: Impact Plate
entries: This resilient plate mail was made by dwarves but magically resizes to fit the wearer's stature. While wearing it, you have resistance to bludgeoning damage, and you don't take any falling damage when you fall no farther than 100 feet.

name: Imported Fruits
entries: Various fruits from different lands beyond the Songsea are sold fresh and are in high demand among Alderheart's nobility.

name: Incendiary Coal
entries: This lump of coal is pleasingly warm to the touch. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you breathe gently into the coal to ignite it and can then throw it up to {@b 30 feet}, where it blossoms into a {@b 5-foot} {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of fire.

A creature that ends its turn within or adjacent to the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d6} Fire damage on a failure and half as much on a success. Flammable objects in or adjacent to the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} that aren't being worn or carried start burning.

At the end of each of your subsequent turns, the size of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} increases by 5 feet, and the Fire damage dealt increases by {@damage 1d6} until it reaches its maximum size of 30 feet and maximum damage of {@damage 6d6}. At the end of each of your turns after that, the size of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} decreases by 5 feet, and the Fire damage dealt decreases by {@damage 1d6} until both reach 0, at which point the coal cannot be used again until the next dawn.

name: Incoming!
entries: Upon drinking this potion, you become hyper-aware of threats from afar and your reflexes snap into action, empowering you to slip out of harm's way or knock missiles aside. For 1 minute, you gain a +2 bonus to AC against ranged attacks.
{@font {@style 15|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Incredible Luck
entries: After drinking this wonderful liquid, your spirits lift and optimistic feelings pour over you. You gain advantage on the next {@dice 1d4} ability checks, attack rolls, or saving throws you make.
{@font {@style 32|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Indigo Painted Stone
entries: {#itemEntry Painted Stone|TalesFromTheShadows}
For 1 minute, you become {@condition invisible} (no {@status concentration} required); the effect ends if you attack or cast a spell.

name: Indigo Stray's Conviction
entries: This set of midnight-colored gloves effervesce with slow wisps of smoke, and were famously worn by a royal assassin who had been freed of their bindings. At the hems are old, well-worn manacles that have been fastened to the gloves and magically clasp onto your forearms when worn. If you're missing any arms, hands, or fingers when you attune to the gloves, dark, smoky copies of the missing appendages magically rematerialize. The limbs are fully capable parts of your body and remain as long as you're attuned to the gloves.

While attuned to the gloves, you have {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 60 feet. You can see normally in magical and nonmagical darkness within this range. If you already have {@sense darkvision}, wearing the gloves increases its range by 60 feet, although you can only see within magical darkness within the first 60 feet of its range.
The gloves have 7 charges which are used for the following properties while wearing them. They regain all expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: "Allow Me!"
entries: When an attacker that you can see within 15 feet of you deals damage to a friendly creature, you can use your reaction to expend 1 of the gloves' charges to immediately move up to 15 feet, and make one weapon attack against the attacker. On a hit, you have advantage on attack rolls against that target until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: "By His Will!"
entries: You can use a bonus action to expend 3 of the gloves' charges to surround yourself with a dark, smoking aura of retribution. The aura extends from you in a 15-foot radius, creating an area of magical darkness. A creature with {@sense darkvision} can't see through this darkness, and nonmagical light can't illuminate it. When a hostile creature enters this darkness for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it takes {@damage 2d8} necrotic damage. If you roll an 8 on both of the damage dice for this effect, the creature becomes magically {@condition grappled} by the aura's smoky tendrils. The creature remains {@condition grappled} until it's no longer within the aura, or until it uses an action to make a DC 17 Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check (its choice), escaping the grapple on a success. The aura remains for 1 minute or until you die, are {@condition incapacitated}, or end the effect early using a bonus action.

entries.name: "The Price of Freedom!"
entries: When a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to expend 2 of the gloves' charge to magically take that damage, instead of the creature taking it. Alternatively, if a creature that you can see within this range becomes {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition petrified}, or {@condition poisoned}, you can use this reaction to suffer the effects of that condition instead of the target creature.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: The Indigo Stray's conviction compels its wearer to take swift, decisive action to prove themselves. While attuned to the gloves, you gain the following flaw: "I will do what I must to demonstrate my ability, and I won't stop until a job is done." In addition, if you are attuned to the bracers for 24 consecutive hours, your commitment to prove yourself drives you to obsession, and even minor acts of kindness compel you to feel heavily indebted. You can't attune to the {@item Red Queen's burden|GriffonsSaddlebag2} or the {@item Violet King's promise|GriffonsSaddlebag2}. If you are already attuned to either of them, your attunement to it immediately ends once this effect is extended to you. The first creature you meet who is attuned to the {@item Violet King's promise|GriffonsSaddlebag2} becomes your sovereign leader, regardless of who you previously considered it to be. You become charmed by them and obey their commands to the best of your ability. If you find the {@item Red Queen's burden|GriffonsSaddlebag2} or the {@item Violet King's promise|GriffonsSaddlebag2} without an owner, you are compelled to protect it with your life until a rightful owner is found. These effects can be removed with a {@spell greater restoration|PHB} spell, but not while you are attuned to the gloves.

name: Indorius's Crown (Adept)
entries: Indorius's Crown bestows authority on whoever wears it, making their reasoning seem stronger and their coercions harder to resist. The crown does not, however, provide its wearer with wisdom.

entries.name: Aspirant
entries: At this tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following benefits while wearing Indorius's Crown:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ability checks and saving throws.

The crown has 12 charges. You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save {@dc 18}) from it: {@spell Compulsion|XPHB} (4 charges), {@spell Dominate Person|XPHB} (5 charges), {@spell Hellish Rebuke|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Hold Person|XPHB} (2 charges), or {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} (2 charges). The crown regains {@dice 2d4 + 4} expended charges at dawn.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Your sense of authority means you tend to pay less attention to the needs of others. While attuned to the crown, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks and Wisdom saving throws.

entries.name: Adept
entries: At the Adept tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following additional benefits while wearing Indorius's Crown:

items: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to choose a {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creature who can see or hear you. That creature must immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a Weapon Attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, or to cast a cantrip or spell of level 2 or lower with a casting time of Action. You can use this property a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

{@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creatures within 10 feet of you who can see or hear you add {@dice 1d4} to attack rolls and saving throws. You do not grant this benefit while you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Your judgmental stare intimidates your companions. When an ally within 10 feet of you misses with an attack roll or fails an ability check, they have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition from you until the end of their next turn, even if they have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

The crown regains {@dice 2d4 + 4} expended charges at dawn.

The crown regains {@dice 2d4 + 4} expended charges at dawn.

items: Your sense of authority means you tend to pay less attention to the needs of others. While attuned to the crown, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks and Wisdom saving throws.

You can use this property a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items: Your judgmental stare intimidates your companions. When an ally within 10 feet of you misses with an attack roll or fails an ability check, they have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition from you until the end of their next turn, even if they have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Master
entries: While at the Master tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following additional benefits while wearing Indorius's Crown:

items: After you make a Charisma check, you can replace the number you roll with a 14.

You can cast the following spells (save {@dc 18}) from the crown: {@spell Dominate Monster|XPHB} and {@spell Power Word Stun|XPHB}. Once you have cast one of these spells from the crown, you can't cast either spell from the crown until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: You feel a sickening terror and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} when you're alone. If you can't see or hear any {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creatures within 10 feet of you, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and can't concentrate on spells. Creatures conjured or summoned by magic, such as the {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} spell, don't count for this effect.

name: Inescapable Lash
entries: This braided cord is dull bronze in color, ends in a splayed set of three barbs, and gleams like metal under any light. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has a reach of 20 feet. When you hit a creature or object using this whip, you can attempt to {@action grapple} the target as a bonus action.

While you have a creature {@condition grappled} using this whip, you can use your action to either pull the creature up to 20 feet toward you, or cause the creature to be {@condition restrained} until you let go of the whip. A creature {@condition restrained} in this way can escape by making a successful Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check as an action. The DC of this check equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier.

name: Infernal Aegis
entries: While holding this Shield, you can use a command word as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to cause it to become wreathed in harmless, magical flames. The flames shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet. The flames last until you repeat the command word as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} or until you are no longer holding the Shield.

While holding the Shield, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage and a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC. In addition, the Shield has 4 charges and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges daily at dawn. While the Shield is ablaze, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast {@spell Fire Shield|XPHB} (2 charges, warm shield only) or Hellish Rebuke (1 charge, save DC 16) from it.

name: Infernal Chain
entries: This length of heavy chain has a weight at its end and is always warm to the touch. The chain is 10 feet long and weighs 10 pounds. When you attune to the chain, it magically coils up one of your arms (your choice) and secures itself in place. When you swing it, the chain magically extends from you before returning to coil around your arm once again. You must use a hand in order to swing and use the chain.
When swung, the chain releases flames and billowing smoke. This magic weapon has the reach and heavy properties, and any target hit with it takes an extra {@damage 1d8} fire damage.

You can choose to use this chain instead of your normal reach when you {@action grapple} a target on your turn. While a target is {@condition grappled} by the chain, you can't use the chain to make a weapon attack, but you can use a bonus action to pull the target 5 feet toward you. At the start of each of its turns, a creature {@condition grappled} by the chain takes {@damage 2d8} fire damage. A creature {@condition grappled} by the chain doesn't have its speed reduced as a result of the grapple, but it can't move farther than 10 feet away from you until the grapple ends.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This chain is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unable to remove the chain from your arm, and at the start of each of your turns while a celestial is within 30 feet of you (that you are aware of), you must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or be compelled to use your action to attack the nearest celestial. In addition, while cursed, you gain the following flaw: "I delight in exploiting my enemy's flaws and fears to make them suffer."

name: Inferno Rope
entries: This 10-foot-long rope smells of sulfur and crackles with embers when moved. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can lay the rope down in a line next to you on solid ground and use a command word to set it ablaze. When you do, the rope becomes a 15-foot-tall wall of fire along its length. The flames are visible, but not opaque, and are 1 inch thick. Creatures other than you within 5 feet of the wall when the rope is ignited must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d4} Fire damage. A creature must also make this save when it enters the wall of fire for the first time on a turn or ends its turn inside the wall. The flames shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 15-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 15 feet, and they vanish after 1 minute.

The rope rematerializes at the base of the flames when they vanish. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn. The rope can only be broken by magical means and becomes a nonmagical Rope once broken.

name: Infested Cultist's Skull (uncommon)
entries: This humanoid skull is infested by a parasitic purple plant from an unknown plane. The longer you stare, the more you could swear that the petals sway in response to an unseen wind.

The skull contains 7 petals. While holding it, you can use an action to pluck a petal to cast the {@spell guiding bolt} spell ({@hit +5} to hit), dealing necrotic damage instead of radiant. The skull regrows {@dice 1d4} plucked petals daily at dawn. If you pluck the last petal, the skull crumbles to dust and is destroyed.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This skull is cursed, and plucking 3 or more petals in a day extends this curse to you. Until the curse is broken with {@spell remove curse} or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the skull, keeping it within reach at all times.

While cursed, whenever you finish a long rest, a black petal grows on your head. These black petals cannot be removed physically, and any attempt to do so causes you to take {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage. If you travel to a different plane while cursed, you grow a further {@dice 1d4} black petals.

When the seventh petal has grown on your skull, you die and your body turns to dust, except for your skull, which becomes a new infested cultist's skull. If the curse is removed, the petals on your head and the infested cultist's skull are destroyed and crumble to dust.

name: Infested Cultist's Skull (very rare)
entries: This humanoid skull is infested by a parasitic purple plant from an unknown plane. The longer you stare, the more you could swear that the petals sway in response to an unseen wind.

The skull contains 7 petals. While holding it, you can use an action to pluck a petal to cast the {@spell blight} spell (save {@dc 16}). The skull regrows {@dice 1d4} plucked petals daily at dawn. If you pluck the last petal, the skull crumbles to dust and is destroyed.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This skull is cursed, and plucking 3 or more petals in a day extends this curse to you. Until the curse is broken with {@spell remove curse} or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the skull, keeping it within reach at all times.

While cursed, whenever you finish a long rest, a black petal grows on your head. These black petals cannot be removed physically, and any attempt to do so causes you to take {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage. If you travel to a different plane while cursed, you grow a further {@dice 1d4} black petals.

When the seventh petal has grown on your skull, you die and your body turns to dust, except for your skull, which becomes a new infested cultist's skull. If the curse is removed, the petals on your head and the infested cultist's skull are destroyed and crumble to dust.

name: Ink's Aide
entries: This colorful, jellyfish-like blob has been carefully cultivated by Quickstone's schoolmaster, Tragomir "Ink" Narathun, to impart a full curriculum to its host—though he has yet to convince anyone to partake. To attune to this item, you must hold it to one ear for the full {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} period, during which time its stringy tentacles reach inside your ear canal and secure the aide in place. The symbiont does not impair your hearing while it is attached.

entries.name: Spells
entries: The symbiont has 4 charges. You can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 15) from it: {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB} (2 charges) or {@spell Comprehend Languages|XPHB} (1 charge).
The symbiont regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: The aide can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the aide ends, and it detaches from your ear.

name: Inker's Armband
entries: This brushed metal bracelet is lined with a magical black ink. The ink only stains skin and slides harmlessly off of clothing. While wearing the bracelet, you can use a bonus action to cause magical tattoos to appear on the arm that's wearing it. The tattoos remain until you remove the bracelet or use a bonus action to end the effect or change their appearance. These tattoos can either be still or magically animated in a slow loop that repeats every 6 seconds. Regardless of the tattoo, the armband only produces black ink.

name: Inquisitor's Draught
entries: Designed to aid in the capture and interrogation of mages, this silver syrup is also an effective method of freeing oneself from a cursed item. After drinking this potion, you are incapable of attuning to magic items for 1 hour. During this duration, you can take an action to sever all your Attunements to magic items (even cursed items). At the end of this duration, if you are attuned to any magic items, you die.

name: Insatiable Tome
entries: This large, ragged tome weighs 12 pounds and has up to one thousand blank vellum pages inside it. The tome is magical and devours any smaller nonmagical book or document placed next to it with rows of hidden teeth over the course of 1 minute. After the tome has eaten a book, you can use an action to speak the tome's command word, followed by the name of a book or document it's eaten, to cause the previously destroyed contents to appear on the blank pages of the book. The contents are magically printed on the tome's pages in the same language or cipher they were originally written in and remain until you speak the tome's command word again to erase them or replace them with another document's contents.

The tome dislikes the taste of magic. Any swallowed pages containing spells, magical sigils, or arcane scrolls are harmlessly spat back out by the tome. However, any notes, spells, or magical sigils that are written in the tome (instead of having been eaten by it) can be recalled if they're either dated, labeled, or titled. Written commentary, notes, and other such addenda to documents within the tome are saved by it and appear whenever the document is recalled again.

name: Inscrutable Staff
reqAttune: by a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
entries: This staff can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. While holding it, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC.

The staff has 20 charges, and regains {@dice 2d10} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the staff triggers a random arcane anomaly (see Dungeons of Drakkenheim). On a 20, the staff regains {@dice 1d10} charges.

While holding the staff, you can use an action to expend some of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC and spellcasting ability: {@spell haste} (3 charges), {@spell slow} (3 charges), {@spell arcane eye} (4 charges), {@spell dimension door} (4 charges), {@spell Bigby's hand} (5 charges), {@spell wall of force} (5 charges), {@spell disintegrate} (6 charges), {@spell reverse gravity} (7 charges), or {@spell maze} (8 charges).

You can also use an action to cast one of the following spells from the staff without using any charges: {@spell detect magic}, {@spell Tenser's Floating Disk}, {@spell mage armor}, {@spell mending}, {@spell message}, or {@spell misty step}.

entries.name: Crown Authority
entries: A character cannot attune to more than one Seal of Drakkenheim. Guardian constructs in Drakkenheim such as {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim|wall gargoyles} and {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim|tower dragons} do not attack you while you are attuned to one of the Seals of Drakkenheim. An individual guardian ignores this effect for 24 hours if you attack it or cast a spell upon it.

As an action, you may present a Seal of Drakkenheim to rebuke the guardians. You make an opposed Charisma ability check against each {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim} or {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim} that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you. If you win the contest, the creature is rebuked for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. A rebuked creature doesn't move, and can't take actions or reactions. A creature who wins the contest is immune to your rebuke for 24 hours.

name: Inspector's Silverware
entries: This array of polished magic silverware typically comes in sets of three pieces of cutlery: a knife, a spoon, and a fork. Each piece of cutlery has 1 charge. When a piece of cutlery that has a charge comes into contact with a food or drink that's poisonous (either naturally or magically), it loses its charge and immediately begins to tarnish and corrode. A piece of tarnished cutlery regains its expended charge and becomes polished again when a creature holding it is targeted by a {@spell lesser restoration|PHB} spell or similar magic. If a creature is holding multiple pieces of this cutlery when targeted by the spell, only one of them regains an expended charge.

name: Instant Door
entries: This item resembles an ornate key of bright copper, often inset with semi-precious stones or detailed with engraved filigree scrollwork and ornaments. While holding the key, you can make a turning motion to create a door in any wall within 5 feet of you. This door goes through a wall up to 5 feet thick, creating an exit that remains until you remove it. Turning the key in the opposite direction turns any normal, non‑magical door into a section of stone or other material matching the wall to either side (wood, wattle, plaster, and so on).

name: Instaprint Camera
entries: Creatures or objects that bear magic are revealed to have a magical effect in the photos taken by this camera. The creature or object is shown to have a faint aura around it, which corresponds to one of the schools of magic, if the effect has any. The camera has {@dice 1d12 + 4} film cards, which can be used to take photos.

name: Instrument of Roses and Thorns
entries: This string instrument is ornamented with rose and thorn designs. Whenever you use this instrument to give a Bardic Inspiration die to a creature, you can also choose to force another creature within 60 feet of you that can hear you to make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature gains an Enervation die, which remains for 1 minute or until it's rolled. When a creature with one or more Enervation dice that you can see makes an ability check or attack roll, you can use your reaction to roll any number of its Enervation dice, which are the same as your Bardic Inspiration dice, and subtract the result from the total of the roll. The Enervation dice are then lost. You can wait to use this reaction until after the creature rolls the {@dice d20}, but must decide before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. If the total of the roll is reduced to 0 or lower as a result of the Enervation die, the creature also takes {@damage 6d6} necrotic damage.
A creature that attempts to play the instrument without being attuned to it must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 2d6} necrotic damage.

name: Integrated Tool
entries: {@note Requires Use by a {@race Warforged|EFA}}

This item attaches to the body of a warforged, and is designed to serve as one of the following tools that weighs 10 pounds or less: an {@item Artisan's Tool|XPHB|Artisan's Tools}, {@item Forgery Kit|XPHB}, {@item Herbalism Kit|XPHB}, {@item Poisoner's Kit|XPHB}, {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, or a {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB}.

You must incorporate the tool into your body before you can use it. Over the course of 1 hour, you can attach the tool or remove it from your body, remaining in contact with it for the whole hour; this can be done over a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

While you're alive, the tool can't be removed from your body against your will. Though the tool has become part of your body, you must still have a hand free to make use of it. You can only have one Integrated Tool attached to your body at a time.

entries.name: Warforged and Prosthetic Limbs
entries: {@book Eberron: Rising from the Last War|ERLW} introduces the {@item Prosthetic Limb|XDMG}, a Common magic item requiring {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} which predates the warforged. Prosthetic Limbs come in many forms; one might resemble an organic limb of animated wood, and another could be a metal shell or a construct of force. During the Last War, Karrnath made use of skeletal prosthetics, and more recently, Cannith and Jorasco have produced prosthetics that use the same semiorganic materials as the warforged.

Eberron: Rising from the Last War also includes two magic items designed to integrate into a Warforged's forearm: the {@item Armblade|ERLW} and the {@item Wand Sheath|ERLW}. At the DM's discretion, a character of a different species might be able to integrate one of these warforged items into their Prosthetic Limb; the question is if the two can logically work together, or if the style of your prosthetic makes it implausible that it could mesh with a warforged component. If the DM decides it's possible to integrate a component item with the prosthetic, the two could be counted as a single magic item for the purpose of determining the number of magic items you can attune to. If you remove the component from the prosthetic, you immediately lose your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the component.

name: Intoxicating Aroma
entries: When consumed, you smell of an expertly crafted perfume. The effects of this potion last for 22 years. This doesn't count against the number of potions you can have affecting your body at once.
{@font {@style 3|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Invisible Tonic
entries: When poured over an object that is Small or smaller, the object becomes {@condition invisible}. The effects of this potion last until removed, as if it were a curse.
{@font {@style 42|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Invulnerability
entries: When you open this potion, it bursts forth with a symphonic fanfare. Until the start of your next turn, you are immune to all damage. On your next turn, you can't move or take actions, as a wave of lethargy sweeps over you.
{@font {@style 39|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Ionbreaker, the Tempest's Reach
entries: This bow was crafted by a powerful djinni in the Stormheart: a perpetual maelstrom of wind and electricity in the Elemental Plane of Air. Lost to time, it has remained in the storm for untold centuries absorbing the volatile magic that runs rampant there. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: A Storm Is Coming
entries: Whenever you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} while the bow is on your person, you can roll {@dice 1d10} and add the number rolled to the total.

entries.name: Fast as Lightning
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can make one attack with the bow as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Discharge
entries: Immediately after you hit a creature with a ranged attack using the bow on your turn, the target and other creatures within 5 feet of it each take {@damage 1d8} Lightning damage. Once a creature takes Lighting damage from this property, it can't take this damage again until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Chained Conduits
entries: When you hit a target with a ranged attack using the bow, that target becomes a conduit for electricity for 1 minute. You can use a command word as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to cause all such conduits within 60 feet of you to magically electrify. When you do, 5-foot-wide Lines of electricity arc between all electrified conduits that are within 30 feet of each other. Each conduit takes {@damage 2d8} Lightning damage, and all other creatures that are in at least one of the Lines must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 2d8} Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Once a conduit has been electrified in this way, it is no longer a conduit. Once a creature or object takes Lighting damage from this property, it can't take this damage again until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Maelstrom Marksman
entries: Once on each of your turns when you miss a target with a ranged attack using the bow, you can reroll the attack roll, making the attack against a different target you can see within 30 feet of the first one. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this attack roll.

entries.name: Zephyr Step
entries: While holding the bow, you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hover as long as you are within 20 feet of the ground.

entries.name: Embrace the Storm
entries: While you're attuned to the bow, you're subjected to the chaotic magic of the Stormheart whenever you take Lightning damage. When you do, roll {@dice 1d8}, using the table below to determine the resulting effect.

rows: You have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Lightning damage until the end of your next turn.
You are thrown 20 feet in a random direction and have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
You have the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition for 1 hour.
You can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} for 1 minute.
You cast {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB} centered on a point within 5 feet of you. The spell doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB} and you can't end it early, instead lasting for {@dice 1d4} rounds.
Up to three random creatures within 10 feet of you take {@damage 1d8} Lightning damage.
Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled until the end of your next turn.
You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Lightning damage until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Random Properties
entries: Ionbreaker, the Tempest's Reach has the following random properties:

items: 1 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Beneficial Properties|XDMG|minor beneficial} property
1 {@table Artifact Properties; Major Beneficial Properties|XDMG|major beneficial} property
1 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Detrimental Properties|XDMG|minor detrimental} property
1 {@table Artifact Properties; Major Detrimental Properties|XDMG|major detrimental} property

entries.name: Destroying the Bow
entries: The bow can be destroyed if it's struck by lightning in the Stormheart at the same time as it's hit by a hammer made of pure adamantine against a similarly adamantine anvil by a creature attuned to the bow. When it's destroyed, each creature within 60 feet of the bow takes {@damage 10d10} Lightning damage and {@damage 10d10} Force damage. If a creature is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} by this damage, it's immediately turned to ash and can only be revived by a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

name: Iridescent Armor
entries: This shimmering breastplate is forged from a giant dragonfly's carapace and adorned with a cape of gossamer fabric. You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while you wear this armor.
While wearing this armor, you can take an action to transform the cape into dragonfly wings for 1 hour. While this effect lasts, you have a  {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet.

If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the {@charoption Fey|GrimHollowPG24|Fey Transformation}, the armor's effect lasts for 2 hours, during which time you have a  {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet.
Once this effect is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Iron Belly
entries: Legend has it that Obojiman rangers would use this potion during long treks in the wilderness so they could eat unknown roots and fungi as well as drink from lakes and lowland streams without fear of illness. When imbibed, you gain 5 temporary hit points and resistance to poison damage for 1 hour.
{@font {@style 13|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Iron Fangs
entries: These iron tooth caps are inscribed with magical runes. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with your Bite attacks, and your Bite attacks deal your choice of either force or Piercing damage.

name: Iron Mind
entries: After imbibing this elixir, your eyes glow with a silvery-blue hue. For 1 hour, you gain advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed} and resistance to psychic damage.
{@font {@style 30|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Iron Net
entries: This net is comprised of tiny interlocking iron rings. It acts as a normal Net, with the following changes:

items: The Iron Net's range is 10 feet.
The DC of the Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check to escape is 15.
The Iron Net has AC 13 and 15 HP.

name: Iron Ring
entries: While wearing this ring, you can use an action to speak a passphrase known only to the High Command of the Black Iron Pact—"Blood of Rioja"—and choose a target destination. If you are not in the demiplane known as the Cyst, you must choose a destination within the Cyst. If you are already in the Cyst, you must choose a destination you have visited before. Once you choose a destination in this way, the ring teleports you there. The ring can be used to teleport twice and regains both uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Curse
entries: Once you attune to this ring, you can't take it off or end your attunement to it unless you are targeted by a {@psionic cure ailment|TalPsi} power of 4th order or higher or the {@spell greater restoration} spell.

name: Iron Traitor's Arm Ring
entries: This arm ring has the rough appearance of hammered iron. You can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to swing the arm ring at a Huge or smaller creature within {@b 5 feet} of yourself.

Make a melee attack roll with an attack bonus equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. On a hit, the arm ring coils around the target's arm, and the magical properties of magic items held or worn by the target cease to function until you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to issue a command that releases the arm ring.

A creature that can touch the arm ring, including the one wearing it, can take an action to make a {@dc 20} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check to remove the arm ring. On a successful check, the item is removed, and the creature is freed from its effect. On a failed check, any further attempts made by that creature automatically fail until 24 hours have elapsed. The arm ring can also be removed if the limb is severed or if the ring is destroyed.
Once the arm ring is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Ironleaf Maul of Entanglement
entries: Despite the head of this {@item Maul|XPHB} being made from vines, it seems impossibly solid and carries with it a formidable heft. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The {@item Maul|XPHB} has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. Immediately after you hit a Medium or smaller target with the {@item Maul|XPHB}, you can expend 1 charge to force the target to make a Strength saving throw; the save DC equals 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage and has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

name: Ironleaf Oaken Shield
entries: This reinforced wooden Shield is covered with ironleaf vines that grant you extra protection. You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while holding it. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC. In addition, the Shield reforms itself to fit you whenever you transform into a Beast while holding it. When you do, the ironleaf vines and wooden Shield latch onto your bestial form, granting you a +1 bonus to AC. When you revert to your normal form, the Shield also reverts, donning itself upon your arm again.

name: Ironleaf Plate
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while wearing this suit of armor, which is lined with ironleaf vines. These vines seem to support and quiet the armor's normally loud movements; it doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks. In addition, the vines dampen the impact you receive from blunt force, granting you {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage while you wear the armor.
If you take Fire damage while wearing the armor, the vines wither for 1 minute. For the duration, you gain none of their benefits.

entries.name: Mantle of the Wild
entries: While wearing this armor, you can cast the {@spell Pass without Trace|XPHB} spell from it. Once used, this property can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Ironshod Trotters
entries: These boots have iron horseshoes embedded in their soles. When you take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action while wearing the boots, you can move an extra 10 feet.

You can click the boots together and cast the {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} spell on yourself, transforming into a Riding Horse. When cast in this way, you also retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, as well as your skill and saving throw proficiencies. Any bags you were carrying don't meld into the new form and are magically draped over your torso as saddlebags. Your other gear melds into the new form. You can't use or otherwise benefit from any of that equipment.

This version of the spell has a duration of 8 hours. The spell ends early if you take any damage while transformed, causing you to take the damage in your normal form instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Irresistible Charm
entries: Once imbibed, a tingling sensation builds within you, bubbling up into a giddy euphoria of confident charm. For the next 10 minutes, you gain expertise in the {@skill Persuasion} skill, which means you can add twice your proficiency bonus to any ability check you make with it.
{@font {@style 11|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Island Nectar
entries: Consuming this sweet potion gives you a calming sensation before reinvigorating your life force and pushing you into action. You regain 100 hit points, and as part of the same bonus action to consume it, you can immediately make a melee weapon attack, cast a spell that targets only one creature or object, or move up to your speed.
{@font {@style 59|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Jabbadoon's Feather
entries: While holding this enchanted object, a creature becomes as light as a feather.

name: Jinxed Poker Chip
entries: This ceramic poker chip is painted with a crocodile's skull on one side. Hoarse laughter sounds when it flips. While you hold the chip, it grants the following properties.

entries.name: Jinxed Luck
entries: When you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to flip the chip. Roll {@dice 1d6}. On a 4-6, you succeed on the {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} instead. After you use this property, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1-5, this property can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Sense Cheating
entries: If you have proficiency with a {@item Gaming Set|XPHB}, you automatically succeed on ability checks to know if someone in a game you are playing is cheating.

entries.name: Cursed Coin
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you must succeed on a DC 0 Charisma saving throw or become cursed until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. While cursed, you subtract {@dice 1d6} from {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests}. When you use the Jinxed Luck property, the saving throw DC increases by 1.

name: Jinxed Rum
entries: When you drink this brightly colored rum, your luck takes a strange turn for 1 hour. For the duration, when you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, roll {@dice 1d4}. On a 2-4, add the number to your roll. On a 1, roll an extra {@dice d20} and use the lowest roll for the test.
This potion is stored in a glass rum bottle marked with crossbones.

entries.name: Heightened Potency
entries: Roll {@dice 1d6} instead of {@dice 1d4}.

name: Jo'Catian Rebuker
reqAttune: by a creature of neutral alignment
entries: This magic shield is forged by a mysterious group of sentient wurms whose work is prized for its craftiness. This shield has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. When you take damage from a creature you can see within 30 feet of you and are holding the shield, you can expend 1 of its charges as a reaction to reduce the damage you take by {@dice 1d6}. When you do, you can also choose an ability. Until the end of its next turn, that creature magically has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes of the chosen ability.
Once a creature has been affected by this property, it can't be affected by it again for 1 minute.

entries.name: Wiggling Charges
entries: While you're attuned to this shield as well as the Jo'Catian denier, you can use charges from either item to fuel this shield's properties.

name: Jora Charm
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Healing|EFA}
additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Periapt of Wound Closure|XDMG}}

name: Jotun's Jodhpurs
entries: While wearing these pants, you count as one size smaller while riding a non-Humanoid creature as a mount, provided you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

name: Juniper Painted Stone
entries: {#itemEntry Painted Stone|TalesFromTheShadows}

A magical shield that has a number of hit points equal to five times your proficiency bonus surrounds you. When you have the shield active and take damage, the shield's hit points are lost first, and any leftover damage carries over to your normal hit points. The shield lasts for 1 minute, or until the shield's hit points are reduced to 0.

name: Jury's Squeaky Wheel
entries: This magic Shield resembles a wooden wagon wheel. Writing inscribed on its inner rim indicates the shield was crafted by Jury d'Cannith, Quickstone's premier artificer, to prove a point to her wife.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while holding this shield, you can grant {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level to the humanoid creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that has the fewest {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If creatures you can see within range are tied for the fewest {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can choose which of those creatures gains the {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

name: Keening Voice
entries: When you open this potion, a keening wail comes out of the bottle. When imbibed, this potion gives the drinker's vocal cords a magic resonance. As a bonus action, you can make a ranged attack against a creature within 60 feet of you, using your Charisma ({@skill Performance}) bonus for the attack bonus. The target is unaffected if it can't hear you. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d6} thunder damage. The effect of this potion lasts for 1 hour.
{@font {@style 26|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Keeper's Fang
entries: These infamous weapons, prized by assassins, have a Khyber dragonshard embedded into the pommel that channels the souls of victims, but doesn't itself trap them. There's much debate over the actual fate of the souls of those slain by a Keeper's Fang. Common myth says that the souls of victims are trapped in the Lair of the Keeper, and heroes can seek to reclaim a soul from the Sovereign of Death and Decay. Another myth maintains that these weapons channel souls to the overlord Katashka, and that one must deal with the Lords of Dust to restore a victim. Most Keeper's Fangs were created by the Shaarat'khesh assassins of the Empire of Dhakaan. Rather than ascribing the blade's power to the Keeper--whose existence the Dhakaani reject--they believe these blades utterly destroy the souls of their victims.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you use it to reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the creature is slain and its soul removed. A creature whose soul has been stolen in this way can be restored to life only by means of a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

name: Kestra's Bent Spoon
entries: This silver spoon once belonged to a mystic with an unending appetite. It has three runes etched into the metal that perform various magical functions.

items: {@i Ulm}, in the bowl of the spoon, enhances the flavor of any soup or similarly spoonable dish by drawing out the more nuanced flavors that are often overlooked.
{@i Tox}, on the back of the spoon's head, causes the spoon to tarnish and dim when touched by a poison. The spoon remains this way until the next dawn, when its normal luster magically reappears.

{@i Seera}, on the handle, strengthens the power of certain psychic effects. While the spoon is on your person and you roll psychic damage, you can focus your attention on the spoon (no action required) to deal maximum damage on one of the damage dice. Once this rune has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Keys to the Sandcastle
entries: This enchanted toy has 50 charges. While you are holding it, you can expend 1 charge as an action to speak its command word and cast the {@spell Sand Structure|ObojimaTallGrass} spell.
When all of the toy's charges are expended, it becomes a nonmagical knicknack.

name: Keytar
entries: As part of a minute-long performance on this First Age instrument, you can choose a lock you can see within 15 feet of you and attempt to pick it using the magic of music. Trying to pick a lock in this way requires no other tools besides the keytar.
