Each {@item Scimitar|XPHB} also has its own elemental effect—either cold or fire—that deals an extra {@dice 1d6} Cold or {@damage 1d6} Fire damage on a hit, respectively. The {@item Greatsword|XPHB} instead deals an extra {@dice 1d6} Cold and {@damage 1d6} Fire damage on a hit.
The weapon can be used to cast the {@spell Fire Shield|XPHB} spell twice, and it regains all expended uses daily at dawn. An attuned creature can't cast the spell in this way more than once each day.

name: Luckleaf
entries: This plant is commonly thought to be a special kind of clover. However, a luckleaf is a separate, magical species that grows in random locations across the Material Plane and has 5 leaves. While a luckleaf is on your person, you can choose to expend any number of its leaves (no action required). When you do so, you gain a +1 bonus or take a –1 penalty to any roll you make for each expended leaf. This bonus or penalty can't change the total result beyond the highest or lowest number possible for the die you rolled. You can wait to use this property until after seeing the total of the roll, but before the GM determines the outcome of it. An expended leaf withers and turns to dust. When the last leaf is expended, the plant becomes a nonmagical stem.

name: Luma Feather Robe
entries: This luxuriant robe is made from the feather of a birdfolk spellcaster. Though it appears to be made of many individual plumes, the robe is actually composed of only a single feather, flawlessly copied over and over again by the magic that created it.
You gain the following benefits from wearing the robe.

items: Your Intelligence or Charisma score becomes 22 (your choice when you first attune to the robe).
You have a +1 bonus to saving throws while you wear this robe.

When a target succeeds on a saving throw against one of your spells, you can use your reaction to force that target to repeat that saving throw. The target must use the new result. You can use this property up to three times each day.

name: Luna Moth Cape
entries: This beautiful elven cape is fashioned after the wings of a luna moth. While wearing the cape, you can move an extra 10 feet when you take the {@action Dash} action.

In addition, while wearing this cape, you can speak its command word as a bonus action when you jump to cause it to unfurl and flap downwards, sending you 10 feet into the air when you reach the height of your jump. This property can't be used again until you land on solid ground.

name: Lunar Elixir
entries: When poured out, this silvery liquid rapidly expands and coats the surrounding area, creating a chalky white sheen across everything it touches. For the next 8 hours, gravity in a 20-foot-radius, 300-foot-high cylinder centered on the potion is like the moon's gravity. The jump distance for all creatures inside the cylinder is tripled, and falling damage taken inside the cylinder is halved.
{@font {@style 40|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Lupine Mask
entries: While wearing this dark ceramic mask, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks relying on hearing and smell, as well as on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) checks made to interact with dogs and doglike beasts, such as foxes, jackals, and wolves.

name: Lustrous Harpy Feather
entries: With the right expertise and rituals, a songbird harpy's magic can be suffused throughout her plumage. While wearing this magical feather, you find that people can be much more agreeable—all they need is a little push. When you make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check, you can choose to have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the check (no action required). Once this property is used, the feather loses its luster and becomes nonmagical.

name: Lycanthropy Antidote
entries: Made with fzeg blood, this silvery potion is dotted with swirling flecks of red. Drinking this liquid removes the curse of lycanthropy.

name: Lycanthropy Antidote
entries: This silvery potion, made with {@creature fzeg|GrimHollowLairsEtharis} blood, is dotted with flecks of red. Drinking this liquid removes the curse of werewolf lycanthropy.

name: Mace of the Priest
entries: This magic mace is carried by priests and is a symbol of their devotion to ridding the world of evil. While holding it, you can use a bonus action to adjust its telescoping haft, changing it from a {@item mace|PHB} to a {@item quarterstaff|PHB}, and vice versa. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The weapon has 4 charges and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 of its charges to cast either {@spell cure wounds|PHB} (3rd-level version) or {@spell dispel magic|PHB} from it, using your spellcasting ability modifier.
Alternatively, you can use an action to speak the weapon's command word to cast the {@spell heal|PHB} spell from it. When you do, the weapon releases a flash of light and is destroyed.

name: Mace of the Pumpkin King
entries: This magic mace is actually an enchanted pumpkin whose stem is used as a handle. Its orange exterior is carved into a frightening visage with a toothy maw and unforgiving eyes. Between dusk and dawn, the pumpkin is lit from within with a magical flame that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. While the flame is lit, targets hit by the mace take an extra {@damage 1d4} fire damage, and when you roll a 20 on an attack roll with the flaming weapon, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} of you until the start of your next turn.

name: Machine Oil
entries: When poured over a machine that is in working condition, this dark black liquid powers up the device, allowing it to function as if it were whelmed by a spirit or activated by the {@spell Jolt|ObojimaTallGrass} spell. The machine stays powered by this potion for 1 minute.
{@font {@style 28|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Mage Eater Scythe
entries: This dark metal scythe bears a fiendish grin along its blade. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While holding the scythe, you have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

When you hit a creature with an attack using this scythe, you can spend 2 or more Hit Dice (maximum 4) to deal extra necrotic damage, in addition to the weapon's damage. The extra damage is {@damage 1d6} for each Hit Die you spend. If the creature has cast a spell since the end of your last turn, the extra damage dice become {@dice d10}s, instead of {@dice d6}s, and that creature loses a total number of spell slot levels equal to the number of Hit Dice you spend. Starting with the highest spell slot level that creature has (up to 4th), subtract each slot level from the total, if possible, before moving on to the next remaining spell slot level.

Alternatively, while holding the scythe, you can use an action to spend 5 Hit Dice to create a magical barrier around yourself. While the barrier exists, you can't be affected or detected by spells of 5th level or lower unless you choose to be, and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have advantage of saving throws against spells and other magical effects. The barrier remains as long as you concentrate (as if concentrating on a spell), to a maximum of 1 minute, or until you drop or stow the scythe.

name: Mage Mashers
entries: These brass knuckles are forged from a dull black ore that sparkles with a prism of colors when held to light. They feel heavier than they look like they should be, especially to creatures capable of casting spells.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a creature that can cast at least one spell, that creature takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Force damage. Additionally when you deal damage to a creature that is {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} using this weapon, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw it makes to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

name: Magebane Bomb
entries: This bubbling liquid is distilled from the remains of a magebane ooze. You can throw the container at an enemy's weapon or armor, or at a spellcaster.

Make a ranged weapon attack. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d6} Acid damage. If the weapon was targeted, that weapon takes a -1 penalty to attacks and damage as well. If armor was targeted, that armor takes a -1 penalty to the {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}. Both effects end after the wielder or wearer completes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
A spellcaster hit with a Magebane Bomb has a -1 penalty to hit with spell attacks, and the DCs of saving throws against spells they cast decrease by 1 for 1 minute.

name: Magebane Poison
entries: This dark, bubbling poison is made from a rakshasa's magic-immune blood and tastes sweet and syrupy, despite its gruesome appearance. Each bottle contains one dose of the poison. A creature that ingests this poison must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} poison damage and is {@condition poisoned} for 1 hour. If the {@condition poisoned} creature is a spellcaster, it takes an additional {@damage 4d6} psychic damage and can't cast cantrips until this poison ends. In addition, a {@condition poisoned} spellcaster can only cast spells of 1st level or higher by using a spell slot at least 4 levels higher than the desired slot level, without the added benefits of using the higher spell slot level. For example, a {@condition poisoned} spellcaster can cast the 2nd-level version of magic missile using a 6th-level spell slot. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much poison and psychic damage and isn't {@condition poisoned}.

name: Magentan Sun-Saw
entries: Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

items: {@item Magentan Sun-Saw (Uncommon)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Magentan Sun-Saw (Very Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}

name: Magentan Sun-Saw (Uncommon)
entries: The typical {@item magentan sun-saw|GriffonsSaddlebag2}, an uncommon item, is a falchion with a curved metal guard that protects your hand. The sword has 7 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

When you hit a target with this magic sword, you can expend 1 of its charges as part of the attack to reach your fingers around the weapon's curved guard and pull it like a trigger. When you do, a line of whirring blades of light springs from the weapon's edge and rips around the length of the sword, rending and tearing into the target to deal an extra {@damage 1d6} radiant damage to it. The light is a vibrant magenta.

name: Magentan Sun-Saw (Very Rare)
entries: The typical {@item magentan sun-saw|GriffonsSaddlebag2}, an uncommon item, is a falchion with a curved metal guard that protects your hand. The sword has 7 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

The following magentan sun-saw is a very rare variant with more powerful properties. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, when you expend 1 of the weapon's charges when you hit with an attack, the light is sunlight (albeit still magenta in color) and deals an extra {@damage 2d6} radiant damage to the target, instead of {@dice 1d6}. If the target has the Sunlight Sensitivity or Sunlight Hypersensitivity trait, such as a drow or vampire, it's considered to be in sunlight until the end of its next turn.

name: Mageplate Cap
entries: This pointed hat is fitted with chain and metal that have been enchanted with Abjuration magic. The cap has 2 charges and regains 1 expended charge daily at dawn. While wearing the cap, you can expend 1 charge to cast the {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB} spell from it, targeting only yourself. When the spell is cast in this way, the magical force appears as platelike armor, and your base AC becomes 15 plus your Dexterity modifier instead of the AC the spell normally provides.

name: Mageplate Ring
entries: This thin iron ring has a helm-like visor at its top. The ring has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing this ring, you can use a bonus action to expend 1 or more charges from it to become magically protected by an illusory set of spectral armor. For 1 charge, your base AC becomes 16 (your Dexterity modifier doesn't affect this number). You can increase this base AC by 1 for each additional charge you expend. The illusory armor lasts for 1 minute and sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet for the duration.

name: Magical Prosthetics
entries: The brutal warfare and vicious monsters prevalent across Etharis leave many with {@variantrule Grievous Wounds|GrimHollowCG24}, including missing limbs and other potentially debilitating injuries. The engineers and crafters of the world have made great strides in helping those people deal with those injuries through {@item Prosthetics|GrimHollowPG24}, which are covered in Chapter 5 of the {@book Grim Hollow Player's Guide|GrimHollowPG24|5}.

Magical versions of Prosthetics can be crafted with properties that mimic existing Wondrous Items or Rings. Typically, these Prosthetics replicate the body part that would wear that item. For example, a Magical Prosthetic leg could replicate the effect of {@item Boots of Elvenkind|XDMG}, while a Magical Prosthetic hand might act as a {@item Ring of Protection|XDMG}.

A Magical Prosthetic has the same rarity as the magic item it mimics. It counts as "wearing" an item of that kind, so if you have a Magical Prosthetic leg that mimics {@item Boots of Elvenkind|XDMG}, you can't wear another pair of magic boots.

name: Magician's Judge
entries: An executioner's blade from the {@book Age of Arcanum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|Age of Arcanum}, this magic {@item greatsword|PHB} is one of many similar weapons once used to execute magic-wielding criminals. Though most commonly found in the lands now known as {@book Wildemount|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Wildemount} and {@book Issylra|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Issylra}, a few such blades have found their way to Tal'Dorei.

If you hit a creature with an attack using this weapon, you can cast the {@spell dispel magic} spell from the sword against the target as part of the attack. Alternatively, you can use an action to cast {@spell dispel magic} from the sword against a target of your choice. If you need to make a check with your spellcasting ability modifier as part of casting the spell, you make this check with a +3 modifier or your own spellcasting ability modifier, whichever is higher.
Once you cast {@spell dispel magic} using this weapon, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Magik Oil
entries: This magik oil can be socketed on any item you don't mind getting oil stains on. The slow drip of oil from its never-closing spout imbues the item to which it is attached with magic, rendering the item much more durable. Metal can't be corroded by acid and wood & clothing cease being flammable. Strong magic, such as that from a 6th-level spell or higher, can overcome this enhanced resilience. If socketed on a weapon, that weapon's damage becomes magical. If socketed on armour, the oil lubricates the joints, removing any disadvantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|PHB}) checks the armour normally imposes.

name: Magma War Pick
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Fire damage on a hit. This weapon has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target that is either made of metal or wearing metal armor using the weapon, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra {@damage 2d8} Fire damage to the target.

name: Magnetite Horn
entries: Fashioned from the harvested horn of a magnetite dragon, this charm can be socketed on a ferrous weapon or on a worn item that contains iron, conferring different benefits to each.

entries.name: Ferrous Weapon
entries: While you hold the socketed weapon, when you are hit by a weapon attack made with a ferrous weapon or ammunition that you can see, you can use your reaction to activate the magnetic properties of the horn. When you do so, the attack's weapon or ammunition is pulled towards your own, giving you a {@b +1 bonus} to your AC against the attack as you attempt to parry it and possibly turning the hit into a miss.

entries.name: Ferrous Worn Item
entries: While you wear the socketed item, when a creature within {@b 5 feet} of you is targeted by a weapon attack made with a ferrous weapon or ammunition, you can use your reaction to activate the magnetic properties of the horn. When you do so, roll a {@dice d20}. On an 11 or higher, you become the target of the attack instead.

name: Magnificent Pocket Vanity
entries: This palm-sized brass device contains enough magical makeup for 3 uses. A creature holding the vanity can use an action to expend 1 of its uses to apply the makeup to itself or another willing creature within reach, at which point the creature's appearance magically changes to one of the following forms, as if by the {@spell disguise self|PHB} spell (save DC 13). This version of the spell can visually alter a creature's height by up to 5 feet, although the creature's size does not change, and you roll on the table below to determine which random appearance the creature assumes:

rows: A hunched-over elderly gnomish woman with graying hair, missing teeth, and wearing a ragged, faded dress.
An intimidating half-orc man with deep green skin, black hair pulled back in a bun, and battle-worn hide armor.
A regal and androgynous elf with a tan complexion and golden hair wearing fine leathers and a shimmering cape of red and silver.
A dust-covered human boy of no more than 13 years with messy blonde hair wearing a flimsy cap and half-torn overalls.
A strikingly red tiefling woman with white hair wearing silver plate armor and wielding a polished longsword.
A bald, dwarven man with a peg leg and scarcovered face wearing the garb of a well-traveled sailor.

entries: When the last use of the makeup has been used, the vanity and its makeup become nonmagical.

name: Making Channeling Wand
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Making|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Making|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Making Dragonmark Channel
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Making|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Making|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Making Dragonmark Reservoir
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Making|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Making|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Malleus Macabre
entries: This weapon is a blunt but jagged-edged bludgeon that is the object form of a kokela. You gain a +4 bonus to damage rolls made with this weapon, and attack rolls made with this weapon score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20. If you have abilities that increase your critical range with melee attack rolls, this weapon scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 17-20.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This weapon is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you spend one year at least a mile away from the weapon. While you remain cursed, you're unwilling to part with the club, always keeping it within reach. You also have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls with weapons other than this one, unless no foe is within 60 feet of you that you can see or hear.
Whenever you roll a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} with this weapon, after dealing damage there is a 25% chance the Malleus Macabre casts {@spell Cloudkill|XPHB} at level 9 centered on you.

name: Mammoth Boots
entries: These magic boots are as sturdy as the feet of a mammoth. While wearing the boots, your weight increases by 50 pounds (although you don't feel any different), and {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} composed of ice or snow doesn't cost you extra movement. In addition, whenever you're pushed, pulled, or otherwise moved against your will, the distance you would be moved is reduced by 5 feet.

name: Mandible Bident
entries: This chitinous, two-pronged weapon still shudders with predatory instinct, magically biting down on creatures it hits. Once on each of your turns when you hit a Medium or smaller creature with this magic bident with a melee attack, you can force that creature to make a DC 13 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice). On a failed save, the creature is {@condition grappled} by you and is held in place by the weapon. A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach from this grapple on a success. You can't use the weapon to attack another target while it's grappling a creature in this way, but you can choose to deal {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage to the {@condition grappled} creature automatically in place of any attack you'd make with it as part of the {@action Attack} action, as the weapon's pincers clamp down tightly around the target.

You can release a creature from the bident's grapple on your turn (no action required). The weapon releases a creature from its grasp early if you let go of the weapon or are {@condition incapacitated}.

name: Manifested Nostalgia
entries: After consuming this clear and flavorless potion, you quickly undergo a radical transformation, becoming the child version of yourself for the next 4 hours. For the duration, you are one size smaller (to a minimum of Small), and your Strength and Dexterity become 10, unless those scores are already less than 10.
{@font {@style 13|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Manor Key
entries: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA}}

This long key, studded with tiny Siberys dragonshards, can only be used by a creature with the {@feat Mark of Hospitality|EFA}. You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to trace the outline of a door in the air with the key and cast {@spell Mordenkainen's Magnificent Mansion|XPHB} without requiring Material components. The spell ends after 24 hours or when you use the key to lock the door and dismiss the effect; at that time, any creatures within the mansion are expelled into an open space near its entrance. Once used, the key cannot be used again until the next dawn.

name: Mantle of Otherworldly Charisma
entries: Structured from the fur and skin of a monstrosity and the horns of a fiend, and coated in the dust of fey creatures, this mantle is imbued with charming energies.
Your Charisma score is 19 while you wear this magic cape. It has no effect on you if your Charisma is 19 or higher without it.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Mantle of Otherworldly Charisma requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus

items.name: [Hair]
entries: Fur from a Monstrosity

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Skin from a Monstrosity

items.name: [Natural Weapons]
entries: Horns from a Fiend

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Fey Dust

name: Mantle of Security
entries: This soft cloak was once a child's beloved blanket and has been miraculously enchanted by their hopes and dreams. While worn as a cloak, you can't be {@condition frightened}, and magic can't put you to sleep. When unclasped, it can still be used as a warm blanket. When used as a blanket while sleeping or over the course of a short or long rest, you can't be unwillingly targeted by the {@spell dream} spell, you gain a +3 bonus to your passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score, and you can't be surprised as a result of being {@condition unconscious}. Regardless of how the cloak is used, you can tolerate temperatures as low as −50 degrees Fahrenheit without any additional protection.

name: Mantle of the Lightbender
entries: This elegant cloak is lined with the iridescent mane of a {@creature lightbender|FleeMortals}. When you're hit with an attack while wearing this cloak, you can use your reaction to reveal that the attacker is attacking a past visual imprint of you. You appear in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of your imprint, the attack misses, then the imprint disappears. You can't use this reaction if the attacker relies on senses other than sight, such as {@sense blindsight}, or if they can perceive illusions as false, as with {@sense truesight}. Once you use the cloak to reveal a past visual imprint of yourself, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Mantle of the Pack Lord
entries: While wearing this enchanted pelt cloak, creatures don't have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll against you as a result of having an ally within 5 feet of you if they normally would, such as from the Pack Tactics trait.

name: Manual of Occult Anatomy +1
entries: Filled with diagrams showing humans with alien features, this book of strange medical lore is written in monster-blood ink infused with draconic dust and then etched onto parchment pages made from aberration skin. The manuscript is bound in a scale-clad cover.

You can use this manual as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Apothecary or Warlock spells. When you use the manual as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs of your Apothecary or Warlock spells.

In addition, the book contains the knowledge of an Apothecary Esoteric Theory or Warlock Eldritch Invocation up to a level determined by the manual's rarity and chosen when the item is created, which you gain while you are attuned to it. This determines which class is required to attune to the item.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Manual of Occult Anatomy requires a Workshop and Components of equal rarity to the item created. The Components required are:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Any Dragon Dust

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Monster Blood from a Monstrosity

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Scales

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Skin from an Aberration

name: Manual of Occult Anatomy +2
entries: Filled with diagrams showing humans with alien features, this book of strange medical lore is written in monster-blood ink infused with draconic dust and then etched onto parchment pages made from aberration skin. The manuscript is bound in a scale-clad cover.

You can use this manual as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Apothecary or Warlock spells. When you use the manual as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs of your Apothecary or Warlock spells.

In addition, the book contains the knowledge of an Apothecary Esoteric Theory or Warlock Eldritch Invocation up to a level determined by the manual's rarity and chosen when the item is created, which you gain while you are attuned to it. This determines which class is required to attune to the item.

name: Many Hands
entries: When you drink this potion, you can call upon an ancient and devious spirit known as Many Hands. When you do, a host of long, spindly, spectral arms reach out from your body. Anyone who can see you when the hands first emerge must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} until the start of your next turn; creatures that are friendly to you have advantage on this save. Additionally, the arms lash out from you, clawing at all other creatures within 20 feet of you. Each creature in that area must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 10d6} necrotic damage and can't regain hit points until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage but suffers no other effect.
{@font {@style 53|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Marlin Lunger
entries: This rapier allows you to sail through the water to pierce your foes. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and you don't suffer the negative effects of underwater fighting when you make an attack with it. Once on each of your turns when you attack with this rapier while underwater, you can glide up to 15 feet through the water, as part of that action, immediately before or after the attack.

name: Marotte of Chance
entries: This flashy bird-shaped jester's baton has been imbued with the magic of the Amaranthine {@deity Clhuran|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting}: the magic of fate. Lumas can tap into this force to unleash all manner of magical effects.

The marotte of chance can be used as an {@item arcane focus|PHB} for your spells. Additionally, the marotte has an unusual heft to it, and it functions as a magical {@item club|PHB} with which you can use your Charisma modifier to make attack and damage rolls. Each time you hit with this weapon, roll a {@dice d100}. On a result of 10 or less, something odd happens. When this occurs, roll a {@dice d10} and consult the Chance Table to determine any additional effects that occur. The attack deals damage as normal, unless otherwise specified.

entries.caption: Chance Table
rows: The attack deals no damage and emits a clear, resonant squeak, audible out to 100 feet.

A bouquet of sweet-smelling flowers springs from the head of the marotte. The attack deals no damage, and the target of your attack must succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition charmed} by you for 1 minute. The {@condition charmed} effect ends the moment you or one of your allies takes hostile actions against the target.
You and the target of your attack immediately switch places. This is a teleportation effect, which emits an audible pop.

Magical lightning arcs from the marotte toward the target of your attack. The target takes {@damage 2d6} points of lightning damage, and each creature within 10 feet of the target (including you) must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} points of lightning damage.

The target of your attack is affected by the effects of an {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell. Roll a {@dice d10}. On an even number, the target is enlarged, and on an odd number, the target is reduced. If the target is unwilling, it can make a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw to avoid the effect.

The marotte transforms into an {@item greataxe|PHB|axe}. Your attack deals {@damage 1d12} + your Charisma modifier slashing damage instead of what it would deal normally. The target of your attack must succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute. A {@condition frightened} creature can attempt a saving throw at the end of its turn, ending the effect on a success. The marotte transforms back into its normal form at the start of your next turn.

The target of your attack glows the color of your choice. Until the start of your next turn, the target sheds {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} in a 15-foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 15 feet and can't be {@condition invisible}.
You turn {@condition invisible} for 1 minute. Roll a {@dice d10}. On an odd number, the target of your attack also becomes {@condition invisible} for 1 minute.

Your attack deals no damage. The target of your attack must succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or turn into a {@creature frog} (as if under the effect of a {@spell polymorph} spell) for 1 minute. Roll another {@dice d10}. On a roll of 1, the effect happens again, targeting you.

Roll twice more on this table, re-rolling 10s. Your attack has both of the effects you rolled combined. If an effect states your attack would deal no damage, this applies only to the attack's original damage roll and not to damage caused by any additional effects.

name: Marotte of the Lord of Fools (Legendary)
entries: This wooden fool's scepter is painted with vibrant, unsettling colors that depict a grinning face. While no creature is attuned to the marotte, the face looks like the infamous Chuckles, the Lord of Fools.

While holding the marotte, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the marotte's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Coulrophobia (Rare+)
entries: When you succeed on a saving throw to avoid the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force the creature that created the effect to make the same saving throw. On a failed save, it has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Fortune's Fool (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB|Hideous Laughter} (save DC = 16 + the marotte's bonus) from the marotte. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk. You regain use of the spell early if you roll a 1 on the {@dice d20} for a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}.

entries.name: Fool's Motley (Very Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell False Life|XPHB} from the marotte. Any clothing or armor you wear looks like a fool's motley for the duration of the spell.

entries.name: Slapstick (Very Rare+)
entries: When a creature is affected by a {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB|Hideous Laughter} spell you cast, you can choose another creature. When that creature deals damage to the target of the spell, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} rather than {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its saving throw to end the spell.

entries.name: Lord of Fools (Legendary)
entries: You can cast {@spell Mass Suggestion|XPHB} (save DC 19) from the marotte. The effect ends on a creature if it is behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} or more than 120 feet from you. A creature affected by your {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB|Hideous Laughter} automatically fails its saving throw against this Mass Suggestion. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Mask of Dendallen
entries: This skull mask covers the top of your face and offers several benefits while worn. The mask has 5 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the mask, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells (save DC 16) from it: {@spell Bestow Curse|XPHB}, {@spell Fear|XPHB}, {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB}, or {@spell Tongues|XPHB}. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws made to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a spell you cast in this way. In addition, you understand any written language that you see.

entries.name: Curse
entries: When you place this cursed mask over your face for the first time, make a DC 16 Intelligence saving throw. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately remove the mask before it extends the curse to you. On a failed save, you become cursed, and the skin surrounding the mask is riddled with blackened veins and sickly gray skin; you take {@damage 5d10} Psychic damage, and you can't remove the mask unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

While wearing this mask, you can't smell or taste anything, and you automatically fail any Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check that relies on smell or taste. In addition, whenever you roll a 1 on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you take {@damage 1d10} Psychic damage. When you remove the mask after being cursed by it, it takes {@dice 1d4} days for the veins and skin on your face to return to normal.
Your voice also changes. Use the table below to determine the new voice.

rows: Your voice deepens and does not echo.
Your voice becomes raspy and you overly enunciate consonant sounds.
Your voice becomes quiet, almost a whisper, but can still be heard as if spoken at a normal volume.
Your voice becomes high-pitched, and your laugh maniacal.
You slur your words, as if your tongue is suddenly too large for your mouth, and your spit releases a faint hiss as it escapes your mouth.
Your voice becomes that of another ally's and changes each time you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Mask of Lethica Nightborne (Legendary)
entries: This immaculate porcelain mask is painted with delicate violet filigree and once belonged to Lethica Nightborne—a priestess of a goddess of night and healing known as the Nightmother.
While wearing the mask, you gain a +3 bonus to Wisdom and Charisma saving throws determined by the mask's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Gift of the Night Goddess (Rare+)
entries: You can see normally in magical and nonmagical {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} and {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}.

entries.name: Soothing Darkness (Rare+)
entries: Creatures of your choice in the area of a {@spell Darkness|XPHB} spell that you cast have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

entries.name: Whispers of Night (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Darkness|XPHB} from the mask. This property can be used twice (Very Rare+: four times), regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Balm of Midnight (Very Rare+)
entries: At the start of your turn, a {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature of your choice within 60 feet of you must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, the condition ends, and if the creature is in an area of {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, it gains {@dice 2d10} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Offering of Burdens (Legendary)
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can touch a willing creature with {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels and transfer any number of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels to yourself, then remove up to two {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels from yourself and regain one expended spell slot of level 5 or lower. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Surcease of Sorrows (Legendary)
entries: You can cast {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB} from the mask (save DC 19). If the target voluntarily fails the saving throw, you can choose a memory that happened at any time in its lifespan. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Mask of Monstrous Forms
entries: This magic mask is made from the skull of a particular monstrosity (with a {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} of 6 or lower). The skull is carved into a mask, engraved with aberrant dust, and then boiled in a vat of mimic mucus, the flesh of a doppelganger, and acidic bile. Finally, a vessel containing the animus of any creature with the Shapechanger trait is placed upon the forehead of the mask, channeling its shapechanging magic.
While attuned to the mask, you can expend two uses of your Wild Shape feature to transform into the monstrosity associated with the mask, instead of a Beast.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Mask of Monstrous Forms requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Animus from a creature that has the Shapechanger trait

items.name: [Bones]
entries: Skull of a Monstrosity*

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Aberrant Dust

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Acidic Bile

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Mucus from a Mimic

items.name: [Organ]
entries: Flesh from a Doppelganger
{@i * The Monstrosity used for this mask determines the form of the shapechange.}

name: Mask of the Maestro
entries: Carved from yew, this mask is shaped in the likeness of a beast's visage and has 3 charges. While wearing the mask, you can expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} on yourself, with a maximum duration of 1 minute.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This item is cursed. Wearing it curses you until you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic. While you remain cursed, you cannot remove the mask.

name: Mask of the Pact Bearer
entries: This mask looks like a normal wooden mask while no one is attuned to it. When you attune to the mask, your patron's lingering presence over you magically reshapes it to represent the visage of your patron. While wearing this mask, you can cast one spell from the table of spells shown in your level 3 Warlock subclass feature without expending a spell slot. The spell must be of a level equal to or less than your Warlock spell slot level. A spell cast in this way is always cast at its lowest level, regardless of your normal Warlock spell slot level. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Mask of the Wielder
entries: Though most worgs prefer to fight with their teeth or steel jaws, there are those that desire to wield a Dhakaani blade against their enemies. This ornate mask is set with magical gems that focus your subconscious thoughts into a subtle form of telekinesis, allowing you greater control over objects you hold in your teeth.

While wearing the mask, you can use your mouth to wield any Melee weapon that does not have the Heavy, Two-Handed, or Reach properties. If you use the mask to wield a weapon that has {@itemProperty V|XPHB|Versatile}, you can only wield it as if you were using a single hand.

name: Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Crocodile)
entries: These dark ceramic and gold masks are fashioned after animals that are sacred in certain cultures. Each mask's appearance and properties are based on the sacred beast it represents. While attuned to a mask, you can end your attunement to it and attune to a different one over the course of 1 minute, instead of over the course of one or more short rests.
While wearing a crocodile mask, you gain a swimming speed of 30 feet and can hold your breath for up to 10 minutes at a time.

name: Masks of the Sacred Beasts
entries: Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

items: {@item Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Crocodile)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Lion)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Hawk)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Mule)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Jackal)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}

name: Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Hawk)
entries: These dark ceramic and gold masks are fashioned after animals that are sacred in certain cultures. Each mask's appearance and properties are based on the sacred beast it represents. While attuned to a mask, you can end your attunement to it and attune to a different one over the course of 1 minute, instead of over the course of one or more short rests.

While wearing a hawk mask, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight, and attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls. In addition, you can cast the {@spell feather fall|PHB} spell at will, targeting only yourself.

name: Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Jackal)
entries: These dark ceramic and gold masks are fashioned after animals that are sacred in certain cultures. Each mask's appearance and properties are based on the sacred beast it represents. While attuned to a mask, you can end your attunement to it and attune to a different one over the course of 1 minute, instead of over the course of one or more short rests.
While wearing a jackal mask, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks and immunity to necrotic damage.

In addition, you can use an action to fire a beam of deathly green magic from your forehead at a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The creature must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 7d8 + 30} necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once this property of the mask has been used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

A humanoid killed by this necrotic damage rises at the start of your next turn as a {@creature mummy|MM} under your control. The mummy acts on its own initiative count. On your turn, you can mentally command the mummy if it is within 120 feet of you and you aren't {@condition incapacitated} (no action required). You decide what action the mummy takes and where it moves during its next turn, or you can issue it a general command, such as to attack your enemies or guard a location.

The {@creature mummy} remains until you dismiss it as a bonus action, until it's reduced to 0 hit points, or until you are no longer attuned to any {@item masks of the sacred beasts|GriffonsSaddlebag2|mask of the sacred beast}, causing it to turn to dust. You can only create and control one mummy at a time in this way

name: Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Lion)
entries: These dark ceramic and gold masks are fashioned after animals that are sacred in certain cultures. Each mask's appearance and properties are based on the sacred beast it represents. While attuned to a mask, you can end your attunement to it and attune to a different one over the course of 1 minute, instead of over the course of one or more short rests.

While wearing a lion mask, you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on smell. In addition, your nails extend into claws, turning your unarmed strikes with your hands into magic weapons that deal slashing damage with a damage die of {@damage 1d6}.

name: Masks of the Sacred Beasts (Mule)
entries: These dark ceramic and gold masks are fashioned after animals that are sacred in certain cultures. Each mask's appearance and properties are based on the sacred beast it represents. While attuned to a mask, you can end your attunement to it and attune to a different one over the course of 1 minute, instead of over the course of one or more short rests.

While wearing a mule mask, your Strength score increases by 2, to a maximum of 20, you count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift, and you have advantage on Strength and Dexterity ability checks and saving throws against being knocked {@condition prone}. In addition, when you hit a Large or smaller creature with a melee weapon attack, you can use a bonus action to force that creature to make a DC 16 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice). On a failed save, the creature is knocked {@condition prone}.

name: Massive Cluster
entries: Delerium is a magical mineral left behind by the meteor that landed in Drakkenheim. It appears in geode clusters of translucent, sharp-edged crystals which reflect octarine light. The eldritch stones softly hum in dissonant tones, and glow brightly at night or when exposed to magic. Deposits are found throughout Drakkenheim, often fused into stone streets and buildings like crystalline moss.
A typical delerium fragment is about the size of a finger. Crystals may be fist-sized or slightly larger, and geodes may be as big as a pumpkin. Massive clusters might grow taller than a human.

entries.name: Delerium Properties
entries: All delerium samples have the following traits regardless of size:

items: {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage; as well as Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from non-magical weapons.
{@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistant} to Acid, Cold, Fire, and Lightning damage; as well as Slashing and Piercing damage from magical weapons.
{@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerable} to Bludgeoning damage from magical weapons.

Unless contained within an {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}, delerium shatters and crumbles into worthless ash when reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. However, delerium geodes release a random {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} when destroyed.

entries.name: Delerium Hazards
entries: When a humanoid creature touches delerium without protective gear for the first time on their turn, or ends their turn in bodily contact with delerium, they must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage and gain one level of {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.

entries.name: Delerium Harvesting
entries: Delerium found in Drakkenheim is usually fused into the ground or stone buildings. It is carefully extracted using handheld mining equipment such as shovels, picks, hammers, and chisels. Consult the table to determine how long it takes characters to extract delerium. Lacking proper equipment, extraction takes ten times as long. Massive clusters are impossible to extract without heavy equipment or powerful magic.

entries.name: Uses for Delerium
entries: Delerium has vast arcane potential. Beyond trade, crystals are used for several purposes:

entries.name: Spell Component
entries: Delerium may be used as an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} or material component for any spell on the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list. When casting a spell which requires a costly material component, a spellcaster may instead use delerium of equivalent or greater value to the required cost.

entries.name: Magic Items
entries: Delerium is an exceptional material for creating magical items of all kinds. Any existing magic item described in the Basic Rules could be made with delerium. Fragments, shards, crystals, and geodes may be used to make uncommon, rare, very rare, and legendary items respectively. At the GM's discretion, characters who can cast level 5 spells or higher may learn techniques to craft magic items of their own during their downtime.

entries.name: Stable Delerium
entries: The process for crafting magic items with delerium renders the crystals stable. Unless otherwise specified, characters do not take damage nor risk {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} when they touch or handle stable delerium. Stable delerium is damaged and destroyed in the same manner as a normal magic item of its kind.

entries.name: Delerium Dust
entries: Delerium dust is made by grinding the crystals against one another to create a fine powder. This milling process is extraordinarily hazardous unless performed within an {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}. Delerium dust can be used in alchemy, as a spell component, a reagent for brewing potions, or mixed into inks used to scribe spell scrolls. {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB} & Ammunition. Delerium fragments may be used as ammunition for a {@item Sling|XPHB} or fashioned into a makeshift {@item Club|XPHB}. Such weapons and ammunition deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage, and humanoid creatures struck must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}. Delerium used as ammunition in this way is destroyed.

name: Master Machinist's Marvelous Mallet
entries: This immaculate silver hammer is polished to a mirror finish. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The weapon has 7 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the hammer, you can expend 1 charge to cast the {@spell Mending|XPHB} cantrip from it, touching the hammer to the object. Casting Mending in this way affects an area up to 5 feet on a side, instead of 1 foot. Alternatively, you can expend 3 charges as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and touch a creature's armor with the hammer to magically enchant it. The enchantment lasts for 1 minute and grants the armor's wearer a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}. A creature can only be affected by one of these enchantments at a time.

entries.name: Extraordinary Quality
entries: A flute of extraordinary quality that grants +2 to {@skill Performance|XPHB} checks.

name: Mastercraft Instrument
entries: These musical instruments are not just the work of the finest luthiers and artisans in Etharis, they have secret embellishments and innovations that can add to a musical performance.

If you are proficient in the instrument and have a {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} of at least +4, all Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks made using a Mastercraft Instrument have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

name: Mastery Gem
entries: This red gemstone seems to glint with some sort of liquid inside. The gem is immune to all damage. It contains magic absorbed from countless other sources that it uses to overpower the attunement requirements of certain magic items. While holding this gem against an item with an attunement requirement you don't meet, you can ignore that requirement and attune to the item anyway; the item can't be a Legendary item or Artifact. The gem fuses to the surface of the item and encases the area around it in a crystalline shell.

You can end your attunement to the item as normal, even if the item is cursed. Ending your attunement to a cursed item in this way breaks the curse's effects on you. When you end your attunement to an item the gem is fused to, it detaches from the item, allowing you to use it on another one and leaving behind the crystalline shell. When it detaches in this way, it removes the item's magic with it, causing the item to become nonmagical.

name: Matron's Mug
entries: This rustic stoneware mug is warm to the touch and exudes a feeling of comfort while held. You can speak its command word as an action to cause it to fill with a rich, creamy drink that tastes like chocolate. When you drink this beverage, it fills you with a rejuvenating and magical vigor that builds over the course of 1 minute. At the end of this minute, you can choose to recover one expended spell slot by spending a number of Hit Dice equal to the spell slot's level, up to a maximum of 5. Once the mug has created this beverage, it can't create it again until the next dawn.

name: Meat Hookshot
entries: When the {@race Manikin|SGEHPP} of the Sloered Abattoir gained sentience, the Scions sent enforcers to quell this threat to Luyarnha's delicate existence. From the abattoir's meat hooks and the blunderbusses of the slain enforcers, The Slaughtered—as the manikins named themselves—crafted these versatile weapons. Nicknamed "the meat hook", the hookshot is a trick weapon used by hunters to help close the gap to their prey in a devastating whirl of blades and gunpowder.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the hookshot is two one-handed weapons connected by a short length of chain: a {@item Sickle|XPHB} and a {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP}. In its Transformed state, the weapon is a single two-handed weapon: a {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} with a bladed attachment that can act as a {@item Battleaxe|XPHB}.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: While Untransformed, the {@item Sickle|XPHB} has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} property, and the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} doesn't have the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property. Using this pair of weapons together requires the {@item Sickle|XPHB} to be held in one hand and the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} in the other. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with the {@item Sickle|XPHB}, you can make an attack with the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, ignoring the {@itemProperty SGEHPP:Bar|SGEHPP|Barrel} property.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can attack with either the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} or the bladed attachment (which uses the stats of a {@item Battleaxe|XPHB} wielded with two hands). In addition, this item gains the Hookshot property.

entries.name: Hookshot
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you can launch the sickle from the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP}, to which it remains attached by a length of sturdy chain. Make a ranged attack roll against a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes Slashing damage equal to {@damage 1d4} plus your Dexterity modifier. If the creature is your size or smaller, it must succeed on a {@dc 13} Strength saving throw or be pulled in a straight line to the nearest unoccupied space to you. If the creature is larger than you, you are pulled in a straight line to the nearest unoccupied space to it. At the end of your turn, the hook detaches from the creature and reattaches itself to the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP}.

name: Medallion of Mettle
entries: This ostentatious medallion draws the eye of even casual onlookers. Whenever you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you gain an additional {@dice 1d6} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

items: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA}}

name: Medi Spectacles

items: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Detection|EFA}}

additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Eyes of Minute Seeing|XDMG}}

name: Meditative Trance
entries: This violet-colored potion smells like lavender and citrus. The next time you take a short rest after ingesting it, you enjoy a deep, dreamless sleep, granting you the benefits of a long rest, even if you already benefited from a long rest in the past 24 hours.
{@font {@style 47|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Medusan Lavalier
entries: This pair of metallic snakes forms a twisting necklace that hangs around your neck. It coils and moves almost imperceptibly, keeping latched together at the nape of your neck where the snakes' tails intertwine. You can wear or remove the necklace using an action. While wearing this necklace, you can't become {@condition petrified} or otherwise turned to stone against your will. If you are already {@condition petrified} or turning to stone when you wear the necklace, the effect is suppressed until you remove it, provided that its duration has not expired in the meantime.

name: Medusan Signet
entries: When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright while wearing this ring, you don't fall {@condition prone} but are immediately turned to stone and are {@condition petrified}. You remain {@condition petrified} until you die or are targeted by the {@spell greater restoration} spell, or until you regain any number of hit points, regaining consciousness and returning to your normal form when you do. While {@condition petrified} in this way, you don't make death saving throws at the start of each of your turns, although you still suffer failures if you take damage. In addition, critical hits against you while {@condition petrified} become normal hits, as your stone form offers some protection. When you regain consciousness, you also gain {@dice 2d6 + 3} temporary hit points that last for 1 minute as the stone form's lingering protection slowly fades. Once this property has been used 3 times, the ring turns to dust and is destroyed.

name: Medzo's Crossbow
entries: This crossbow once belonged to a savage gambler. Scoring a critical hit with this magic weapon doesn't double the weapon's damage dice, and when you roll a 1 on an attack roll made with it, the weapon jams and can't be used again until the end of your next turn.

A target hit with a ranged attack from this crossbow takes {@damage 3d4} piercing damage, instead of its normal damage. When you hit with an attack using this weapon and roll three of the same number on its damage dice, use the matching number to determine what effect occurs using the table below. When this happens, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} piercing damage.

rows: You can reroll one of the weapon's damage dice, even if it was a matching number. You must use the new roll.
The next attack roll made against the target before the end of your next turn has advantage.
The target has disadvantage on attack rolls it makes until the end of your next turn.
If the target is a hostile creature, 30gp magically appears at your feet.

name: Melodious Bird Calls
entries: When you drink this frothy liquid, you can perfectly mimic the call of any songbird for 24 hours.
{@font {@style 1|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Memento Mori
entries: This sealed letter, infused with Chronomancy magic, contains a written description of how the creature that reads it shall die. The letter always contains specific descriptions, such as "The red-eyed orc drove its blade through Faizon the Blue's heart," but may also use cryptic or vague language. It never specifies an exact time. Once a creature has read the letter, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Death Saving Throws, and dies only after gaining five {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} failures, instead of three. However, when the creature arrives at the moment of its death described in the letter, it dies without making Death Saving Throws if it is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Once a Memento Mori is opened and read, it becomes an ordinary letter. Its effects end only if the creature that read it dies and is later restored to life.

name: Merriment
entries: Is this just booze? For the next hour, you become incredibly intoxicated. For the duration, you gain expertise in a skill of your choice, which means your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it. Until this effect ends, all ability checks you make that don't use the chosen skill are made with disadvantage.
{@font {@style 19|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Merry Berry
entries: This small fruit is highly sought after by cooks and sweet-lovers everywhere, both for its flavor as well as its unique sensory-enhancing properties. Eating a Merry Berry raw yields a taste and texture like that of a rich shortbread—the perfect way to end a day of adventure or travel.

Cooking the berry, whether it be in a cuisine or simply roasted over a campfire, brings out more magical effects. When properly cooked, a creature that eats the fruit has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence and Wisdom checks that rely on smell or taste for the next 24 hours, as well as on ability checks made using {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB} for the duration.
Overcooking the fruit not only cooks out the berry's benefits but also results in a soggy and overall bland dish.

name: Messenger Owl Seed
entries: When thrown, the seed turns into a normal {@creature owl} with an Intelligence score of 14 and the ability to speak Common and Umbral. It will carry a spoken message and any object weighing up to 1 pound for a distance of up to 30 miles, delivering them to a particular person, a creature with a particular title or station (such as the "guard at the east gate of the Court of Golden Oak" or "the Baron of Grenstad"), or to a particular place ("the queen's bedchamber" or "the Hedgehog Tavern").
Once its mission is accomplished, the messenger owl waits for up to 4 hours for a return message or object to carry back to you. If no object or message is provided, it flies away and disappears.

entries.name: Illusion Seeds
entries: Illusion seeds are wondrous items first created in the Shadow Realm and reliant on a supply of shadow matter to power their effects—each such seed generates an illusion and those illusions can take quite powerful forms. While illusion seeds are fairly permanent in the Shadow Realm, where there is shadow matter to empower and sustain the illusions, they are notably less permanent anywhere else. In the mortal world and on other planes, the effects of illusion seeds last for {@dice 2d12} hours and then crumble away in a small burst of glittering light and shadows.

To use an illusion seed, its owner merely needs to throw it 5 feet or more from themselves (to avoid being caught in the magical effect). Once expended, their effects are permanent (in the Shadow Realm), though they can be unraveled using {@spell dispel magic} (DC 13).

name: Meta Mantle
entries: This short scarlet robe's interior and sleeves hold hundreds of arcane runes that have been embroidered with platinum thread. While wearing the robes, you can change your known Metamagic options whenever you finish a long rest. In addition, you gain the following three Metamagic options to choose from.

entries.name: Delayed Spell
entries: When you take the {@action Ready} action to ready a spell that targets a point within its range, you can spend 3 sorcery points to choose a point you can see within that spell's range. Readying this spell doesn't require concentration, can be released as a reaction within 1 minute, and when the spell is released, it targets the chosen point (even if you can no longer see it) and is cast as though you were in the same space as when you took the {@action Ready} action. A spell readied in this way fades and has no effect if it's not released within 1 minute. You can only have one spell readied at a time in this way.

entries.name: Emergency Spell
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack or you take damage, you can use your reaction and spend 6 sorcery points to cast a spell that has a casting time of 1 action or bonus action.

entries.name: Expanded Spell
entries: When you cast a spell that affects an area such as a line, cone, or sphere, you can spend 2 sorcery points to increase its area of affect. A line's length increases by 15 feet, a cone's size increases by 5 feet, a cube's size increases by 5 feet on a side, a sphere's radius increases by 5 feet, and a cylinder's diameter or height increases by 5 feet or 10 feet, respectively (your choice).

name: Meta Medallion
entries: This small medallion is 1 inch tall and made of a strange metal that contains a mote of pure magic. While wearing the medallion, your understanding of Metamagic expands, granting you one additional Metamagic option of your choice. As long as you continue to wear the medallion, you can change this option when you finish a long rest.

name: Metronome Drum
entries: This neatly painted {@item drum|XPHB} is attached to a leather shoulder harness, so it can be struck at waist height. Local folklore suggests that this instrument can have an almost hypnotic effect on those in earshot, but only if played at the correct tempo.

You can play this {@item drum|XPHB} as an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}. Once a day, up to three Humanoids within a 30 ft {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of the {@item drum|XPHB} beat must succeed on a {@dc 14} saving throw or have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition and become {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} towards you. The targets make their saving throws with advantage if you or your allies are fighting them. The {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition ends after 1 hour or when you stop playing the {@item drum|XPHB}. When the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition ends, the targets know they were {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you.

name: Midwife Shears
entries: These scissors are shaped to resemble a stork. Their blades are forever wickedly sharp, and the threads they cut are more than merely physical.

entries.name: Cut the Unseen Thread
entries: While holding the scissors, you can cast {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} (+4 bonus) or {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} from them. Once either spell is cast from the scissors, that spell can't be cast from them again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Curse of the Severed Thread
entries: When you make a saving throw to avoid being pushed or to avoid the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, you have a -1 penalty to the roll. This penalty increases by 1 each time you use the Cut the Unseen Thread property. If you fail such a save by 5 or more, you are pushed {@dice 1d6 x 5} feet straight away from the source of the save, in addition to any other distance pushed.

name: Millstone of Grinding
entries: This 5-ton, 10-foot-diameter flat stone bears the inscription "All is Grist."

While the mill is operational, the millstone can pulverize any Small or Tiny mundane object placed in the hole at its center. The object becomes a pinch of magic flour. As an action, a creature can add this flour to water, causing the object to return to its original form.

name: Mimickey
entries: This bone and flesh keyring can be socketed on any weapon or held item. As an action, you can hold the item by the keyring and spin it in a circle, causing the socketed item to shrink to the size of a key. Using an action to spin it while key-sized returns it to its normal size.

name: Mimicloak
entries: This strange cloak is made using the enchanted remains of a young mimic. While wearing it, you can use a bonus action to speak its command word to change the style, color, and apparent quality of the cloak. The garment's weight doesn't change. Regardless of its appearance, the cloak can't be anything but a cloak with these properties.

While wearing this cloak, you have advantage on ability checks made to escape from a {@action grapple}. Whenever you make an ability check to escape a grapple or free yourself from restraints, the creature or object holding you takes {@damage 1d10} piercing damage as the cloak's fabric magically splits into a toothed maw to bite it.

name: Mind Over Might
entries: When consumed, this chalky elixir turns an intellectual scholar into an athlete. For the next 24 hours, you can use your Intelligence or Wisdom modifier (your choice), in place of your Strength or Dexterity modifier, when making Strength ({@skill Athletics}) and Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks. You also gain proficiency in those skills for the duration, if you don't already have it.
{@font {@style 50|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Mind Transfer
entries: When imbibed, this acrid elixir loosens your soul from your body and prepares it for transfer. The first time you are touched by a creature after consuming this potion, your mind and soul transfer into that creature's body. While inhabiting the creature's body, you can force it to make a contested Intelligence or Wisdom check (you both choose which ability to use) at the start of each of its turns. If you succeed, you gain total control over the creature until the start of its next turn. While your mind and soul are away, your body is left {@condition unconscious}. If the creature dies while your mind and soul are still inside it, you also die. You inhabit the creature's body for 1 hour, until you dismiss the effect as an action, or until the creature is targeted by a {@spell Dispel Evil and Good} spell.
{@font {@style 52|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Mindmaster's Monocle
entries: This ancient golden monocle's lens is a roughly hewn ruby. While you wear this monocle, it magically floats in front of your eye, instead of resting on your face, and you can see clearly through its ruby lens. While peering through the lens, you always know if a creature you can see is concentrating on a spell. You perceive a concentrating creature's head as being shrouded in an indigo mist.
This monocle has 10 charges for the following properties. It regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Spells
entries: While wearing the monocle, you can use an action to expend some of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: {@spell arcane eye|PHB} (4 charges), {@spell detect thoughts|PHB} (2 charges), or {@spell rary's telepathic bond|PHB|telepathic bond} (5 charges).

entries.name: Mental Assault
entries: While wearing the monocle, you can use a bonus action to expend 3 of its charges to attempt to break a creature's concentration on a spell. The target must be within 60 feet of you, and you must be able to see it. When you do, make an Intelligence check contested by the target's spellcasting ability check. If you win the contest, the target's concentration on the spell ends.

name: Mindrazor
entries: This rapier was forged using shattered fragments of a powerful psionic crystal and ore from a falling star. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

This rapier has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a creature with an attack roll using this weapon, you can expend 1 charge to attempt to inflict a psionic wound. The target must succeed on a DC 17 Intelligence saving throw or become vulnerable to psychic damage for 1 minute (save ends at end of turn).

name: Minotaur's Map
entries: The minotaurs of Droaam have no issues navigating the winding streets of the region's great cities, and their understanding has been captured in these fragile maps. When you speak the map's command word while in the city for which it was made, you can add twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to any Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks made to navigate or track a creature through the city for 1 hour. At the end of the hour, the map crumbles to dust.

name: Mirror of Infinite Transpondence
entries: These silver hand mirrors always come in pairs. When activated as an action, a mirror establishes a visual link with its paired mirror for 10 minutes, with the two mirrors acting as opposite sides of the same open window. The mirrors create this connection even if both are on different planes.

When a single mirror of infinite transpondence is found, the GM decides where its paired mirror is and who possesses it. A random possessor and location can be determined by rolling on the table below. Named bearers are described in {@book chapter 2|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2}.
Once the connection between the two mirrors has been activated three times from either end, it can't be activated again until the next dawn.

entries.caption: Mirror Locations
rows: None; the mirror is in an empty dungeon
{@book Ouestra, the Voice of Memory|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|2|Ouestra, the Voice of Memory}

name: Mirrorlight Edge
entries: This roughly hewn crystal sword bends light in unexpected and dangerous ways. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can use a command word to cause it to emit up to two ghostly projections of itself. The sword can have up to two of these projections at a time, which last until you dismiss them (no action required). When swung, the ghostly projections make the sword difficult to see. When you miss a target with an attack roll using the sword while it has at least one projection, you can dismiss one of its projections to reroll the {@dice d20}, and you must use the new roll.

When you hit a target with this weapon while it has at least one projection, the ghostly projections become razor sharp. Targets hit by the sword take an extra {@damage 1d4} Slashing damage for each projection it has.

The sword sheds {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius while it has one projection or in a 20-foot radius while it has two. Sheathing the {@item Scimitar|XPHB} contains the projections and their light without dismissing them.

name: Mirrorlight Piercer
entries: This crystalline {@item Spear|XPHB} bends the light it generates in such a way that it becomes tangible. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property.

While you hold the {@item Spear|XPHB} in one hand and have another hand free, you can use a command word as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to create a ghostly projection of the {@item Spear|XPHB} in your free hand. The projection uses the same weapon statistics as the {@item Spear|XPHB}. When you create a projection in this way, you can make one attack roll with either the {@item Spear|XPHB} or the projection as part of that action. If you make a ranged attack roll with the projection, it disappears after it hits or misses the target. If you're still holding the crystalline {@item Spear|XPHB} when this happens, it magically recreates the projection in your free hand again (no action required).

The projection lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or until a creature other than you holds it. If you drop or stow the crystalline {@item Spear|XPHB}, its projection disappears until you hold the {@item Spear|XPHB} again. The {@item Spear|XPHB} can only have one projection at a time. While it has a projection, both the {@item Spear|XPHB} and its projection shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 10 feet.

name: Misthaven Miscellany
entries: This small embroidered pouch is said to contain the cast-off goods discarded by the Merchant of Misthaven, an archfey of Thelanis. When you reach into the pouch, you can pull out a random trinket (see page 46 of the 2024 version of the fifth edition Player's Handbook or any other random trinket table of your choice). A trinket pulled from this pouch disappears when you pull another trinket from the pouch.

name: Mistwalker Armor
entries: This dark leather armor releases thin wisps of fog from its seams. While wearing this armor, you can use an action to cast the {@spell fog cloud|PHB} spell (2nd-level version) from it. Once this property of the armor has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

In addition, fog doesn't obscure your vision, and while you're in opaque fog, you can use your movement to teleport to an unoccupied space that you can see in the fog. Doing so costs an amount of movement equal to the distance you teleport.

name: Mithril Mail-shirt
entries: A Mithril {@item Chain Shirt|PHB|mail-shirt} is half its normal weight, and can be worn under normal clothes. When you are wearing it, your base Armour Class is 14 + your Dexterity modifier (max 4), and you are considered proficient with it if you have proficiency with light armour.

name: Mockingblade
entries: This magic sword helps you more effectively add insult to injury. You are proficient with the Mockingblade while you're attuned to it. The sword has 6 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn.
