entries: The typical {@item Orostead iced tea|GriffonsSaddlebag2}, a common potion, is a specialty alcoholic beverage that creates harmless sensory effects with each sip. When made, a tea has enough for {@dice 6 + 1d4} sips before it's used up, instead of a single use. You can take a sip as an action. When you drink this potion, roll on the table below to determine which one of the following effects occur:

rows: You suddenly become drenched with illusory salt water. After 1 minute, it dries.
You're suddenly overwhelmingly warm ({@chance 50|50%}) or cold ({@chance 50|50%}) for 1 minute.
You remain frozen in place for 1 second, as if briefly removed from time.
You gain the effect of the {@spell speak with animals} spell for 1 minute.
You suddenly teleport 5 feet into an unoccupied space next to you.
Any clothing you wear becomes various shades of gray for 1 minute.
Static charge builds up on you. Touching or being touched by anything for the next minute causes a sharp shock of electricity to leap between you.

Your skin, hair, and eye colors are inverted. In addition, roll a {@dice d12}. You grow or shrink a number of inches equal to the result of the die, shrinking by odd numbers or growing by even ones. After 1 minute, your appearance returns to normal.

entries: The drink is incredibly refreshing with notes of lemon, tea, and cherry, and has virtually no alcoholic bite to it. Regardless, due to its magical nature, the alcohol within this potion affects a creature twice as much as the alcohol within a nonmagical beverage.

name: Orostead Iced Tea
entries: Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

items: {@item Orostead Iced Tea (Common)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Orostead Iced Tea (Very Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}

name: Orostead Iced Tea (Very Rare)
entries: The following {@item Orostead iced tea|GriffonsSaddlebag2} is a very rare variant with additional properties. It also tastes better. When made, a tea has enough for {@dice 6 + 1d4} sips before it's used up, instead of a single use. You can take a sip as an action.

When you take a sip of this potion, roll a {@dice d8} and consult the table below instead to determine which one of the following benefits you gain. Once you've gained a benefit from the table, you can't gain that same benefit again until you finish a long rest.

rows: For 1 hour, you gain a +2 bonus to Strength ability checks and saving throws, as well as attack and damage rolls for weapons that use Strength.
For 1 hour, you gain a +2 bonus to Dexterity ability checks and saving throws, as well as attack and damage rolls for weapons that use Dexterity.

For 1 hour, you gain a +2 bonus to Intelligence ability checks and saving throws. If Intelligence is your spellcasting ability, you also gain a +2 bonus to your spell attack rolls and spell save DC for the duration.

For 1 hour, you gain a +2 bonus to Wisdom ability checks and saving throws. If Wisdom is your spellcasting ability, you also gain a +2 bonus to your spell attack rolls and spell save DC for the duration.

For 1 hour, you gain a +2 bonus to Charisma ability checks and saving throws. If Charisma is your spellcasting ability, you also gain a +2 bonus to your spell attack rolls and spell save DC for the duration.
Choose a benefit from the table, even if you've already gained it since you finished your last long rest.

You recover expended spells slots with a combined level that is equal to or less than 8, and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. If you don't have any expended spell slots, you can use an action to cast the {@spell fireball} spell once within the next 8 hours, casting the spell at 6th level and using a spell save DC of 16 when you do.

name: Orphan's Cradle
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In both states, the weapon is a {@item Morningstar|XPHB} with the {@itemProperty R|XPHB|Reach} property.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: The flowers growing in the cradle exude a sickly sweet scent that calms the mind of men and chases away nightmares. Humanoids within 10 feet of the cradle have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions. In addition, the cradle has the Cleansing Miasma and Vile Miasma properties.

entries.name: Cleansing Miasma
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can cleanse one Humanoid you can see within 10 feet of you. It gains {@dice 1d12} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} and can end one of the following conditions: {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, or {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}. Once a creature has benefited from this property, it can't benefit from it again for 1 hour.

entries.name: Vile Miasma
entries: When you hit a Beast or an Undead with this weapon, the target must succeed on a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute, even if the target is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. A {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to Vile Miasma for the next 24 hours.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: When Transformed, the cradle's plants ignite, and it deals an extra {@damage 2d6} Fire damage on a hit. In addition, the weapon gains the Fanned Flames and Withering Flames properties.

entries.name: Fanned Flames
entries: As an action, you can rotate the cradle wildly around you, fanning the flames. Each creature in a 20-foot Cone must make a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 3d6} Fire damage and {@damage 3d6} Poison damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Beasts and Undead have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this saving throw. After this property is used, Orphan's Cradle reverts to its Untransformed state and can't be Transformed again for {@dice 1d4} rounds.

entries.name: Withering Flames
entries: When you hit a Beast or an Undead with this weapon, you can force the target to make a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to your choice of one of the following damage types until the start of its next turn: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Radiant. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to Withering Flames for the next 24 hours.

name: Osseous Spike (rare)
entries: {@i Component: astral bone (unique - bonemonger)}

The essence of the malicious bonemonger always hungers for more victims, and this craving persists even after death. Those who hold this jagged lance can feel its insatiable desire to be bathed in blood, and see shadowy claws crawl across its surface when it has gone too long without...
This lance has {@b 3 charges} and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Syphoning Splinters
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack using this lance, you can expend {@b 1 charge} to cause the tip of the lance to explode into sharp splinters; the creature must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 4d4} piercing damage and some of the splinters are embedded inside of it for {@b 1 minute}. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effects. A creature with splinters inside of it takes {@damage 2d4} necrotic damage at the end of each of its turns, and you regain hit points equal to half the necrotic damage dealt this way as the splinters syphon the victim's vitality into you. A creature with splinters inside it or another creature within 5 feet of it can use an action to make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|PHB}) check, removing the splinters on a success.

name: Osseous Spike (very rare)
entries: {@i Component: astral bone (unique - bonemonger)}

The essence of the malicious bonemonger always hungers for more victims, and this craving persists even after death. Those who hold this jagged lance can feel its insatiable desire to be bathed in blood, and see shadowy claws crawl across its surface when it has gone too long without...
This lance has {@b 4 charges} and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Syphoning Splinters
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack using this lance, you can expend {@b 1 charge} to cause the tip of the lance to explode into sharp splinters; the creature must make a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 4d4} piercing damage and some of the splinters are embedded inside of it for {@b 1 minute}. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers no additional effects. A creature with splinters inside of it takes {@damage 2d4} necrotic damage at the end of each of its turns, and you regain hit points equal to half the necrotic damage dealt this way as the splinters syphon the victim's vitality into you. A creature with splinters inside it or another creature within 5 feet of it can use an action to make a {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|PHB}) check, removing the splinters on a success.

entries.name: Crippling Impalement
entries: As an action while holding this lance, you can cause its shadowy hands to extend and try to grab a creature that you can see within {@b 20 feet} of you, forcing it to make a {@dc 16} Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is seized by the hands, pulled to within 5 feet of you, and has an arm or leg (your choice) skewered by the lance, taking {@damage 6d4} piercing damage. The shadowy hands then release the creature. Until the end of its next turn, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls made with the use of its arms if you skewered its arm, or has its speed reduced to 0 feet if you skewered its leg. Once this property of the lance has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Ottaveggr Talharpa
entries: This Northlands Lyre is strung with cords made of braided jotun hair. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can play the talharpa to grant all your allies within {@b 60 feet} who can hear it {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saves against the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition and on Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) checks for {@b 1 hour}. Once this ability has been used, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

name: Otyugh Cloak
entries: This gruesome, magical otyugh pelt still holds some of its natural abilities. A single tendril bearing three eyes hangs from the back of the cloak's hood. While wearing the cloak, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to telepathically communicate with a creature you can see within 60 feet of you that can understand a language, sending either simple messages or images when you do. The receiving creature can't respond to these messages.

The tendril hanging from the hood is 3 feet long and offers some limited articulation. While wearing the cloak, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to mentally control the tendril enough to perform a simple task within 5 feet of you, such as to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial. The tendril can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

In addition, while wearing the hood, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to close your eyes and magically see through the eyes of the tendril. When you do, you have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. You can control the tendril while looking through its eyes in this way. You return to your normal senses when you reopen your eyes or lower the hood.

name: Ouroboros Rapier
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you roll an 8 on the damage die for an attack made with this weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Poison damage. In addition, when you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll made with this weapon against a creature, the target must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 3d6} Poison damage and has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.

name: Overgrown Barkshield (rare)
entries: This crude shield made of bark and wood teems with life as if it were still part of a tree. The smell of sap and various fragrant flowers perfumes the air around you.

entries.name: Bark Armour
entries: As an action, you can place the shield on your torso and speak the command word, causing the wood and vines to wrap around your figure. For one hour, or until you end this effect as an action, you are unable to hold a shield and you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain {@dice 3d8} temporary hit points.
You gain the benefits of the {@spell barkskin} spell (no concentration required).
You have advantage on saving throws made to resist being {@condition poisoned}.

entries: When this effect ends, the barkshield falls from its place on your torso, fading to a lifeless shade of grey. This property can't be used again until you finish a long rest when the shield blooms with life once more.

entries.name: Vines and Thorns
entries: While attuned to this shield, you can use an action to animate one of the shield's thorny vines and make a melee weapon attack ({@hit +8} to hit, reach 30 ft.) against one target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 3d8} piercing damage, and, if the target is a Large or smaller creature, or an object that weighs less than 500 pounds, you pull it up to {@b 10 feet} closer to you.

name: Overgrown Barkshield (uncommon)
entries: This crude shield made of bark and wood teems with life as if it were still part of a tree. The smell of sap and various fragrant flowers perfumes the air around you.

entries.name: Bark Armour
entries: As an action, you can place the shield on your torso and speak the command word, causing the wood and vines to wrap around your figure. For one hour, or until you end this effect as an action, you are unable to hold a shield and you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain {@dice 1d8} temporary hit points.
You gain the benefits of the {@spell barkskin} spell (no concentration required).
You have advantage on saving throws made to resist being {@condition poisoned}.

entries: When this effect ends, the barkshield falls from its place on your torso, fading to a lifeless shade of grey. This property can't be used again until you finish a long rest when the shield blooms with life once more.

entries.name: Vines and Thorns
entries: While attuned to this shield, you can use an action to animate one of the shield's thorny vines and make a melee weapon attack ({@hit +5} to hit, reach 30 ft.) against one target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 2d8} piercing damage, and, if the target is a Large or smaller creature, or an object that weighs less than 500 pounds, you pull it up to {@b 10 feet} closer to you.

name: Overgrown Barkshield (very rare)
entries: This crude shield made of bark and wood teems with life as if it were still part of a tree. The smell of sap and various fragrant flowers perfumes the air around you.

entries.name: Bark Armour
entries: As an action, you can place the shield on your torso and speak the command word, causing the wood and vines to wrap around your figure. For one hour, or until you end this effect as an action, you are unable to hold a shield and you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain {@dice 5d8} temporary hit points.
You gain the benefits of the {@spell barkskin} spell (no concentration required).
You have advantage on saving throws made to resist being {@condition poisoned}.

entries: When this effect ends, the barkshield falls from its place on your torso, fading to a lifeless shade of grey. This property can't be used again until you finish a long rest when the shield blooms with life once more.

entries.name: Vines and Thorns
entries: While attuned to this shield, you can use an action to animate one of the shield's thorny vines and make a melee weapon attack ({@hit +10} to hit, reach 30 ft.) against one target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 4d8} piercing damage, and, if the target is a Large or smaller creature, or an object that weighs less than 500 pounds, you pull it up to {@b 10 feet} closer to you.

name: Overmatter Totem
entries: This totem is made out of a {@condition petrified} overmind tongue encased in hard, translucent resin. While holding it, you can use an action to detach one ear, eye, or hand from your body. The body part has AC 10, hit points equal to half your hit point maximum, a flying speed equal to half your greatest movement speed, and it can hover.
Your detached body part acts on your turn and follows your telepathic commands. Each body part can only take the following actions:

entries.name: Ear
entries: Your ear can hear. Anything your detached ear hears, you hear. On your turn, your ear can use an action to make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to hear.

entries.name: Eye
entries: Your eye can see and has any special senses you have, except for {@sense tremorsense|MM}. Anything your detached eye sees, you see. On your turn, your eye can use an action to make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to see.

entries.name: Hand
entries: Your hand can carry and manipulate Tiny objects.

On your turn, your hand can use an action to interact with an object you can see or to make one attack using a light weapon against a target you can see. This attack uses your attack bonus and ability score modifier.

If your detached body part is within 5 feet of you, it can use an action to reattach to you. If your body part is reduced to 0 hit points or is ever more than 60 feet away from you, it falls to the ground, lifeless, and must be reattached manually. Reattaching a body part manually takes 1 hour.

name: Overseer's Spade
entries: This golden shovel is miraculously resistant to impacts and scrapes. As an action, you can touch the tip of the shovel to a patch of loose earth within 5 feet of you and speak its command word. When you do, you can magically excavate up to a total of eight contiguous 5-foot cubes of loose, nonmagical earth, starting from where you touched the shovel. It takes 1 minute for these changes to take effect. Any dirt or stone removed in this way is destroyed, leaving behind any loose metals or gemstones within the excavated area. The shovel can only remove up to eight 5-foot cubes of earth in this way each day.

name: Overshield
entries: While holding this large Shield, you gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC. The bonus becomes +2 while you have at least 1 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB|Temporary Hit Point}. While you have {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, the Shield emits a slight blue glow.

In addition, you can channel the heroic resolve within the Shield as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to gain {@dice 1d6 + 8} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Owlbear Leather Armor
entries: This set of leather armor was made from the remains of a hardy and ferocious owlbear. While wearing this armor, if you fail a Constitution saving throw against an effect from a hostile source, you can choose to succeed instead. Once this property of the armor has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Pack of LeviBubble Sugarbombs
entries: This delicious gum comes in packs of five and can be blown into large, levitating bubbles 1 foot in diameter. You need to chew a piece of the gum for 1 minute before its magic can be used. Once it's been chewed for at least 1 minute, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while the gum is in your mouth to blow a single bubble with it. When you do, you gain the effect of the {@spell Levitate|XPHB} spell, as if you had cast it, provided the bubble stays attached to the gum in your mouth. While the effect doesn't require your {@status Concentration|XPHB}, it does end early and cause you to fall if you take an action to pop it or if the bubble takes any damage; the bubble is a loose object for the purpose of any attack or effect that would target it. The effect ends on its own after 10 minutes, allowing you and the bubble to float gently down to the ground if you're still aloft. The gum becomes nonmagical, albeit still delicious, once this bubble's effect ends.

When you take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to blow this bubble, you can remove it from your mouth as part of the same action and stick it on another creature or loose object within 5 feet of you. When you do, the stuck target gains the effect of the {@spell Levitate|XPHB} spell, instead of you, but you have no control over it; the effect otherwise functions as described above. An unwilling creature that succeeds on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw avoids having the bubble stuck to it.

name: Pack of Revisibility Bombs
entries: A pack of revisibility bombs typically includes {@dice 1d3 + 3} fist-sized bombs when found. You can use an action to throw a bomb at a point that you can see within 60 feet of you. The bomb explodes at the point where it impacts, destroying the bomb and releasing a dispelling vapor in a cloud around it. When the bomb explodes, each creature within 30 feet of it must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature becomes visible if it isn't already, and can't become {@condition invisible} for 1 minute. Objects within the area that aren't being worn or carried automatically become visible if they're {@condition invisible} and can't become {@condition invisible} for 1 minute.

name: Painter's Sun Hat
entries: This well-made hat can come in any shape, size, or form and from casual inspection seems to be mundane in nature. However, when the hat is placed on the ground as an action and its command word is spoken, it begins to float into the air. The hovering hat then produces an illusion of a humanoid of your choice that you are familiar with, with the caveat that the illusion is wearing the hat. The figure can't move and fails to hold up to physical inspection. The illusion remains until the hat is moved out of place, or until the command word is spoken once more, causing the hat to float back to the ground. A DC 10 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals the figure is an illusion.

name: Pair of Tiny Violin Rings
entries: This pair of golden rings play a sad, sad melody when you rub the two fingers wearing them together. Creatures that know the {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} cantrip can use this set of rings as a Somatic component for the spell instead of the normal Verbal component required by it.

name: Paper Cartridge Bullet, Armor-Piercing
entries: This ammunition works like an {@itemProperty AP|GrimHollowPG24|Armor-Piercing} Melee weapon, but you fire the ammunition as a projectile from a Ranged weapon.

name: Paper Cartridge Bullet, Blessed
entries: When you hit with Blessed ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Radiant. Also, if the target is Fiend, Fey, or Undead, that creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn.

name: Paper Cartridge Bullet, Brutal
entries: Designed to open wide wounds, such as with a broad-bladed arrowhead, Brutal ammunition works like a {@itemMastery Brutal|GrimHollowPG24} Melee weapon.

name: Paper Cartridge Bullet, Desecrated
entries: When you hit with Desecrated ammunition, the weapon's damage type becomes Necrotic. Also, if the target is Celestial, Humanoid, or Plant, that creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn, and the creature can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn.

name: Paper Cartridge Bullet, Incendiary
entries: When you hit with Incendiary ammunition, the target takes an additional {@damage 1d4} Fire damage.

name: Paradise Plumage
entries: After drinking this potion, you are instantly adorned with striking and distinctive plumage. You can control it to create dazzling displays of shimmering feathers, iridescent colors, and stunning patterns. When you do so, you gain advantage on all Charisma ({@skill Performance}) checks made to distract or amaze. The effects of this potion last for 24 hours.
{@font {@style 9|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Paragon's Plate
entries: This ancient set of armor, which includes boots, greaves, a cuirass, gauntlets, and a helm, fully encases you in a shell of imposing steel, such that no part of your body is visible. While wearing this armor, you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. If you have 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you must still make {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws}, but you can continue to move and act.
If you die while wearing this armor, you can continue to move and act within it for up to 1 minute, though you lose the ability to speak and to cast or concentrate on spells.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This armor is cursed, a fact revealed only when {@spell Identify|XPHB} is cast on the armor or you attune to it. While attuned to the armor, it is impossible to remove. Additionally, you automatically fail all {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws} as the armor's magic puts an immense strain on your body.

name: Paranoia
entries: When you drink this potion, you gain heightened senses along with the sneaking suspicion that you are being stalked. For the next 8 hours, you can't be {@status surprised}.
{@font {@style 12|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Passage Channeling Wand
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Passage|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Passage|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Passage Dragonmark Channel
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Passage|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Passage|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Passage Dragonmark Reservoir
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Passage|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Passage|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Passing Memory
entries: When brewed, this powerful elixir stores one of the creator's memories of their choice within it. When consumed by another creature, that creature gains the stored memory.
{@font {@style 28|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Pathfinder's Boots
entries: Silver eyelets decorate these soft leather boots. While wearing these boots, you gain a +2 bonus to your AC and your walking speed increases by 10 feet.

The boots have 7 charges. While wearing them, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells from them: {@spell feather fall}, {@spell jump}, or {@spell shield}. The boots regain {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Cursed Sentience
entries: The boots are a sentient and cursed magic item, as described {@book above|FleeMortals|3|Magic Items|4}.

name: Pathfinder's Pebble
reqAttune: by a cleric of the nature domain, druid, or ranger
entries: This polished pebble is inscribed with the holy symbol of {@deity Reya|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} and carries a powerful blessing from the Amaranthine. So long as you carry the pebble and are outdoors, you always know which way is north.

When holding the stone, you can spend an action to focus your mind on your surroundings, allowing you to cast {@spell commune with nature} once per day. You regain the ability to do so each dawn. Additionally, by grasping the pebble tightly and speaking out loud the name of a fixed location you are familiar with on the same plane of existence, the pebble will grant you knowledge of the shortest, most direct physical path toward it. As long as you are holding the pebble, you know how far the named location is from you and in what direction it lies. Furthermore, you can automatically determine which path is the shortest and most direct route (but not necessarily the safest route) to the destination. This lasts until you have either arrived at your destination, you select a new destination in the same manner described above, or you dismiss the effect at any time, costing no action.

name: Pathseeking
entries: This potion is brewed for the specific task of detecting tracks left by a secret path potion. These tracks appear to you as glowing footprints made with uncanny detail. You also gain the ability to see into the Spirit Realm (Ethereal Plane). The effects of this potion last for 1 hour.
{@font {@style 12|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Pearl of Wisdom Quiver
entries: This magic Quiver is made from the shell of an enormous oyster. Arrows you pull from it are magical and are coated with a pearlescent, hydrophobic coating. Ranged attack rolls made with these Arrows ignore the normal drawbacks of underwater combat. The Arrows become nonmagical once they hit a target or are held by a creature other than you.

entries.name: Create Pearl
entries: You can use a command word to cause the Quiver to create a magical pearl. You can hold onto this pearl or give it to another creature. When a creature with the pearl makes a Wisdom check or Wisdom saving throw, it can choose to make the check or save with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. When it does, the pearl turns to dust. The pearl is visibly magical and disintegrates on its own after 24 hours if left unused. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Pegasus Quill
entries: The feather adorning this quill was a gift from a mighty pegasus and has a beautiful, pearlescent shimmer. When you write with this magic quill, the time it takes for you to write something, such as copying a spell into a spellbook or creating a spell scroll, is halved.

name: Pelt of the Pack Lord
entries: This pelt cape is made from the fur of a Garmyr stitched carefully into the leathers of a ratling, decorated with the talons of a harpy, and polished to a shine with contaminated ichor.
While you are attuned to this pelt and are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against that creature.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Pelt of the Pack Lord requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Monstrosity Animus

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Contaminated Ichor

items.name: [Hair]
entries: Fur from a Garmyr

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Skin from a Ratling

items.name: [Natural Weapon]
entries: Claws from a Harpy

name: Pendant of Grave Regeneration
entries: While you wear this pendant, your skin becomes pale and cold to the touch, and you regain 5 hit points at the start of your turn if you have at least 1 hit point.

entries.name: Curse
entries: Attuning to this pendant extends its curse to you. Until the curse is broken with a remove curse spell or similar magic, you can't take it off, and your creature type is Undead instead of your normal type.

name: Pendant of Prismatic Protection
entries: The jeweled pendant has 3 charges, which are replenished when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you take Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend 1 charge from the pendant to gain resistance to that damage type until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Pendant of Prismatic Protection requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus from an Elemental

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Elemental Dust

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Any two Elemental Fluids from different Elementals

name: Pendant of the Tempered Fury
entries: This magic silvered pendant glows with a simmering flame of rage trapped inside its clenched fist. Small sparks shoot out from between the pendant's metal fingers. The fiery anger from the pendant tightens your focus and allows you to shrug off some of the damage you take. If you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield while you wear this pendant, all Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage you take is reduced by 3.

In addition, the pendant has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to ignite your hands in a magical flame, causing them to shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 10 feet. Whenever you deal damage with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} while your hands are wreathed in this fire, it can deal your choice of Fire damage or its normal damage type, and it deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Fire damage on a hit. Your hands remain lit for 1 minute or until you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to quench them.
Any flame created by the pendant, whether it be on your hands or on the pendant itself, is harmless to you.

name: Pendant of Thieves' Sight
entries: While wearing this pendant, you know Thieves' Cant. In addition, you can more easily recognize the patterns used in linguistic codes, granting you a +5 bonus to Intelligence checks made to understand a written or spoken cipher.

name: Pendants of Belonging
entries: These pendants come in sets of four, six, or eight. While worn, a creature always knows the direction of the other pendants in its set.

name: Penitent Pummelers
entries: These brass knuckles are made of gold and etched with a holy symbol over each knuckle. You gain a +1 to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon.
When you hit a Fiend or Undead with this weapon, that creature takes an extra {@damage 1d12} Radiant damage.

name: Pennypuncher Slingshot
entries: This slingshot requires two hands to attack and is adorned with coin-like designs. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, when you make a ranged attack with this weapon and use a coin as its ammunition, it deals extra damage on a hit based on the value of the coin you use:

Recovering coins fired in this way follows the normal rules for recovering ammunition. Depending on the nature of the battlefield, you may recover more or fewer coins than normal as determined by the GM.

name: Peppermince Sugarbomb
entries: This hard, minty sugarbomb slowly dissolves in your mouth over the course of 1 hour. At any point, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to crunch down and break the sugarbomb into tiny, painful shards. You take {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage from the shards but are temporarily enchanted by the candy. Whenever you hit a target with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} that deals Piercing or Slashing damage while you're enchanted in this way, the target takes an extra 2 damage. This enchantment fades after 1 minute.

entries.name: Upset Stomach
entries: You can only be under the effects of one sugarbomb that has this property at a time. Eating a sugarbomb that has this property while under the effects of another one causes the effects of the first sugarbomb to immediately end and be replaced by the new one's. This rapid change is difficult to stomach, forcing you to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute.

name: Peregrine Spear
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic spear. When you make a ranged attack with this spear, you can speak its command word to cause the weapon to soar through the air straight toward the target and magically build momentum. Hit or miss, the spear flies back to your hand immediately after the attack. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} piercing damage for every 5 feet the spear flew before hitting it, up to a maximum of {@damage 12d4} extra damage. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Perfect Memory
entries: For 1 hour after drinking this potion, everything you see and hear is recorded perfectly in your memory. You can recall these memories up to 24 hours later. After that, all the memories begin to fade with only the most memorable parts remaining.
{@font {@style 7|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Performer's Puppet
entries: This simple puppet is a favorite among street performers and traveling thespians. While wearing the puppet on your hand, you can use a bonus action to change the style, color, and shape of the puppet's clothing and face. The material is always made of a colored canvas, but its eyes, stitching, and other descriptive details can change when using this property. In addition, while wearing the puppet on your hand and holding it aloft, your voice originates from the puppet instead of you.

name: Perfume
entries: This aromatic liquid is made from rare ingredients, including floral extracts, wakewyrm ambergris, and essential oils. When daubed lightly on the skin, fur, or feathers, it leaves you smelling pleasant for 8 hours. It comes in a small, stoppered crystal vial containing 20 uses.

name: Periapt of Reflection
entries: This perfectly reflective charm magically helps you meditate and focus your mind. Whenever you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw while wearing the necklace, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reroll the save, and you must use the new roll.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This periapt is cursed, a fact that is only revealed when the curse extends to you due to rolling a 1 on a saving throw after using the periapt to reroll it. Until the curse ends, the mirrored surface of the necklace dulls into an ugly, flat gray while you wear it. The curse persists even if you aren't wearing the necklace, and you remain cursed until you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

While you're cursed, your reflection in any mirrored surface within 10 feet of you turns into an ugly, horrifying visage of your deepest insecurities. In addition, when you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw (including the roll that reveals this curse), you take {@damage 1d8} Psychic damage.

name: Periscope Rod
entries: This silver rod is 1 foot long and is polished to a mirror finish. Its two ends are bent in different directions and are emblazoned with the symbol of an eye. While holding the rod, you can speak its command word as either an action or as part of making a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, placing your eye against one of the rod's ends. When you do, you can magically see through the rod and outside the far end as if the rod were a spyglass. While looking through the rod in this way, you can use a bonus action to mentally control the angle of the rod's ends, as well as its length. The rod can grow up to 5 feet long in this way, and returns to its normal size when your remove your eye from it.

name: Permanent Parchment
entries: This violet piece of parchment is smooth and pleasant to write on. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and use either of the command words, "lock" or "unlock," to magically lock or unlock the parchment, respectively. While locked, the sheet can't be torn by hand, damaged by fire, or damaged by immersion in water, and any ink already on the page can't be removed, smeared, or otherwise changed without the use of magic. New ink added to a locked sheet of Permanent Parchment runs off the page like water. While unlocked, the parchment behaves like a nonmagical sheet of paper.
If the sheet is unlocked, you can use another command word, "clear," to cause any ink on the sheet of parchment to magically evaporate without leaving any marks behind.

name: Petal Dancer Ward
entries: This cape is made of colorful and aromatic petals. While wearing the cape, petals drift behind you as you walk and disappear before touching the ground. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically change the color of these petals. While wearing the cape, you can cast the {@spell Druidcraft|XPHB} cantrip from it, and Beasts and Plant creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you.

name: Phantom Walkers
entries: While wearing these boots, the DC of any ability checks made to track your movements using your footprints increases by 5.

In addition, you can use a bonus action to cause the boots to leave behind no footprints for 1 minute. When you do, another set of similar footprints appear on the ground that lead in random directions. These footprints last for 8 hours and travel up to 300 feet. A successful DC 13 Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals that the footprints are magical. Once this property of the boots has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Pharazorthok Sprout
entries: This hand-sized fleshy sapling has writhing tentacles for branches and bulbous yellow eyes studding its trunk. You can take an action to plant it in the ground in your space, at which point it begins whispering telepathically to you. While the sprout is planted and within 30 feet of you, you have truesight with a range of 30 feet.

Anyone in the sprout's space can take an action to uproot it. If left in the ground for 1 minute, the sprout experiences a growth surge, uproots itself, and becomes a {@creature Roper|XMM} that is {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} to you and your allies.

name: Phase Axe
entries: This crystalline {@item Battleaxe|XPHB} seems to be almost transparent when looking at the bladed head from different angles. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} property with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. The first time on your turn when you hit a target with a ranged attack roll using the axe, you can force another creature within 10 feet of the target to make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, that creature takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage.

If you can see the axe and are within 60 feet of it, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically return the axe to your outstretched hand. When you do, the weapon phases through any obstacle in its path that isn't more than 5 feet thick or made of lead.

name: Phial of Stoutmilk
entries: This thick glass bottle holds viscous, white, fizzing liquid. Tied around the bottle's neck is a worn tag that once listed the ingredients and stated dose.

For 1 hour after drinking this potion, when you take bludgeoning damage, reduce the total damage taken by {@dice 1d4}. Your Strength and Constitution scores both increase by 2 until the potion's effects wear off.

name: Philter of Boundless Joy
entries: As you imbibe this potion, you remember a time of pure happiness and joy, usually related to love, parenthood, or some other enormous, life-altering event—the specific memories depend on the philter's creator. You have advantage on Charisma ability checks for 1 hour and immediately gain the effects of a short rest.
The effects of this philter cancel the effects of a philter of deep despair.

entries.name: Memory Philters
entries: First distilled by gnomes in the Court of Midnight Teeth, memory philters have since gained a large following among the fey. Each such philter contains a distilled emotion, specific memories, or a particular moment in time. The sable elves, shadow fey, shadow goblins, and wyrd gnomes all prize these ersatz memories, and the longer-lived fey in particular prize the memories of the young as a way of reliving fresh, youthful emotion. Some of these philters have game effects while others are prized more for their value as status items, entertainment, or simply for the smug sense of having stolen passionate moments from mortals.

All memory philters superficially resemble potions: they are contained in flasks or small vials, often quite beautifully shaped or painted to hint at the contents. Their ability to transfer memories makes them also useful to a GM to dispense clues or story elements to players (as in a memory that reveals a secret door, a plot point, or a murderer's identity).

name: Philter of Deep Despair
entries: As you imbibe this potion, you remember a time of heart-rending sorrow, grief, and despair related to death, loss, or failure—the specific memories depend on the philter's creator. You have advantage on Wisdom saving throws for 1 hour but cannot take bonus actions of any kind during that time.
The effects of this philter cancel the effects of a philter of boundless joy.

name: Philter of Enchanted Fortune
entries: As you imbibe this potion, you remember a time of staggering good fortune, accomplishment, and success—the specific memories depend on the philter's creator. You have advantage on the next three ability checks, attack rolls, or saving throws you make (including death saving throws).

name: Philter of Innocence
entries: As you imbibe this potion, you return to a childlike state, remembering your life as it was in your formative years—the specific memories depend on the philter's creator. You have resistance to psychic damage for 1 hour and have advantage on Constitution ability checks during that time.

name: Philter of Loving Kindness
entries: As you imbibe this potion, you remember a time of love and acceptance—the specific memories depend on the philter's creator. You cannot be affected by spells from the school of enchantment for 1 hour.

Their ability to transfer memories makes them also useful to a GM to dispense clues or story elements to players (as in a memory that reveals a secret door, a plot point, or a murderer's identity).

name: Philter of Lust
entries: As you imbibe this potion, you are overtaken with memories and feelings from a time of physical desire—the specific memories depend on the philter's creator. You must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be overcome by a fit of lust for 1 minute. While in a fit of lust, you seek out either a person whose affection you desire or, more rarely, an object of consuming passion (usually a token, trophy, or fetish of some kind) to claim for yourself. On a successful saving throw, only the memories are passed to you. You can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of your turns, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Memory Philters
entries: First distilled by gnomes in the Court of Midnight Teeth, memory philters have since gained a large following among the fey. Each such philter contains a distilled emotion, specific memories, or a particular moment in time. The sable elves, shadow fey, shadow goblins, and wyrd gnomes all prize these ersatz memories, and the longer-lived fey in particular prize the memories of the young as a way of reliving fresh, youthful emotion. Some of these philters have game effects while others are prized more for their value as status items, entertainment, or simply for the smug sense of having stolen passionate moments from mortals.

All memory philters superficially resemble potions: they are contained in flasks or small vials, often quite beautifully shaped or painted to hint at the contents. name: Philter of Mercy
entries: As you imbibe this potion, you remember a time of mercy, atonement, and forgiveness—the specific memories depend on the philter's creator. You are immune to being {@condition frightened} for 1 hour and have advantage on Wisdom ability checks during that time.
The effects of this philter cancel the effects of a philter of righteous anger.

name: Philter of Righteous Anger
entries: As you imbibe this potion, you are overtaken with feelings of anger and memories of justice denied, betrayals, or blasphemy—the specific memories depend on the philter's creator. You must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or be overcome by a fit of rage for 1 minute. While in a fit of rage, you have advantage on melee attack rolls, and your melee weapon attacks deal an extra 3 ({@damage 1d6}) damage. You cannot distinguish friend from foe and must attack the nearest creature. If no creatures are nearby, you must dash in the direction of the nearest living creature. If no other creature is near enough to move to and attack, you stalk off in a random direction, seeking a target for your anger. On a successful saving throw, only the memories are passed to you. You can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of your turns, ending the effect on a success.
The effects of this philter cancel the effects of a philter of mercy.

name: Philter of Waking Dreams
entries: As you imbibe this potion, you remember a particular scene of importance, such as a duel, kiss, theft, betrayal, murder, or funeral—the specific memories depend on the philter's creator. You can take no action for 1 round while caught up in these memories and thereafter cannot forget these events: any creature seen in such a memory will be remembered, as well as their name, by you as someone you have seen before. With a successful DC 13 Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check, you may note details of importance within the waking dream, including the relationships of people within the dream, their status, and the location of the dream.
False memories cannot be created via a philter of waking dreams, though what the imbiber remembers may be colored by time or strong emotion.

name: Phoenix Breastplate
entries: This golden breastplate has the shape of a phoenix worked into its design. While wearing this armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC and resistance to fire damage.

When you're reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can choose to drop to 1 hit point instead. When you do, a fiery explosion surrounds you. Hostile creatures within 30 feet of you must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 3d10} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. You and other friendly creatures within the area regain a number of hit points equal to the same amount, instead of taking fire damage. Once this property of the armor has been used, it can't be used again until {@dice 1d6 + 1} days have passed.

name: Phoenix Elixir
entries: When imbibed, this elixir burns your throat and ignites an ember within you. For 24 hours, you are immune to fire damage. When the potion's magic finally fades, the fire inside of you burns intensely from within, consuming you in flames and turning your body to ash. 1 hour later you appear in the nearest bonfire, reborn anew. All objects and clothing that were on your person when you were turned to ash are left by your original body.
{@font {@style 48|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Phoenix Rocket Sword
entries: This heavy, steel greatsword creates a powerful fan of flames from curious, whirring chambers mounted to the blade. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The sword has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn.

As an action, you can hold the sword out in front of you and speak its command word to expend up to 5 of its charges, causing a jet of flame to erupt from it. When you do, the sword emits a roar that's audible out to 100 feet, and you must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed back 20 feet for each charge you expend. You can choose to fail this saving throw, whose DC equals 10 + the number of charges you expend. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks. Pointing the blade down and expending charges in this way launches you upward instead. If you do and you are not launched, the sword's flames spread out in a 15-foot radius circle, centered on you.

The jet of flame spreads out in a 15-foot cone and moves with you if you're pushed. Any creature in the area when the flame first appears or when it moves into the creature's space must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 3d6} fire damage, or half as much fire damage on a success. The fire damage increases by {@damage 1d6} for each additional charge you expend beyond the first.

If you strike an object because of this forced movement, such as a wall or floor, you take {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage for every charge you expend and are knocked {@condition prone}. If you strike a creature, you and that creature take the same bludgeoning damage and must each succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 10 + the number of charges you expend) or be knocked {@condition prone}.

name: Photosynthetic Skin
entries: This vibrant green potion tastes like freshly cut grass. For the next 24 hours, while the sun is out, you regain 1 hit point at the start of every hour.
{@font {@style 8|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Pick and Pocket
entries: This brass and steel dagger can also be used as part of a set of {@item thieves' tools|PHB} when picking locks. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, as well as on any ability check you make using {@item thieves' tools|PHB} to pick open a lock, provided you use the dagger as part of the set of tools.

While holding the dagger in one hand and a small enough object in another, you can use an action to speak the dagger's command word and twist it in the air as if it were a key. When you do, the object is shunted into a special demiplane, where it remains until you either twist the dagger in the opposite direction on your turn (no action required) or until you're no longer holding the weapon. If you have a free hand, the stored object reappears in it when the object leaves the demiplane. Otherwise, it reappears at your feet. The demiplane can only store one object at a time, which must be no more than 1 foot on a side and weigh no more than 10 pounds.

name: Pig Snout
entries: After drinking this pink pastel potion, there is a brief uncomfortable transformation, where the imbiber grows a beautiful, snuffling pig snout. For the next hour, you become very fond of truffles, perhaps even to the point of belligerence, and you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on smell.
{@font {@style 27|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Pigment
entries: When consumed, this multicolored potion allows you to produce a variety of oil paints from the tips of your fingers. You can change the color of the paints at will, and they never seem to run out. The effects of the potion last for 8 hours.
{@font {@style 14|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Pigskin Armor
entries: This strong, flexible armor made from the hide of ogre swine is surprisingly supple. It is considered light armor rather than medium armor. When a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} is scored on you, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 17-20, you treat it as a hit instead.
However, while wearing the armor, you snore uncontrollably while sleeping, and your food intake doubles.

name: Pike of the Forgotten Legion
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The weapon has 6 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 2} expended charges daily at dusk. While holding this {@item Pike|XPHB}, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17) from it: {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Phantom Steed|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} (1 charge), or {@spell Spirit Guardians|XPHB} (2 charges).

entries.name: Spectral Warrior
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with this {@item Pike|XPHB}, you can choose to summon a spectral warrior from it. Until the start of your next turn, the target is haunted by this warrior, causing it to have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against you. This property has no effect against Undead creatures.

entries.name: Haunting Phalanx
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while holding this {@item Pike|XPHB} to expend 3 charges and point it forward commandingly. Five spectral, {@item Pike|XPHB}-wielding warriors appear before you and march in a 25-foot-wide, 50-foot-long {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} in a direction you choose. Any creature within the area must make a DC 17 Intelligence saving throw; Undead creatures automatically succeed on the save. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 3d10} Necrotic damage and {@damage 3d10} Psychic damage and is affected by the weapon's Spectral Warrior property. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

name: Pisces Shield
entries: This round iron shield is emblazoned with two spiraling golden koi. If the shield is submerged in water for at least 1 minute, the koi begin to animate and swim across the surface of the shield for up to 24 hours. While the koi are swimming in this way, the next time you roll a 1 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw while holding the shield, you can treat the roll as if it were a 20 instead. When you do, the koi stop swimming, and they can't swim again until 24 hours have passed.

name: Plaguebane Mask
entries: This birdlike mask's blend of magic and science is as unique as it is helpful. While wearing it, you can easily lift it above your face to eat or speak more clearly. The mask's beak is lined with magical flowers that react to and purify airborne toxins before they pass through it. While wearing the mask, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition as well as the effects of magical contagions if they came from an airborne source, and you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to any Poison damage that those effects might deal.

In addition, the flowers have 3 charges and regain {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn as new flowers bloom. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can hold the beak's nostrils closed with a free hand and expend 1 charge to exhale a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} of thick pollen in front of you. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 2d8} Poison damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of its next turn unless it has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

name: Plainscow
entries: The hulking plainscow is an exceptionally sturdy beast of burden native to the {@book Dividing Plains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Dividing Plains} and used by the people of central Tal'Dorei for centuries. Though many wild herds still roam the plains, domesticated plainscows are more common, used as {@quickref Mounts and Vehicles|PHB|1|0|mounts}, pack animals, and livestock. Plainscows are unusually empathetic for beasts, and often bond with a rider for life. They stand 6 feet tall, weigh about two tons, and live for 70 years.

entries.name: Market Value
entries: Plainscows can be bought in {@book Westruun|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Westruun} for 200 gp. A plainscow has a carrying capacity of 1,500 pounds.

name: Planar Rapier
entries: This thin blade seems to toe the line between planes of existence, occasionally allowing it to bend the planes to extend beyond its normal reach. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The {@item Rapier|XPHB} has 5 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. When you make a melee attack roll with the {@item Rapier|XPHB}, you can expend 1 charge to extend the weapon, increasing its reach for the attack by 5 feet.

Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge immediately after making a melee attack roll with the {@item Rapier|XPHB} against a target within 5 feet of you, causing the weapon to extend and pierce through the original target. Make an additional melee attack roll with the {@item Rapier|XPHB} against a second target 5 feet behind the original one; the second target must be within 10 feet of you. This additional attack is made as part of the initial attack, and the second target doesn't benefit from using the original one as cover.
Whenever you expend a charge from this weapon, the planes around the extended blade begin to tear, causing the target to take an extra {@damage 2d8} Force damage on a hit.
After the attack with the extended blade, it returns to its normal size.

name: Planchette of Adela Druskenvald (Legendary)
entries: A small, heart-shaped silver pointer hangs from a silver necklace. It is inscribed with occult symbols. When placed on an open book or other assortment of letters, the air nearby feels heavy and cold.

While wearing the planchette, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to Intelligence and Wisdom ability checks determined by the planchette's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Sense the Unseen (Rare+)
entries: The planchette has 5 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dusk. You can expend charges to cast the following spells from it: {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Locate Object|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB} (2 charges).

entries.name: Starlight Ward (Rare+)
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Radiant damage. When you take Radiant damage, for the next minute, the star-sigils on the planchette shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 10 feet.

entries.name: Vision Beyond (Very Rare+)
entries: The planchette now has 9 charges and regains {@dice 1d8 + 1} expended charges daily at dusk. You can also cast {@spell Find Traps|XPHB} (2 charges) and {@spell Sending|XPHB} (3 charges) from it.

entries.name: Spirit Ward (Very Rare+)
entries: When you fail a saving throw against the {@spell Magic Jar|XPHB} spell or possession (such as by a {@creature ghost|XMM}), you can expend 3 charges to succeed instead.

entries.name: Third Eye Opened (Legendary)
entries: The planchette now has 13 charges and regains {@dice 1d12 + 1} expended charges daily at dusk. You can also cast {@spell Divination|XPHB} (4 charges), {@spell Contact Other Plane|XPHB} (5 charges), and {@spell Etherealness|XPHB} (7 charges) from it.

name: Planchette of Adela Druskenvald (Rare)

entries: When you fail a saving throw against the {@spell Magic Jar|XPHB} spell or possession (such as by a {@creature ghost|XMM}), you can expend 3 charges to succeed instead.

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When the Plate of the Dawnmartyr reaches an awakened state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The armor's bonus to AC increases to +2.
You are immune to the {@condition frightened} condition.
You have resistance to fire damage.
The fire damage you deal when you rebuke an attacker increases to {@damage 2d6}.

name: Plate of the Dawnmartyr (Dormant)
entries: Beautiful silver scrollwork and priceless cut rubies adorn this set of brass-and-gold armor. Legend holds that it was worn by Duana, High Priest of the {@deity The Dawnfather|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, when she was martyred in the Battle of Ghor Dranas in the final days of the {@book Calamity|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|The Calamity}. In more recent times, it was worn by {@creature Pike Trickfoot|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, a legendary cleric of the {@deity The Everlight|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, while fighting against {@book the Chroma Conclave|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|The Chroma Conclave} and {@deity The Whispered One|Exandria|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: While the Plate of the Dawnmartyr is in a dormant state, you gain a +1 bonus to AC while wearing it. When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to rebuke that creature, dealing it {@damage 1d6} fire damage.

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When the Plate of the Dawnmartyr reaches an exalted state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The armor's bonus to AC increases to +3.
When you rebuke an attacker, you can choose to deal either fire damage or radiant damage.

When you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can choose to have a blast of healing flame surround you. You regain 1 hit point and are lifted to your feet. Each enemy within 10 feet of you takes {@damage 2d6} fire damage or radiant damage (your choice). This property of the armor can't be used again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

name: Pnakotic Manuscripts
reqAttune: by a DC 15 Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB} check)
entries: The Pnakotic Manuscripts originate from a long-lost species that once walked the world, long before the rise of humans, elves, and other intelligences. These creatures communed with the Cthulhu Mythos and were perhaps their servitors. This strange tome was written before time began its proper flow and grants insights into its workings. By reading it, you learn to move between time's beats.

entries.name: Language:
entries: {@language Primordial|XPHB}.

entries.name: Attunement Check:
entries: Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) DC 15. To end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the Pnakotic Manuscripts, you must be the target of a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Benefits:
entries: While attuned to the Pnakotic Manuscripts, you gain the following benefits:

items: You double your bonus to {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}.
You gain a +10 bonus to {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Dexterity saving throws.
You gain a +1 bonus to AC.
Once per turn while moving, you can teleport back to any spot you occupied during your current move.

entries.name: Drawbacks:
entries: You age at an accelerated rate. After one week, you age an additional week. After two weeks, you age an additional four weeks. After three weeks, you age an additional six weeks, and so on. If you remove your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to this item and later attune to it again, you preserve this drawback's progress.

entries.name: Insight-No Time to Tarry (+15):
entries: You hate any activity that takes more than a few moments. You grow impatient as your attention fades and you seek something new to do, leaving critical work unattended as you start a new project or seek out something new to do.

entries.name: Lore:
entries: The Pnakotic Manuscript allows you to automatically succeed all checks made to learn about time and its nature.

name: Pocket Portal
entries: When buried and left to sit for 24 hours, this potion will sprout and form a temporary portal to the Spirit Realm from knotted roots and mud. The portal stays open for 24 hours before closing.
{@font {@style 38|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Pocket Stomach
entries: When imbibed, your stomach temporarily functions as a {@item bag of holding}, allowing you to store any object you can fit in your mouth inside its extradimensional space. The effects of this potion last for 1 hour, after which you throw up anything consumed.
{@font {@style 38|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Poison Popper
entries: You can throw this inedible fruit at a point you can see within 60 feet of you, causing it to explode and release a cloud of noxious gas in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on that point. The cloud spreads around corners and lingers for 1 minute. A moderate wind (at least 10 miles per hour) disperses the cloud after 4 rounds. A strong wind (at least 20 miles per hour) disperses it after 1 round.

The cloud's area is {@quickref Vision and Light||2||lightly obscured}, and when a creature enters it for the first time on a turn or starts their turn there, they must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 14 ({@damage 4d6}) poison damage and is {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute (save ends at end of turn). While {@condition poisoned} in this way, a creature's speed is halved. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and suffers no other effect.

name: Pollinator Pants
entries: While wearing this pair of black-and-yellow striped pants, any flower you move within 5 feet of magically blossoms, as if by the {@spell druidcraft} spell.

The pants have 3 charges and regain {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the pants, you can use an action to expend 1 of their charges to cast the {@spell speak with plants} spell from them. This version of the spell only affects plants within the spell's range that have at least one flower on them. When you speak with a plant in this way, you do so by making a combination of somatic gestures and dance-like steps, rather than using your voice. These movements come naturally to you for the duration of the spell and magically convey your message.

entries.name: Beekeeper's Commitment
entries: While you are attuned to three magic items that have this named property, the pants regain all expended charges daily at dawn, instead of {@dice 1d3}, and gain the following benefit:

entries.name: Sting
entries: When you take the {@action Attack} action on each of your turns, you can use a bonus action to make a special unarmed strike against a creature within 5 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} piercing damage from the attack. When you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this unarmed strike, the target takes an extra 10 poison damage from the attack and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned} until the end of your next turn.

name: Pollinator Visor
entries: This chitinous mask rests over your ears and can be raised or lowered using an action to sit on top of your head or in front of your eyes. The mask has two large, eye-like lenses that improve your vision and allow you to visualize scents. While wearing the mask over your eyes, you gain advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight and smell.

The mask has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the mask over your eyes, you can expend 1 of its charges as an action to cast the {@spell animal messenger} spell from it, targeting a Tiny insect or similar creature within range, such as a centipede, spider, wasp, or scorpion. When cast in this way, the insect covers about 25 miles per 24 hours for a flying messenger, or 12 miles for other insects.

entries.name: Beekeeper's Commitment
entries: While you are attuned to three magic items that have this named property, the mask regains all expended charges daily at dawn, instead of {@dice 1d3}, and gains the following benefit:

entries.name: Bug
entries: When you use the mask to cast the {@spell animal messenger} spell, you can direct the insect to surreptitiously follow the spell's recipient for the duration instead. When you do, you must also provide the insect with a trigger word or phrase. When the recipient speaks the trigger word or phrase, the insect magically begins to record the following words spoken by the recipient and any other creature it's speaking to. The insect can record up to 25 total words in this way, or up to 6 second's worth of other sounds. Once it has a recording, you hear it in your mind as the insect magically communicates it to you across any distance, provided that you're on the same plane of existence. The message replicates the sound of any recorded creature's voice. The spell then ends, and the insect makes its way back to where you cast the spell.

name: Poltergeist Candle Holder
entries: This pewter candle holder makes your hand feel slightly numb while holding it. While holding it, you can use a bonus action to speak its command word to cause the candle holder to magically hover just above your shoulder. The holder floats back to the ground if anything other than a candle is placed on it. In addition, any candle in the holder releases a thin wisp of smoke while lit. The smoke hangs motionless in the air, regardless of wind, and dissipates after 6 seconds.

name: Pomade of Ten Thousand Styles
entries: This canister of waxy pomade has magical properties, allowing you to change your hair's color, style, thickness, and length (up to 1 foot longer or shorter per use). The canister steadily replenishes its pomade over time. It can hold up to 4 uses at a time and regains {@dice 1d4} expended uses daily at dawn. Applying 1 use of the pomade takes 1 minute.

Once you've used this product in your hair, it returns to its normal appearance after you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Hair produced by the pomade that's been cut off turns to dust after 24 hours. If you use the pomade every day for 7 days to make the same changes, the changes become permanent.

name: Portable Cannonballs
entries: This bag contains twenty iron balls, each measuring one inch in diameter and weighing 1/4 of a pound. When poured out of their bag as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, the balls function as {@item Ball Bearings|XPHB}.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can speak the command word, which causes a number of the balls that you choose to expand into full-size cannonballs weighing 10 pounds each, suitable for firing from a cannon. A creature in the path of one or more cannonballs rolling downhill must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d10} Bludgeoning damage and have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition if it is Large or smaller.

Each iron ball can also be used as a {@item Sling Bullet|XPHB} or a {@item Firearm Bullet|XPHB}. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} when you make an attack with an iron ball as ammunition, you can expand it in midair. On a hit, this attack deals Bludgeoning damage equal to {@dice 2d12} plus the ability modifier used for the attack roll instead of the weapon's normal damage.

name: Pot Lid
entries: When taking the attack action with a finesse or light melee weapon that you're holding in one hand, you can use a bonus action to attack with a pot lid that you're holding in the other hand. On a hit, the pot lid deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage. You don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative.

name: Potion of Attunement
entries: As an action, you can pour a drop of this potion onto a magic item that requires attunement and drink the rest. Once you do so, you instantly become attuned to that item.
{@font {@style 35|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Potion of Controlled Mutation
entries: This sickly-looking potion contains a writhing mass of tentacles that animate and uncomfortably crawl down the imbiber's throat when consumed. The taste is pungent and fishy, and results in the sudden outbreak of random, but temporary, mutations.

When you consume this potion, you gain the effects of one randomly determined Mutation until you start a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can roll on the {@table Mutations|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} table twice, choosing which mutation manifests. You don't gain any {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels as a result of this Mutation. When the effect ends, your body returns to normal.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Potion of Controlled Mutation requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Animus from an Aberration

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Contaminated Ichor

items.name: [Organs]
entries: Any two Organs from an Aberration

name: Potion of Dragon's Breath
entries: Drinking this potion grants you a brief surge of draconic power. Once within the next minute, you can replace one of your attacks when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with an exhalation of magical energy, which has the same effects as the Dragonborn's Breath Weapon trait. The damage type for the exhalation is randomly determined from the Draconic Ancestors table in the Dragonborn species description when this potion is created. The amount of damage the exhalation deals and its save DC are determined by the potion's rarity, as shown in the table below.

rows: {@item Potion of Dragon's Breath (Very Rare)|24GriffonsSaddlebag1|Very Rare}

entries: When crafting a Potion of Dragon's Breath, you can use the harvested stomach and gizzard of a fallen dragon in place of the raw materials normally needed to craft a magic item. If you do, the exhalation's damage type is determined by the kind of dragon the materials were sourced from, and the potion's rarity is determined by the dragon's age category: Uncommon (young dragon), Rare (adult dragon), or Very Rare (ancient dragon). Once you start crafting a Potion of Dragon's Breath in this way, if you don't spend at least 2 hours working to craft it on a given day before finishing it, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the harvested materials are destroyed, and the potion spoils.

Once you start crafting a Potion of Dragon's Breath in this way, if you don't spend at least 2 hours working to craft it on a given day before finishing it, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the harvested materials are destroyed, and the potion spoils.

name: Potion of Exertion
