entries: When you drink this potion, you gain a surge of manic energy allowing you to take another action this round at initiative count 1.
{@font {@style 42|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Potion of Fog
entries: When you drink this potion, a billow of thick fog pours from your mouth, duplicating the effect of the {@spell Fog Cloud} spell (no {@status concentration} required) centered on you. The cloud lasts for 1 hour, and it moves with you, remaining centered on you. As an action, you can expel all remaining fog from your stomach, causing it to remain centered on that space for the duration. The fog produces a scent of your choice.
{@font {@style 16|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Potion of Freezing
entries: Pouring this grayish-blue potion into any liquid will cause that liquid to freeze solid for 1 hour, after which it begins to thaw as normal. This effect can freeze no more than a 20-foot cube of liquid.
{@font {@style 34|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Potion of Glacial Resistance
entries: This brew is made from the ground horns of keppmirs. When consumed, this potion allows you to breathe underwater for 1 hour, during which time you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage. It tastes salty and gives off a slight warmth.

name: Potion of Harm
entries: This concoction is the result of a failed attempt to make a {@item Potion of Heal|GrimHollowCG24}. It is indistinguishable from that potion without using divination magic of level 3 or higher.

When you imbibe this potion, roll {@dice 1d4}. That becomes your new {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} total. If the Potion of Harm is given to a creature with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, they instantly suffer a {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} failure and begin dying if they are {@variantrule Stable|XPHB}.

name: Potion of Heal
entries: This ebon liquid is made from the remains of a downcast vampire. When you imbibe this potion, you regain all your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

name: Potion of Healing Touch
entries: When this glowing blue potion is poured on your hands, it gives you the ability to heal. As a bonus action, you can touch a creature, causing it to regain {@dice 2d4} hit points. This potion's effects last 1 hour or until you have used this ability.
{@font {@style 22|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Potion of Holistic Wellness
entries: When you uncork this potion of scintillating liquid, your senses are calmed with the smell of vanilla and honey along with a warm spring breeze. When imbibed, you feel like your whole soul is embraced in a loving hug, causing you to regain {@dice 4d8 + 4} hit points, and removing any conditions affecting you, excluding the {@condition grappled}, {@condition prone}, or {@condition restrained} condition.
{@font {@style 48|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Potion of Life Sharing
entries: This shimmering liquid changes colors constantly within its vial. Made from the acid glands of the dreaded wolfentroika, this potion allows you to share your life force with others. After drinking this potion, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to choose a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see or hear. That creature regains {@dice 4d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and you take an equal amount of Necrotic damage, which can't be reduced or prevented in any way. The effect ends after 1 minute, at which point you gain 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}.

name: Potion of Malice
entries: This brew is made from the spore sacs of three grippers. When consumed, this potion causes the imbiber to give off spores that anger enemies within 10 feet. Those enemies must succeed on a {@dc 10} Wisdom saving throw, or they must target the imbiber with their attacks for 1 minute. All weapon attacks are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

name: Potion of Near-Death Portent
entries: This potion's cloudy grey fluid has a golden thread suspended in it. Drinking this potion gives you a vague vision of your potential death. The next time within {@b 1 hour} that you would be reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and roll {@dice 1d20}. If the roll is 10 or higher, you take no damage. If the roll is less than 10, you are reduced to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

name: Potion of Relentlessness
entries: This viscous potion is made from quoxxarie blood. After drinking this potion, when you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} you can expend a {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} (no action required) and set your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to 1. This effect lasts for 1 minute, at the end of which you must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} for each {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} spent during the potion's duration.

name: Potion of Reprieve
entries: When imbibed, this potion offers temporary relief from an ill effect. For the next hour, you gain the benefit of an effect of your choice from the {@spell Greater Restoration} spell. When this potion's effects end, you lose the chosen benefit, causing the ill effect to return.
{@font {@style 45|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Potion of Rest
entries: This pale blue elixir has a jasmine flower suspended within it. It is brewed using {@creature Swarm of Bluebees|HumblewoodTales|bluebee} venom, which helps the imbiber sleep calmly and deeply.

Drinking this potion before taking a long or short rest causes the imbiber to wake with {@dice 1d10 + 5} temporary hit points. The imbiber also awakens healed of one level of {@condition exhaustion}. This is in addition to what the rest would normally provide.

name: Potion of Soft Steps
entries: When you drink this frothy brew, you float an inch off the ground and walk on a cushion of air. For the next 10 minutes, you gain a +2 bonus to Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks, and you leave no discernible tracks.
{@font {@style 29|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Potion of Spell Recovery
entries: When you drink this potion, you recover expended spell slots of your choice of levels 1-5. The spell slots must have a combined level that is less than or equal to {@dice 1d3 + 3}.

name: Poundwise Porter
entries: For 1 minute after you drink this potion, you gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.
This potion is thick and dark brown topped with a cream colored froth.

name: Power Collar
entries: This spiked leather collar is adjustable in size and has a buckle on its side in the shape of a bear's head. You can place the collar on a willing Medium or smaller creature using an action. If the creature is a friendly beast companion or a familiar (such as one summoned by the {@spell find familiar} spell), you can speak the collar's command word as part of this action to create a magical bond between you and the creature. The bond remains until the collar is removed. While the bonded creature is wearing the collar, its hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your character level.

In addition, you can use a bonus action to speak the collar's command word while you can see the bonded creature within 30 feet of you. When you do, the creature gains the effect of the Enlarge option from the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell (no concentration required). Alternatively, if you drop to 0 hit points while the bonded creature is within 30 feet of you, it can use its reaction to gain the spell's effect instead. Once this property of the collar has been used, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed.

If the beast or familiar wearing the collar is a transformed humanoid or other creature, such as by the {@spell polymorph} spell or similar magic, the bond fails when you speak the command word and the collar has no effect. If the bonded creature is a familiar summoned by the {@spell find familiar} spell, the collar and familiar disappear into a pocket dimension together whenever you temporarily dismiss it. If the bonded familiar is dismissed forever or drops to 0 hit points, it leaves the collar behind. A creature can only gain the benefits of one magical collar at a time.

name: Precipit, the Formless
entries: This magic coral staff was first found within the Great Reef of the Elemental Plane of Water. Its origins beyond that are entirely unknown, with some suggesting it was made by the plane itself rather than forged or crafted by a mere creature's hands. Attuning to the staff bestows some of its planar powers to you, allowing you to breathe underwater and ignore any of the drawbacks caused by a deep, underwater environment. In addition, while holding the staff, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.
This staff has 15 charges, which are used to power its various properties. The staff regains {@dice 1d8 + 7} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: State Change
entries: The staff has a powerful control over the various states of water. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while holding the staff, you can mentally command the staff's ever-present bounty of water to magically change its state into a gas, liquid, or solid. The properties of each state are detailed below. Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when you are targeted by an attack or spell to force the staff to change its state more rapidly.

When you do, the staff's change is immediate, potentially affecting the outcome of the incoming attack or spell. You take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when you know you are the target of the attack or spell, but before knowing the result of the roll.

entries.name: Gas
entries: When the staff enters its gaseous state, the water surrounding it becomes a fine mist. While holding the staff in this state, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning and Piercing damage.
Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.
You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.
You can move through the space of any creature, regardless of its size, and another creature's space isn't difficult terrain for you.
{@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Gas Spells
entries: While holding the staff in its gas state, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from it: {@spell Cloudkill|XPHB} (5 charges), {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Gaseous Form|XPHB} (3 charges), {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} (2 charges), or {@spell Wind Walk|XPHB} (6 charges).

entries.name: Tailwind
entries: While holding the staff in its gas state, you can expend 2 charges and use a command word as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to grant additional benefits to you and nearby allies. Until the end of your next turn, you and your allies within 30 feet of you can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and don't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} by moving.

entries.name: Liquid
entries: When the staff enters its liquid state, the water surrounding the staff becomes a swirling torrent. While holding the staff in this state, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning and Slashing damage.
Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.
You have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.
You can stand on and move across any liquid surface as if it were solid ground.

When an enemy that you can see misses you with a melee attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force that creature to repeat the same attack against a different creature of your choice (other than itself).

entries.name: Liquid Spells
entries: While holding the staff in its liquid state, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from it: {@spell Blur|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Control Water|XPHB} (4 charges), {@spell Create or Destroy Water|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB} (2 charges), or {@spell Water Breathing|XPHB} (3 charges).

entries.name: Tide Turner
entries: While holding the staff in its liquid state, you can expend 3 charges and use a command word as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to send out a wave of ethereal water to buffet and push your enemies. Each enemy of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a DC 18 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 4d8} Bludgeoning damage and is pushed either 20 feet toward you or away from you (your choice). On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

entries.name: Solid
entries: When the staff enters its solid state, the water surrounding the staff becomes a frozen shell. While holding the staff in this state, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Piercing and Slashing damage.
Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 5 feet.
You have a +3 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}.
If you're pushed against your will, the distance you are pushed is halved.
You gain 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of each of your turns, which vanish if the staff changes state.

entries.name: Solid Spells
entries: While holding the staff in its solid state, you can expend some charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18; +10 attack bonus) from it: {@spell Cone of Cold|XPHB} (5 charges), {@spell Ice Storm|XPHB} (4 charges), {@spell Ray of Frost|XPHB} (0 charges, or 1 charge to cast at level 5), or {@spell Wall of Ice|XPHB} (6 charges).

entries.name: Deep Freeze
entries: While holding the staff in its solid state, you can expend 4 charges and use a command word as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to send out a chilling blast to freeze your foes. Enemies of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 4d8} Cold damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much Cold damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of its next turn instead.

entries.name: Random Properties
entries: Precipit, the Formless has the following random properties:

items: 2 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Beneficial Properties|XDMG|minor beneficial} properties
2 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Detrimental Properties|XDMG|minor detrimental} properties

entries.name: Destroying the Staff
entries: The only way to destroy the staff is to keep it untouched by water for 100 years while on the Elemental Plane of Water, at which point it crumbles to dust. Any amount or precipitation (such as a puff of misty air, a drip of water, or the touch of ice) during that time reinvigorates the staff's bounty of water.

name: Prickleskin
entries: Drinking this potion causes spines to emerge all over your body. These spines lay flat but can be controlled by you to stand on end. When you successfully grapple a creature and as a bonus action while it remains {@condition grappled}, you can deal {@damage 1d4} piercing damage to the target. The effects of this potion last for 1 minute.
{@font {@style 22|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Prism Glasses
entries: This pair of magical glasses fits snugly against your face without needing to rest over your ears. The lenses are made using miniscule prisms that amplify color in dim conditions. If you have {@sense darkvision} while wearing these glasses, you perceive color for the first 15 feet you see in darkness, instead of shades of gray. In addition, a colorblind creature wearing these glasses can perceive color normally.

name: Prismatic Javelin
entries: This dark crystal {@item Javelin|XPHB} has a prismatic head that can refract light into beautiful displays of color. Immediately after you hit a target with a ranged attack roll using the {@item Javelin|XPHB}, it disappears in a small burst of light before reappearing in your open hand.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can throw the {@item Javelin|XPHB} at a point you can see within 120 feet of you and use a command word. The {@item Javelin|XPHB} erupts at that point in a dazzling display of color and light, casting painful {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet. Each creature of your choice within the {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} that isn't behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. For each target, roll {@dice 1d6} to determine which beam of light affects it, consulting the table below. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 2d10} damage of the type corresponding to the beam's color for each beam of light it is struck by. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

rows: The creature is struck by two beams of light. Roll twice, rerolling any 6.

name: Profane Charm
entries: This charm is a charred feather harvested from a fallen angel, wrapped in silver wire. While you wear this charm, your creature type appears to be Humanoid for the purpose of {@spell Detect Evil and Good|XPHB} and similar effects.

name: Profane Mask
entries: This cloth mask converts the words that pass through it into vile obscenities. While wearing the mask over your mouth, your words are heard as angry insults and swears instead of the ones you intend. You don't hear these words. If a creature takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the words, the creature can determine that they aren't your own with a successful DC 10 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. Verbal spell components, command words, and actual obscenities you say are unaffected by the mask's magic and are heard normally by creatures within earshot.

name: Projected Thoughts
entries: When you drink this gritty potion, a 1-foot-diameter bubble emerges from the top of your head. The bubble lasts for 1 hour and moves with you, remaining centered on you. Until this effect ends, you can choose to project your thoughts into the bubble, where they manifest as illusory but silent words or images (your choice), which anyone can see.
{@font {@style 2|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Prospector's Wand
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA}
entries: This Y-shaped wand, bearing the emblem of the {@feat Mark of Finding|EFA}, has 5 charges. While holding the wand, you can use any of its properties:

entries.name: Finding
entries: You can expend 2 charges to cast {@spell Locate Creature|XPHB} from it.

entries.name: Location
entries: You can expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Locate Object|XPHB} from it.

entries.name: Prospecting
entries: You can expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Locate Animals or Plants|XPHB} from it, with the following benefits.
You can describe or name a specific kind of mineral and locate it instead of a Beast or Plant.

You can specify the minimum quantity of that Beast, Plant, or mineral that you wish the spell to find within a 30-foot-radius sphere, such as "at least 3 pounds of Eberron dragonshards" or "at least five deer." You learn the direction and distance to the closest occurrence in that {@status Concentration|XPHB}, if any are present.

entries.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Prosthetics
entries: The brutal warfare and vicious monsters prevalent across Etharis leave many with {@variantrule Grievous Wounds|GrimHollowCG24}, including missing limbs and other potentially debilitating injuries. The engineers and crafters of the world have made great strides in helping those people deal with those injuries through Prosthetics.

When a creature with a {@variantrule Grievous Wounds|GrimHollowCG24|Grievous Wound} uses a Prosthetic, they ignore the penalties imposed by the {@variantrule Grievous Wounds|GrimHollowCG24|Grievous Wound} while wearing a Prosthetic that replaces the lost or wounded body part.
Some Prosthetics can be enchanted with magic, giving them even further powers. Rules for Magical Prosthetics can be found in the {@i Grim Hollow Campaign Guide}.

name: Prototype Thunderberd
entries: This halberd is a long-lost prototype from a nowdissolved military research facility. Electricity magically courses through the weapon along specially channeled grooves in its hollow haft. When you hit with an attack using this halberd, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} lightning damage.

This halberd has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. While the weapon has at least 1 charge, you can use an action to load a {@item crossbow bolt|PHB} into its haft toward the bottom of the weapon. Powerful magnetic forces inside the hollow weapon stabilize the bolt and charge it with electricity. When you take the {@action Attack} action while holding this loaded weapon, you can expend 1 or more of its charges to make a special ranged attack with it by leveling and firing the halberd as if it were a crossbow. When you do, you don't make an attack roll for the attack, and the bolt is magically launched forward from the weapon in a 1-foot-wide line that's 10 feet long, plus an extra 10 feet for each charge you expend. Each creature in the line must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} piercing damage, plus {@damage 1d6} lightning damage for each charge you expend. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much piercing and lightning damage. After the attack, the bolt is destroyed.

If you expend the halberd's last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the weapon becomes overcharged and splinters into an explosion of shrapnel, destroying the halberd. Each creature within 10 feet of the weapon must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 10d6} piercing damage, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Prying Mace
entries: This mace was used by ruthless inquisitors during the Upheaval, a century-long war against magical secrets. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, when you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this weapon against a living creature with an Intelligence of 6 or higher that speaks at least one language, you immediately learn what the last lie was that it told. You don't learn the truth behind the lie, only the phrase or phrases that were used when telling it. If the phrase is in a language you don't understand, you still learn the phrase, but not its meaning.

name: Psi Lenses
entries: Psi lenses come in pairs, with each shard of iridescent glass made to fit flush with the other's irregularly chiseled edge. When you touch one lens while the other is on the same plane of existence as you, you can use an action to teleport to the space containing the other lens, or the closest unoccupied space if the lens's space is occupied.
After a lens is used to teleport, the pair can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Puce Painted Stone
entries: {#itemEntry Painted Stone|TalesFromTheShadows}
For 1 minute, your weapon attacks deal additional fire damage equal to twice your proficiency bonus.

name: Pumpkin Patch Guard
entries: When consumed, this warming harvest beverage transforms your head into a Jack-O'-Lantern. From your newly formed eyes, you cast a cone of glowing light, which causes creatures in a 15-foot cone to be under the effects of the {@spell Faerie Fire} spell. At the start of each of your turns while the effects last, you decide which way the cone faces and whether the cone is active. The effect of the potion lasts for 1 minute.
{@font {@style 42|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Punch Card
entries: This old punch card from a long-forgotten tea shop somehow holds a unique enchantment, which punches a hole in the card every time the creature carrying it is hit by an attack; a hole can't be punched in the card by any means other than this enchantment. When found, the card has {@dice 1d6} punches already in it. When the tenth hole is punched in the card, the magic is released, reducing the incoming attack's damage to 0. The card's magic then fades.

name: Purging Dagger
entries: This chiseled wooden {@item Dagger|XPHB} is a relic crafted from the bough of a holy tree and is always miraculously sharp. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Radiant damage on a hit. This extra damage increases to {@dice 2d4} when you hit an Undead with the {@item Dagger|XPHB}, causing blue tongues of holy flame to flash along the weapon's edge.

When you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll made with this weapon against an Undead, you can choose to plunge the blade into the target's body and leave it there. When you do, the {@item Dagger|XPHB} emits {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 15-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 15 feet. The light is sunlight. While the blade is lodged in a target in this way, that target takes {@damage 3d4} Radiant damage at the start of each of its turns, and the {@item Dagger|XPHB} continues to emit sunlight. To end this effect, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 16 Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, removing the {@item Dagger|XPHB} on a success. Once removed, the blade vanishes and reappears on the ground at your feet or in your free hand (your choice each time).

name: Purging Rod
entries: Once per day while holding this rod, you can use an action to cast {@spell purge contamination|DungeonsDrakkenheim}. After casting the spell, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the rod melts into sludge.

name: Purity Spear
reqAttune: by a Creature of Good Alignment
entries: This beautiful {@item Spear|XPHB} has a long handle carved of ivory and is tipped with the spiraling horn of a unicorn. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While attuned to the {@item Spear|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution and Wisdom saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

The {@item Spear|XPHB} has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the {@item Spear|XPHB}, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17) from it: {@spell Calm Emotions|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Detect Evil and Good|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Dispel Evil and Good|XPHB} (5 charges), {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} (5 charges), {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} (2 charges), or {@spell Purify Food and Drink|XPHB} (1 charge). In addition, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to expend 1 charge to touch a creature with the {@item Spear|XPHB}. The target regains {@dice 2d8 + 2} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition ends on it if it had that condition.

entries.name: Charge
entries: If you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a target immediately before hitting it with a melee attack roll using the {@item Spear|XPHB}, the target takes an extra {@damage 2d8} Piercing damage.

entries.name: Curse Breaker
entries: While attuned to the {@item Spear|XPHB}, you are immune to being cursed by spells and other effects. If you are already affected by a curse when you attune to the {@item Spear|XPHB} or are attuned to a cursed item, the effects of the curse are suppressed for you as long as you remain attuned to the {@item Spear|XPHB}.

name: Purse Piglet
entries: This ceramic piglet figurine is glazed with a friendly pink coating that's soft to the touch, and it has a hole in the top that can be stoppered with a cork. When you drop a coin in the piglet and stopper it, the figurine animates and imprints on you, considering you its owner. As the piglet's owner, you can magically learn how much money is inside it by holding and gently shaking it, causing it to oink happily.

Once animate, the piglet happily eats any coin handed to it, storing it inside. The piglet will spit out exact change when you or an ally asks for it, even converting the coins within it into larger or smaller denominations. The figurine can only hold coins and will spit or sneeze out anything else you place inside it. The piglet squeals with glee and prances about excitedly when you deposit or feed it coins. The piglet can eat up to 1,000 coins of any denomination every hour it spends eating them; it will eat Electrum Pieces with less enthusiasm. The piglet remains the same size regardless of how many coins are inside it.

The piglet is exceptionally loyal and will listen to commands given by you and allies you designate. It walks beside you or the nearest designated ally in their space as best it can, but it vanishes into a pocket dimension if neither you nor a designated ally is within 30 feet of it. The figurine can be magically summoned to you or a designated ally as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} by using the command words, "Come home, little piggy." You or a designated ally can tell the figurine to return to its pocket dimension by taking a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to use the command words, "Go to market, little piggy."

When asking for 10 percent or more of its total stockpile, the piglet looks disappointed before carrying out the request. The piglet can eject its own stopper and roll over on its back to empty itself of coins when it's asked for a large amount, but it will always retain at least one Copper Piece unless you physically remove it. The figurine returns to its inanimate form when there are no more coins inside it.

The piglet is a Tiny object and can be attacked while it is animate. It has AC 10, HP 5, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage. If the piglet drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it cries out and shatters into hundreds of ceramic pieces, causing the coins inside it to scatter. The piglet rematerializes before you again after {@dice 1d4} days. If you die, the piglet becomes distraught and empties itself of all its coins, returning to its inanimate ceramic form atop whatever coins were inside it.

Placing the piglet inside an extradimensional space created by a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG}, {@item Portable Hole|XDMG}, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. When this happens, the piglet is permanently destroyed, and its contents are lost. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} is sucked through it and deposited in a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way and can't be reopened.

name: Puzzle Ring of Vitality, Life, and Power
entries: This ring is blessed by a god of life and healing. While wearing the ring, you can use your Lay On Hands on a creature up to 10 feet away from you instead of needing to touch it.

entries.name: The Outer Ring
entries: The inner, golden ring is covered by a silver puzzle ring that grants various benefits. The puzzle ring is made up of three distinct bands. As the bands are fitted together in an elaborate and ever-changing puzzle, you radiate an aura that heals and supports you and your allies. As a Study action while holding or wearing the ring, you can attempt to solve one band of the puzzle, which must each be attempted within a set amount of time and in a fixed order:

items: The first band slides into place with a successful DC 5 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. Once solved, you begin to radiate an aura in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, which lasts for 1 minute. When you create the aura and at the start of each of your turns while it persists, you can restore {@dice 2d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to one creature in it.

The second band can then be solved with a successful DC 10 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. When it slides into place, the aura's power increases. While in the aura, you and your allies have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage, and your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximums can't be reduced. If an ally with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} starts its turn in the aura, that ally regains 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}.

After that, the third and final band can be solved with a successful DC 15 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. When the band fits into place to complete the puzzle, the aura's power is maximized. While in the aura, you and your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. When an affected creature makes a saving throw against a spell or magical effect that allows a save to take only half damage, it takes no damage if it succeeds on the save.

entries: The aura ends early if you take off the ring or drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Once the aura ends, this property can't be used again until 1 day has passed for each band that you solved. If you solve all three bands, roll {@dice 1d3} when the aura ends. On a 1 or 2, the number of days that must pass before this property can be used again is reduced by the number rolled. On a 3, this property can be used again immediately.

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When Pyremaul reaches an awakened state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The weapon's bonus to attack rolls increases to +2.
The extra fire damage dealt by the weapon increases to {@damage 2d6}.

As an action, you can slam Pyremaul into the ground to cast the {@spell burning hands} spell at 2nd level (save {@dc 15}). You can't use this property again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|short or long rest}.
Whenever you score a critical hit with this weapon, the target must succeed on a {@dc 15} Strength {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} or be knocked {@condition prone}.

name: Pyremaul (Dormant)
entries: Forged from deep red iron, this massive hammer is set with a brilliant fire opal that shimmers with eternal flame. It is rumored to be currently wielded by {@book Grand Legate Phaestor, the fire giant ruler of Vulkanon|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|6|fire giants}, somewhere beneath the {@book Cliffkeep Mountains|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Cliffkeep Mountains}.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: While Pyremaul is in a dormant state, you gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit with an attack using this weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} fire damage.
Additionally, you can choose to have this weapon shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet (no action required).

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When Pyremaul reaches an exalted state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The weapon's bonus to attack rolls increases to +3.
The extra fire damage dealt by the weapon increases to {@damage 3d6}.
When you cast {@spell burning hands} with the weapon, you do so at 3rd level and the save DC increases to 17.

When you score a critical hit with this weapon, the {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} to avoid being knocked {@condition prone} increases to 17. You also roll an extra {@damage 3d6} fire damage when determining the extra damage for the critical hit.

When you kill a creature with an attack using this weapon, you can take {@damage 10d10} fire damage and immolate the creature's corpse. This damage can't be reduced in any way, and you die if this damage reduces you to 0 hit points. The immolated creature and everything it is wearing and carrying, except magic items, are reduced to a pile of ash. The creature can be restored to life only by means of a {@spell true resurrection} or a {@spell wish} spell. You can't use this property of the maul again until 7 days have passed.

name: Quagmire Maul
entries: This old, withered hammer seemingly belongs in a swamp. Regardless of the conditions the hammer is kept in, it is always damp and smells of bog water. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The hammer has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 1 or more charges and slam the hammer into the ground at a point within 5 feet of you. The area in a 5-foot-radius circle centered on that point transforms into a sickly, swamp that lasts for 1 minute. This area is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. For each charge you expend after the first, the circle's radius increases by 5 feet. While you're holding the hammer, you can traverse the magical swamp as if it were normal terrain.
If you expend the last charge from the hammer, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the hammer turns into viscous muck in your hands and is destroyed.

name: Quake Hammer
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can smash the hammer into the ground at a point within 5 feet of you or throw it at a point on the ground within 60 feet of you, sending out intense tremors in a 10-foot-radius circle centered on that point. Each creature in the area other than you must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d6} Bludgeoning damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.
Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Quakescale Armor
entries: Fashioned from the scales of a quake drake, this armor rumbles softly with the sound of thunder during storms. While wearing it, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Thunder damage.

name: Queen's Token
entries: This humble acorn is one of the mightiest gifts a Faerie queen can bestow upon her subjects. While holding the acorn, you can cast the {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell. After using the acorn in this way, it immediately teleports back to the queen who bestowed it.

If the {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell is used in a way that the queen would perceive as a threat to herself or her realm, the spell does not work. Instead, the creature who made the wish immediately transforms into an oak tree. Only a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell cast with the Queen's Token can return a creature transformed in this way to its original state.

name: Quick Change Ring
entries: This ring grows and shrinks to fit its wearer, but always seems slightly large for the finger it's on. The ring has an extradimensional space inside it dedicated to carrying armor. You can magically bind one set of unworn light, medium, or heavy armor to this extradimensional space over the course of 1 hour by resting the ring on top of the armor. Only one suit of armor can be bound to the ring's extradimensional space. Binding a second suit breaks the bond with the first one, causing it to be forced from the extradimensional space and appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the ring. While wearing the ring, you're considered to be within 100 feet of any armor stored inside its extradimensional space.

While wearing this ring, you can use an action to speak its command word and touch a suit of bound armor, even if you're wearing it, to shunt it into the ring's extradimensional space. Speaking the command word again while the armor is in this extradimensional space causes you to magically don the armor, adjusting to fit you as needed, or causes it to appear at your feet (your choice). If you're already wearing a suit of armor when you don one in this way, the bound armor appears at your feet instead. If the armor would magically prevent you from doffing it, this property of the ring has no effect.

You can create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect when you don or doff a suit of armor with the ring in this way, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor.

When found, the ring has a {@chance 50} chance to have a set of bound armor in its extradimensional space. The GM can choose a suit of bound armor from the following table or roll a {@dice d12} to determine it randomly.

name: Quickdraw
entries: This curious contraption is in fact a small, surreptitious {@item Hand Crossbow|XPHB} that can be worn on a wrist or forearm without requiring a free hand to use it. In order to use the crossbow, you must also wear two special rings on adjacent fingers on the arm the weapon is attached to. One ring carries a thin but flexible string that connects to the firing mechanism of the crossbow. The other ring is equipped with a very small but functional blade that's used to sever the first ring's string. When the string is severed, the crossbow fires. It takes 1 minute to reload the crossbow and reset its rings.

While the rings are set and the crossbow is loaded, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make a ranged attack roll with it. Alternatively, you can make this attack roll as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} at the start of your first turn of a combat.

name: Quicksilver Clay
entries: This small orb of silver, watery liquid is strangely dry to the touch. While holding the 1-inch-diameter metallic sphere in the palm of your hand, you can mentally control the form that it takes as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. The liquid stretches and turns into the imagined shape and remains centered in your hand.

Regardless of the form, it can be no larger than the palm of your hand and is always a liquid. You can cause the liquid to revert to its natural orb state at any time (no action required). It immediately reverts if it leaves your hand. Consuming the liquid is harmless, but it takes {@dice 1d4} days to exit the body.

name: Quickstone Boomstick
entries: Whenever you cast a spell of 1st-level or higher using this Rod as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you can choose to release its power in a thunderous burst. All creatures within 5 feet of you (including you) must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, affected creatures take {@damage 1d4} Thunder damage for each level of the spell you cast, and are {@condition Deafened|XPHB} until the end of their next turn.

name: Quickstone Whisperer
entries: This ancient, heavy marble torc is strangely warm to the touch. Though it resembles stone jewelry, the torc is in fact a simple symbiont which grants a limited form of control over earth and the ability to manipulate quickstone without the usual rituals. To attune to it, you must wear it around your neck for the full {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} period, during which time it coils around your throat like a snake.
While wearing the torc, you can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to transform a 5-foot cube of quickstone between its soft and wet forms, or irreversibly change it into its fixed form.

entries.name: Spells
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can use the symbiote to cast {@spell Mold Earth|FoEQuickstone} or {@spell Meld into Stone|XPHB}. Once you use the torc to cast {@spell Meld into Stone|XPHB}, the spell can't be cast in this way until the next dusk.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: The torc can't be removed from you while you're attuned to it, and you can't voluntarily end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to it. If you're targeted by a spell that ends a curse, your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the torc ends, and it uncoils from around your neck.

name: Quiver of Elemental Chaos
entries: This quiver has a lid with 5 holes in it and has depictions of the Elemental Planes on its side. It has 4 buttons along its top that correspond to each of the four elements: Air, Earth, Fire, and Water.

entries.name: Elemental Ammunition
entries: The quiver can have up to 5 arrows or bolts on display at a time, which appear through the holes in its lid. You can press one of the quiver's buttons using a bonus action to cause it to create and display 1 elemental arrow or bolt. The type of arrow or bolt depends on the button you press. The quiver can produce up to 5 of each type of ammunition in this way each day.

Any arrow or bolt created by this quiver is magical and has the following properties based on its element. The ammunition is only magical for you, and any arrow or bolt removed from the quiver loses its magic at the end of the turn.

entries.name: Air Ammunition
entries: This ammunition is weightless and whistles softly as it moves. This piece of ammunition can be fired at its long range without disadvantage and deals an extra {@damage 1d6} thunder damage to any target it hits. In addition, any magical atmospheric effect that the arrow passes through cast at 3rd level or lower, such as a {@spell fog cloud} or {@spell stinking cloud}, is dispelled.

entries.name: Earth Ammunition
entries: This ammunition carries an uncanny force behind it and turns to stone at its end. When you hit with a ranged attack using this ammunition, the target takes an extra {@damage 2d6} bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 feet away from you.

entries.name: Fire Ammunition
entries: This ammunition has tongues of fire licking up its side and spews embers at the slightest movement. When shot, it erupts into a plume of white-hot flame. This piece of ammunition deals an extra {@damage 1d6} fire damage to any target it hits. Hit or miss, the ammunition explodes. The target and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} fire damage.

entries.name: Water Ammunition
entries: This ammunition has a silky texture and glitters with watery reflections. A ranged attack made with this ammunition ignores the normal penalties of underwater fighting and deals an extra {@damage 2d6} piercing damage to any target it hits, or {@damage 3d6} piercing damage if the target is made of fire. In addition, any nonmagical flames within 10 feet of this ammunition's point of impact are extinguished when it hits.

entries.name: Paraelemental Ammunition
entries: You can press two compatible elemental buttons at the same time as a bonus action to create a paraelemental arrow or bolt: a hybrid piece of ammunition. Water and Air create Ice, Fire and Earth create Magma, Earth and Water create Ooze, and Air and Fire create Smoke. This ammunition appears from a special compartment in the quiver's lid. The quiver can create 1 of each type of paraelemental ammunition each day. A non-compatible combination, such as Fire and Water or Air and Earth, has no effect.

entries.name: Ice Ammunition
entries: This special piece of frosted ammunition is cold to the touch and casts off snowflakes when it moves. When you hit with a ranged attack using this ammunition, the target takes an extra {@damage 3d6} cold damage and must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target is {@condition paralyzed} for 1 minute. On a success, the target's speed is halved until the end of its next turn. A creature with resistance or immunity to cold damage automatically succeeds on the saving throw. A {@condition paralyzed} target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The effect ends early if the {@condition paralyzed} target takes fire damage.

entries.name: Magma Ammunition
entries: This special piece of glimmering ammunition is warm to the touch and flakes off in sooty pieces. When you hit with a ranged attack using this ammunition, the target takes an extra {@damage 3d6} fire damage. Hit or miss, the area in a 10-foot-radius sphere centered on the point of impact becomes unbearably hot until the end of the turn. Each creature within the area must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of {@condition exhaustion} from the sudden flash of heat. A creature with resistance or immunity to fire damage automatically succeeds on the saving throw.

entries.name: Ooze Ammunition
entries: This special piece of sticky ammunition gives off a faint, alchemical odor. This ammunition creates a unique {@spell grease} spell (save DC 15) at the point of impact. This version of the spell covers a 20-foot-square area, and any creature that starts its turn {@condition prone} in the area takes {@damage 1d6} acid damage.

entries.name: Smoke Ammunition
entries: This special piece of black ammunition feels smooth like coal to the touch and releases a faint wisp of smoke. This ammunition duplicates the effect of the {@spell fog cloud} spell (2nd-level version) at the point of impact, with the exception that this fog is pitch black.

name: Quiver of Energy
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one of the following damage types: Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. The first time each turn that you hit a target with a weapon attack using ammunition drawn from this quiver, the attack deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the chosen type.

name: Rabbit's Speed
entries: Within seconds of downing this potion, you feel a distinct lightness and spring in your step. For the next 10 minutes, your walking speed increases by 5 feet.
{@font {@style 1|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Radiant Defender
entries: This {@item Maul|XPHB} has a narrow Shield covering its handle that can be rotated to protect the wielder's grip. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While wielding the guarded {@item Maul|XPHB}, taking the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action also gives you a +2 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn. In addition, when a creature within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack roll while you're benefiting from the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a melee attack with the {@item Maul|XPHB} against that creature. On a hit, the attack deals an extra {@damage 1d8} Radiant damage. Once you take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you lose the {@item Maul|XPHB}'s bonus to AC until you take the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action again.

name: Radiant War Pick
entries: This silver and golden weapon is wrapped in fragments of holy vestments and glimmers spectacularly in sun and moonlight. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit with an attack using this war pick, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} radiant damage. If the target is a shapechanger or undead, this radiant damage is maximized.

In addition, while holding the war pick, you can use an action to expend a use of your Channel Divinity to cast the {@spell moonbeam} (6th-level version) or {@spell sunbeam} spell from it (save DC 16). Once this property of the weapon has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

You can use an action to speak the war pick's command word to cause it to shed bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. Speaking the command word again puts out the light.

name: Rain and Thunder Seed
entries: This seed must be used outdoors, and when thrown, you gain control of the weather within a 5-mile radius for up to {@dice 1d8} hours. You can change precipitation, temperature, and wind, shifting the weather within 30 minutes, for instance, from a clear day to a cloudy and rainy one, from warm to arctic cold, and from moderate winds to a storm. The effects of a rain and thunder seed must always make the weather less pleasant than they were before: colder, rainier, and windier, never the reverse. While the seed often produces thunder, any lightning does not strike near you, but neither is the lightning under your control.
The effects of a rain and thunder seed can be countered or dispelled by either a {@spell control weather} or {@spell counterspell} spell.

entries.name: Illusion Seeds
entries: Illusion seeds are wondrous items first created in the Shadow Realm and reliant on a supply of shadow matter to power their effects—each such seed generates an illusion and those illusions can take quite powerful forms. While illusion seeds are fairly permanent in the Shadow Realm, where there is shadow matter to empower and sustain the illusions, they are notably less permanent anywhere else. In the mortal world and on other planes, the effects of illusion seeds last for {@dice 2d12} hours and then crumble away in a small burst of glittering light and shadows.

To use an illusion seed, its owner merely needs to throw it 5 feet or more from themselves (to avoid being caught in the magical effect). Once expended, their effects are permanent (in the Shadow Realm), though they can be unraveled using {@spell dispel magic} (DC 13).

name: Ramuh's Katar
entries: This punch knife style weapon is carved from a single chunk of superconductive dark violet metal that binds to the fist and forearm with black leather straps.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against a creature with this magic weapon, that creature takes an extra {@damage 2d6} Lightning damage. Additionally, while you are attuned to this magical weapon, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls and you can cast {@spell Jump|XPHB} on yourself.

name: Rapid Withdrawal
entries: When you drink this potion, motes of pink light erupt from your body and orbit around you. For 1 minute, whenever you take damage from a hostile creature, you can use your reaction to teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@font {@style 48|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Raptor Feather Robe
entries: This luxuriant robe is made from the feather of a birdfolk spellcaster. Though it appears to be made of many individual plumes, the robe is actually composed of only a single feather, flawlessly copied over and over again by the magic that created it.
You gain the following benefits from wearing the robe.

items: Your Intelligence or Charisma score becomes 22 (your choice when you first attune to the robe).
You have a +1 bonus to saving throws while you wear this robe.

When casting a spell that deals damage to a single target, so long as you have already expended some of your movement during that turn, your spell deals additional damage equal to your character level.

name: Rat Tooth Dagger
entries: When you hit with an attack as part of an {@action Attack|XPHB} action using this magic dagger and apply your Sneak Attack to the damage roll, you can make an additional attack using this dagger as part of the same action. If that attack hits and meets the criteria for your Sneak Attack, you can apply half your Sneak Attack dice (rounded down) to the attack's damage.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Rat Tooth Dagger requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Venom

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Bark

items.name: [Natural Weapons]
entries: Claws from a Ratling

name: Ratatam's Glowskin Elixir
entries: When you drink this potion, your skin begins to shed {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} in a 10-foot radius around you. As a bonus action, you can choose to intensify this light—shedding {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} in a 10-foot radius, and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 10 feet—or diminish the intensity again. Additionally, you can take an action to produce a flare of blinding light around you. Each creature within 30 feet of you that can see must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or become {@condition blinded} for 1 minute. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The effects of this potion last for 8 hours or until you use the flare.
{@font {@style 37|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Ratbite
entries: These pungent weapons are made of leather of dubious origin with clumps of fur still attached. The leather grip fits snugly over the knuckles, with rat teeth and bits of bone sticking out the outward facing side. It gives off an unpleasant odor.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with these magic weapons. While you are attuned to these weapons, you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to magical contagions. Any creature who takes damage from this Constitution saving throw or contract Sewer Plague. When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against a creature with these magic weapons, it takes an extra {@damage 2d4} Necrotic damage and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws against magical contagions for seven days.

name: Rattling Armor
entries: This armor is made of humanoid bones and enchanted with glamours of terror. While wearing this armor, you have resistance to necrotic damage. In addition, you can use an action to cast the {@spell fear} spell. This property of the armor can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Raven's Slumber
entries: This black crystal pendant is a magical gateway to a small pocket dimension. You can use the pendant as an improvised weapon to make a melee or ranged weapon attack against a Large or smaller creature. On a hit, the target must succeed on a {@dc 10} Wisdom {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} or be trapped within the crystal. A creature that wants to be trapped can intentionally fail this {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw}.

Only one creature at a time can be held in a raven's slumber. That creature is aware of the passage of time and can see the world outside of this talisman as if through a window. You can release a held creature to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you as a bonus action.

If a companion creature granted to you by a class feature, or a beast that you've tamed as a companion, is reduced to 0 hit points while within 100 feet of you, it is immediately drawn into the pendant and stabilized. If the pendant already holds a creature, this effect fails.

name: Ravenflight Axe
entries: When you attack a creature with this Handaxe and one of your allies is within {@b 5 feet} of the target, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage.

entries.name: Swarm Attack
entries: Once per day, you can release the weapon from your hand as an action, at which point it transforms into a {@b 60-foot} {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} of swarming ravens. Make a ranged weapon attack with the axe against each creature of your choice in the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Immediately after completing the last attack, the weapon reappears in your hand. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Ravenous Gazer
entries: Acquiring forbidden knowledge always comes at a cost. Any creature that attunes to this glaive is considered proficient with it. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the gazer is a {@item Glaive|XPHB}. In its Transformed state, the gazer is a {@item Glaive|XPHB} that can be used as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}.

To transform this weapon, you must feed it your blood: each time you shift this weapon into its Transformed state, or start your turn with the weapon in its Transformed state, you take {@damage 1d4} Necrotic damage, which can't be reduced or prevented in any way. This damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: While the weapon is in its Transformed state, it grants you a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls, increases your spell save DC by 1, and gives you {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet.

name: Ready Gunk
entries: This sticky paste is fashioned from the powdered bone armor of a bone trader. After you treat a weapon, {@item Shield|XPHB}, or other item that can be wielded in one or two hands with the paste, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to summon and equip it, as long as the item is within 30 feet of you. After using this effect three times, it loses its potency.

name: Ready Gunk
entries: This sticky paste is fashioned from the powdered bone armor of a {@creature bone trader|GrimHollowLairsEtharis}. When you treat a weapon, shield, or other item that can be wielded in one or two hands, you can use a bonus action to summon and equip it, as long as the item is within 30 feet of you. After using the magic of the paste three times, it loses its potency.

name: Realmswarden Greataxe
entries: This ancient stone axe hilt is intricately carved. At its center is a gap that houses a single, perfect diamond that's magically suspended in place and glows with an uncanny energy. While grasping the hilt, you can use a bonus action to cause a wide blade of pure prismatic light to radiate from the axe's head, or make the blade disappear. The axe's blade emits bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals force damage instead of slashing damage. When you hit an aberration or undead with it, that target takes an extra {@damage 1d12} radiant damage.
While the blade persists, you can use a bonus action to expand or reduce its radius of bright and dim light by 5 feet each, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet each.

The light that comes from the diamond at the axe's center and forms the blade can be wrought to create powerful, destructive glyphs. Over the course of 1 minute, you can trace a glyph onto the surface of the axe, starting with the gem at its center, to recreate the effects of the {@spell symbol} spell (save DC 17) with the following changes:

items: The glyph you create as part of the spell exists on the axe and moves with it.
The glyph can only be triggered when you hit a creature with the axe. Once that creature makes a saving throw against the glyph's effect, the spell ends.
The spell only affects the target that triggered the glyph.
Aberrations and undead have disadvantage on the saving throw to resist the spell's effects.

entries: Once this property of the axe has been used, it can't be used again until 12 hours have passed. You can only have one glyph on the axe in this way at a time.

name: Reap and Sew
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals Force damage on a hit instead of Piercing. While attuned to the weapon, you can cast the {@spell Mending|XPHB} cantrip from it.

A special, needle-like {@item Bolt|XPHB} is magically bound to the crossbow. When fired, this {@item Bolt|XPHB} leaves a faint thread of arcane energy behind it. The {@item Bolt|XPHB} returns to the crossbow and loads itself after each attack made with it, allowing you to ignore the crossbow's {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading} property.

The crossbow has 4 charges and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a Large or smaller creature with this crossbow's special {@item Bolt|XPHB}, you can expend 1 charge to tether the target to a point on the ground within 5 feet of it. If the target attempts to move more than 10 feet away from that point before the end of its next turn, it must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.

If the special {@item Bolt|XPHB} is somehow destroyed or lost, it reappears loaded in the crossbow after 24 hours. The weapon functions like a nonmagical crossbow while separated from the {@item Bolt|XPHB} for longer than 1 minute.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This weapon is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you must make a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw whenever you attempt to begin a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. On a failed save, you are overcome with the urge to craft and are forced to sew, knit, crochet, or cross-stitch feverishly for at least 1 hour before being able to rest.

name: Reaper's Ammunition
entries: If a creature takes damage from this magic ammunition, it dies. The ammunition then becomes nonmagical.

name: Reaper's Revenge
entries: When you drink this potion, you are filled with intense and violent vigor, gaining {@dice 3d8} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. For 1 minute, when one of your enemies dies within 30 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to regain {@dice 1d8} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
The base of this glass potion bottle is shaped like a skull, and the images of scythes run up its neck.

entries.name: Heightened Potency
entries: For 1 minute after drinking this potion, when you hit a {@status Bloodied|XPHB} creature with an attack roll and deal damage to it, the creature takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage.

name: Reaver's Lodestone
entries: This stone has a hole drilled through its center, through which runs a leather thong. One end of the stone has the rune for "person" etched into it, and the other bears the rune for "gold." The stone has {@b 3 charges} and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can spend {@b 1 charge} and whisper "person" or "gold" and dangle the stone from the thong.

When using the command "person," the stone orients and gently pulls toward some number of people. The strength of the pull is stronger when the targets are closer or higher in quantity. The range is 1 mile per gathering of 100 humanoid people, 10 miles for 1000 people, or 100 miles for 10,000 people. A gathering is a temporary or permanent living community, such as a hamlet, village, or town.

When using the command "gold," the stone orients and pulls you toward valuables. The strength of the pull is stronger when the targets are closer or more valuable. The range is 10 feet for coins or art objects worth a total of 100 GP, 100 feet for coins or art objects worth a total of 1000 GP, or 1000 feet for coins or art objects worth a total of 10,000 GP.
Whether you use it to find people or gold, it pulls you for 1 minute.

name: Recall Crystal
entries: As an action, you can smash this small clear crystal to teleport yourself and any equipment you are wearing or holding back to the Alderheart council chambers.
Once used, this item is destroyed.

name: Red Claw's Regalia
entries: This dragon scale robe is miraculously insulated and comfortable. While wearing the robe, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can tolerate temperatures of 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower without any additional protection.
Your Constitution increases by 2, to a maximum of 22.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.
You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage.
You can stand on and move across molten rock, unharmed, as if it were solid ground.

entries: The hem of this robe glimmers with slowly shifting embers. While wearing the robe, your steps leave behind small motes of harmless fire and scorched earth that disappear after 1 second.

name: Red Queen's Burden
entries: This brass, battle-scarred glaive was famously wielded by a tyrannical queen. You must have a Strength score of 17 or higher to wield this weapon. The queen's intensity still burns inside this weapon, making its handle always warm to the touch. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it deals an extra {@damage 1d6} fire damage to any target it hits.

The glaive has 7 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, a magical, illusory crown appears on your head. The crown is brass and has a number of horns equal to the number of charges the weapon has remaining. When you expend 1 or more charges from the glaive, the horns adorning the illusory crown burn away in a shower of embers.
While holding the glaive, you can expend 1 or more of its charges to impose your will on the creatures around you, using the following commands:

entries.name: "Cower"
entries: When you hit a target with the glaive, you can expend 2 charges to exude an imposing aura of dominance. All hostile creatures within 15 feet of you must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} of you until the end of your next turn. The target of the attack has disadvantage on this saving throw.

entries.name: "Execute"
entries: Immediately after you make an attack with the glaive as part of the {@action Attack} action, you can expend 1 charge to command a willing creature other than you to use its reaction to make one weapon attack. The creature must be able to see and hear you. If the attack hits, it deals an extra {@damage 2d6} fire damage.

entries.name: "Survive"
entries: As a bonus action, you can expend 1 or more charges to grant a creature other than you a number of temporary hit points equal to 5 times the number of charges you expend, plus your Strength modifier. The creature must be able to see and hear you.

Alternatively, while holding the glaive, you can expend 2 of its charges at the start of your turn (no action required) to become an unyielding pillar of defense. When you do, your movement speed becomes 0 and you gain the following benefits until the start of your next turn:

items: You gain a +2 bonus to AC.
You can use your reaction up to three times, instead of once, before the start of your next turn. You can use no more than one reaction per turn.
When a creature within 10 feet of you makes an attack against you or another target, you can use your reaction to make a melee attack with the glaive against the attacking creature.
When you hit a creature with an attack using the glaive, that creature must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, its speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: The Red Queen's burden makes its wielder angry and untrusting. While attuned to the weapon, you gain the following flaw: "I can only trust one person. Everyone else is either a subject, a threat, or both." You or your GM determine who you can trust. In addition, if you are attuned to the weapon for 24 consecutive hours, your hotheadedness leaves your mind open to weakness and distraction. You are vulnerable to psychic damage and have disadvantage on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks. These effects can be removed with a {@spell greater restoration} spell, but not while you are attuned to the weapon.

name: Redeemer's Regards
entries: A bow designed for holy warriors who prefer to keep evil at a distance. Any ranged attack you make with this weapon is considered to be a melee weapon attack for the purposes of using your Divine Smite feature and meeting the requirements of any paladin spell you cast with "smite" in its name.

In addition, when you expend a 1st-level spell slot to use your Divine Smite feature on an attack made with this bow, you can choose to not expend the spell slot instead. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Redsmith Crucible Set
entries: This set of magic {@item smith's tools|PHB} from the dwarven Redsmith family includes a stone crucible that's been enchanted with minor transmutation magic. If you are proficient with {@item smith's tools|PHB} or are a dwarf, you can use an action to speak the tools' command word and lower a nonmagical weapon made of metal into the crucible and hold it there for 10 minutes. At the end of that time, make a DC 10 Strength check using the {@item smith's tools|PHB}. On a success, the weapon is magically reforged. A reforged weapon counts as magical, and when you pull the reforged weapon from the crucible, you can change it into another type of weapon that shares the same properties as the original one. For example, a {@item light hammer|PHB} could become a {@item handaxe|PHB}, or a {@item longsword|PHB} could become a {@item warhammer|PHB}. These benefits last for 24 hours, at which point the weapon becomes nonmagical once more and returns to its original form.
Once this property of the tools has been used, it can't be used again for 24 hours. In the meantime, the tools can still be used as magic {@item smith's tools|PHB}.

name: Redsmith Hammer
entries: This dwarven smithing hammer has runes running from end to end. When beaten against an anvil, the runes around the hammer glow a bright red and emanate heat, allowing a blacksmith to use the hammer to mold weapons and armor using only the hammer and anvil.

name: Refined Delerium Dust
entries: This pouch contains an ounce of purified and magically charged delerium dust. It may be ingested as an action. When you consume a full pouch, you gain advantage on spell attack rolls and saving throws against spells for one minute.
You gain one {@adventure level of contamination|DungeonsDrakkenheim|12} when you consume refined delerium dust.

name: Reflector Shield
entries: This magic shield is formed from the shell of an Anomollusk combined with leather from an aberration as its handle. It's fused together and coated in contaminated ichor and inset with a rare animus. Once complete, the shell gives off an otherworldly hue that shimmers in kaleidoscopic patterns. The shield can reflect attacks and magic.

When you take Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, or Thunder damage from a creature you can see within 60 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause the creature to take the same damage (you still take the damage).

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Reflector Shield requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Contaminated Ichor

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Shell from an Anomollusk

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Skin from an Aberration

name: Rejuvenating Draft
entries: Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

items: {@item Rejuvenating Draft (Uncommon)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Rejuvenating Draft (Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Rejuvenating Draft (Very Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Rejuvenating Draft (Legendary)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}

name: Rejuvenating Draft (Legendary)
entries: When you drink this potion, you regain all spent Hit Dice. When you drink the legendary variant of a {@item rejuvenating draft|GriffonsSaddlebag2}, your age is reduced by {@dice 1d4} years (to a minimum of 1 year old).

name: Rejuvenating Draft (Rare)
entries: When you drink this potion, you regain {@dice 1d4 + 3} spent Hit Dice.

name: Rejuvenating Draft (Uncommon)
entries: When you drink this potion, you regain {@dice 1d3 + 1} spent Hit Dice.

name: Rejuvenating Draft (Very Rare)
entries: When you drink this potion, you regain {@dice 1d6 + 4} spent Hit Dice.

name: Rejuvenation Potion
entries: When you drink this bright purple potion, you immediately gain the benefits of a short rest.
After you consume a Rejuvenation Potion, you can't benefit from consuming another until you finish a {@dice 1d4} Long Rests.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Rejuvenation Potion requires a Very Rare Workshop and the following Very Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Fey Dust

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Any Elemental Fluid

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Monster Blood from a Dragon

items.name: [Organ]
entries: Heart from a Fiend

name: Relentless Bulwark
entries: This hefty metal Shield is virtually impenetrable. The Shield has 6 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the Shield, you can expend 1 charge to cast the {@spell Shield of Faith|XPHB} spell from it. Whenever you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on the spell, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend another charge to succeed on the save instead. You can only take this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} if you're holding the Shield.

name: Reliquary of Holy Memories
entries: Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

items: {@item Reliquary of Holy Memories (Uncommon)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Reliquary of Holy Memories (Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Reliquary of Holy Memories (Very Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Reliquary of Holy Memories (Legendary)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}

name: Reliquary of Holy Memories (Legendary)
entries: This scepter holds the bones of a powerful martyred saint and are said to contain the echoes of their memories. The rod can also be used as a magic {@item mace|PHB}.

While attuned to this rod, you can prepare one additional spell for each bone held within the rod, up to a maximum of 5. The rarity of the reliquary is determined by the number of bones inside. The legendary variant of this item contains 5 bones, and you can prepare 5 extra spells while attuned to it.

name: Reliquary of Holy Memories (Rare)
entries: This scepter holds the bones of a powerful martyred saint and are said to contain the echoes of their memories. The rod can also be used as a magic {@item mace|PHB}.

While attuned to this rod, you can prepare one additional spell for each bone held within the rod, up to a maximum of 5. The rarity of the reliquary is determined by the number of bones inside. The rare variant of this item contains 3 bones, and you can prepare 3 extra spells while attuned to it.

name: Reliquary of Holy Memories (Uncommon)
entries: This scepter holds the bones of a powerful martyred saint and are said to contain the echoes of their memories. The rod can also be used as a magic {@item mace|PHB}.

While attuned to this rod, you can prepare one additional spell for each bone held within the rod, up to a maximum of 5. The rarity of the reliquary is determined by the number of bones inside. The uncommon variant of this item contains 1–2 bones, and you can prepare 1–2 extra spells while attuned to it.

name: Reliquary of Holy Memories (Very Rare)
entries: This scepter holds the bones of a powerful martyred saint and are said to contain the echoes of their memories. The rod can also be used as a magic {@item mace|PHB}.

While attuned to this rod, you can prepare one additional spell for each bone held within the rod, up to a maximum of 5. The rarity of the reliquary is determined by the number of bones inside. The very rare variant of this item contains 4 bones, and you can prepare 4 extra spells while attuned to it.

name: Requiem Bliss
entries: When you smoke requiem bliss, you experience feelings of euphoria. You summon the spirit of a single deceased person whose name you know. The spirit takes on the physical characteristics it had in life and might touch you, though it cannot harm you. You can ask the spirit questions as the {@spell speak with dead} spell with the following exceptions: you can ask up to ten questions, and the spirit cannot lie to you. In addition, you are simultaneously granted the benefit of the {@spell contact other plane} spell (without taking psychic damage or going insane) as the summoned spirit consults with others and relates information about a single question that would otherwise be unknown to it.
