If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the {@charoption Lycanthrope|GrimHollowPG24|Lycanthrope Transformation}, you can hold this rod in your teeth and use it while in hybrid or kindred form.

name: Rod of the Sovereigns' Servant
entries: While holding this rod of blackened bone, you can cast the {@spell speak with dead} spell without expending a spell slot.

Additionally, while you hold the rod, you can cast the following spells using your spell save DC: {@spell animate dead} as a 5th-level spell, {@spell bestow curse}, {@spell geas}, and {@spell raise dead}. Once the rod has been used to cast one of these four spells, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dusk.

name: Rod of Thought Projection
entries: While holding this rod, you can use an action to create a mental connection with a willing humanoid creature that you can see within 120 feet of you. The connection lasts as long as you concentrate (as if concentrating on a spell), or until the other creature chooses to close it or moves farther than 120 feet away from you. For the duration, you can communicate with it telepathically. In addition, as part of the action to open this connection or as an action on a subsequent turn while it remains open, you can choose to see through the creature's eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining the benefits of any special senses that the creature has. During this time, you are {@condition deafened|PHB|deaf} and {@condition blinded|PHB|blind} with regard to your own senses.

If the creature is unwilling, it must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or have the mental connection be established anyway. The creature is aware of the effect when it makes the saving throw. At the end of each of the creature's turns, it can make another Wisdom saving throw. On a success, the connection is severed, and the effect ends. Once the rod has been used on an unwilling creature in this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Rod of Water Absorption
entries: This hollow rod has a hole at its end and four sections that each magically hold up to 10 gallons of water. Each hollow section is capped with a ring of glass, allowing you to see inside the rod and know how much water is stored within it. The rod weighs 3 pounds, regardless of how much water is stored inside.

While holding the open end of the rod underwater, you can speak its first command word as an action to cause it to begin absorbing water for the next minute. The rod can only absorb water. If the rod is submerged in this way for the full duration, it absorbs 10 gallons of water. The rod can hold up to 40 gallons at any time in this way, and can absorb up to 100 each day.

While holding the rod, you can use an action to speak its second or third command words. When you speak the second command word, you cast the {@spell create or destroy water} spell (Create Water only) from the rod. You can cast the spell at up to 4th level in this way. Each gallon of water you create as part of the spell is drawn from the pool of water within the rod. If you cast this spell from the rod and cause the water to fall as rain, the spell consumes 10 gallons of water for each of the spell's slot levels.

Speaking the third command word causes 10 or more gallons of water to erupt from the rod in a torrent of water, up to the maximum amount remaining within the rod. This water is drawn from the pool of water within the rod. The water is shot in a line 30 feet long and 1 foot wide. Any creature in the line must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d6} bludgeoning damage for every 10 gallons of water used from the rod and is pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much bludgeoning damage and isn't pushed.

name: Rod of Wild Dominion
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Handling|EFA}
entries: This rod of varnished oak is capped at both ends with a Siberys dragonshard. While holding the rod, you can use any of its properties:

entries.name: Dominion
entries: You can cast {@spell Dominate Beast|XPHB} from the rod. When you cast the spell in this manner, the duration increases to up to 1 hour. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell. After the rod is used to cast this spell, it can't be used to do so again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Handling
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Wild Speech
entries: You can cast {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} from the rod.

name: Rope Caster
entries: This magic weapon is a favorite among infiltrators. Its firing mechanism has no string, unlike other crossbows. Instead, this weapon can only be loaded with {@item hempen rope (50 feet)|PHB|rope}. As a bonus action, you can load a length of rope into the crossbow. When you do, individual strands from the rope magically latch onto the weapon's limbs and pull the mechanism taut. You can make a ranged attack with the crossbow to fire the rope at a willing creature or an object within range that isn't being worn or carried. If it hits, the target takes no damage from the attack but is bound by the rope. If the rope is long enough, it magically wraps around the target in a single loop and securely ties itself, leaving the remaining rope to hang from the knot. If the target is a willing creature, the rope ties itself around the creature's chest or waist as a harness but does not restrain them. If the attack hits an unwilling creature, the rope falls harmlessly to the ground without being tied.
A creature can use its action to make a DC 10 Strength or Dexterity check, releasing a bound object within its reach on a success.

name: Rose Quartz Koi
entries: This Tiny crystalline sculpture of a fish weighs 2 pounds and looks miraculously lifelike. When you place or release the sculpture at a point underwater, it comes to life and swims around in a 5-foot-cube centered on that point. If placed in a container of salt water that's no larger than 5 feet on a side, the water inside becomes fresh after 10 minutes. You can use an Action to recapture the swimming sculpture.

name: Royal Blade of Amphibios
entries: This expertly crafted blade is ornamented with rose gold designs of frogs and lily pads. While holding the rapier, you can stand on and move across any liquid surface as if it were solid ground, you can hold your breath for up to 30 minutes at a time, and you gain a swimming speed of 30 feet. In addition, any creature with the Amphibious trait can understand the meaning of your words when you speak, though you gain no special ability to understand them in return.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, the blade has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you take the {@action Attack} action while holding the weapon, you can choose to expend 1 of its charges to transform the blade into a lashing, silver pseudopod that loosely resembles a frog's tongue. Until the end of your turn, the weapon adds 10 feet to your reach when you attack with it and deals slashing damage, instead of piercing, and on a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 10 feet straight toward you.

name: Royal Incinerator
reqAttune: by a druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
entries: This crimson and gold staff exudes authority and is always warm to the touch. While held, a mote of harmless fire sparks into life and floats above its crownlike head.

This staff can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} fire damage. You have resistance to fire damage while you hold this staff.

The staff has 15 charges for the following properties. The staff regains {@dice 2d6 + 3} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the staff erupts into a pillar of flame and is destroyed. The flames erupt in a 20-foot-radius cylinder that's 80 feet tall. Each creature in the area must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 8d6} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Protective Flames
entries: When a creature that you can see hits you with an attack while you're holding the staff, you can use your reaction to expend any number of charges from the staff to reduce the attack's damage against you by an amount equal to 5 times the number of charges you expend. If the attacker is within 5 feet of you, it also takes fire damage equal to the amount of damage that was reduced in this way

entries.name: Spells
entries: While holding this staff, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC and spell attack bonus: {@spell fire shield} (4 charges, warm shield only), {@spell fireball} (3 or more charges), or {@spell scorching ray} (2 or more charges). When you cast {@spell fireball} or {@spell scorching ray} from the staff in this way, you can increase the spell slot level by one for each additional charge you expend.

name: Rubberskin
entries: When you drink this blue goo, your skin turns into a thick gray rubber. For 1 hour, you have resistance to lightning damage.
{@font {@style 25|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Ruby Red Bike
entries: This bicycle has a walking speed of 70 feet. After using this bicycle to move at least 60 feet on your turn, you can use an action to produce a fiery wall in the path you took, as if from the {@spell Wall of Fire} spell. Once this property of the bicycle has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Runestone of the Wild Titan (Legendary)
entries: This mighty granite runestone is etched with complex glyphs on much of its angular surface. Though an incredible burden to carry, it thrums with the power of the wild titan. The stone weighs 50 pounds.
While holding the stone, you gain a +3 bonus to Strength and Constitution saving throws determined by the runestone's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Crushing Weight (Rare+)
entries: When you are within 5 feet of a creature with the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to set the stone on the creature to give it the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. The creature can take an action to make a Strength saving throw (DC = 16 + the stone's bonus), pushing the stone free and ending the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition on a success.

entries.name: Boulder Throw (Very Rare+)
entries: You can throw the stone as a Simple Ranged weapon using Strength for the attack and damage rolls. The stone has the Heavy and Thrown properties. It has a normal range equal to twice your Strength score and a long range equal to five times your Strength score. On a hit, it deals {@damage 2d10} Bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC = 16 + the stone's bonus) or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Recall (Very Rare+)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can call the stone back to you, provided it is within 1 mile. If you have an empty hand, it appears in your hand; otherwise, it appears at your feet in your space.

entries.name: Primal Vitality (Legendary)
entries: While you stand on fertile soil or unworked stone, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength and Constitution saving throws, and you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 2d6} + your Strength modifier at the start of each of your turns.

entries.name: Pummeling Boulder (Legendary)
entries: The damage of the Boulder Throw property increases to {@dice 3d10}, and the stone deals double damage to objects and structures.

name: Runestone of the Wild Titan (Rare)
entries: This mighty granite runestone is etched with complex glyphs on much of its angular surface. Though an incredible burden to carry, it thrums with the power of the wild titan. The stone weighs 50 pounds.
While holding the stone, you gain a +1 bonus to Strength and Constitution saving throws determined by the runestone's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Crushing Weight (Rare+)
entries: When you are within 5 feet of a creature with the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to set the stone on the creature to give it the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. The creature can take an action to make a Strength saving throw (DC = 16 + the stone's bonus), pushing the stone free and ending the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition on a success.

name: Runestone of the Wild Titan (Very Rare)
entries: This mighty granite runestone is etched with complex glyphs on much of its angular surface. Though an incredible burden to carry, it thrums with the power of the wild titan. The stone weighs 50 pounds.
While holding the stone, you gain a +2 bonus to Strength and Constitution saving throws determined by the runestone's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries: When you are within 5 feet of a creature with the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to set the stone on the creature to give it the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. The creature can take an action to make a Strength saving throw (DC = 16 + the stone's bonus), pushing the stone free and ending the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition on a success.

entries.name: Boulder Throw (Very Rare+)
entries: You can throw the stone as a Simple Ranged weapon using Strength for the attack and damage rolls. The stone has the Heavy and Thrown properties. It has a normal range equal to twice your Strength score and a long range equal to five times your Strength score. On a hit, it deals {@damage 2d10} Bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC = 16 + the stone's bonus) or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Recall (Very Rare+)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can call the stone back to you, provided it is within 1 mile. If you have an empty hand, it appears in your hand; otherwise, it appears at your feet in your space.

name: Rust Arrow
entries: Rust arrows are typically made in sets of 5 using the remains of a rust monster's antennae and chitinous hide. When found, a quiver of rust arrows contains {@dice 1d3 + 2} of the magic ammunition. Once it hits a target, an arrow flakes away into dust and is destroyed.

When you make a ranged attack with a rust arrow and hit a target that is either wearing nonmagical metal armor or holding a nonmagical metal shield or weapon, that armor or weapon takes a permanent and cumulative –1 penalty to its AC or damage rolls, respectively. You choose what object takes the penalty. If an armor's penalty reduces its AC to 10 or its bonus to AC to +0, or if a weapon's penalty drops to –5, the object is destroyed.
If the target is a nonmagical ferrous metal object that isn't being worn or carried, the arrow destroys a 1-foot cube of it.

name: Sacrificial Brand (Drawn)
entries: The carving, notorious among hunters and commonly dubbed the "Brand of Death" is a harbinger of an early demise for those burdened with its curse. Nevertheless, Steinhardt and Martyr Tulio—valiant souls undaunted by fear—carved the eldritch sigil into their own skin willingly. By bearing the ominous symbol, they sought to lure the beasts closer to them during the Hunt, granting their brothers-in-arms moments of respite amidst the chaos.

entries.name: Drawn (Common)
entries: During the three days of the Blood Moon, all Evil-aligned creatures within Luyarnha gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to locate creatures with this Eldritch Carving.

name: Sacrificial Brand (Scarified)
entries: The carving, notorious among hunters and commonly dubbed the "Brand of Death" is a harbinger of an early demise for those burdened with its curse. Nevertheless, Steinhardt and Martyr Tulio—valiant souls undaunted by fear—carved the eldritch sigil into their own skin willingly. By bearing the ominous symbol, they sought to lure the beasts closer to them during the Hunt, granting their brothers-in-arms moments of respite amidst the chaos.

entries.name: Scarified (Rare)
entries: During the three days of the Blood Moon, all Evil-aligned creatures within Luyarnha gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to locate creatures with this Eldritch Carving. If they are within 120 feet of a creature bearing the Eldritch Carving, they know their exact location and receive a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls against them, and they have a -3 penalty to attack rolls and damage rolls against other creatures not bearing the brand.

In addition, creatures bearing this carving begin to painfully bleed from it when {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} monsters within 300 feet of them are aware of their position. They can't be {@status Surprised|XPHB} for the duration of the Blood Moon.

name: Sacrificial Brand (Tattooed)
entries: The carving, notorious among hunters and commonly dubbed the "Brand of Death" is a harbinger of an early demise for those burdened with its curse. Nevertheless, Steinhardt and Martyr Tulio—valiant souls undaunted by fear—carved the eldritch sigil into their own skin willingly. By bearing the ominous symbol, they sought to lure the beasts closer to them during the Hunt, granting their brothers-in-arms moments of respite amidst the chaos.

entries.name: Tattooed (Uncommon)
entries: During the three days of the Blood Moon, all Evil-aligned creatures within Luyarnha gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to locate creatures with this Eldritch Carving. If they are within 120 feet of a creature bearing the Eldritch Carving, they know their exact location and receive a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls against them.

entries.caption: Sage's Trinkets Table
rows: A small teacup with the emblem of a talon painted in indigo ink on its surface
A ticket for one free hug, handwritten on wrinkled parchment
A tiny cheese wheel coated in a red wax rind
A delicate porcelain thimble in the shape of a gallus beak
A dark velvet sachet filled with dried lavender
A tuft of strig feathers, bound together by a worn bowstring
A green silk handkerchief embroidered with bright red strawberries
A small burlap pouch marked "seebies," filled with corn kernels

name: Sail of Favorable Winds
entries: These gorgeous sails are embroidered with swirls and contours to make them appear like fluffy white clouds. While sailing, a ship flying these sails treats any wind as though it were a tailwind, coming from straight behind the ship, and thus can maintain maximum speed without the need to tack or adjust the sails. This has no effect if the ship is becalmed and there is no wind available at all.

name: Saint Vitruvio's Phylactery
reqAttune: by a bard, cleric, druid, or paladin
entries: You can use an action to cast one of the following spells from the phylactery: {@spell bless}, {@spell death ward}, {@spell greater restoration}, {@spell prayer of healing}, or {@spell revivify}. The spells use your spellcasting ability and spell save DC. Once the phylactery has been used to cast a spell, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Crown Authority
entries: A character cannot attune to more than one Seal of Drakkenheim. Guardian constructs in Drakkenheim such as {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim|wall gargoyles} and {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim|tower dragons} do not attack you while you are attuned to one of the Seals of Drakkenheim. An individual guardian ignores this effect for 24 hours if you attack it or cast a spell upon it.

As an action, you may present a Seal of Drakkenheim to rebuke the guardians. You make an opposed Charisma ability check against each {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim} or {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim} that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you. If you win the contest, the creature is rebuked for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. A rebuked creature doesn't move, and can't take actions or reactions. A creature who wins the contest is immune to your rebuke for 24 hours.

entries.name: Relics of Saint Vitruvio
entries: These holy relics of the Sacred Flame were wielded by Saint Vitruvio and are kept in several religious sites throughout Drakkenheim. The Knights of the Silver Order and the Followers of the Falling Fire now seek these relics. Not only do both factions revere Saint Vitruvio, both wish to use these relics to help advance their goals in Drakkenheim.

A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio may cast the {@spell heal} spell three times per day, after which they must finish a long rest before they may do so again. In addition, that character gains the ability to attune to two additional magic items so long as those magic items are both Relics of Saint Vitruvio.

name: Salamander Flame Gauntlets
entries: These dark metal gauntlets were forged using fire from the heart of a salamander. While wearing them, your unarmed strikes with your hands deal an extra 1d4 fire damage to any target they hit. In addition, you can use a bonus action to cast the {@spell flame blade} spell (4th-level version, no concentration required) from the gauntlets, using either your spellcasting ability or your choice of Strength or Dexterity for the spellcasting ability of the spell when you do.

While holding the fiery blade, you can use an action to make a ranged spell attack with it instead. When you do, the blade becomes a fiery spear with a range of 30 feet. On a hit, the spear deals {@damage 4d6} fire damage. Immediately after the attack, the fiery blade reforms in your hand.

name: Salamander Sauce
entries: When you drink this potion, you take {@damage 2d4} Fire damage. For 1 hour, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage and whenever you deal damage with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, it can deal your choice of Fire damage or its normal damage type.
This potion is bright red and smells of hot peppers and spices. It is typically drizzled on food prior to eating but it is possible to consume it straight from the bottle.

name: Salt of Thawing
entries: You can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to spread this salt on a {@b 5-foot} square area within {@b 10 feet} of you. Ice up to 1-foot thick in that area instantly melts.

name: Sands of War
entries: This sand table is filled with black volcanic sand. It is 15 feet long, 5 feet wide, and 3 feet tall. While you touch the table, you have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill History}) checks to recall military lore and on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks.

When you use an action to speak the table's command phrase—"Prepare for war" in Infernal—the table turns into a 10-inch-tall, 3-inch-wide hourglass that weighs half a pound and is filled with black volcanic sand. You can speak the phrase again as an action to turn the hourglass back into a table, provided the hourglass has enough space to expand.
While you carry the hourglass, you are resistant to fire damage.

Additionally, while you hold the hourglass, you can use a bonus action to flip it and give yourself supernatural tactical insight. For 10 minutes, when you make an attack roll or saving throw, you can roll a {@dice d4} and add the number rolled to the attack roll or saving throw. Once this bonus action is used, it can't be used again until the following dawn.

A creature in possession of the hourglass can use an action to smash it on a solid surface. The hourglass is destroyed, and it explodes in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on it. Each creature in that area must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 44 ({@damage 8d10}) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Sandstorm Dancer
entries: This golden cloak billows illusory sand around you when you walk or cast a spell. The cloak has 8 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the cloak, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 15) from it: {@spell Blur|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Call Lightning|XPHB} (3 charges), {@spell Create or Destroy Water|XPHB} (1 charge), or {@spell Hallucinatory Terrain|XPHB} (4 charges).

name: Sandstorm Staff
entries: Many of the discarded weapons of the Last War have found their way into the hands of the people of the Barrens. This sliver of a broken {@object Siege Staff|ExploringEberron24} can deliver a powerful punch when it needs to, but ejects an exhaust of swirling dust when exerted.
This staff can be wielded as a magic {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}. The staff has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn.

When you cast a spell using this Staff as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}, you can expend 1 charge to gain a +1 bonus to all spell attack rolls you make for that spell. If you do so, the staff conjures a 5-foot diameter vortex of dust in your space. At the start of each of your turns, roll a {@dice d20} for each dust vortex the staff has created. On a roll of 11 or higher, the dust vortex moves 5 feet in a random direction. On a roll of 10 or less, the dust vortex disappears.

Any creature that starts its turn within 5 feet of any of the dust vortexes must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, an affected creature takes {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage and is {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the end of its turn.

name: Sangromancer's Vial
entries: This vial of red glass and gold filigree is useful to practitioners of blood magic. As part of the {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} process, you fill the vial with your own blood. Choose up to 10 of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} and roll them, reducing your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum by an amount equal to the result. This creates a pool of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} that you can expend in place of your own when you cast a {@filter Sangromancy spell|spells|subschool=sangromancy}.

Each time you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the pool is replenished, restoring a number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} equal to half the number you rolled during {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}.
If you end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the vial, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum returns to normal after you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Sarkaas' Gladrags
entries: Deven Sarkaas of Littlehand Haberdashers in Quickstone knows all too well how important it is to look one's best... and how 'best' can be very different depending on who (or what) you're meeting with. Deven stitched this fine cloak and sent it to Graywall to be enchanted, only to lose track of the garment on the return journey.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while wearing the cloak, you can speak its command word to transform your outfit into finely crafted garments appropriate to the culture of one creature of your choice that you can see. Regardless of its appearance, the outfit can't be anything but clothing. Although it can duplicate the look of other magical clothing, the outfit doesn't gain its magical properties.

name: Sash of Sorcerous Synergy
entries: This miraculous, one-shouldered robe is made from fine fabrics that have been steeped in powerful magic and fastened with an ornate buckle. The sash has 5 charges and regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. When an ally that you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell while you're wearing this robe, you can use your reaction to expend 1 or more of the sash's charges to twist the spell with one of your known Metamagic options, without spending any sorcery points. The number of charges you expend is equal to the number of sorcery points the Metamagic option would normally cost. If using the sash would cause the spell to target a second creature, you choose the new target.

In addition, when you use a Metamagic option on a spell while wearing this sash, you can change the style, color, and material of the garment and buckle. The sash's weight doesn't change. Regardless of its appearance, the sash can't be anything but a one-shouldered robe.

name: Satchel of Beast Chow
entries: This hefty satchel is 1 foot tall, weighs 2 pounds, and has {@dice 2d4 + 2} servings of magical, nondescript food inside it when found. The morsels of food come in small, halfinch cubes and smell as if they could have been made of either savory meats, enriched plants, or both. If a beast or monstrosity with a challenge rating of 2 or lower and an Intelligence of 3 or lower eats a serving of this food from your hand or similar outstretched vessel, it must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for 1 hour. While charmed, the creature regards you and your companions as friends, and you have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) and Charisma checks made to interact with the creature. If the creature takes any damage from you or your companions for the duration, the charm ends early. If the charm lasts for the full duration, the creature remains nonhostile toward you until you threaten it.

name: Scale of Kethelrax
entries: This Dagger is said to have been created by Kethelrax the Cunning, the kobold warlord of Shaarat Kol. Its short, crimson blade resembles a red dragon's scale, and tiny flames dance along its edge.

While you are holding this Dagger, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells. Additionally, you can cast {@spell Fire Bolt|XPHB} as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, using Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma (you choose when you Attune to the dagger) as the spellcasting ability.
Whenever you hit with a weapon attack using this Dagger, you can choose to deal Fire damage instead of Piercing damage.

name: Scarf of Muffling
entries: This soft and well loved scarf wraps snugly around the wearer's neck, making anyone who adorns its feel extra cozy. As an action, you can throw the scarf at a creature within 60 feet of you. The target must succeed a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw or the scarf magically wraps around its mouth, preventing it from speaking. A creature can use its action to make a DC 14 Strength check, pulling the scarf off itself or another creature within its reach on a success. The scarf can be thrown in this way 3 times, and it regains all expended uses daily at dawn.

name: Scarlet Scourge
entries: This whip is made from the severed vertebrae of a slain vampire's victims. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The whip siphons blood from creatures that it hits. Whenever you hit a Small or larger living creature with the whip that is not a construct, ooze, plant, or undead, the bone blade at its end absorbs some of its blood and gains 1 charge. The whip can hold up to 10 charges and loses its charges whenever you finish a short or long rest. While holding the whip, you can use a bonus action to speak its command word to convert these charges into healing energy. When you do, the whip loses all its charges and you regain 2 hit points for each charge lost.
For every 5 charges the whip has, the muscle fibers that hold it together loosen and add 5 feet to the weapon's reach.

name: Scepter of Faith
entries: This rod is imbued with the last remaining magic from a pious saint. While holding the rod, you can use a bonus action to cast the {@spell shield of faith} spell from it on a creature other than you within range. When an attacker within 60 feet of you deals damage to a creature under the effect of this spell, you can use your reaction to cause a spectral shield to appear before it and push the attacker 5 feet away from the creature.

In addition, while holding the rod, you can use an action to cast either the {@spell guardian of faith} or {@spell find the path} spell. When cast in this way, {@spell find the path} can only be used to find the route to a temple or other holy site. Once the rod has cast either of these spells in this way, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

name: Sceptre of Saint Vitruvio
entries: This staff can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. The staff has 10 charges. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: {@spell guiding bolt} (1 charge), {@spell flaming sphere} (2 charges), or {@spell flame strike} (5 charges). The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Relics of Saint Vitruvio
entries: These holy relics of the Sacred Flame were wielded by Saint Vitruvio and are kept in several religious sites throughout Drakkenheim. The Knights of the Silver Order and the Followers of the Falling Fire now seek these relics. Not only do both factions revere Saint Vitruvio, both wish to use these relics to help advance their goals in Drakkenheim.

A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio may cast the {@spell heal} spell three times per day, after which they must finish a long rest before they may do so again. In addition, that character gains the ability to attune to two additional magic items so long as those magic items are both Relics of Saint Vitruvio.

name: Scholar's Cap +1
entries: This hat carries with it the cleverness and knowledge of many previous scholars. While wearing it, you gain a +1 bonus to Intelligence checks and Intelligence saving throws. In addition, for every 5 days you spend researching a subject, you gain knowledge as if you had been researching it for 1 additional day.

name: Scholar's Cap +2
entries: This hat carries with it the cleverness and knowledge of many previous scholars. While wearing it, you gain a +2 bonus to Intelligence checks and Intelligence saving throws. In addition, for every 5 days you spend researching a subject, you gain knowledge as if you had been researching it for 2 additional days.

name: Scholar's Cap +3
entries: This hat carries with it the cleverness and knowledge of many previous scholars. While wearing it, you gain a +3 bonus to Intelligence checks and Intelligence saving throws. In addition, for every 5 days you spend researching a subject, you gain knowledge as if you had been researching it for 3 additional days.

name: Scorching Cleaver
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This {@item Battleaxe|XPHB} has 8 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn. As long as the weapon has at least 1 charge, attacks you make with it deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Fire damage on a hit. When you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll made with this weapon, it regains 3 expended charges.

entries.name: Erupting Slash
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 3 or more charges to slash the air in front you with the {@item Battleaxe|XPHB}. When you do, a 5-foot-wide, 30-foot-long {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} of fire erupts from the blade. Creatures in the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} Fire damage for each expended charge. The DC for the save is equal to 8 plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and the number of charges you expended. If you expend 4+ charges in this way and leave the {@item Battleaxe|XPHB} with 0 remaining charges, the weapon overheats. When it overheats, this effect deals an extra {@damage 3d6} Fire damage, and creatures that succeed on the save take half as much damage from the effect.

name: Scorned Heart Breastplate
entries: This brass breastplate is torn apart in its center by a crimson gemstone. You gain a +1 bonus to AC for every two allies within 10 feet of you (up to a maximum of +2) while you wear this armor. In addition, while wearing this armor, you can cast {@spell hellish rebuke} (save DC 15) as a 3rd-level spell from it, using your reaction. Once the armor has been used to cast this spell, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This armor is cursed. Attuning to the armor curses you until you are targeted by the {@spell remove curse} spell or similar magic; removing the armor fails to end the curse. While cursed, you have disadvantage on saving throws to resist becoming charmed, and you have disadvantage on Charisma checks to interact with any creature you find attractive.

name: Scorpion Lasher
entries: This whip was constructed using salvaged pieces of a giant scorpion and drips with a sickly venom. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with this weapon, you can cause the whip to deal an extra {@damage 1d6} poison damage. When you do, if the creature is Medium or smaller, it must also succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be pulled 5 feet closer to you.

name: Screaming Longbow
entries: Arrows fired from this sickly {@item Longbow|XPHB} let out a screeching howl that is audible up to 100 feet away as they streak toward their target. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 2d4} Thunder damage. When you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll made with this weapon, the target and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute.

name: Scribing Channeling Wand
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Scribing|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Scribing|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Scribing Dragonmark Channel
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Scribing|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Scribing|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Scribing Dragonmark Reservoir
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Scribing|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Scribing|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Scroll of Mapping
entries: Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

items: {@item Scroll of Mapping (Uncommon)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Scroll of Mapping (Very Rare)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}

name: Scroll of Mapping (Uncommon)
entries: By using an action to read the scroll, you cause the arcane script on the page to vanish and become an inked map of the surrounding area. The map shows the area in a 1-mile radius centered on the point where you read the scroll and indicates both structures and topography. By touching the map, a small light appears at your location to indicate where you are. Using a series of natural gestures when touching the page, you can cause the map to change its scale or displayed portion of the area. The scroll isn't destroyed when you read it, but can't be used again to create a different map.

name: Scroll of Mapping (Very Rare)
entries: The following {@item scroll of mapping|GriffonsSaddlebag2} is a very rare variant with additional properties.

This map is in color and displays the names of large and small locations, depending on the map's scale, such as the name of the region, street, or nearby shop. In addition, you can use an action to touch the map and ask it where a familiar person or place is that you can name or clearly describe. If the person or place is somewhere that can be shown on the map, an X appears on it at the target's location. If there are multiple targets with the same name or description within the area, multiple marks appear. If the target is a creature that's in a different form, such as being under the effects of a polymorph spell, or can't be detected by divination magic or scrying sensors, the map doesn't display its location. If the target is moving, the X follows its movements for the duration. The marked target remains shown on the map for 10 minutes, after which time the X vanishes. Once this property of the map has been used, it can't be used again until 12 hours have passed.

name: Scroll of Nightmares
entries: Using an action to read this dark scroll causes horrifying memories, fears, and regrets to violently invade the minds of up to 10 creatures of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you. Each creature must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 5d10} psychic damage and becomes {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute or until it takes damage. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much psychic damage and isn't {@condition frightened}. At the GM's discretion, non-sentient creatures, such as some constructs, oozes, plants, and undead, are immune to this effect.
Reading the scroll causes its script to flash and burn away as each word is spoken. Once the scroll has been used, it turns to ash and is destroyed, releasing a final wail as its magic is consumed.

name: Scroll of Spell Power
entries: When you roll damage for a spell of level 1 or higher, you can expend this scroll to re-roll a number of the damage dice up to the level of the spell cast. You must use the new rolls.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Scroll of Spell Power requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Monster Blood from a Fey, Dragon, or Giant

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Skin from a Monstrosity

name: Scroll of the Jester
entries: Using an action to read this scroll, your appearance magically changes to become a jester. At the same time, 8 perfect illusions of jesters that are identical to you appear in random unoccupied spaces within 30 feet of you. When the jesters appear, each creature of your choice within 60 feet of you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you as if you had cast the {@spell enthrall} spell (no concentration required).

Each jester is indistinguishable from you and shares your AC, initiative, speed, and bonuses to saving throws. On your turn, you can mentally command each jester where to move (no action required). You can choose to see through a jester's eyes, hear what it hears, or speak through it in your own voice. A creature with {@sense truesight} can determine which jester is you.

The jesters remain as long as you concentrate (as if concentrating on a spell), to a maximum of 1 minute. A jester disappears early in a plume of confetti if it takes any damage, if it's more than 120 feet away from you, or if you choose to expend it in order to create one of the following effects:

items: As an action, you can expend 1 or more jesters to cast one of the following spells (save DC 15, no concentration required): {@spell charm person} (1 jester), {@spell color spray} (1 jester), {@spell confusion} (4 jesters), {@spell greater invisibility} (4 jesters), {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|PHB|hideous laughter} (1 jester), {@spell hypnotic pattern} (3 jesters), {@spell levitate} (2 jesters), or {@spell major image} (3 jesters). When you cast a spell in this way, you can cause the spell to originate from you or from a jester that you can see.

As a bonus action or as a reaction when you take damage, you can expend 1 jester to immediately and imperceptibly teleport, swapping places with it. The jester disappears after it arrives in your original space.

entries: When the last jester disappears, any effects or spells created by the scroll or its jesters end.

name: Scumweed Armor
entries: Scumweed is slimy and thick. Dried scumweed can even make hardy armor in a pinch and more than a few monsters and witches have been known to use it for precisely that purpose.

name: Scuttling Lantern
entries: As an action, you can touch the Scuttling Lantern to activate it (causing it to shed {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} in a 30-foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 30 feet) or deactivate it (snuffing out the light). While the lantern is lit, you can command it to move once on each of your turns (no action required), provided you are the one who activated it. When you do so, the lantern moves up to 20 feet in a direction of your choice. It deactivates if it is ever more than 500 feet away from you. The lantern can move through water and across any solid surface (including up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings). If you command the lantern to follow you, it will always remain within 10 feet of you, provided no obstacles impede its path.

name: Scythe of the Harvest Terror (Legendary)
entries: This menacing scythe with a rusted blade was wielded by the Harvest Terror, a demon of secrets and fear. The scythe appears old and worn, with a handle wrapped in ancient, weathered cloth. The blade is etched with hatch marks, tallying its kills.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by its rarity. While holding the scythe, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Feed on Fear (Rare+)
entries: Once during your turn, when you attack with the scythe and hit a creature that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, it takes an extra {@dice 1d10} (Legendary: {@dice 2d10}) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Sweep of Dread (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Fear|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the scythe's bonus, no {@status Concentration|XPHB} required) from the scythe. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Harvest of the Hidden Word (Very Rare+)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can force one creature you can see that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition to make a Charisma saving throw (DC = 16 + the scythe's bonus). On a failed save, you learn one fact that it deliberately keeps secret. The creature is then immune to this property for 24 hours.

entries.name: Seed of Terror (Very Rare+)
entries: Immediately after you hit a creature with the scythe, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to force one creature within 30 feet of the creature you hit to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 16 + the Scythe's bonus). On a failed save, the creature gains the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Lurking Terror (Legendary)
entries: When a creature you can see that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition ends its turn within 60 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creature can see.

name: Scythe of the Harvest Terror (Rare)
entries: This menacing scythe with a rusted blade was wielded by the Harvest Terror, a demon of secrets and fear. The scythe appears old and worn, with a handle wrapped in ancient, weathered cloth. The blade is etched with hatch marks, tallying its kills.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by its rarity. While holding the scythe, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Feed on Fear (Rare+)
entries: Once during your turn, when you attack with the scythe and hit a creature that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, it takes an extra {@dice 1d10} (Legendary: {@dice 2d10}) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Sweep of Dread (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Fear|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the scythe's bonus, no {@status Concentration|XPHB} required) from the scythe. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Scythe of the Harvest Terror (Very Rare)
entries: This menacing scythe with a rusted blade was wielded by the Harvest Terror, a demon of secrets and fear. The scythe appears old and worn, with a handle wrapped in ancient, weathered cloth. The blade is etched with hatch marks, tallying its kills.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by its rarity. While holding the scythe, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Feed on Fear (Rare+)
entries: Once during your turn, when you attack with the scythe and hit a creature that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, it takes an extra {@dice 1d10} (Legendary: {@dice 2d10}) Psychic damage.

entries.name: Sweep of Dread (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Fear|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the scythe's bonus, no {@status Concentration|XPHB} required) from the scythe. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Harvest of the Hidden Word (Very Rare+)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can force one creature you can see that has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition to make a Charisma saving throw (DC = 16 + the scythe's bonus). On a failed save, you learn one fact that it deliberately keeps secret. The creature is then immune to this property for 24 hours.

entries.name: Seed of Terror (Very Rare+)
entries: Immediately after you hit a creature with the scythe, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to force one creature within 30 feet of the creature you hit to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 16 + the Scythe's bonus). On a failed save, the creature gains the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

name: Scythed Arm Blades
entries: These steel arm blades are razor sharp, 4-foot-long scythes that are fastened to two locking bracers made of spinal bones. The fasteners are made from fine leather with steel buckles. Delerium crystals are embedded in the armbands, infusing the blades with energy.
These magic shortswords function as a pair and must be wielded together for their magic properties to function. Attuning to the shortswords counts as being attuned to one magic item.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with these magic shortswords. While attuned to these weapons, you can activate the Nick mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you're using with these weapons.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating Scythed Arm Blades requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus

items.name: [Bones]
entries: Spine

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Plates

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Skin from any Beast or Monstrosity

items.name: [Natural Weapons]
entries: Two Blades from a Reautomata

name: Sea Serpent Hairpin
entries: This golden, twisting hair pin wraps around a tiny silver sword and gives your fingers and skin a slight grip while underwater. Whenever you use the Grapple option of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} while you're wearing the pin and are either submerged or swimming in water, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on any ability check or saving throw it makes to avoid or end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition.

name: Sea Sink Boots
entries: These weighted boots are used by the Mariners' Guild to quickly descend into the Shallows and explore the shallow beds. While wearing the boots, all nonmagical speeds you possess are reduced to 10 feet, you descend into water at a rate of 100 feet per round, and you can walk across the ocean floor as if you weren't buoyant.

name: Seafarer's Jacket
entries: This long captain's jacket carries with it an air of authority. Water slides off of it with ease and magically enhances your comfort in the ocean. While wearing the jacket, you gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and you have proficiency with {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}. If you already had proficiency with {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} with them instead.
In addition, you can cast the {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB} spell (level 2 version) from the jacket. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Sealskin Cloak
entries: While wearing this cloak, as an action, you can assume the form of a creature seal, gaining its bite attack ({@damage 1d8} piercing damage), AC 12, and 40 ft swim speed. You retain your own ability scores, hit points, and saving throws.

name: Seat Belt
entries: While wearing this belt and standing on a solid surface, you can begin to sit down in an open space as if there were a chair beneath you. When you do, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically summon an {@condition Invisible|XPHB}, incorporeal chair, sitting on it instead of crouching or falling to the ground. The chair can be of any style you choose (such as a stool, recliner, throne, or rocking chair) and can support up to 500 pounds. While it is comfortable, it can't be interacted with beyond simply sitting on it. The chair disappears if it is no longer on a solid surface or if you're no longer sitting on it.

name: Second Chance
entries: A pocketwatch that keeps perfect time is always a useful bit of kit. Socketed on any clothing or armour, this specimen is even more special, allowing its user a second chance to perform some action.

As a bonus action, immediately before you make an ability check or attack roll, you can activate the stopwatch, setting a call-back marker. After you make the ability check or attack roll (and after you know the outcome), you can choose to rewind time by a few seconds to the moment you took the bonus action (no action required). You must then reroll the ability check or attack roll and use the new result.
Whether or not you choose to rewind to the call-back marker, after you use this property, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Second Fiddle
entries: A hand-me-down fiddle that's been enchanted over time by the sheer number of bards to have played it. You have a +3 bonus to Charisma ({@skill Performance}) checks made with this fiddle. In addition, if you're a bard and are holding the fiddle when a creature other than you who can see and hear you rolls a Bardic Inspiration die, you can use your reaction to play a magical note on the fiddle. When you do, the creature can roll the Bardic Inspiration die again and choose either result. You can use this reaction before or after the creature rolls the Bardic Inspiration die, but before the GM says whether the roll succeeds or fails. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Second Skin
entries: This harness is woven from the hides of slain lycanthropes. When you attune to this item, the harness melds into your flesh, making it tough. Your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} is 14 + your Dexterity modifier. When you take Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage from a source that is not silver, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to halve the damage (rounding down).
While you wear the harness, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks to interact with lycanthropes.

name: Secret Path
entries: When this potion is applied to a pair of boots, it allows their wearer to leave a trail of magical tracks that are {@condition invisible} to the naked eye. This trail is only visible to a creature who can see {@condition invisible} objects (such as one benefiting from see invisibility or {@sense truesight}) or has imbibed a pathseeking potion. When this potion is brewed, the creator can choose the color of the tracks. The boots leave tracks for 24 hours, and the tracks last for one month before fading from view.
{@font {@style 17|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Seed of Rebirth
entries: This fist-sized, magic seed can be attuned to by four or fewer creatures over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. If each creature attuned to the seed participates in gently planting it in fertile soil, the seed immediately begins to flourish, growing into a majestic, flowering tree over the course of 7 days. At the end of that time, the tree is 60 feet tall and 5 feet in diameter at its base, and its canopy extends out in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} around the tree. The tree has a number of large limbs equal to the number of creatures attuned to the seed. Once planted in this way, no other creatures can attune to the seed, and the attuned creatures' attunement doesn't end as a result of being more than 100 feet away from the seed for 24 hours or dying. A creature's attunement to the seed immediately ends if it commits a malicious affront to nature.

When a creature attuned to the seed is dead for at least 1 minute, its soul returns to the tree, and its body crumbles into a rich soil that recreates the "enrichment" effect of the {@spell Plant Growth|XPHB} spell, centered on the body. The soul returns to the tree regardless of the circumstance of the creature's death or how far away it was from the tree when it died (even if it was on another plane of existence). The returned soul is stored in a shelled nut that the tree grows at the time of the creature's death from the large limb associated with that creature.

After {@dice 1d6 + 1} days, the nut falls from the tree and breaks apart, revealing the creature in its new body, as if by the {@spell Reincarnate|XPHB} spell. Once a creature is reincarnated in this way, its attunement to the seed ends.

When a creature's attunement to the seed ends, the tree limb associated with that creature withers and dies. The tree is magical and can't be destroyed by nonmagical means. If the tree is destroyed, all creatures attuned to the seed are no longer attuned to it. Any creature attuned to the seed is magically alerted if the tree is being attacked, if it's destroyed, or if one of its large limbs dies. Once all of the tree's large limbs die, the tree splits apart and disintegrates, releasing another Seed of Rebirth to the astral winds that carry it to a new location on a different plane of existence.

name: Seeing Glass
entries: This ornate silver hand mirror is decorated with a motif of withered roses. The mirror's reflection always shows the true form of any creature viewed in it as if the viewer had {@sense Truesight|XPHB}.
If the Seeing Glass is turned upon a vampire, the glass immediately shatters and is destroyed.

name: Seeing Glass
entries: This ornate silver hand mirror is decorated with a motif of withered roses. The mirror's reflection always shows the true form of any creature viewed in it as if it were seen by the {@spell true seeing} spell. You can see {@condition invisible} creatures, the true form of shapechanger, and the true faces of creatures attempting to disguise their hideous appearance.
If the seeing glass is turned upon a {@creature vampire}, the glass immediately shatters and is destroyed.

name: Seeker's Compass
entries: This brass compass has two needles: one large, and one small. The large needle always indicates magnetic north and is unaffected by magical effects that would otherwise mislead it. The small needle remains motionless until activated.

While holding this compass, you can speak its command word as an action to cast the {@spell locate object} spell from it and activate the smaller needle. This version of the spell has a duration of 1 hour, doesn't require concentration, and causes the smaller needle to indicate the direction of the object located by the spell. If the small needle can't detect the object specified by the spell, it spins wildly for a moment and then becomes motionless again. Once used, this property of the compass can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Seeking Smoke
entries: When thrown at a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you, this shimmering liquid explodes, releasing a billowing cloud of smoke. The targeted creature must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, or be coated in a cloak of smoke for 1 minute. A creature coated in smoke has disadvantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks made to hide.
{@font {@style 20|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Seer's Starlight Cloak
reqAttune: by a cleric, druid, or wizard
entries: This deep purple cloak is hemmed with a silver lining that radiates into starburst patterns around the head and arms. When in darkness, tiny stars can be seen from within the cloak's fabric. A constellation of stars in the shape of an eye can always be seen on the front of the cloak's dramatic hood. While wearing the cloak, you can use an action to cast the {@spell guidance} spell.

While you can see the night sky and are wearing the cloak, you can use an action to cast the {@spell augury} spell. When you do, the omens are represented by the number of shooting stars that appear in the sky:

items: {@b Three or more shooting stars,} for good results
{@b One shooting star,} for bad results
{@b Two shooting stars,} for both good and bad results
{@b Nothing,} for results that aren't especially good or bad

entries: Once this property of the cloak has been used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Seidr Rune Necklace
entries: This necklace is made of carved runes strung with giant's hair. The runes glow faintly blue. While wearing this necklace, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to learn and influence the future of one individual that you are familiar with.

You choose a type of situation from battle, diplomacy, trade, trickery, or other situation. The GM tells you if that individual is likely to encounter such a situation today. For the remainder of the day, you know when that individual is in that type of situation, and as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you may add or subtract {@dice 1d10} from a die roll they just made during that event, though you have no additional knowledge of what transpired where the individual is.
You may not take this {@action Magic|XPHB} action again until the next dawn.

name: Sensorius Maximus
entries: This effervescent green potion tastes like an old sock. When imbibed, it heightens all the senses with an expansive, almost euphoric feeling. For the next hour, you gain a +3 bonus to Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks.
{@font {@style 1|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Sentinel Channeling Wand
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Sentinel Dragonmark Channel
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Sentinel Dragonmark Reservoir
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Sentinel|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Septum Ring of the Great Minotaur
entries: This septum barbell is made from tempered gold and is studded with rubies. While wearing the ring as a nose piercing, your Strength score increases by 2, to a maximum of 22, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks. In addition, your carrying capacity is doubled, and you can perfectly recall any path you've traveled within the last 24 hours.

name: Seraphim's Stiletto
reqAttune: by a creature of good alignment
entries: This magic dagger is made from elven gold and a fine sliver of unicorn horn. The dagger has a pool of 20 hit points that replenishes daily at dawn. As an action, you can touch this dagger to a creature you can see within 5 feet of you and speak its command word. When you do, you can restore a number of hit points to that creature from the pool, up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool.

When you hit an undead creature with a melee attack using this dagger, you can expend a number of hit points from the pool, up to the maximum amount remaining, as part of the attack. When you do, you deal extra radiant damage to that creature equal to twice the number of hit points you expend in this way.

name: Serpent Dart
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically coat this {@item Dart|XPHB} with thick, emerald green poison. The poison remains for 1 minute or until an attack using this weapon hits a creature. That creature must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take an extra {@damage 2d8} Poison damage and have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Serpent Fin Oars
entries: These silvery enchanted oars are lighter and stronger than typical wooden oars and come in sets sufficient to outfit a single ship. While sailors are rowing these oars, the ship's pilot has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks to control the ship.
When a ship outfitted with these oars is adjacent to another rowed ship, the ship can take an action to slash that ship's oars, destroying them.
As long as at least one of the oars is unbroken, and that oar remains on the ship, 1 additional oar is magically produced each dawn until there are enough to outfit the ship.

name: Serpent Hide
entries: While wearing this armor, you can speak its command word to take on the form of a {@creature giant constrictor snake}. You retain this form as long as you like, but once you return to your normal form, you cannot use it again until after a long rest.

name: Serpentine Mirror
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}

name: Servitude Choker
entries: This necklace can animate small nonliving objects and have them fulfill simple tasks for you. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can drape or wrap the necklace around a Small or smaller nonmagical object that weighs less than 50 pounds and isn't attached to or carried by anything else. The adorned object springs to life, sprouting little arms and legs, and becomes a mindless creature under your control until you remove the necklace or it takes damage. The servant has an AC of 10 and a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 20 feet.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can mentally command the servant if it's within 60 feet of you. The servant can perform simple tasks that a Human servant could do, such as fetching things, cleaning, mending, folding clothes, lighting fires, serving food, and pouring wine. The servant can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds. Once you give it a command, the servant performs the task to the best of its ability until it completes the task, then waits for your next command. If you command the servant to perform a task that would put it in danger or move it more than 60 feet away from you, the servant does nothing.
The necklace can animate an object for up to 8 hours or until it takes damage. When the effect ends, the necklace can't be used again for another {@dice 1d8} hours.

name: Set of Numat's Trick Tubes
entries: This drab pair of empty ceramic cylinders are magically linked. Each tube is 3 inches in diameter and 1 foot tall. Placing an object inside one of the tube and closing its lid creates a quiet whoosh sound as the object is magically teleported to the other tube, which makes a similarly quiet thud. A tube can't send more than 2 pounds of material at a time and can't be used to send a creature. Both tube must be on the same plane of existence and have their lids closed in order for an object to be teleported between them.

name: Set of Secret Scribe Candles
entries: This pair of candles are magically linked, and they never seem to run out of wick. They can be used as normal candles, but magically won't light Paper or Parchment on fire.

If you light one of the candles while the other one isn't lit, the first candle begins to burn with a blue flame. By holding a piece of Paper or Parchment over the flame, any nonmagical ink on the page is burnt off, leaving the page unmarked. When you finish using the candle in this way, you can extinguish the flame as normal.

Once the blue flame is extinguished, the linked candle immediately comes alight with a regular orange flame, which smells of lavender and can't be extinguished by nonmagical means. By holding a blank piece of Paper or Parchment over the orange flame, the ink from the first page is magically burnt onto the new one over the course of 1 minute as the candle heats it. Once all the ink has been transcribed onto a new page in this way, the orange flame winks out.

name: Seven Cryptical Books of Hsan
reqAttune: by a DC 20 Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB} check)
entries: These seven scrolls each cover a different topic concerning the relationship between the gods, the material world, and the planes. Those who master them can create doors to other worlds.

entries.name: Language:
entries: {@language Celestial|XPHB}.

entries.name: Attunement Check:
entries: Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) DC 20. To end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the Seven Cryptical Books of Hsan, you must visit each of the seven realms that it allows access to.

entries.name: Benefits:
entries: While attuned to the Seven Cryptical Books of Hsan, you gain the following benefits:

items: If you have the spellcasting class feature, you can prepare one additional spell for each spell level you can cast. That spell must be chosen from the Cleric spell list.
You gain a +1 bonus to the DC of any spell you cast that is on the Cleric spell list.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Wisdom saving throws.
You gain one additional spell slot of the highest level you can use.

You can cast {@spell Gate|XPHB} once per day without expending a spell slot. Wisdom is your casting ability for this spell. When you cast it, you open a gate to a location described in the books. If you use this feature again while at the location, the spell connects to the second location in the books. There are seven such locations, and using this feature at the seventh one returns you to the place where you first used this ability. The specific locations are left to the DM to decide, but legend has it that each is a domain of a long forgotten deity since claimed by agents of the Cthulhu Mythos.

entries.name: Drawbacks:
entries: You have an overwhelming drive to use the books to visit the realms it allows you to access. If you go a week without using the Gate feature, you gain a level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} that you cannot lose until you cast {@spell Gate|XPHB} using this item and travel through the portal you created.

entries.name: Insight-Enemy of the Dark (+20):
entries: You are an ardent foe of the Cthulhu Mythos. When you encounter their agents and entities, you are compelled to defeat them and drive them back to the dark corners of the cosmos that spawned them. You struggle to leave any location that has been overrun with their foul evil.

entries.name: Lore:
entries: The Seven Cryptical Books of Hsan allows you to automatically succeed all checks made to learn about dead gods.

name: Severed Reaction
entries: Consuming this foggy brew gives you a headache you can never quite alleviate. While under the effects of this potion, you can take two reactions each round instead of one. Each time you take a second reaction, you lose a number of hit points equal to half your level. This potion's effect is {@b permanent}, and it doesn't count against the number of potions you can have affecting you at once.
{@font {@style 59|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Shaarat'doovol, the Blade of Truth
entries: This blade was forged in khaar'draguus, the lava pits below Sharn, and wielded by an ancient Dhakaani hero who fell in battle against the daelkyr Belashyrra. A sentience lies within the blade; it doesn't communicate with words, but while attuned, you can feel its emotions and desires. Shaarat'doovol was forged to protect the innocent from the machinations of the daelkyr, and if it feels you are serving that purpose, it can grant great power.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit an Aberration with this weapon, the Aberration takes an extra {@damage 2d10} Radiant damage.

entries.name: Unyielding Duty
entries: If you have the favor of the sword, it guides you and shields you from unnatural influences. While wielding this sword, it can choose to grant you the following benefits:

items.name: Truesight
entries: You gain {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 90 feet.

items.name: Fortified Mind
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

name: Shadow Channeling Wand
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Shadow Child
entries: You are filled with intense feelings of confusion before an apparition emerges from your body that resembles a young girl with onyx skin and hair and piercing green eyes. Only you can see it, and it can't speak. It functions as the {@spell Unseen Servant} spell and lasts for 1 hour.
{@font {@style 25|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Shadow Dragonmark Channel
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Shadow Dragonmark Reservoir
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.
