Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Shadow Drinker
entries: This wicked {@item Dagger|XPHB} can absorb the shadows cast by your foes. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a Small or larger enemy with a melee attack roll using this {@item Dagger|XPHB}, you can choose to absorb that creature's shadow as part of the attack.

When you do, the creature no longer casts a shadow, and the {@item Dagger|XPHB} becomes shrouded in a dark haze, which extends to surround you while you're holding the {@item Dagger|XPHB}. As long as the haze is surrounding you, you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition while you're entirely in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}.

The dark haze remains for up to 10 minutes. A creature hit by the shrouded {@item Dagger|XPHB} takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage from the attack; this extra damage increases to {@dice 2d6} if the target is the creature missing its shadow. The haze ends early immediately after you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell, or if you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end it. Once the haze ends, the shadow immediately returns to the creature from whom it was taken.
You can only have one shadow absorbed in this way at a time. Once the {@item Dagger|XPHB} steals a creature's shadow, it can't steal that creature's shadow again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This {@item Dagger|XPHB} is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic. As long as you remain cursed, you have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Radiant damage.

name: Shadow Grimoire
entries: This thick tome is covered in inky black nightmare hide and bound with iron overlaid with silver. Delicate silver runes are inlaid in a circular pattern across the cover. The pages within are written in silver ink on jet-black paper. The book is extremely well-crafted, durable, and waterproof and measures just over 12 inches tall, 9 inches wide and 1 inch thick.
While the grimoire is on your person, you have advantage on all skill checks pertaining to shadow or darkness magic, geography, history, and denizens of the Shadow Realm.

entries.name: Sentience
entries: The Shadow Grimoire is a sentient neutral spellbook with an Intelligence of 15, a Wisdom of 15, and a Charisma of 14. It has an Armor Class of 15 and 20 hit points. It regains {@dice 1d8 + 4} hit points each evening at dusk. It has hearing and normal vision out to a range of 30 feet and {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 60 feet.
The book can speak, read, and understand Common and Umbral and can communicate with its owner telepathically out to a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Personality
entries: The Shadow Grimoire is intelligent, haughty, and extremely proud of its abilities and its unique nature. Once it decides to reveal its sentience and awareness, it expects to be treated in every way like a highly regarded equal. If the grimoire is confident its owner shares its outlook and goals, it reveals its abilities and complies with most requests.

It is often mysterious, cryptic, and prone to falling silent for long periods of time without cause or explanation. If it feels it is being mistreated or not shown the proper level of respect, the grimoire snaps itself shut and refuses to open or use any of its abilities until the situation changes to its satisfaction.

The grimoire has little interest in good or evil, law or chaos. Its primary interests lie in magic, specifically shadow and darkness magic or anything pertaining to the Shadow Realm. The grimoire is single-minded in its desire to learn all it can about shadow magic, and it expects its owner to share this desire. It insists that its owner prepare at least a few of the spells contained within its pages every day (the more, the better, of course). If the owner refuses, the grimoire may (at the GM's discretion) demand to be given to someone more worthy of it, make it impossible for its owner to attune to it, suppress one or more of its properties, or attempt to take control of its owner.

If the Shadow Grimoire attempts to take control of its owner, the owner must make a Charisma saving throw with a DC equal to 12 + the grimoire's Charisma modifier. On a failed save, the owner is {@condition charmed} by the grimoire for {@dice 1d12} hours. While {@condition charmed}, the owner must try to follow the grimoire's commands. Whether the attempt to control its owner succeeds or fails, the Shadow Grimoire can't use this power again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Bookish
entries: As an action, the Shadow Grimoire can open and close itself and flip instantly to any page it desires, including the current scroll page (see below). A DC 25 Strength check is required to close it, pry it open, or tear out a page against its will.

entries.name: Shadow Jump (3/Day)
entries: The Shadow Grimoire can move from one shadow into another. As a bonus action, when the grimoire is in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} or darkness, it can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see that is also in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} or darkness.

entries.name: Sunlight Vulnerability
entries: The Shadow Grimoire must always remain cloaked in shadow or the darkness of night. The grimoire is damaged if exposed to direct sunlight (not merely a {@spell daylight} spell). For every minute the Shadow Grimoire is exposed to sunlight, it takes {@damage 1d8} radiant damage. If this damage exceeds the book's total hit points, the Shadow Grimoire bursts into gray flame and is forever destroyed.

entries.name: Warded
entries: The Shadow Grimoire is protected by a {@spell glyph of warding}. The glyph can be triggered by the grimoire if it feels threatened. The glyph causes explosive runes to erupt in a 20-foot-radius sphere of crackling, shadowy energy. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 5d8} cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once the glyph of warding goes off, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Enveloped by Shadows (Requires Attunement)
entries: The Shadow Grimoire's secrets cling to your mind like the shadow realm itself. Only you can read its contents; to all others, its pages appear pure black. As your level increases, you gain the following benefits while holding or carrying this book.

items.name: 5th level
entries: The Shadow Grimoire is a spellbook that contains the following spells (see {@i Deep Magic} by Kobold Press):
Cantrips: {@spell claws of darkness|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell douse light|bookofebontides}, {@spell shadow bite|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell shadow blindness|TalesFromTheShadows}
1st level: {@spell black ribbons|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell cloak of shadow|bookofebontides}, {@spell shadow armor|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell shadow hands|TalesFromTheShadows}

2nd level: {@spell dark path|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell darkbolt|bookofebontides}, {@spell negative image|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell shadow puppets|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell slither|bookofebontides}
3rd level: {@spell call shadow mastiff|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell shadow tendrils|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell shadow trove|TalesFromTheShadows}
4th level: {@spell black hand|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell hide in one's shadow|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell shadow step|bookofebontides}
5th level: {@spell dark dementing|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell shadow gateway|bookofebontides}
6th level: {@spell become nightwing|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell black well|TalesFromTheShadows}
7th level: {@spell conjure shadow titan|TalesFromTheShadows}, {@spell dying of the light|TalesFromTheShadows}
8th level: {@spell creeping darkness|TalesFromTheShadows}
9th level: {@spell umbral storm|TalesFromTheShadows}

In addition, the Shadow Grimoire contains a special scroll page—a single spell from among the spells transcribed within it, that you may cast directly from the book as if it were a scroll. Once the spell is cast, another spell (other than the one just cast) randomly becomes the next spell that can be cast directly from the book. The spell is always of a level you can cast. You must spend an action to flip pages and find the new scroll-page spell. Once found, the scroll page can be marked for future reference. You do not need to provide a material component and casting the spell does not remove it from the spellbook. Once you have used the scroll page 3 times, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

items.name: 9th level
entries: You gain {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 30 feet. If you already have {@sense darkvision}, you can see in magical darkness out to a range of 30 feet as if in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light}. In addition, the Shadow Grimoire's {@spell glyph of warding} saving throw DC increases to 14, and the cold damage increases to {@dice 6d8}.

items.name: 13th level
entries: When the area you occupy is in {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} or darkness, you can use a bonus action to step through the shadow and emerge from another shadow up to 200 feet away.

In addition, the Shadow Grimoire's Intelligence becomes 16, its Wisdom 16, its Charisma 15, its Armor Class 17, and its hit points 25. Finally, the grimoire's {@spell glyph of warding} saving throw DC increases to 15, and the cold damage increases to {@dice 7d8}.

items.name: 17th level
entries: You can use an action to transport yourself and up to eight willing creatures to the Shadow Realm as if you had cast the {@spell plane shift} spell. You can't do this again until you finish a long rest. In addition, as an action, you may now choose which spell in the grimoire becomes a scroll page.

entries.name: GM Note
entries: The Shadow Grimoire is a powerful magic item. It is important to remember the Shadow Grimoire is the final authority on if and when its powers are used. The grimoire typically acquiesces to the owner's wishes, but that is hardly absolute—it always retains full control of its abilities. Essentially, the GM should treat the Shadow Grimoire as an NPC as well as a magic item, which makes it an excellent tool for dispensing special clues and other campaign information that might not be easy to convey otherwise. The grimoire can be a teacher and mentor as well as a mysterious source of secrets and knowledge.

If a PC decides to keep the grimoire, the GM should observe and cultivate the symbiotic relationship between them carefully. While the Shadow Grimoire retains control over its special abilities, it still relies on its owner to carry it around so it can learn and influence events.

entries.name: Fabled Items
entries: The Shadow Grimoire is a fabled item. Fabled items are a special kind of magic item that scales in power as the character does. Fabled items encompass all levels of rarity.

{@creature The Dusk Queen|TalesFromTheShadows} received the Shadow Grimoire as a gift while she still dwelt in the realm of shadow. Little is known about who gave her the grimoire or the motives behind the gift. Some say it was to aid the Dusk Queen in bringing darkness to the realms of light, others say it was secretly a means for her enemies to thwart her plans.

Whatever the case, the mysterious Dusk Queen bonded with the dark tome and used its strange abilities to amass great power on the Material Plane. Many whisper that the Shadow Grimoire was perhaps the Dusk Queen's most prized possession.
Properties and Attunement
A fabled magic item begins as a common magic item. It grants a small but useful property to any character that possesses it. This minor property does not require attunement to use.

To utilize any of the higher-level properties, a character must attune to the fabled item per the standard magic item attunement rules. Once attuned to the fabled magic item, the character can use the fabled item's more powerful properties as the character increases in level. When an attuned character reaches a property's specified level, the property listed at that level becomes immediately available to the character.

If a character of a level higher than 1st attunes to a fabled item, the item's level-dependent properties, up to the character's current level, become available to the character. If a character chooses not to become attuned to the fabled item, the item remains a common magic item, granting the character only its minor property, regardless of the character's level. Unless otherwise noted, all properties granted by a fabled item are in effect if the character is wearing, carrying, or touching the item.
For much more information about fabled items, see Vault of Magic from Kobold Press.

rows: Bonus Action, Shadow Grimoire Stat Increase, {@spell Glyph of Warding} Increase

name: Shadow Ink
entries: Once penned, this special ink can only be seen and read in total darkness. While in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, any written or tattooed words, illustrations, or other marks made with the ink glow with a soft, colored light. One bottle of Shadow Ink provides enough ink to fill 50 pages with writing, illustrations, or other such markings.

A {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} spell reveals only that there is something faintly magical about the area where this ink has been used, but it doesn't reveal the kind of magic or how to interact with it.

name: Shadow Portal Scroll
entries: Written on black leather in letters of glowing white, a shadow portal scroll opens a portal as a form of invitation from a fey enchanter, goblin shaman, or other powerful arcanist of the Shadow Realm. All creatures within 10 feet of you when the scroll is read are transported to the Shadow Realm, usually near the scroll maker's residence.

name: Shadow Puppet
entries: Once consumed, this potion gives sentience to your shadow. The shadow starts to act independently of you but is still bound to your body. It has its own emotions and personality but can't interact with the world in any way beyond what a normal shadow could. The effects of this potion last until removed, as if it were a curse. This doesn't count against the number of potions you can have affecting your body at once.
{@font {@style 46|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Shadow Sibling
entries: Crafted by Dyrrn the Corruptor, this black jewel-like object fuses to the center of your forehead when you attune to it. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can cause the sibling to exude or retract an ectoplasmic shadow that surrounds your body and conceals you from prying eyes. While the shadow is active, Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made to see you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made to {@action Hide|XPHB}.

In addition, when you are hit by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend one Hit Die to shield yourself. Roll the die and add the result to your AC, including against the triggering attack. This bonus lasts until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

name: Shadow Tag
entries: This silver coin is embossed with the visage of a hooded, near-faceless figure with eyes that are always dark. While holding the coin, you can use an action to whisper its command word and toss it into a creature's shadow that you can see within 10 feet of you. When you do, the coin magically dissolves and tags the creature's shadow, causing a smoky, pitch-dark copy of the coin to appear in your hand instead.

While you're within 1000 feet of the tagged creature's shadow, small points of light appear within the dark coin's eyes that look in the shadow's direction. If the dark coin's eyes are looking toward the shadow, you can grasp the coin and use an action to speak its command word again, destroying the coin and immediately teleporting you to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the tagged creature. Alternatively, when you destroy the coin, you can force the tagged creature to make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature teleports to an unoccupied space on solid ground that you can see within 15 feet of you. A creature can choose to fail the saving throw.

If the tagged creature doesn't have a shadow, such as if it becomes {@condition invisible}, the dark coin's eyes disappear until the creature's shadow reappears. The dark coin remains for 24 hours or until you destroy it. If the dark coin lasts for its full duration, there is a {@chance 50} chance that the normal coin reappears and replaces it. If the coin doesn't reappear at the end of the duration, it's destroyed.

name: Shadow Ward
entries: This eerily still cloak seems to absorb some of the light that touches it. While wearing the cloak, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks. In addition, the cloak has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dusk. When you're hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to halve the attack's damage against you (round down) and teleport in a plume of black smoke to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you.

name: Shadow Weaver's Guise
entries: This patchwork gray cloak has three bone clasps at its neck. Whenever you cast an evocation spell that deals damage while wearing this cloak, you can choose to change its damage type to necrotic for that casting of the spell.

entries.name: Curse
entries: Once you don this cursed cloak, you are unwilling to remove it unless you are targeted by the {@spell remove curse} spell or similar magic. While wearing the cloak, you are considered to be undead whenever you are in dim light or darkness. In addition, if you can normally cast the {@spell light} or {@spell dancing lights} cantrips, you are unable to cast them while wearing the cloak.

name: Shadowscale Shroud
entries: Enchanted by powerful drow, this dark and shadowy dragon scale armor protects you from both damage and light. While wearing this armor, you have a +2 bonus to AC and resistance to necrotic damage, and if you have the Sunlight Sensitivity trait, you are unaffected by it.

In addition, this armor doesn't impose disadvantage on your Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks, and when you attempt to hide in areas of dim light or darkness while wearing it, you gain a +5 bonus to the roll.

entries.name: Shadow Shift
entries: While in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use an action to turn {@condition invisible}. You remain {@condition invisible} for up to 10 minutes or until you use a bonus action to become visible again. You become visible early if you enter an area of bright light or if you attack or cast a spell. While you're {@condition invisible} in this way, you have resistance to all damage except force and radiant, and you can use a bonus action to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness. In addition, while you're {@condition invisible} in this way, you can't be targeted by any divination magic or perceived through magical scrying sensors against your will.

Once this property of the armor has been used, it shouldn't be used again until the next dusk. Each time it is used again before then, you must expend either 6 Hit Dice, rolling each one and taking force damage equal to the total rolled, or suffer one level of {@condition exhaustion} (your choice). Force damage taken in this way ignores resistance and immunity.

name: Shadowshawl
entries: This light gray shawl is made of thick fabric that looks like woven spider webs. While wearing the shawl with its hood up, your face is hidden within a small pocket of magical {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, and you have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. If you already had {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, its range increases by 60 feet. You can see through the hood's pocket of {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} as if it were nonmagical.
In addition, while the hood is up, light-based effects (such as the {@spell Sunbeam|XPHB} spell) can't cause you to have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition.

name: Shadowsmoke Dragon Pipe
entries: This magic pipe leaves behind odorless smoke that dissipates quickly. Its head easily detaches, allowing you to refill it. The pipe has 4 charges and regains {@dice 1d3 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 1 charge to blow a small, condensed ring of smoke at yourself or an ally that you can see within 30 feet of you.

When you do, the target can choose to immediately gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition (no action required), or it can choose to wear the smoke as if it were a physical ring. A creature can only wear one of these smoke rings at a time, and it lasts for 1 minute or until the creature takes a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. A creature that turns {@condition Invisible|XPHB} in either way has that condition until the start of its next turn or until it makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.

name: Shadowsteel Focus
entries: Shadowsteel Focus is a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} that contains some amount of Shadowsteel. Any {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} can be made as a Shadowsteel Focus.

There is no benefit to using a Shadowsteel Focus instead of a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}; however, a spellcaster with the {@feat Shadowsteel Adept|GrimHollowPG24} and {@feat Shadowsteel Master|GrimHollowPG24} feats can gain the benefits associated with that feat when they use a Shadowsteel Focus.

name: Shaedenstaff
reqAttune: by a Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard
entries: This staff is made from the reclaimed horn of a huge Undead creature. While you're attuned to the staff, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to resist mental stress effects. The staff can also be wielded as a magic {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}.

The staff has 15 charges for the following properties and regains {@dice 2d6 + 3} expended charges daily at dusk. If you expend the last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the staff disintegrates in a plume of pitch black smoke and emits a terrifying scream audible out to 300 feet.

entries.name: Annihilating Strike
entries: When you hit with a melee attack using this staff, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage to the target.

entries.name: Spells
entries: While holding the staff, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: {@spell Calm Emotions|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Darkness|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Dispel Evil and Good|XPHB} (5 charges), {@spell Inflict Wounds|XPHB} (level 3 version, 3 charges), or {@spell Circle of Death|XPHB} (6 charges).

name: Shape-Shifter's Circlet
entries: This ivory circlet allows you to recreate some of the natural features of other creatures. While wearing the circlet, you can spend 1 minute to gently massage your ears, forehead, or temples. When you do, you can choose to create one of the following features or effects:

items: You can cover or replace your own ears with the form of another creature's.
You can cause one or more horns or antlers to grow atop your head.
You can change your eyes, including their color and pupil shape.

entries: You can only have 1 of these effects active at a time. The effect lasts until you dismiss it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, remove the circlet, or have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition. You don't gain any of the senses or abilities of another creature by recreating its physical features in this way.

name: Shard
entries: Delerium is a magical mineral left behind by the meteor that landed in Drakkenheim. It appears in geode clusters of translucent, sharp-edged crystals which reflect octarine light. The eldritch stones softly hum in dissonant tones, and glow brightly at night or when exposed to magic. Deposits are found throughout Drakkenheim, often fused into stone streets and buildings like crystalline moss.
A typical delerium fragment is about the size of a finger. Crystals may be fist-sized or slightly larger, and geodes may be as big as a pumpkin. Massive clusters might grow taller than a human.

entries.name: Delerium Properties
entries: All delerium samples have the following traits regardless of size:

items: {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage; as well as Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from non-magical weapons.
{@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistant} to Acid, Cold, Fire, and Lightning damage; as well as Slashing and Piercing damage from magical weapons.
{@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerable} to Bludgeoning damage from magical weapons.

Unless contained within an {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}, delerium shatters and crumbles into worthless ash when reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. However, delerium geodes release a random {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} when destroyed.

entries.name: Delerium Hazards
entries: When a humanoid creature touches delerium without protective gear for the first time on their turn, or ends their turn in bodily contact with delerium, they must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage and gain one level of {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.

entries.name: Delerium Harvesting
entries: Delerium found in Drakkenheim is usually fused into the ground or stone buildings. It is carefully extracted using handheld mining equipment such as shovels, picks, hammers, and chisels. Consult the table to determine how long it takes characters to extract delerium. Lacking proper equipment, extraction takes ten times as long. Massive clusters are impossible to extract without heavy equipment or powerful magic.

entries.name: Uses for Delerium
entries: Delerium has vast arcane potential. Beyond trade, crystals are used for several purposes:

entries.name: Spell Component
entries: Delerium may be used as an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} or material component for any spell on the sorcerer, warlock, or wizard spell list. When casting a spell which requires a costly material component, a spellcaster may instead use delerium of equivalent or greater value to the required cost.

entries.name: Magic Items
entries: Delerium is an exceptional material for creating magical items of all kinds. Any existing magic item described in the Basic Rules could be made with delerium. Fragments, shards, crystals, and geodes may be used to make uncommon, rare, very rare, and legendary items respectively. At the GM's discretion, characters who can cast level 5 spells or higher may learn techniques to craft magic items of their own during their downtime.

entries.name: Stable Delerium
entries: The process for crafting magic items with delerium renders the crystals stable. Unless otherwise specified, characters do not take damage nor risk {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} when they touch or handle stable delerium. Stable delerium is damaged and destroyed in the same manner as a normal magic item of its kind.

entries.name: Delerium Dust
entries: Delerium dust is made by grinding the crystals against one another to create a fine powder. This milling process is extraordinarily hazardous unless performed within an {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}. Delerium dust can be used in alchemy, as a spell component, a reagent for brewing potions, or mixed into inks used to scribe spell scrolls. {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB} & Ammunition. Delerium fragments may be used as ammunition for a {@item Sling|XPHB} or fashioned into a makeshift {@item Club|XPHB}. Such weapons and ammunition deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage, and humanoid creatures struck must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}. Delerium used as ammunition in this way is destroyed.

name: Shard Crown (legendary)
entries: From the horn and eyes of a magnetite dragon is crafted this crown of magnetite. The creature's commanding presence and power over the blood of others allow the wearer of this object to bend its foes to its will.

Critical hits against you made with ferrous weapons or ammunition become normal hits while you wear this crown. In addition, while wearing this crown, you know the {@spell magnetobolt|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} cantrip ({@hit +9} to hit or your spellcasting attack modifier, whichever is higher) and, in extreme cold, you can cast the {@spell fly} spell on yourself at will.
The crown has {@b 12 charges} and regains {@dice 1d8 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Bloodbend
entries: As an action, you can expend {@b 1 charge} as you gesture to a creature you can see within {@b 30 feet} of you and speak a one-word command. If the target has blood, it must succeed on a {@dc 17} Wisdom saving throw or instantly use its reaction to follow the command (GM's discretion). If the creature has no reaction remaining, it must use its reaction to follow the command the next time it regains it. The property has no effect on a target that doesn't have blood. Commands include:

items.name: Throw
entries: The creature throws an object it is holding in a direction you choose with all its might.

items.name: Sit
entries: The creature sits, falling {@condition prone} and not moving until the end of its next turn.

items.name: Attack
entries: The creature makes one weapon attack against a creature of your choice within its reach/range.

entries.name: Magnetovision
entries: As a bonus action, you can expend {@b 1 charge} allowing you to sense the locations of all ferrous metals within {@b 60 feet} of you for the next {@b 10 minutes}. This vision is blocked by a thin sheet of lead.

entries.name: Crown of Shards
entries: As a bonus action, you can expend {@b 1 charge} to shoot a shard of magnetite at a target within {@b 90 feet} of you. Make a ranged spell attack ({@hit +9} to hit), which deals {@damage 4d6} piercing damage on a hit. This shard can bend around corners and ignores half and three-quarters cover.

name: Shard Crown (rare)
entries: From the horn and eyes of a magnetite dragon is crafted this crown of magnetite. The creature's commanding presence and power over the blood of others allow the wearer of this object to bend its foes to its will.

Critical hits against you made with ferrous weapons or ammunition become normal hits while you wear this crown. In addition, while wearing this crown, you know the {@spell magnetobolt|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} cantrip ({@hit +7} to hit or your spellcasting attack modifier, whichever is higher) and, in extreme cold, you can cast the {@spell levitate} spell on yourself at will.
The crown has {@b 5 charges} and regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Bloodbend
entries: As an action, you can expend {@b 1 charge} as you gesture to a creature you can see within {@b 30 feet} of you and speak a one-word command. If the target has blood, it must succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or instantly use its reaction to follow the command (GM's discretion). If the creature has no reaction remaining, it must use its reaction to follow the command the next time it regains it. The property has no effect on a target that doesn't have blood. Commands include:

items.name: Throw
entries: The creature throws an object it is holding in a direction you choose with all its might.

items.name: Sit
entries: The creature sits, falling {@condition prone} and not moving until the end of its next turn.

items.name: Attack
entries: The creature makes one weapon attack against a creature of your choice within its reach/range.

name: Shard Crown (very rare)
entries: From the horn and eyes of a magnetite dragon is crafted this crown of magnetite. The creature's commanding presence and power over the blood of others allow the wearer of this object to bend its foes to its will.

Critical hits against you made with ferrous weapons or ammunition become normal hits while you wear this crown. In addition, while wearing this crown, you know the {@spell magnetobolt|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} cantrip ({@hit +8} to hit or your spellcasting attack modifier, whichever is higher) and, in extreme cold, you can cast the {@spell fly} spell on yourself at will.
The crown has {@b 8 charges} and regains {@dice 1d4 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn.

entries.name: Bloodbend
entries: As an action, you can expend {@b 1 charge} as you gesture to a creature you can see within {@b 30 feet} of you and speak a one-word command. If the target has blood, it must succeed on a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw or instantly use its reaction to follow the command (GM's discretion). If the creature has no reaction remaining, it must use its reaction to follow the command the next time it regains it. The property has no effect on a target that doesn't have blood. Commands include:

items.name: Throw
entries: The creature throws an object it is holding in a direction you choose with all its might.

items.name: Sit
entries: The creature sits, falling {@condition prone} and not moving until the end of its next turn.

items.name: Attack
entries: The creature makes one weapon attack against a creature of your choice within its reach/range.

entries.name: Magnetovision
entries: As a bonus action, you can expend {@b 1 charge} allowing you to sense the locations of all ferrous metals within {@b 60 feet} of you for the next {@b 10 minutes}. This vision is blocked by a thin sheet of lead.

name: Shard of Moonlight
entries: While attuned to this weapon, you gain the following benefits:

items: You are proficient with Greatswords and Longswords.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and the blade deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Radiant damage on a hit.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom saving throws, except those made to resist Madness.
You can use this weapon as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sentience
entries: The Shard of Moonlight is a sentient weapon, with the same personality as the Great One whose flesh it was carved from. The weapon sporadically communicates telepathically with its wielder through images and sounds, though it doesn't speak.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the shard is a metallic {@item Longsword|XPHB} that absorbs light. In its Transformed state, the weapon is a {@item Greatsword|XPHB} that pulses with lunar energy. In both states, this weapon has the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: The blade seems to guide your strikes. Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with this weapon, you can immediately make a second attack (no action required). It has the Void Absorption property.

entries.name: Void Absorption
entries: The void that fills the blade is capable of absorbing magic. While holding the shard, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to absorb a spell that is targeting you, including spells with an area of effect. The absorbed spell's effect is canceled, and the spell's energy—not the spell itself—is stored in the shard in the form of charges. The number of charges gained is equivalent to the level of the spell when it was cast (1 charge for cantrips). The shard can absorb and store up to 10 charges. If the shard doesn't have enough empty charges for a spell, it fails to absorb it. The shard regains all charges each time the moon changes.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: To transform the blade, you must take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while under direct moonlight. The transformation lasts for 1 minute, or until you end it early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. While the blade is Transformed, the extra Radiant damage it deals on a hit increases from {@damage 1d6} to {@damage 2d6}, and you can expend the charges stored within the shard. When the shard loses all charges, the transformation ends.
Each time you make an attack in the Transformed state, you can expend charges to create special effects:

entries.name: Revealing Glow
entries: As part of making an attack, you can expend 1 charge to empower the blade. On a hit, it deals an extra {@damage 1d12} Radiant damage, and until the start of your next turn, the target sheds {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius. While affected by the light, the target can't have the {@condition Invisible} condition, and attack rolls against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Transient Moonlight
entries: As part of making an attack, you can expend 2 charges to release a wave of moonlight where the blade slashes, creating a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} of moonlight originating from you. Each creature in the area must make a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 2d12} Radiant damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Lunar Explosion
entries: Instead of making an attack, you can expend 3 charges to raise the blade upward and release a burst of moonlight energy. Each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a {@dc 18} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 3d12} Radiant damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If a creature falls {@condition Prone|XPHB} within 5 feet of you, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a melee weapon attack against them with the shard. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

name: Shared Burden
entries: This set of chained rings and bracers is a sign of the pact you forged with your patron. Once you attune to the item, the small spikes that line the inside of the bands become harmless to you and feel like a warm, gentle caress against your skin. You can also use the item as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Warlock spells.

Whenever you deal damage to a creature with a Warlock spell, you can choose to add your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) to the spell's damage. When you do, you take Psychic damage equal to half your Charisma modifier (round up). This Psychic damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB}.

name: Sharkrazor Mantle
entries: While wearing this magic sharkskin cloak, you have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet and can breathe underwater. While you're wearing the cloak, whenever a creature successfully grapples you or causes to you have the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and is touching you, it takes {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage. The creature takes this damage again at the start of each of its turns until that condition ends or it is no longer touching you.

In addition, while wearing the cloak, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks made to find or track a creature that's missing any of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and your attack rolls against targets that have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} as a result of that condition if the target is missing any of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

name: Sharp Mind
entries: When you drink this potion, your mind becomes charged with magical energy. For the next 8 hours, you gain a +2 bonus to Intelligence saving throws, and you gain resistance to psychic damage. In addition, you can devour whole tomes of text, reading 10 times faster than normal.
{@font {@style 49|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Sheep Dragon Brew
entries: One swig of this hearty potion will see you growing a thick coat of sheep dragon wool all around your body. Besides keeping you warm, it aids your survival and protects you from the cold. For the duration, your AC increases by 1, and you gain resistance to cold damage. The effects of the potion last for 1 hour.
{@font {@style 43|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Sheer Cold
entries: The blade of this {@item Battleaxe|XPHB} is made from a shard of the Everglacier and never melts. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals Cold damage on a hit instead of Slashing.

When you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll made with this weapon, the ground in the direction of the target in either a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} or 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} (your choice) is covered in a layer of slick ice for 1 minute. The ice is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. When a creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. In addition, the original target of the attack must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. The {@condition Restrained|XPHB} target can take an action to make a DC 15 Strength check. On a successful save, that condition ends.

name: Shepherd's Bane
entries: It is said that this potion was first brewed in the Gale Fields by a young shepherd looking to protect their flock. The irony was not lost on them when they drank the potion and took on wolflike features. When you drink this potion, you grow claws which last for 1 hour. For the duration, your unarmed strikes using your claws deal slashing damage equal to {@dice 1d6} plus your Strength modifier, instead of the bludgeoning damage normal for an unarmed strike.
{@font {@style 7|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Shield of Blinding
entries: While holding this shield, you can speak its command word and choose one creature that you can see within range to make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, the target is {@condition blinded} for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make a new saving throw to regain their sight.

name: Shield of Crows
entries: While holding this shield, you can speak its command work to summon a {@creature swarm of ravens}. For up to 12 hours, these birds will scout terrain, warn you of enemies, and keep watch while you sleep. They do not engage in combat on your behalf and flee if attacked or threatened. After the duration, the shield cannot summon another swarm until after you have left a {@item loaf of bread|PHB}, bits of dried meat, or similar food on the shield during a short rest.
In addition, while holding the shield, you gain the ability to speak with crows and other corvids.

name: Shield of Dawn's Herald
entries: The shield has 3 charges, and it regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding this shield, you can expend 1 charge to create a beam of light 10 feet wide and 120 feet long to illuminate everything in front of the shield. All creatures in this beam of light appear in their true form: shapeshifters appear as their unshifted forms, illusions fail to disguise their users, and so on. You can maintain this beam for up to 1 minute, requiring {@status concentration}.
Additionally, undead in the beam take {@damage 1d6} radiant damage each round they remain in the beam.

name: Shield of Marius Renathyr (Legendary)
entries: Crafted from polished gold and white enamel and adorned with an intricate design of a rose encircled by thorny vines, this Shield was once owned by Marius Renathyr, a knight-errant destined for a terrible fate.
While holding this Shield, you gain a +3 bonus to AC determined by the Shield's rarity, in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Valorous Guard (Rare+)
entries: When a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add 2 + the Shield's bonus to the creature's AC, potentially causing the attack to miss. When a creature within 5 feet of you fails a Dexterity saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add 2 + the Shield's bonus to the creature's total, potentially causing it to succeed.

entries.name: Honor of the Vanguard (Very Rare+)
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and an ally you can see is within 30 feet of an enemy, you can teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of that ally and gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to 5 times the Shield's bonus.

entries.name: Righteous Wrath (Very Rare+)
entries: When you use the Valorous Guard property to cause an attack to miss, the next time you hit that attacker with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} before the end of your next turn, it takes an extra {@dice 1d8} (Legendary: {@dice 3d8}) Radiant damage.

entries.name: As Terrible as the Dawn (Legendary)
entries: You can cast {@spell Flame Strike|XPHB} (save DC 19) from the Shield. If you are in the spell's area, you regain {@dice 5d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} instead of taking damage. Once the spell is cast from the Shield, it can't be cast from it again until the next dusk.

name: Shield of Marius Renathyr (Rare)
entries: Crafted from polished gold and white enamel and adorned with an intricate design of a rose encircled by thorny vines, this Shield was once owned by Marius Renathyr, a knight-errant destined for a terrible fate.
While holding this Shield, you gain a +1 bonus to AC determined by the Shield's rarity, in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Valorous Guard (Rare+)
entries: When a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add 2 + the Shield's bonus to the creature's AC, potentially causing the attack to miss. When a creature within 5 feet of you fails a Dexterity saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add 2 + the Shield's bonus to the creature's total, potentially causing it to succeed.

name: Shield of Marius Renathyr (Very Rare)
entries: Crafted from polished gold and white enamel and adorned with an intricate design of a rose encircled by thorny vines, this Shield was once owned by Marius Renathyr, a knight-errant destined for a terrible fate.
While holding this Shield, you gain a +2 bonus to AC determined by the Shield's rarity, in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC, and you can use the following properties.

entries: When a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add 2 + the Shield's bonus to the creature's AC, potentially causing the attack to miss. When a creature within 5 feet of you fails a Dexterity saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add 2 + the Shield's bonus to the creature's total, potentially causing it to succeed.

entries.name: Righteous Wrath (Very Rare+)
entries: When you use the Valorous Guard property to cause an attack to miss, the next time you hit that attacker with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} before the end of your next turn, it takes an extra {@dice 1d8} (Legendary: {@dice 3d8}) Radiant damage.

name: Shield of Otters
entries: While holding this shield, you can speak its command word to summon a pair of otters (use {@creature giant weasel} statistics). For up to 12 hours, these aquatic mammals will scout aquatic and riparian terrain, warn you of enemies, and keep watch while you sleep. They do not engage in combat on your behalf and flee if attacked or threatened. After the duration, the shield cannot summon another otter pair until after you have left fish, shellfish, or similar food on the shield during a short rest.
In addition, while holding the shield, you gain the ability to speak with otters and other aquatic mammals, such seals.

name: Shield of Shadow Form
entries: While holding this shield, you have a +1 bonus to AC.

Additionally, you can use an action to transform yourself and everything you wear and carry into a shadowy cloud for 10 minutes. The effect ends if you drop to 0 hit points or use an action to end it.

While in this form, your only method of movement is a flying speed of 10 feet. You can enter and occupy the space of another creature. When you end your turn in another creature's space, that creature takes {@damage 6d8} necrotic damage.

You have resistance to mundane damage, and you have advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws. You can pass through small holes, narrow openings, and even mere cracks, though you treat liquids as if they were solid surfaces. You can't fall and remain hovering in the air even when {@condition stunned} or otherwise {@condition incapacitated}.

While in the form of a shadowy cloud, you can't talk or manipulate objects, and any objects you were carrying or holding can't be dropped, used, or otherwise interacted with. You can't attack, cast spells, or manifest powers.
Once you use the shield to transform into a shadowy cloud, that property can't be used again until the following dusk.

name: Shield of Swans
entries: This shield has 3 charges, and it regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. When you speak its command word and expend one charge, you gain a fly speed of 60 feet for {@dice 1d4} rounds (and you know when this ends).
In addition, while holding this shield you can speak with swans and other aquatic birds.

name: Shield of the Justicars
entries: One of the original arms from the Upheaval, this shield can be used to release a magically discordant pulse. While holding this shield, you have a +1 bonus to AC. This bonus is in addition to the shield's normal bonus to AC.

In addition, the shield has 4 charges and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you casts a spell, you can use your reaction to expend 1 of the shield's charges and speak its command word. When you do, the target must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes a –2 penalty to its spell attack bonus and saving throw DC until the end of the turn, including against the triggering spell.

name: Shield of the World Serpent
entries: This shield is shaped from a scale of Jormungandr. While wielding the shield, you cannot be pushed or pulled against your will. At the start of each of your turns, you may end any {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions on you.

name: Shield of Yggdrasil
entries: This massive tower Shield requires a Strength score of 17 or higher in order to adequately wield it. The Shield is of dwarven make and functions as a small battlement, granting you a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while you wield it. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC.

entries.name: Shield Plant
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can plant this Shield on the ground in your space to barricade yourself behind it, granting you {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} against ranged attacks from the direction you're facing. While wielding the planted Shield, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 5 feet and can't increase, and Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage you take from weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} is reduced by 3. You can uproot the Shield to end this effect as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

You can doff the Shield when planting it by taking a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to do so instead of a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. When you do, the Shield remains upright and in place, and it can be used as {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} by any creature standing directly behind it in the space it was left in. The Shield falls down if you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, or if a creature within 5 feet of it takes a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to knock it over with a successful DC 20 Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check. You can move the Shield while it's planted by donning it again.

This Shield has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend 1 charge when you plant the Shield, or on a subsequent turn as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, to magically send out metal roots along the ground in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the Shield. The area is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} but it doesn't cost you or your allies extra movement. Moving the Shield causes the roots to shift and move with it. The roots remain until you uproot the Shield or it falls down.

name: Shielding Turtle Sugarbombs
entries: These sticky chocolate candies are filled with an enchanted molasses and caramel center and come in packs of two. You can eat one of these sugarbombs as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. When you do, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet for 1 minute. If you have training with Shields and are wearing one on your back, you gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced in this way. If you're wielding a Shield, you don't gain this bonus to AC.

entries.name: Upset Stomach
entries: You can only be under the effects of one sugarbomb that has this property at a time. Eating a sugarbomb that has this property while under the effects of another one causes the effects of the first sugarbomb to immediately end and be replaced by the new one's. This rapid change is difficult to stomach, forcing you to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute.

name: Shifter's Shine (Common)
entries: The typical {@item shifter's shine|GriffonsSaddlebag2}, a common potion, is a specialty alcoholic beverage that causes your face to appear more glamorous. For 1 hour after drinking this potion, your skin's complexion clears, appears healthier, and grows more taut. Your face, while largely unchanged, is distinctly more attractive and exudes a weak aura of enchantment magic. When you make a Charisma check while under the effects of this potion, you can choose to forgo rolling the {@dice d20} to get a 10 on the die. Once you use this property, you can't use it again for the remainder of the potion's duration. The potion is a rich honey color and swirls lazily around, regardless of how it's handled. It can be found in any sort of vessel, though it is usually found in glass jars. The eye of a shapeshifter drifts along the potion's bottom, making it a daunting beverage for the average taverngoer to order. It has an extremely strong alcoholic taste with a hint of caramel. Due to its magical nature, the alcohol within this potion affects a creature twice as much as the alcohol within a nonmagical beverage.

name: Shifter's Shine
entries: Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

items: {@item Shifter's Shine (Common)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}
{@item Shifter's Shine (Uncommon)|GriffonsSaddlebag2}

name: Shifter's Shine (Uncommon)
entries: The typical {@item shifter's shine|GriffonsSaddlebag2}, a common potion, is a specialty alcoholic beverage that causes your face to appear more glamorous. For 1 hour after drinking this potion, your skin's complexion clears, appears healthier, and grows more taut. Your face, while largely unchanged, is distinctly more attractive and exudes a weak aura of enchantment magic. When you make a Charisma check while under the effects of this potion, you can choose to forgo rolling the {@dice d20} to get a 10 on the die. Once you use this property, you can't use it again for the remainder of the potion's duration. The potion is a rich honey color and swirls lazily around, regardless of how it's handled. It can be found in any sort of vessel, though it is usually found in glass jars. The eye of a shapeshifter drifts along the potion's bottom, making it a daunting beverage for the average taverngoer to order. It has an extremely strong alcoholic taste with a hint of caramel. Due to its magical nature, the alcohol within this potion affects a creature twice as much as the alcohol within a nonmagical beverage.
The following {@item shifter's shine|GriffonsSaddlebag2} is an uncommon variant with additional properties. It also tastes better.
When you drink this potion, you gain the effects of the {@spell alter self} spell for 1 hour (no concentration required) or until you end the effect as a bonus action.

name: Shimmering Spectacles
entries: While wearing these glasses, you can use a bonus action to cause them to briefly shine. When you do, the glasses cast bright light in a 5-foot radius and obscure your eyes until the end of your turn.

name: Shipwright's Watch
entries: This glimmering spyglass is actually coated in a fine layer of fool's gold. While peering through the spyglass, you can rotate a ring at the front of the telescope to toggle between looking directly ahead of you or directly behind you, as if you were turned around.

name: Shock and Ore
entries: This pair of rough and ready War Picks are said to have been created by the first miners to quarry quickstone in the Barrens. They have long been passed around as heirlooms and rewards. These magical picks are a single magic item for the purposes of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}.
You gain the following benefits while wielding both picks:

items: The picks have the{@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} weapon property.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with the picks.
The picks have 3 charges, which they share. They regain {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn.

When you hit a target with a Melee attack using Shock, you can expend 1 charge as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to deal an additional {@damage 2d8} Lightning damage. A creature affected by this damage can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
When you hit a target with a Melee attack using Ore, you can expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Earth Tremor|FoEQuickstone} as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, centered on the target.

name: Shooting Star
entries: Tiny specks of starlight gleam from the dark surface of this magic longbow at night. The bow is strung with an invisible string that appears only when it's drawn. When pulled, the string emits a soft yellow glow as motes of starlight appear and float around the bow's frame. Drawing the bow without first nocking an arrow creates a magic arrow of pure starlight in its place and intensifies the bow's glow. The starlit arrow shines bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this weapon when you use a starlit arrow, which deals radiant damage instead of piercing damage. Hit or miss, the starlit arrow disappears immediately after the attack.

entries.name: Falling Stars
entries: As an action, you can speak the bow's command word and fire a starlit arrow into the air above you, choosing a point that you can see within 60 feet of you. The arrow immediately vanishes and creates a shower of tiny, magical stars that fall and land in a 30-foot-radius circle on the ground centered on the point you chose. Each creature of your choice within the area must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. A target takes {@damage 3d6} radiant damage and {@damage 3d6} force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one, as a shower of magical stars slam into the ground around them. This property can't be used again until the next dusk.

In addition, when you use a starlit arrow and roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this weapon, a tiny magical star appears and strikes the target. The target must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d6} radiant damage and {@damage 1d6} force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Immediately after a falling star hits the ground or a target, it disappears.

name: Shovel of Yorgrim (Legendary)
entries: This shovel features a steel blade and collar at the end of a makeshift walking stick, appearing old and well-used. It was once the shovel of Yorgrim of the Shadestone Clan, who could commune with the spirits of the dead. It occasionally emits a faint whispering sound when handled.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by its rarity. While holding the shovel, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Death-Kenning (Rare+)
entries: When you hit an Undead with the shovel, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} immediately after the hit to learn its {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities}, if any.

entries.name: Deathspeaker (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Gentle Repose|XPHB} and {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} from the shovel.

entries.name: Deny Death's Touch (Very Rare+)
entries: You and your allies within a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Bind Deathly Servant (Legendary)
entries: When a Humanoid dies within 30 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to turn its soul into a {@creature Specter|XMM} that obeys your commands. If the Humanoid was {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you when it died, you can turn the soul into a {@creature Wraith|XMM} instead. You can control one creature at a time with this property. The Undead disappears after 8 hours, when you create a new creature with this property, or when it dies.

entries.name: Psychopomp (Legendary)
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you and one willing creature that isn't Undead that you touch become wraithlike until the end of your next turn. While wraithlike, you can move through other creatures and objects as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. If you end your turn inside an object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take {@damage 1d10} Force damage. If the creature you touch is Undead, it must succeed on a DC 19 Charisma saving throw or have {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to all damage until the start of your next turn. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

name: Shovel of Yorgrim (Rare)
entries: This shovel features a steel blade and collar at the end of a makeshift walking stick, appearing old and well-used. It was once the shovel of Yorgrim of the Shadestone Clan, who could commune with the spirits of the dead. It occasionally emits a faint whispering sound when handled.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by its rarity. While holding the shovel, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Death-Kenning (Rare+)
entries: When you hit an Undead with the shovel, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} immediately after the hit to learn its {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities}, if any.

entries.name: Deathspeaker (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Gentle Repose|XPHB} and {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} from the shovel.

name: Shovel of Yorgrim (Very Rare)
entries: This shovel features a steel blade and collar at the end of a makeshift walking stick, appearing old and well-used. It was once the shovel of Yorgrim of the Shadestone Clan, who could commune with the spirits of the dead. It occasionally emits a faint whispering sound when handled.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by its rarity. While holding the shovel, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Death-Kenning (Rare+)
entries: When you hit an Undead with the shovel, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} immediately after the hit to learn its {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities}, if any.

entries.name: Deathspeaker (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Gentle Repose|XPHB} and {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB} from the shovel.

entries.name: Deny Death's Touch (Very Rare+)
entries: You and your allies within a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

name: Shroud of Ending
entries: You must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw when you attune to this artifact. On a failure, the Shroud of Ending causes you to magically age {@dice 5d10} years. For the next hour, you have disadvantage on all attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws as your body is temporarily weakened by your sudden advance in age. If this causes you to age beyond the average natural lifespan for your race, you instantly die, and your soul rises immediately as a {@creature ghost} sworn to protect the artifact.

As long as you are attuned to this artifact, you deal {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage to any plant you touch that isn't also a creature. Creatures with the plant or beast type within 30 feet of you become hostile toward you. Additionally, you stop aging and no longer require food or sleep to live. Whenever you are no longer attuned to this item, you immediately age a number of years equal to the amount of time you would have aged naturally while attuned to the artifact. If this causes you to age beyond the average natural lifespan for your race, you instantly die.

entries.name: Blessings of Tyton
entries: While wearing the cloak, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +2 bonus to your AC and saving throws.
You can see in darkness as if it were {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light}.
You are immune to poison damage, the {@condition poisoned} condition, and all diseases.
You have advantage on death saving throws, and on saving throws against effects that would kill you instantaneously.

entries.name: Hasten the Sunset
entries: While wearing the cloak, you can spend an action to cause a living creature you can see within 120 feet of you to age rapidly. The creature must make a {@dc 17} Constitution saving throw, instantly aging {@dice 6d10} years on a failure and aging by one year on a success. On a failed saving throw, the target becomes cursed, automatically failing any Strength or Dexterity checks and making all other attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws at disadvantage. This effect lasts until a {@spell remove curse} spell is cast on the target. If the target ages over the average natural lifespan for their race, they die. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until a week has passed.

entries.name: Shade's Form
entries: While wearing the cloak, you can cast {@spell etherealness}. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Step of the Night's Shadow
entries: While wearing the cloak, you gain the ability to teleport to a location within an area of {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light or darkness} within 500 feet of you as an action. You arrive at exactly the spot desired, so long as it is an area of {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light or darkness}. It can be a place you can see, one you can visualize, or one you can describe by stating distance and direction, such as "200 feet straight downward" or "upward to the northwest at a 45-degree angle, 300 feet." For the teleportation to succeed, you must arrive in an area of {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light or darkness}; otherwise, you are teleported to the nearest such area within range. If no such area of {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light or darkness} exists, the teleportation fails. You can bring along objects as long as their weight doesn't exceed what you can carry. You can also bring one willing creature of your size or smaller carrying gear up to its carrying capacity. The creature must be within 5 feet of you when you use this property. If you would arrive in a place already occupied by an object or a creature, the teleportation fails. After you use this property, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 1, you can't use it again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Destroying the Cloak
entries: The only way to destroy the Shroud of Ending is for a Cleric of {@deity Ardea|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} of at least 17th level to present it to the rising sun. The cleric must say a prayer, returning the power of night and death to {@deity Tyton|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting}, and cast the {@spell daylight} spell on the cloak. The power within the Shroud of Ending will recognize the coming of {@deity Ardea|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting|Ardea's} dawn and return to {@deity Tyton|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting|Tyton's} realm. A faintly magical but powerless cloak will be left behind, which resembles the sky at dusk.

name: Shroud of Kairious
entries: The top of this brass censer has silhouettes of hourglasses and the sun punched through its surface.

When issued its command word, the censer begins to emit a hazy, jasmine-scented shroud of vapor in a 15-foot radius centered on it for 2 hours. The vapor shroud does not affect your vision or the vision or visibility of the creatures inside of it. Creatures standing inside the vapor shroud are immune to Oshragora's temporal distortions and magic spells and effects that alter time, such as {@spell slow}, {@spell haste}, or {@spell time stop}.

Once per day, while the censer is emitting vapor, you can use the command word to jump backwards in time 1 hour, losing any progress or ill effects gained during the erased hour. Once you have used this function, the censer ceases emitting vapor.
Once the censer has been used, it cannot be used again until noon the next day.

name: Shtriga Nonna's Pot of Plenty
entries: This black iron pot weighs only 2 pounds. As an action, you can speak one of the following command phrases to activate its effect:

entries.name: Boil, Boil, Until You Spoil
entries: The cauldron fills with a hearty stew. It creates enough stew to feed fifteen Humanoids. The food is tasty and seasoned well, and spoils if uneaten after 24 hours.

entries.name: Bubble, Bubble, Toil and Trouble.
entries: The cauldron fills with stew, as if you said "Boil, boil, until you spoil,"but the stew is poisoned. A creature who consumes the stew must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 24 hours.
Once the pot has been used in either of these ways, the pot can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Sibling Purses
entries: These two sibling coin pouches open up 5 inches wide and can hold up to 5 pounds each. When you place an object into one of the pouches, and the other pouch is within 20 feet of it, you can cause the object to teleport into the other pouch, provided there is room to accommodate the object.

name: Siege Staff
reqAttune: by a bard, cleric, druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
entries: This stony staff has been carved into the shape of a castle tower. The staff has 10 charges for the following properties, which use your spell save DC and spell attack bonus, and regains {@dice 1d8 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, a the staff crumbles into rubble and is destroyed.

entries.name: Battering Strike
entries: This staff can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff. When you hit with a melee attack using this staff, you can expend 1 of its charges to cause the target to take an extra {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, it's also pushed 5 feet away from you. In addition, when you attack an object with the staff and hit, maximize your weapon damage dice against the target.

entries.name: Fire Pot
entries: While holding the staff, you can use an action and expend 1 or more charges to cast the {@spell grease} spell from it. You can increase the size of the square covered by the spell by 5 feet for each additional charge you expend in this way (up to a 20-foot square). When you expend 2 or more charges to cast the spell in this way, creatures also take {@damage 2d6} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Trebuchet
entries: While holding the staff, you can use an action and expend 3 charges to magically create and fling a boulder at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Any target within 5 feet of the point must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 4d8} bludgeoning damage, and if it's Medium or smaller, it is also pushed 10 feet away from the point. On a successful save, a target takes half as much bludgeoning damage and isn't pushed. Maximize the bludgeoning damage dice against any object or structure hit by the boulder. After it lands, the boulder disappears.

name: Sight of Sin
entries: When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of a {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} spell (no {@status Concentration|XPHB} required) for 10 minutes, and during that time, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks to discern hidden motives or deception.
This potion is stored in a round glass flask. An iron band wraps around the bottle, ornamented with a goat's skull.

entries.name: Heightened Potency
entries: For the duration, you also gain the effect of the {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB} spell.

name: Signet Rings of Blindness, Deafness, and Silence
entries: Each of these three signets is decorated with the carving of a skull and a pair of skeletal hands that cover either its eyes (blindness), ears (deafness), or mouth (in an area of silence). Each ring has 1 charge, which it regains daily at dawn. If you are wearing the corresponding signet when you have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} or {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition or are in an area of magical silence, you can expend that ring's charge (no action required) to end that condition or speak a word or phrase (such as a spell's Verbal component) that can be heard through magical silence. Wearing the rings together as a set combines their collective charges, potentially allowing you to use one ring's property multiple times.

name: Signet Rings of the Fey Court
reqAttune: by an Elf or Fey Creature
entries: This set of wooden rings once belonged to a powerful Fey who ruled over a domain on the Feywild. You must be wearing all four rings in order to attune to them and use their magic. While wearing the rings, you know the {@spell Druidcraft|XPHB} cantrip. In addition, you gain the Elf's Trance trait if you don't already have it.

Each ring has an associated season: autumn, spring, summer, or winter. The four rings each contain 2 charges and regain all expended charges when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Once a ring has no remaining charges, the small landscape adorning the top of it withers until it regains its charges.

entries.name: Season's Resistance
entries: You can expend 1 of a particular ring's charges as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when you take damage of the type corresponding to that ring: spring (Radiant), summer (Fire), autumn (Necrotic), or winter (Cold). When you do, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage type until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering damage.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries: You can expend any 2 charges from the rings as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when an enemy targets you with a spell or other magical effect. When you do, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering spell or effect. The 2 charges don't need to be from the same ring.

name: Silence of the Drowned
entries: When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of the {@spell Silence|XPHB} spell (no {@status Concentration|XPHB} required) as a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you for 10 minutes, and for the duration, squid tentacles emerge from your mouth.
This sculpted clay jar is painted in a deep blue and adorned with squid tentacles. Uncorking it reduces all noise in the area as if you are underwater, and the liquid within is a coppery blue-green.

entries.name: Heightened Potency
entries: For the duration, you can spit ink from your mouth as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. One creature within 30 feet of you makes a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target gains the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target is immune to this property for the next 24 hours.

name: Silencing Satchel
entries: This magic satchel has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend 1 charge and tighten the satchel's drawstring to inflict a silencing hex on a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be cursed for 1 minute. While the target is cursed, its mouth is sealed shut. The target can't cast any spell with a Verbal component, consume potions, or take in food or drink. The target makes a DC 15 Charisma save at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse early on a success.

name: Silken Socks of Slickening
entries: This pair of magic, smooth socks are iridescent and oily to the touch. While wearing both socks on your feet, you can use them to cast the {@spell Grease|XPHB} spell (save DC 13) centered on a point within 5 feet of you. The magical oil runs off the socks to the ground at your feet, causing the ground to become slick. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Silver Coin of Duvra
entries: This silver coin is embossed with the trickster dragon Duvra on one side (heads), and a sailing ship on the other (tails). Whenever you or another creature you can see flips this coin, you can control whether it lands heads, tails, or on its side.

name: Silver Eagle Studded Cuirass
entries: This studded leather armor is worn by an elite guard of a longstanding alliance between elves and humans. While you're wearing it, any critical hit against you becomes a normal hit.

In addition, when a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack while you're wearing this armor, you can use your reaction to speak its command word. When you do, a pair of ghostly eagle wings appear from the back of the armor. The wings beat the air around you and push you back up to 10 feet away from the attacking creature, without provoking opportunity attacks. In addition, the sudden movement takes you out of harms way, reducing the damage you take from the triggering attack by {@dice 2d6}. Once this property of the armor has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Silver Lycan Chime
entries: This small silver bell exudes Divination magic, especially while under a full moon. While hung, the bell rings a unique, magical melody if a Lycanthrope passes within 15 feet of it, or within 60 feet of it during a full moon.
