entries: When poured, this dark elixir stains the earth and creates a 10-foot cube that is void of the island's magic, as if it were under the effects of the {@spell Antimagic Field} spell. This effect lasts for 1 year.
{@font {@style 55|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Spiritwalker Breastplate
entries: When you drop to 0 hit points while wearing this armor, your spirit leaves your body and appears as a floating, ghostly version of yourself. The spirit remains there for 1 minute or until you regain consciousness, at which point the spirit returns to your body. For the duration, you don't suffer a death saving throw failure as a result of taking damage, and you can only die from damage if the total damage you take on a turn equals or exceeds your hit point maximum. You still make death saving throws at the start of each of your turns while in this state; however, the number you must roll to succeed on a death saving throw increases by 1 for every 5 feet away from your physical body your spirit is at the start of each of your turns.

Your spirit is tethered to your physical body and can't be farther than 30 feet away from it at any time. The spirit has your senses, a flying speed of 30 feet, and can hover. On your turn, it can only move and take the {@action Help} action. The spirit is immune to all damage and is incorporeal, but an effect that turns undead will automatically send your spirit back to your physical body and end the effect early.
Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Splinterguard
entries: The protective panels that adorn this splint armor are made from carefully molded pieces of ironleaf lumber, a wood renowned for its remarkable durability. Even if you aren't attuned to the armor, you gain the following benefits:

While you're wearing this armor, any critical hit against you becomes a normal hit. In addition, the first time each day you're struck by a critical hit, the armor's panels splinter into countless shards of painful, wooden shrapnel. Other creatures within 10 feet of you must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 3d8} piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Once this happens, the armor's wooden panels are cracked until the following dawn, at which point they magically regrow. Until the panels regrow, the armor can't be splintered again and suffers a –2 penalty to the AC it offers. The panels can't be repaired by magical or mundane means, but a {@spell plant growth} spell can cause the panels to regrow early once before each dawn.

If you're attuned to this armor, you're considered proficient with it, and you don't suffer disadvantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks you make as a result of wearing it. In addition, creatures hit by the armor's shrapnel when it splinters take {@damage 5d8} piercing damage, instead of {@damage 3d8}, and you can choose which creatures in the area are affected by it when it happens.

name: Splintershot
entries: This {@item Shortbow|XPHB} can cause an Arrow to shatter and unleash a devastating spray of magical shrapnel. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can use a command word to destroy one nonmagical Arrow you have nocked in the bow and send splintering shards of arcane energy out in front of you. When you do, each creature in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d6} Piercing damage, or {@damage 3d6} Piercing damage if the creature was within 5 feet of you.

name: Splitter
entries: This {@item Halberd|XPHB}'s haft is made of rough, dark wood and is miraculously easy to heft. The bladed end of the {@item Halberd|XPHB} looks like a hatchet that's been absorbed by the hewn wood. While holding the {@item Halberd|XPHB} with two hands, you can use a command word as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically split the weapon into its more basic components.

When you do, the {@item Halberd|XPHB} deconstructs in your hands, leaving you with a {@item Handaxe|XPHB} in one hand and {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} in the other. Both the {@item Handaxe|XPHB} and {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} have the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property. You can combine the two weapons to reform the {@item Halberd|XPHB} by repeating the command word as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while you're holding both the {@item Handaxe|XPHB} and the {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. If the weapon is split into the {@item Handaxe|XPHB} and {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}, the bonus is a +1 with each weapon instead.

entries.name: Halberd
entries: If you hit a creature with the {@item Halberd|XPHB} and roll a 10 on the damage die, that creature's energy is sapped. Its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn, and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet for the same duration.

entries.name: Handaxe and Quarterstaff
entries: If you're wielding the {@item Handaxe|XPHB} and {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} in different hands, you gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}, and when you make an extra attack as a result of using these weapons' Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren't already adding it to the damage. The {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} deals Necrotic damage on a hit, and it deals maximum damage to plants and Plant creatures. Immediately after you make a ranged attack with the {@item Handaxe|XPHB}, it flies back to your hand.

name: Spymaster's Signet
entries: While wearing this ring, you can cast {@spell disguise self} at-will. In addition, you can turn invisible as an action. Anything you are wearing or carrying is invisible with you. You remain invisible for one minute, or until you use a bonus action to become visible again. Once you use this power, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Crown Authority
entries: A character cannot attune to more than one Seal of Drakkenheim. Guardian constructs in Drakkenheim such as {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim|wall gargoyles} and {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim|tower dragons} do not attack you while you are attuned to one of the Seals of Drakkenheim. An individual guardian ignores this effect for 24 hours if you attack it or cast a spell upon it.

As an action, you may present a Seal of Drakkenheim to rebuke the guardians. You make an opposed Charisma ability check against each {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim} or {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim} that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you. If you win the contest, the creature is rebuked for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. A rebuked creature doesn't move, and can't take actions or reactions. A creature who wins the contest is immune to your rebuke for 24 hours.

name: Squasher
entries: This enormous squash is strangely durable and makes for a functional magic weapon. Druids wielding this weapon can use their Wisdom modifier instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of melee attacks using it.

name: Sream's Stoppered Oasis
entries: This tall decanter is filled with water from a miraculous oasis in the H'rethi Desert and is stoppered with a small, overgrown planter. You can pour the water out of the bottle on top of the planter as an action to create a magical oasis that fills up to a 100-foot-square space over the course of 10 minutes.

The oasis has a pond filled with clean water and exotic, fruit-bearing trees that can nourish up to fifteen humanoids or five steeds for 24 hours. The area within the oasis is always under the effects of the {@spell alarm} spell. A {@creature swarm of poisonous snakes|MM} appears to defend the oasis for each creature that sets off the alarm (maximum of 3), whose rattling tails act as the audible alarm. The swarms are friendly to you and your companions, but don't obey verbal commands. Roll initiative for the summoned swarms as a group, which have their own turns. A swarm disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or when there are no more hostile creatures within the oasis.

The oasis remains for 24 hours or until dispelled by a {@spell dispel magic} spell cast at 5th level or higher. The atmosphere within the space is comfortable and dry, regardless of the weather outside the oasis. A friendly creature within the oasis can't be {@condition frightened} and regains an extra {@dice 1d4} Hit Dice when it finishes a long rest.
Drinking the water in the bottle has no effect, but tastes refreshing.

name: Staff of Briars
entries: This wooden staff is made from the harvested claws of a braerog. It has 10 charges. While holding the staff, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to expend 1 charge and cause thorn-covered rose vines to sprout up, covering a 20-foot square centered on a point within 5 feet of you. This area becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.
Once created, the briars are non-magical. They grow (or wither) as appropriate for the environment, just as a normal plant would.
The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the staff turns into rose petals and is lost forever.

name: Staff of Climbing Ivy
reqAttune: by a bard, druid, sorcerer, or warlock
entries: This staff is formed from several strands of leafy vines that have grown together into the shape of a twisted walking stick. It is rigid and sturdy.
The staff has three command words. While holding the staff, you can speak one of its command words to cause an effect.

entries.name: Growth
entries: Speaking the first command word as a bonus action causes up to 120 feet of creeping vines to grow from the staff towards a solid surface or unattended object you can see. The vines grow at a speed of 30 feet per round.

entries.name: Grasp
entries: Speaking the second command word, costing no action causes the vines to firmly affix themselves to a surface or unattended object within their reach. The vines can only be anchored to one object or surface at a time.

entries.name: Grapple
entries: Speaking the third command word as an action causes the vines to retract into the staff at a speed of 30 feet per round. If anchored to a solid surface, the vines will pull the staff's wielder towards the surface at the same speed. If anchored to an object, the vines will pull the object towards the wielder of the staff.

When the vines are extended, they can be attacked. The extended vines have an Armor Class of 14, 45 hit points, and vulnerability to fire and slashing damage. The vines have a Strength score of 16 and can bear up to 240 pounds of weight at once. Weight in excess of this will cause the vines to begin to tear, dealing 10 points of damage to them each round. If the vines drop to 0 hit points, the staff is destroyed. The vines regain all lost hit points when they retract into the staff.

name: Staff of Contaminated Power
reqAttune: by a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
entries: This staff can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.

The staff has 20 charges for the following properties. The staff regains 1 charge each hour it rests in the Deep Haze. You can also touch a delerium crystal to the staff, which causes it to regain {@dice 2d8 + 4} charges, then the crystal crumbles to dust. If you expend the last charge, you immediately gain {@dice 1d6} {@adventure levels of contamination|DungeonsDrakkenheim|12}.

entries.name: Spells
entries: While holding the staff, you can use an action to expend some of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC and spellcasting ability: {@spell delerium orb|DungeonsDrakkenheim} (1 charge), {@spell warp bolt|DungeonsDrakkenheim} (2 charges), {@spell ride the rifts|DungeonsDrakkenheim} (3 charges), {@spell delerium blast|DungeonsDrakkenheim} (4 charges), {@spell conjure the deep haze|DungeonsDrakkenheim} (5 charges), and {@spell ray of contamination|DungeonsDrakkenheim} (6 charges). You don't gain any {@adventure contamination levels|DungeonsDrakkenheim|12} when you cast these spells using charges from this staff.

name: Staff of Cubic Cultivation
entries: This staff has a perfect cube of blue crystal at its top that slowly drips with a viscous ooze. The staff has 10 charges. As an action, you can tap the head of the staff on the ground and expend 1 or more of its charges to create a 5-foot cube of a mysterious, gelatinous material for each expended charge. Each cube appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you or adjacent to another cube you create as part of this action. The cubes are translucent objects that have AC 10, 20 hit points, and resistance to acid damage. Creating a cube in a space smaller than 5 feet across causes the cube to squeeze and fit the space. A cube remains for 1 minute or until it's reduced to 0 hit points, after which it dissolves into a puddle of slime and vanishes.
You can climb or walk on the cubes. However, their sticky surfaces are considered {@quickref difficult terrain||3}.

The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the gem on top of the staff shatters and is destroyed, creating a gelatinous cube in its place that's hostile toward you. When this happens, the staff becomes a nonmagical quarterstaff.

name: Staff of Farryn of the Greenwood (Legendary)
entries: This twisted wooden staff is crowned by a trinket-adorned deer's skull. It was fashioned by Farryn before she delved into the dark lore of Gorthos. Soft, fragrant moss and earthy mushrooms grow along the staff's length.

While holding the staff, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the staff's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Living Ward (Rare+)
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Servant of the Cycle (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB} (level 3 version) from the staff. When you do so, the next time you hit with an attack before the end of your next turn, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Cycle's Balance (Very Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Revivify|XPHB} from the staff. When you do so, the next time a creature fails a saving throw against a spell you cast in the next hour, it and creatures of your choice within 20 feet of it take {@damage 4d10} Necrotic damage. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Sacrifice of Flesh (Very Rare+)
entries: When a spell you cast restores {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take Necrotic damage up to twice the level of the spell that can't be reduced or prevented in any way. If you do so, the target regains additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to three times the damage you take.

entries.name: Death Blossom (Legendary)
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you dies, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make flowers bloom around them. Creatures of your choice within 30 feet of the dead creature regain {@dice 4d8} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and gain {@dice 2d8} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Staff of Farryn of the Greenwood (Rare)
entries: This twisted wooden staff is crowned by a trinket-adorned deer's skull. It was fashioned by Farryn before she delved into the dark lore of Gorthos. Soft, fragrant moss and earthy mushrooms grow along the staff's length.

While holding the staff, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the staff's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Living Ward (Rare+)
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Servant of the Cycle (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB} (level 3 version) from the staff. When you do so, the next time you hit with an attack before the end of your next turn, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

name: Staff of Farryn of the Greenwood (Very Rare)
entries: This twisted wooden staff is crowned by a trinket-adorned deer's skull. It was fashioned by Farryn before she delved into the dark lore of Gorthos. Soft, fragrant moss and earthy mushrooms grow along the staff's length.

While holding the staff, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the staff's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Living Ward (Rare+)
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Servant of the Cycle (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB} (level 3 version) from the staff. When you do so, the next time you hit with an attack before the end of your next turn, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Cycle's Balance (Very Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Revivify|XPHB} from the staff. When you do so, the next time a creature fails a saving throw against a spell you cast in the next hour, it and creatures of your choice within 20 feet of it take {@damage 4d10} Necrotic damage. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Sacrifice of Flesh (Very Rare+)
entries: When a spell you cast restores {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take Necrotic damage up to twice the level of the spell that can't be reduced or prevented in any way. If you do so, the target regains additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to three times the damage you take.

name: Staff of Favorable Winds
reqAttune: by a Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard
entries: While holding this staff, {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} caused by wind doesn't cost you extra movement. The staff has 10 charges. While holding it, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: {@spell Cone of Cold|XPHB} (5 charges), {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB} (2 charges), or {@spell Wind Wall|XPHB} (3 charges).

In addition, while holding the staff, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to create a harmless sensory effect using the air around you. For example, you can cause leaves to rustle, slam shutters closed in a sudden gust, or cause your clothing to billow dramatically.
The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the staff turns to dust and is blown away by a sudden flurry of wind.

name: Staff of Radiance
reqAttune: by a druid, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
entries: This staff of yarrow wood is often bleached white with points of glowing golden warmth embedded in the wood. You have resistance to radiant damage while you hold this staff.

The staff has 10 charges. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: {@spell burning radiance|BookOfEbonTides}* (4 charges), {@spell daylight} (2 charges), {@spell searing sun|BookOfEbonTides}* (3 charges), or {@spell sunburst} (5 charges). You may cast the {@spell douse light|bookOfEbonTides}* or {@spell light} cantrips without expending a charge. (Spells marked with an asterisk are from Deep Magic.)
The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the staff turns to a cloud of fireflies and is destroyed.

name: Staff of the Dream Shepherd
entries: This staff's cushioned handle is lined with soft wool and decorated with star and moon patches. While the staff is within 5 feet of you, you can use an action to immediately fall asleep, but otherwise can't be put to sleep by magical means. While attuned to the staff, you regain 1 extra Hit Die whenever you finish a long rest.

In addition, while holding the staff, you can use an action to summon a flock of spectral sheep. The sheep run in a line 20 feet long and 10 feet wide originating from you before disappearing. Each creature of your choice in the area must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, taking {@damage 2d6} psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If a creature fails the saving throw and has 20 hit points or fewer after taking this damage, it also falls asleep. Undead and creatures immune to being charmed can't be put to sleep in this way. A sleeping creature is {@condition unconscious} and stays asleep for 1 minute, until it takes damage, or until someone uses an action to shake or slap the creature awake. Once this property of the staff has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Staff of the Four Seasons
reqAttune: by a Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard
entries: This staff's form changes with the seasons. It has 10 charges and can be wielded as a magic {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. As long as the staff has at least 1 charge, your melee attacks with it deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage on a hit. This extra damage's type is based on the staff's season: spring (Radiant), summer (Fire), autumn (Necrotic), or winter (Cold).
Over the course of 10 minutes, you can focus on the staff to change its form to a different season. It remains in this form for 8 hours before reverting to the current season again.

While holding the staff, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC and spell attack modifier. The spells you can cast from the staff in this way are determined by its season, as shown in the table below.

rows: {@spell Guiding Bolt|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Moonbeam|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Plant Growth|XPHB} (3 charges)
{@spell Burning Hands|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Spike Growth|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Fireball|XPHB} (3 charges)
{@spell Inflict Wounds|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Pass Without Trace|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Vampiric Touch|XPHB} (3 charges)
{@spell Color Spray|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Darkvision|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Sleet Storm|XPHB} (3 charges)

entries: The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the staff loses all foliage and vitality, becoming a gnarled, nonmagical {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}.

name: Staff of the Magpie
entries: This magic stone staff weighs 10 pounds and has the bust of a magpie at its top. While holding the staff, you gain a +1 bonus to Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks you make to search for treasure or a specific item you're looking for.

The staff has 10 charges. While holding the staff, you can expend some charges to cast either Fly (3 charges) or Locate {@variantrule Object|XPHB} (2 charges) from it. The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the staff becomes a nonmagical {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} as the magpie springs to life and flies away.

name: Staff of the Mirage
entries: This staff has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the staff vanishes and is lost.

entries.name: Spells
entries: You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC; you gain a +2 bonus to your spell save DC when casting a spell in this way: {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Hallucinatory Terrain|XPHB} (4 charges), {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Mislead|XPHB} (5 charges), or {@spell Silent Image|XPHB} (1 charge).

name: Staff of the Mustang
entries: This dark {@item wooden staff|XPHB} is carved in the shape of a majestic stallion. The staff has 10 charges. While holding the staff, you can expend 1 charge to cast the {@spell Phantom Steed|XPHB} spell from it. In addition, you can use a command word while holding the staff and expend 1 charge to take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the staff breaks in two as if bitten and is destroyed. When this happens, the sound of hooves can be heard galloping away in an indiscernible direction.

name: Staff of the Reverent Warrior
entries: This staff was made as a means of worship rather than war by a retired warrior using the weapons he'd once wielded. The staff is adorned with blades and channels the inner focus of a warrior. This staff can be wielded as a magic {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. Even if you aren't attuned to the staff, attacks with it can deal either Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage on a hit (your choice each time).

This staff has 10 charges. While attuned to the staff, you know the {@spell True Strike|XPHB} cantrip. When you cast this spell while holding the staff, you can expend 1 or more charges to enhance the spell in one or more of the following ways:
You can expend 2 charges to cast the spell as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.
You can expend 1 charge to cause the next attack roll made against the target before the end of your next turn to have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.
On a hit, you can expend 1 charge to cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Radiant damage.

The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the staff becomes a nonmagical {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}, but attacks with it can still deal either Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage.

name: Staff of the Sorcerer King
entries: This ebony staff bears a bronze spear tip and additional blades carved to depict a winged scarab. The staff can be wielded as a magic spear that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. You are considered proficient with this weapon while you are attuned to it, even if you aren't proficient with spears. While holding the staff, you gain these benefits:

items.name: Spell Power
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls.

items.name: Cull Subjects
entries: Humanoids have a -2 penalty to saving throws against your spells.

items.name: Spell Shield
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells that target only you.

entries.name: Cursed
entries: This staff is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. Until the curse is broken with {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} or similar magic, you are unwilling to part with the staff, keeping it within reach at all times. In addition, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls made with weapons other than this one.

While cursed, you must make a {@dc 17} Constitution saving throw each day at midnight. On a failed save, your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by 10 unless you are Undead. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum can only be restored by a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell. If your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced to 0 while cursed, you die and immediately rise as a {@creature Wight|XMM}.

name: Staff of the Vineyard
reqAttune: by a cleric, druid, monk, or ranger
entries: This staff can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff. A clutch of up to 10 grapes hangs from the end of the staff's magical length of vine. A creature within reach of the staff can use an action to eat one of the grapes, which duplicates the effect of eating a berry from the {@spell goodberry} spell. {@dice 1d10} eaten grapes regrow on the clutch daily at dawn.

While holding the staff, you can use an action to cast the {@spell entangle} spell from it (save DC 13), causing twisting grapevines to sprout from the ground in the target area. If a creature {@condition restrained} by these vines makes a Strength check to free itself and fails, that creature becomes magically drunk until the end of its next turn. A drunk creature is {@condition poisoned} for the duration. Once this property of the staff has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Staff of the Void
reqAttune: by a cleric, sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
entries: This staff of ironwood is often cracked and gnarled with points of purple, wriggling movement seemingly moving through the wood. You have resistance to psychic damage while you hold this staff.

The staff has 10 charges. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: {@spell life drain|BookOfEbonTides}* (5 charges), {@spell living shadows|BookOfEbonTides}* (4 charges), {@spell maddening whispers|BookOfEbonTides}* (2 charges), or {@spell void strike|BookOfEbonTides}* (3 charges). You may cast the {@spell word of misfortune|BookOfEbonTides}* cantrip without expending a charge. (Spells marked with an asterisk are from Deep Magic.)
The staff regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} expended charges daily at midnight. If you expend the last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the staff turns to ash and is destroyed.

name: Stalaga Spear
entries: This magic {@item Spear|XPHB} is made of dark, polished granite and has a large ruby set in its head. Though it is made of stone, it weighs no more than a normal {@item Spear|XPHB} and is enchanted to prevent it from shattering. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The {@item Spear|XPHB} has 4 charges and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges daily at dawn. While you're within 5 feet of a surface made of unworked stone or earth, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and expend 1 charge to plunge the {@item Spear|XPHB} into that surface. The {@item Spear|XPHB} vanishes into the stone or earth and emerges as a sharp stone spike, 1 foot wide and 10 feet long, from another stone or earthen surface that you can see within 60 feet of you, such as the ground or a cave wall. The spike erupts perpendicularly from that surface and forces any creature in a 5-foot-wide, 10-foot-long {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} in that direction to make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} Piercing damage and is pushed up to 5 feet away from the spike. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

While you're within 60 feet of the stone spike and within 5 feet of a surface made of unworked stone or earth, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and use a command word to magically recall the {@item Spear|XPHB}. The stone spike crumbles, and the {@item Spear|XPHB} inside vanishes back into the surface it erupted from before reemerging from the surface next to you into your open hand. If you don't have an open hand, it falls to the ground at your feet.

name: Stalagmight Geode
entries: This snapped-off rock formation has a cache of magical, growing crystals inside it. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a creature with this weapon and roll the maximum number possible on the weapon's damage die, the crystals rapidly grow and increase the weapon's damage die by one size, up to a {@damage d12}. For example, when you roll an 8 on the weapon's normal {@damage d8} damage die, its damage die magically becomes a {@damage d10} after the attack. Immediately after you roll a 12 on a d12 damage die in this way, each creature within 5 feet of the greatclub (other than yourself) must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 1d12} piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one, as the weapon's crystals explode into shrapnel. Once the crystal explodes, the weapon's damage die becomes a {@damage d8} again.

name: Stalk Symbiote
entries: This ocular organ, harvested from a living Aberration, melds with the skull of its host. If you are a Humanoid, you can attune to this item by stitching it into your scalp during the {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} process. At the end of this time, the stalk burrows into your skull and bonds with your brain. Non-Humanoids cannot attune to the Stalk Symbiote.
While attuned to this item, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Symbiotic Senses
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks, and you do not have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls when surprised.

items.name: Aberrant Power
entries: If you have achieved at least Stage 1 of the {@charoption Aberrant Horror|GrimHollowPG24|Aberrant Horror Transformation}, you have blindsight with a range of 10 feet.

items.name: Symbiote Link
entries: You cannot voluntarily end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the Stalk Symbiote. If it is physically removed from your body, it regrows in {@dice 1d4} hours unless you receive a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell before it grows back (which also ends your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}).

name: Stallion Seed
entries: When thrown, the seed turns into a magical, swift courser with an Intelligence score of 14 and the ability to speak Common and Umbral. It will carry you for up to 30 miles, delivering you to a particular place or following a particular road or path.
If engaged in combat, the stallion acts as a normal {@creature warhorse}. It flees (with you) at the first opportunity.

entries.name: Illusion Seeds
entries: Illusion seeds are wondrous items first created in the Shadow Realm and reliant on a supply of shadow matter to power their effects—each such seed generates an illusion and those illusions can take quite powerful forms. While illusion seeds are fairly permanent in the Shadow Realm, where there is shadow matter to empower and sustain the illusions, they are notably less permanent anywhere else. In the mortal world and on other planes, the effects of illusion seeds last for {@dice 2d12} hours and then crumble away in a small burst of glittering light and shadows.

To use an illusion seed, its owner merely needs to throw it 5 feet or more from themselves (to avoid being caught in the magical effect). Once expended, their effects are permanent (in the Shadow Realm), though they can be unraveled using {@spell dispel magic} (DC 13).

name: Stalwart Staff
entries: A carved walking stick with a handle wrapped in worn leather, this magic staff gives you better endurance. While you use this staff as a walking stick while traveling on foot, you have advantage on the first save you make to endure a forced march.

name: Star Map of Creation
entries: This scroll displays what the night sky looked like at the creation of the Mundane World. If you have proficiency with the {@skill Arcana} or {@skill Nature} skill, you can spend 1 minute holding and studying the map and search it for an omen about the results of a specific course of action that you plan to take within the next 30 minutes. The GM chooses from the following possible outcomes:

items: Good omen
Bad omen
Mixed omen that has both good and bad results
No omen for a result that isn't especially good or bad

entries: The omen doesn't take into account any possible circumstances that might change the outcome, such as the loss or gain of equipment or a companion.
If the map is used two or more times in 24 hours, there is a cumulative {@chance 25} chance for each reading after the first that you get a random reading. The GM makes this roll in secret.

name: Star Metal Ring
entries: This heavy steel ring is set with a chunk of shimmering star metal. While wearing this ring, your appendages are crusted with iridescent star metal. Your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} are considered magical and deal Force damage.

entries.name: (Requires Attunement)
entries: This magic maul is made of a durable, light metal and has a long haft, giving it a reach of 10 feet. When you hit a creature with this maul, they are hexed until the end of their next turn. Whenever a creature hexed in this way makes an attack roll or saving throw, they must roll a {@dice d4} and subtract the number rolled from the attack roll or saving throw.
While you hold the maul, you can use an action to change the appearance of its head, choosing its shape and color.

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When Star Razor reaches an awakened state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The weapon's bonus to attack and damage rolls increases to +2.
When a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to create a burst of radiance from the sword, dealing {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to the attacker.
You can cast the {@spell see invisibility} spell from the sword as an action, and the save DC for spells cast using the sword increases to 15.

name: Star Razor (Dormant)
entries: The thick, grooved blade of this shining silver {@item longsword|PHB} is lined with etched runes that sparkle blue in the light. Star Razor—known also as Dwueth'var—was thought to have been destroyed or lost after the {@book Calamity|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|The Calamity}, but new rumors suggest that it might be wielded by a half-orc somewhere in {@book Wildemount|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Wildemount}.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: While Star Razor is in a dormant state, you can hold this magic longsword and use a bonus action to speak the command word {@i Galas-var}, causing the sword to emit a pale blue glow that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. This glow lasts until you use a bonus action to speak the command word again, or until you drop or sheathe the sword.

items: While this longsword is glowing, you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with the weapon, and you have resistance to radiant damage.

You can cast the {@spell faerie fire} spell from the weapon as an action, requiring no components (save {@dc 13}). Once a spell has been cast using Star Razor, that spell can't be cast from the sword until the next dawn.

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When Star Razor reaches an exalted state, you gain the following benefits:

items: The weapon's bonus to attack and damage rolls increases to +3.

The burst of radiance you can create as a reaction when hit with a melee attack deals {@damage 1d12} radiant damage, and you can immediately teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 15 feet of you as part of the same reaction.
You can cast the {@spell fly} spell from the sword as an action, and the save DC for spells cast using the sword increases to 17.

name: Starbreaker
entries: This glowing {@item Morningstar|XPHB} sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet while you hold it. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Radiant damage on a hit. In addition, you can cast the {@spell Daylight|XPHB} spell using the weapon. Once the weapon has been used to cast this spell, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Starmetal Ring
entries: This roughly crafted metal ring seems to have an otherworldly pull on other metallic items. While touching an object with the hand that bears this ring, you can spend 1 hour forging a magical bond between the ring and the object, provided the object weighs no more than 25 pounds and is at least 50 percent metal. Only one object can be bound to the ring in this way at a time.

While wearing the ring, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turn to magically pull its bound object up to 20 feet toward you, provided the object is within 40 feet of you and isn't behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}. The pulled object bounces harmlessly off of creatures and other objects in its path. If you pull the object into your space, you can catch it in your free hand if you have one. Otherwise, it falls to the ground at your feet.

name: Starmetal Shard Spear
entries: This weapon's otherwise small blade is made larger by 3 sharp fragments of starmetal that remain magically connected to it. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you hit a creature with an attack using the head of this spear, you can choose to leave 1 of the fragments embedded in its body. As a bonus action, you can speak the spear's command word to cause all embedded shards to magically return to the blade of the spear, flying through the air and avoiding creatures and objects to do so. When you do, the target takes {@damage 1d6} slashing damage for each embedded shard as it leaves the body. If all 3 shards are embedded in the same creature when you speak the command word, the creature's speed is also halved until the end of your next turn. If the spear is ever more than 120 feet away from a shard, the shard magically returns to the spear without harming the creature it was embedded in.
Immediately after you make a ranged attack with the spear, the weapon flies back to your hand.

name: Starmetal Shield
entries: This open metal Shield hovers above its paired gauntlet, protecting you but leaving your hand free. While wearing the gauntlet, you are considered to be wielding the Shield, but you have a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} instead of a Shield's normal bonus to AC. Whenever you're targeted by an attack roll made with a metal weapon or projectile, this bonus becomes +3 instead.

entries.name: Shooting Star
entries: While wearing the gauntlet, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to throw the Shield, bouncing it between clustered targets before it returns to your arm. Choose up to three creatures, objects, or points. The first target must be within 30 feet of you, and any additional targets the Shield bounces toward must be within 10 feet of the target before it. You can't select the same target more than once each time you throw the Shield.

Make a ranged attack roll against each target. The targets gain no benefit from {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} or {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover} for the attack. You are proficient with these attacks and add either your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice) to their attack rolls and damage rolls. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 2d8} Slashing damage. The Shield flies back to the gauntlet after reaching its final target. It bounces harmlessly off of any other creatures or objects in its path.

name: Starmetal Sliver
entries: This slim blade was forged using strange, unearthly metals from a meteorite. When you use an action to toss this magic dagger into the air, it orbits your body at a distance of {@dice 1d3} feet. Another creature can use an action to grasp the dagger to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful DC 24 Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. You can use an action to seize and either wield or stow the dagger.

When you take the {@action Attack} action while the dagger is orbiting you, you can use a bonus action to cause the dagger to attack a target within 10 feet of you. The dagger uses your attack roll and ability score modifier to damage rolls. Immediately after the attack, the dagger returns to orbit you.

In addition, the dagger creates a small gravitational field that wards off harm. While the dagger orbits you, when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by {@dice 1d10 + 4}. If the damage is reduced to 0, the missile slows to a stop without hitting you and falls to the ground at your feet.

name: Starmetal Solar Axe
entries: This magic weapon is forged using iron from the stars. While you're attuned to this weapon, you can call upon its latent stellar energy to catalyze change within the metal, creating endothermic and exothermic reactions. The weapon can be fissioned into two separated Battleaxes or fused back into a {@item Greataxe|XPHB}. It has the following properties based on its current state.

entries.name: Fused State (Greataxe)
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 2d6} Fire damage on a hit. While holding the axe, flames erupt from its edges and a small star burns in its center. These flames shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet. The light is sunlight.

entries.name: Fissioned State (Battleaxes)
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with each of these magic weapons, which deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Cold damage on a hit. The axes orbit you slowly while they aren't being held or stowed. You can equip an orbiting {@item Battleaxe|XPHB} as if it were sheathed. In addition, if you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make one melee attack with an orbiting {@item Battleaxe|XPHB} against a target you can see within 20 feet of you.

entries.name: State Change
entries: This weapon can change between its two states using the following properties:

entries.name: Fission
entries: While holding the fused {@item Greataxe|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and use a command word to magically split it apart into its fissioned state. When you do, electrical energy is released, forcing other creatures within 30 feet of you to make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 3d6} Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This property can't be used again for 12 hours.

entries.name: Fusion
entries: While holding both fissioned Battleaxes, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and use another command word to magically recombine the weapon into its fused state. When you do, the sudden generation of heat creates a wave of fire around you, forcing other creatures within 30 feet of you to make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 3d6} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This property can't be used again for 12 hours.

name: Starmetal Striker
entries: This {@item Light Hammer|XPHB} was forged using the remains of a comet and is cold to the touch. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra {@damage 1d4} Cold damage on a hit. The hammer leaves behind a crackling mist when thrown, and it flies back to your hand immediately after making a ranged attack with it.

name: Static Shock
entries: This potion makes you feel tingly as it charges you up with static electricity. Immediately after a creature touches you or hits you with a melee attack made with a metal weapon in the next 24 hours, you can use your reaction to send a charge of static electricity back at that creature, dealing {@damage 1d10} lightning damage to it. Once you do so, the effects of this potion end.
{@font {@style 14|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Status Signets
entries: These silver rings often come in pairs and indicate the well-being of its wearer. If you and another friendly creature you can see are wearing these rings within 100 feet of each other, you are magically aware of the other creature's current number of hit points and condition.

name: Steam Harpoon
entries: A curious mesh of magic and steam-powered mechanism, this spear's barbed head can be launched from its shaft and quickly retrieved using the attached chain. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Once on each of your turns when you attack with the spear, you can choose to make a special ranged attack with it, firing the spear head toward a target within 20 feet of you. This ranged attack uses your Dexterity modifier for its attack and damage rolls. On a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 15 feet toward you. A Huge or larger target automatically succeeds on the saving throw. Hit or miss, the spear's head then reels back and reattaches to the top of the weapon immediately after the attack.

name: Steppe Rations
entries: These small rations are made of smoked plants, dried berries, ground nuts, and honey, baked into a chewy bar. Though not sufficiently filling for a day of travel, a bar will stave off hunger for 2 hours. These rations are spiced in such a way that they warm you from the inside out. When you eat a bar, you gain resistance to cold damage for 1 hour. You can only benefit from this effect for 1 hour per day.

name: Steps of the Trickster
entries: These shoes allow you to freely change the sound of your steps while wearing them. Changing the sound of your steps doesn't change their volume but can make them sound as though the shoes are made of a different material. For example, your steps can sound like a beggar's bare feet, a dancer's sharp heels, or an approaching guard's metal boots.

name: Steward's Seal
entries: While wearing this badge, you can cast {@spell mage hand}, {@spell prestidigitation}, {@spell purify food and drink}, and {@spell unseen servant} at-will.

You can use an action to cast one of the following spells: {@spell animate objects}, {@spell create food and water}, {@spell dispel magic}, or {@spell telekinesis}. Once the badge has been used to cast one of these spells, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn. You can choose your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score as the spellcasting ability for casting these spells, and use your proficiency bonus to determine their attack bonus and saving throw DC.

entries.name: Crown Authority
entries: A character cannot attune to more than one Seal of Drakkenheim. Guardian constructs in Drakkenheim such as {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim|wall gargoyles} and {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim|tower dragons} do not attack you while you are attuned to one of the Seals of Drakkenheim. An individual guardian ignores this effect for 24 hours if you attack it or cast a spell upon it.

As an action, you may present a Seal of Drakkenheim to rebuke the guardians. You make an opposed Charisma ability check against each {@creature wall gargoyle|DungeonsDrakkenheim} or {@creature tower dragon|DungeonsDrakkenheim} that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you. If you win the contest, the creature is rebuked for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. A rebuked creature doesn't move, and can't take actions or reactions. A creature who wins the contest is immune to your rebuke for 24 hours.

name: Sticky Hand
entries: While holding this children's toy in one hand, you can cast the {@spell Retrieve|ObojimaTallGrass} spell.

name: Stink Bomb
entries: This smelly explosive can be primed and thrown up to 30 feet as an action. It explodes at the start of your next turn. Creatures within 20 feet of it must make a {@dc 12} Constitution {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} or be {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute. A creature can repeat this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Stink Brew
entries: It stinks, and now so do you! After drinking this potion, all other creatures within 15 feet of you must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be unable to willingly move closer to you for the duration. A creature that hasn't yet made this save must immediately do so when it moves within 15 feet of you. The effects of the potion last {@dice 1d4} rounds.
{@font {@style 11|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Stitching Needle
entries: This black iron needle easily pierces the skin. If a creature's mouth is sewn shut with a Stitching Needle, it loses the ability to speak and cast spells with verbal components. The creature gains the ability to communicate with {@variantrule Telepathy|XPHB} out to a range of 60 feet.
Stitching the mouth of a willing, {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}, or {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} creature takes 10 minutes. Removing the stitches takes 1 minute.

name: Stonemason's Companion
entries: These tools were crafted by a lonely stonemason with a desire for a companion. You gain a +1 bonus to ability checks made using this set of mason's tools.

If you are proficient with mason's tools, you can use these tools to carve 10 gp worth of fine stone into the shape of a Small or smaller creature over the course of a full workday, mimicking the effects of the {@spell find familiar} spell with the following changes: the familiar is an elemental and, while it remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a stone statue.

When the familiar falls to 0 hit points, the spell ends and it crumbles into a pile of nonmagical rubble. While a familiar created by the stonemason's companion exists, you can't use the tools to create another one.

name: Storm Channeling Wand
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA}
entries: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

items.name: Casting Time
entries: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 {@action Magic|XPHB} action to instead be cast as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Duration
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.

items.name: Range
entries: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.

items.name: Regaining Charges
entries: The wand regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Storm Dragonmark Channel
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA}
entries: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.

While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Storm Dragonmark Reservoir
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA}
entries: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA|Spells of the Mark} list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Storm Seer Lamp
entries: This crystal lantern gives off a faint, refreshing smell that reminds you of being near the ocean. As a bonus action, you can touch the crystal to cause it to glow, casting bright light in a 5- to 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional number of feet equal to the chosen radius. You can alter the radius or cause the light to fade using a bonus action to touch the crystal again. Once the lamp has glowed for a total of 8 hours, it can't be used again in this way until the next dusk.

In addition, the lamp can detect incoming storms up to 3 hours before they arrive. If an approaching storm would affect the area within 1 mile of the lamp, the crystal's light becomes an eerie, cold gray.

name: Storm Sickle
entries: This {@item Sickle|XPHB} sparks with electricity as beads of water form and drip from its blade. The weapon can be used to make special ranged attacks by slashing it through the air to send out blades of storming wind.

You're proficient with these attacks, which have a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet, use your Strength modifier for their attack rolls and damage rolls, and deal {@damage 1d4} Slashing damage on a hit.
Attacks with this magic {@item Sickle|XPHB} deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Lightning damage on a hit, regardless of whether you attack with the weapon itself or use its special ranged attack.

name: Storm Thrower Harpoon
entries: You have a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you make a ranged attack with the {@item Trident|XPHB}, it deals an extra {@damage 1d8} Lightning damage on a hit. Immediately after hitting or missing, you can use the chain attached to the weapon's handle to pull it back to your hand as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

In addition, this {@item Trident|XPHB} acts as a conduit for the sky's ferocious power. Immediately after hitting a creature with the {@item Trident|XPHB}, you can call down a bolt of lightning upon the target, provided it's unobstructed from the sky. The target and each creature within 5 feet of it must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 6d10} Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that is submerged in water or wearing metal armor has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the save, and you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the Lightning damage dealt by this effect. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Impale
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can try to impale and pull a creature toward you. If the target is no more than one size larger than you, make a ranged attack against it using the {@item Trident|XPHB}. On a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 20 feet toward you.

name: Storm's Embrace
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Storm|EFA}
additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Ring of Feather Falling|XDMG}}

name: Storm's Eye Shield
entries: Emblazoned on the face of this round shield is a cyclone design that magically swirls based on the likelihood and proximity of thunderstorms. While holding this shield, you have resistance to lightning damage. When you take lightning damage from a hostile source while holding this shield, you can use your reaction to cast the {@spell thunderwave} spell (save DC 15) from it. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

In addition, while the shield is flat on the ground, you can perform a 1 minute ritual to cast the {@spell augury} spell from it. When you do, the omens are represented by how the cyclone's design changes:

items: {@b Calm clouds,} for good results
{@b Roiling clouds,} for bad results
{@b A flash of lightning,} for both good and bad results
{@b Nothing,} for results that aren't especially good or bad

entries: Once this property of the shield has been used, it can't be used again until it's been in the presence of another thunderstorm for at least 1 hour.

name: Stormbinder's Cloak
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold, Lightning, and Thunder damage while wearing this cloak. You also ignore any Obscurement created by magical or non-magical clouds, fog, or mist. Lastly, whenever you cast a level 1+ spell that deals Cold, Lightning, or Thunder damage, you may treat the spell as if you had cast it with a spell slot 1 higher than the slot used.

name: Stormbrewer Bracers
entries: This pair of electrum bracers are always covered in a thin layer of condensation. When you roll initiative while wearing the bracers, they begin to billow out wafting clouds around your wrists. The clouds surrounding your wrists grow darker with every charge the bracers have, becoming fierce storm clouds when fully charged. The bracers can hold up to 5 charges, which are lost after 1 minute. The bracers gain 1 charge after you hit a hostile creature with a melee weapon attack while wearing them. If the bracers have 5 charges when you hit a creature in this way, they unleash a burst of electricity and lose all their stored charges, dealing {@damage 1d8} lightning damage to the target of the attack and up to 2 other creatures of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you.
In addition, while wearing the bracers, you can use your reaction when you take lightning damage to reduce that damage by {@dice 1d8 + 4} and cause the bracers to gain 1 charge.

name: Stormhorn
entries: This wooden horn is carved from lightning-struck yew. It has {@b 6 charges} and regains {@dice 1d6} charges each day at dawn. It can be blown as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast a spell—{@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Sleet Storm|XPHB} (3 charges)— using your spell save DC.

name: Stormrider Boots
entries: These dark leather boots look to be of common make, but a subtle pattern of swirling storm clouds upon their soles suggests the potency of their enchantment. You can activate these boots as part of your movement, gaining the following benefits until the end of your turn:

items: You have a flying speed of 90 feet.
{@action Opportunity attack|PHB|Opportunity attacks} against you are made with {@quickref Advantage and Disadvantage|PHB|2|0|disadvantage}.

Whenever you move within 5 feet of a hostile creature, it must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} or take {@damage 3d8} lightning damage. A creature can't be damaged in this way more than once per turn.

entries: Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Stormstruck Staff
entries: This wooden {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} has been scarred by lightning, and an amplifying crystal is embedded at its head. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra 1 Lightning damage on a hit.

Whenever the {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} takes Lightning damage or you take Lightning damage while holding it (from a source other than the {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} itself), the crystal glows brilliantly and pulses with electrical energy for 1 minute. It also glows in this way while under the effect of the {@spell Shillelagh|XPHB} spell. While the crystal is glowing in this way, it emits {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 10 feet, and the extra Lightning damage the {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} deals on a hit increases to {@dice 1d6}.

name: Stormwalker's Cloak
entries: While wearing this cloak, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Shocking Feedback
entries: The cloak has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. You can expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Hellish Rebuke|XPHB} from the cloak (DC 13), and the spell deals your choice of Lightning or Thunder damage instead of the usual Fire damage.

entries.name: Storm Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning and Thunder damage.

name: Storrbani

entries.name: Fabled Magic Items
entries: Fabled magic items are distinct as a rarity. A fabled item grows in power alongside the character who wields it. Rules for fabled items are summarized here, and a few fabled magic items can be found in this chapter.
A fabled magic item begins as a Common magic item. The item grants a minor, useful trait to its owner that doesn't require {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to use.

To access any higher-level trait, a PC must attune to it using standard {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} rules. Once attuned, a PC can use the fabled item's more powerful properties as they increase in level. If a PC higher than 1st level attunes to a fabled item, its level-dependent properties, up to the character's current level, are immediately available.

At the GM's discretion, an item's more powerful properties might become available only after the character completes a particular quest or event related to the item's story rather than immediately upon reaching each property's required level.
If a PC chooses not to attune to a fabled item, it remains a common magic item, granting only its minor property, regardless of the character's level.
Unless otherwise noted, properties granted by a fabled item are in effect as long at the character is wearing, carrying, or touching the item.

This longsword is supernaturally light and easy to use. Its weight is reduced to 1 pound, and it gains the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} weapon property. Sparks trail from Storrbani's blade as though it were a burning branch. When you hit a target with Storrbani, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} Fire damage as the blade burns upon impact.
As your level increases, you gain the following benefits while wielding or holding this weapon if you are attuned to it:

entries.name: 5th Level
entries: The rune Gebo appears on the blade. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch the rune and cast {@spell Shield of Faith|XPHB} on a creature (besides yourself) you can see within {@b 60 feet}. You don't need to {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrate} on the spell to maintain it. Once used in this way, you must finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} before you can use it again.

In addition, the spirit of Thogar Giant-Hewer awakens within the longsword. It becomes a sentient, Lawful Neutral weapon with Intelligence 8, Wisdom 13, and Charisma 10. It has hearing and vision out to a range of 60 feet. It communicates telepathically with its wielder, and it can speak in a gravelly voice much like an angry growl. It can read and understand Common and Giant. Thogar's spirit is passionate but not particularly bright. It wants the wielder to confront giants and trolls, and (secretly) to fall in glorious battle against the forces of Jotunheim so that wielder and blade may feast and fight together in eternal Valhalla. It urges its wielder to seek out and destroy evil trolls and giants, and to never back down from a fight. If its wielder displays cowardice or refuses an opportunity to battle an evil troll or other giant, the spirit sulks, suppressing the magical properties of the weapon until the following dawn.

entries.name: 9th Level
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon, and the amount of Fire damage it deals increases to {@damage 2d6}. In addition, the rune Tiwaz appears on the blade. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch this rune and give the extra Fire damage from this blade to the weapon of a creature you can see within {@b 60 feet}. At the end of your next turn, the Fire damage property returns to Storrbani.

entries.name: 13th Level
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon instead of a +1 bonus. In addition, the rune Thurisaz appears on the blade. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch this rune. When you do so, your attack rolls with this magic weapon score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 until the end of your next turn. If the target is a creature of the giant type, Storrbani deals an extra {@damage 1d8} damage on a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB|critical hit}.

entries.name: 17th Level
entries: You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon, instead of a +2 bonus. In addition, the rune Ansuz appears on the blade. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch the rune and gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage until the end of your next turn. Once used, the sword can't be used again in this way until the next dawn.

name: Storyteller's Stein
entries: These steins are enchanted with a clever version of the {@spell prestidigitation} spell that reacts when in the company of a good story. Whenever you tell a story while holding this stein, its lid opens and closes like a mouth to emit sounds and other harmless sensory effects that accompany the tale. For example, if you're telling the story of a thunderstorm at sea, the stein can create the sounds of rumbling thunder and creaking floorboards, or allow you to spew illusory flames after taking a drink from the stein when you tell the story of an ancient red dragon's deadly breath.

name: Straitjacket
entries: This stained grey jacket has long arms reaching the floor and contains dozens of restraining straps. This magical jacket takes 10 minutes to don or doff. While wearing this item and not wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|XPHB}, you add your Intelligence modifier to your {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}. Also, you can cast spells without using Somatic or Material components that don't have a GP value listed. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.

If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the {@charoption Aberrant Horror|GrimHollowPG24|Aberrant Horror Transformation}, you may roll twice whenever rolling on the {@table Unstable Form|GrimHollowPG24|Unstable Form table} and choose either result.

name: Strig Feather Robe
reqAttune: by a sorcerer, warlock, or wizard
entries: This luxuriant robe is made from the feather of a birdfolk spellcaster. Though it appears to be made of many individual plumes, the robe is actually composed of only a single feather, flawlessly copied over and over again by the magic that created it.
You gain the following benefits from wearing the robe.

items: Your Intelligence or Charisma score becomes 22 (your choice when you first attune to the robe).
You have a +1 bonus to saving throws while you wear this robe.

Your spell attacks have advantage against foes that have not yet acted in this combat. Treat any successful spell attack roll made against a {@status surprised} creature as though it were a critical hit.

name: Stuffy Familiar
entries: This small stuffed animal is soft to the touch and perfect for hugging. If you can cast the {@spell find familiar} spell, you can use the animal as the material component for the spell, without it being consumed. When you do, the familiar inhabits the form of the stuffed animal, whose appearance you can change as part of casting the spell in this way. The familiar is a construct, in addition to being either a celestial, fey, or fiend, but its statistics are otherwise unchanged from its normal form. The familiar's stuffed animal form must be appropriate to the statistics of its normal animal one. For example, a familiar within a griffon stuffed animal could use the statistics for a {@creature cat} or {@creature hawk}, but not a {@creature poisonous snake}. The stuffed animal grows or shrinks to match the size of the familiar's normal form.

While the familiar remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal stuffed animal. If you temporarily dismiss the familiar, the stuffed animal and familiar disappear into a pocket dimension together. If the familiar is dismissed forever or drops to 0 hit points, it leaves the stuffed animal behind.

name: Stylist's Circlet
entries: While wearing this leather circlet, you can use a bonus action to change your hair's length, color, and styling. When you remove the circlet, your hair returns to its natural appearance. Your hair can grow up to 5 feet long in this way, and any hair you cut off immediately vanishes.

name: Styx Boots
entries: These boots are usually made of heavy, sturdy leather—perhaps it's demon hide or some other planar creature's hide. While wearing these boots, you can walk over any body of water as if it were normal terrain, and you can slide or skate over relatively calm waters, snow, ice, sand, magma, or other smooth surfaces at double your normal walking speed. If the snow or ice is on a hill, you move at triple your normal walking speed. You can still use the {@action Dash} action normally as well.

When combined with the Armor of the Black River, the Styx boots permit you to use any branch of the River Styx and other planar waterways as a form of shadow road. Once per week, you can walk on such a planar waterway for 8 hours and arrive at any other plane of your choosing.

name: Suit of the Lamb
entries: This suit of comfortable woolen clothes, made from the wool of the rare and dangerous poffer, includes a shirt, trousers or a kilt, and thick socks. While wearing the suit, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning damage, and you don't suffer effects from extreme cold weather.

name: Summer's Dance
entries: This beautiful golden blade appears to bend and flex like a reed with your movements. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Additionally, the scimitar has 3 charges and regains 1 expended charge daily at dawn. While wielding this {@item scimitar|PHB}, you can expend 1 charge as a bonus action to cast the {@spell misty step} spell.

name: Sun Eater Staff
entries: This lengthy staff of black wood has veins of black opal and obsidian running through it, and it feels cool to the touch.
This staff can be wielded as a magic quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.
The staff has 10 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 4} charges daily at midnight.

entries.name: Spells
entries: While holding the staff, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC: {@spell Melf's Acid Arrow||acid arrow} (2 charges), {@spell blight} (4 charges), {@spell darkness} (1 charge), {@spell fog cloud} (1 charge), or {@spell wall of force} (5 charges).

entries.name: Consume Light
entries: You can expend 1 charge as an action to extinguish any light sources of your choice that you can see within 120 feet of you.

entries.name: Fire Immunity
entries: When you take fire damage while holding the staff, you can expend 1 charge as a reaction.
You gain immunity to fire damage until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering effect.

name: Sun Eater's Mind
entries: The shifting shadows within this black glass ring constantly move. While wearing this ring, when a creature you can see within 60 feet of you makes a spell attack against you or casts a spell that requires you to make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to pierce the creature's mind. The next attack you make against that creature before the end of your next turn is automatically a critical hit. The ring can be used to pierce a creature's mind three times and regains all uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Sun Eater's Gift
entries: While within 30 feet of a willing creature who is attuned to the Sun Eater's soul, you can use a bonus action to swap places with them. The ring can be used to swap places three times and regains all uses daily at dusk.

name: Sun Eater's Soul
entries: This black metal ring is unnervingly matte, reflecting nothing even in the brightest of light. While wearing this ring, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you is hit with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the damage that creature takes from the attack. The ring can be used to halve damage three times and regains all uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Sun Eater's Grace
entries: When you cast a spell that restores hit points to a creature, you can also restore that same number of hit points to a creature within 30 feet of you who is attuned to the Sun Eater's mind. The ring can be used to restore hit points three times and regains all uses daily at dusk.

name: Sun Shades
entries: These black leather goggles are set with cloudy glass that completely obscures the eyes of the wearer. You can take an action to don or doff these goggles. While wearing these goggles, you ignore your Sunlight Sensitivity, as well as any other ill effects you would suffer due to exposure to sunlight. The goggles also block your {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, preventing you from seeing in the dark.

name: Sunbaked Cassette
entries: This sun-damaged cassette is beginning to lose hold of the magic stored inside it. As a bonus action, you can hold the cassette out in front of you in an attempt to draw out its power. Roll a {@dice d4}; on a roll of 3 or lower, you regain an expended spell slot of a level equal to the number rolled (if you don't have any expended spell slots of that level, you instead regain a spell slot of the next-highest level that you have expended). On a roll of 4, you teleport 30 feet in a random direction.
Once you regain a spell slot in this way you can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Sunbeam Compass
entries: A device that always directs the user to the sun by emitting a small light at the tip of the needle in a glass orb, allowing it to rotate in all directions—a very useful tool when exploring subterranean territory.
Created by {@book Karaline von Ethro|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Karaline von Ethro}.

name: Sundersludge Net
entries: This gelatinous {@item Net|XPHB} is made with the enchanted remains of a gray ooze. A creature takes {@damage 1d6} Acid damage when it gains the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition from the {@item Net|XPHB}, and it takes that damage again at the end of each of its turns until that condition ends. If the creature is wearing nonmagical metal armor, its armor is partly corroded and takes a cumulative -1 penalty to the AC it offers whenever it takes Acid damage at the end of one of its turns. The armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10. The penalty can be removed by casting the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell on the armor. A creature other than you who touches the {@item Net|XPHB} takes {@damage 1d6} Acid damage.

The {@item Net|XPHB}'s sticky composition makes it more difficult to escape from than a mundane one. To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 13 Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, freeing the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} creature on a success. Destroying the {@item Net|XPHB} (AC 10; 5 HP; {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage; {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all other damage) also frees the target, ending the effect and tearing the {@item Net|XPHB} apart.

The torn {@item Net|XPHB} is harmless. If more than half of the {@item Net|XPHB} can be salvaged and stored within a container large enough to hold 5 gallons of liquid for 12 hours, the {@item Net|XPHB} is repaired and can be used once more. Your attunement to the {@item Net|XPHB} ends if the {@item Net|XPHB} remains torn for longer than 48 hours.
