You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to damage from the {@item Net|XPHB} while you're attuned to it. Picking up the {@item Net|XPHB} after throwing it renders it harmless until the next time you throw it. The {@item Net|XPHB} deals no Acid damage if there isn't a creature attuned to it.

name: Suneater Featherfrond
entries: When this featherfrond is socketed on a holdable or wearable item, the item becomes augmented and attuneable. The item gains the Sun Torch property for as long as a creature is attuned to it.

entries.name: Sun Torch
entries: As a bonus action, you can light or snuff out the featherfrond. While lit, it sheds bright light in a {@b 20-foot} radius and dim light for an additional {@b 20 feet}.

name: Sunfeather Shroud (rare)
entries: The feathers of a suneater owlbear possess a brilliant dichromatic effect causing it to sparkle in the sunlight, conferring the ability to dance between patches of sunlight. Particularly well-crafted specimens can augment the magic of the featherfronds, allowing them to generate blinding flashes of light.
While you wear this shroud, you have advantage on Intimidation checks.

entries.name: Sunstep
entries: When you are in bright light, you can use a bonus action to teleport up to {@b 60 feet} to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in bright light. When you do so, roll a {@dice d6}. On a 1, you can't use the Sunstep property again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Blinding Flash
entries: As an action, you can cause the featherfronds to erupt in a dazzling display of bright light. Each creature within {@b 15 feet} of you must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition blinded} for {@b 1 minute}. A {@condition blinded} creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once you activate this property, you can't do so again until the shroud spends at least 1 hour absorbing bright, direct daylight.

name: Sunfeather Shroud (uncommon)
entries: The feathers of a suneater owlbear possess a brilliant dichromatic effect causing it to sparkle in the sunlight, conferring the ability to dance between patches of sunlight. Particularly well-crafted specimens can augment the magic of the featherfronds, allowing them to generate blinding flashes of light.

entries.name: Sunstep
entries: When you are in bright light, you can use a bonus action to teleport up to {@b 60 feet} to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in bright light. When you do so, roll a {@dice d6}. On a 1, you can't use the Sunstep property again until the next dawn.

name: Sunfeather Shroud (very rare)
entries: The feathers of a suneater owlbear possess a brilliant dichromatic effect causing it to sparkle in the sunlight, conferring the ability to dance between patches of sunlight. Particularly well-crafted specimens can augment the magic of the featherfronds, allowing them to generate blinding flashes of light.
While you wear this shroud, you have advantage on Intimidation checks and resistance to radiant damage.

entries.name: Sunstep
entries: When you are in bright light, you can use a bonus action to teleport up to {@b 60 feet} to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in bright light.

entries.name: Blinding Flash
entries: As an action, you can cause the featherfronds to erupt in a dazzling display of bright light. Each creature within {@b 15 feet} of you must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition blinded} for {@b 1 minute}. A {@condition blinded} creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Once you activate this property, you can't do so again until the shroud spends at least 1 hour absorbing bright, direct daylight.

name: Sunken Suitcase
entries: This magic suitcase is indestructible and fully sealed from the outside world. When closed, it magically locks itself, setting its DC equal to {@dice 1d20 + 5}.

name: Super Singing
entries: When consumed, this potion tastes as if it were a freshly brewed tea with the perfect amount of honey mixed in. For the next hour, you are unable to speak without singing, and you have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Performance}) checks using your voice.
{@font {@style 17|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Surgeon's Tools
entries: This set of instruments includes the blades, saws, and sutures needed to remove shrapnel or stitch up wounds. Proficiency with these tools lets you add your proficiency bonus to any checks you make to stabilise a creature or perform other surgery.

name: Sustaining Belt
entries: This wide belt has short, soft grey fur on both its inner and outer faces, with a long strap bearing many more punch holes than an ordinary belt. While wearing this belt, you don't have to consume as much food or water. You can go an additional number of days equal to your Constitution modifier before you suffer the effects of starvation or dehydration.

name: Suude (Blue)
entries: Exandria's most infamous drug, {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} is a glittering powder made from {@book residuum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|An Enchanting Export}. It was first developed by power-hungry archmages in the {@book Age of Arcanum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|Age of Arcanum} as an incense burned to enhance focus during ritual spellcasting. The secret to its refinement has been lost and rediscovered a variety of times since the {@book Calamity|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|1|The Calamity}, and many different types of {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} have been developed by arcanists in search of ever-greater power. It has terrible addictive and mentally degenerative properties, even when used sparingly.

After burning {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} within a vessel and inhaling its fumes as an action, you take 22 ({@damage 4d10}) psychic damage and must make a {@dc 10} Constitution {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw}. On a failure, you become {@condition poisoned} for 1 hour and fall {@condition unconscious} for 1 minute, or until you are shaken awake as an action. During this time, the world seems to move in slow motion, and your vision is twisted in kaleidoscopic colors—yet your focus is never distorted. If one dose of {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, or more, is used within 1 hour of another, the DC of the Constitution {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} is increased by 5 per additional dose. If you fail this save by 10 or more, you instantly drop to 0 hit points.

On a success, you gain the ability to use one of the following Metamagic options as a sorcerer for the next minute, requiring no sorcery points. The type of Metamagic you gain access to depends on the type of {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, and once you use it, you can't use it again until you inhale {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} again.
Blue suude allows you to use the {@optfeature Twinned Spell|PHB} Metamagic option.

entries: Exandria's most infamous drug, {@item suude|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn} is a glittering powder made from {@book residuum|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|An Enchanting Export}. Red suude allows you to use the {@optfeature Distant Spell|PHB} Metamagic option.

name: Swansong Staff
entries: This gnarled, oak {@item staff|XPHB} ends in a crook reminiscent of a swan's neck. It is clearly ancient, and was only recently uncovered from deep within an elven ruin.
You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

Once a day, if the wielder is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the Swansong {@item Staff|XPHB} immediately animates (using the stats of an {@creature Animated Broom|XMM}) to protect them. The weapon acts on the wielder's initiative. If the animated weapon is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or if its wielder regains consciousness, it becomes inanimate once more.

name: Swashbuckler's Boots
entries: While wearing these supple leather boots, {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating Swashbuckler's Boots requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Fey Dust

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Elemental Fluid

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Any

name: Switch
entries: This simple, springy rod is made of twisting vines and twigs. While holding the rod, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to activate it, magically transforming it into a weapon. It can take the form of any kind of Simple or Martial weapon of your choice that deals Bludgeoning or Piercing damage and lacks the {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading} and {@itemProperty R|XPHB|Reach} properties. If you transform the rod into a weapon with the {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition} property, it magically creates its own ammunition when you make a ranged attack with it.

Regardless of the weapon's form, you're proficient with it and can use your Wisdom modifier for its attack and damage rolls instead of Strength or Dexterity. On a hit, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d8} damage of its normal type.

While holding the weapon, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to transform it into another qualifying weapon or temporarily back into its rod form until you transform it into a weapon again. Alternatively, you can expend a second use of your Wild Shape feature as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to extend the bark of the activated rod or weapon to your body, covering yourself in treelike armor. When you do, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to four times your Druid level, and until the rod deactivates, you have an {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} of 17 if your AC is lower than that.

The rod deactivates after a number of hours equal to half your Druid level (round down), immediately reverting to its rod form if it's still a weapon. It deactivates early if you drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or choose to deactivate it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

name: Sword of Resonance
entries: This peculiar brass {@item Longsword|XPHB} is hollow and has {@item lute|XPHB} strings that run along its blade, allowing you to use it as a {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} and {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}. You are proficient with the Sword of Resonance as both an instrument and {@item Longsword|XPHB} while you're attuned to it. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} property.

In addition, the sword's hollow metal blade magically amplifies the music made when using it to inspire allies. Whenever you expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration while holding the sword, it begins to reverberate with thunderous energy. The next time you hit a target with an attack using the sword before the end of your next turn, that target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Thunder damage from the attack.

name: Sword of the Crimson Abbot (Legendary)
entries: This powerful, fiendish sword was once wielded by the Crimson Abbot. While it was created as a gift that brought evil and malice to the corrupted former knight, it has lost its connections to the Crimson Rose. However, its evil origins still linger within. The sword is sleek and polished, with a blade that absorbs light. A blood-red ruby on the hilt is fitted within a setting of thorns and roses.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by the sword's rarity. While holding the sword, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Blood Drain (Rare+)
entries: When you hit a creature with the sword, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Irresistible Hunger (Very Rare+)
entries: Necrotic damage you deal ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}.

entries.name: Vampiric Charm (Very Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the sword's bonus, no {@status Concentration|XPHB} required) from the sword. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Embrace of the Duchess (Legendary)
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can touch the sword to the body of a Humanoid that has been dead for 1 minute or less. The creature must succeed on a DC 19 Charisma saving throw (as if it were alive) or become a {@creature Vampire Spawn|XMM} that dies again at dawn. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Stolen Life (Legendary)
entries: When you deal Necrotic damage with the Blood Drain property, you can expend and roll one {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Points Die}. You regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the number rolled plus the Necrotic damage dealt.

name: Sword of the Crimson Abbot (Rare)
entries: This powerful, fiendish sword was once wielded by the Crimson Abbot. While it was created as a gift that brought evil and malice to the corrupted former knight, it has lost its connections to the Crimson Rose. However, its evil origins still linger within. The sword is sleek and polished, with a blade that absorbs light. A blood-red ruby on the hilt is fitted within a setting of thorns and roses.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by the sword's rarity. While holding the sword, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Blood Drain (Rare+)
entries: When you hit a creature with the sword, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage.

name: Sword of the Crimson Abbot (Very Rare)
entries: This powerful, fiendish sword was once wielded by the Crimson Abbot. While it was created as a gift that brought evil and malice to the corrupted former knight, it has lost its connections to the Crimson Rose. However, its evil origins still linger within. The sword is sleek and polished, with a blade that absorbs light. A blood-red ruby on the hilt is fitted within a setting of thorns and roses.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with this magic weapon determined by the sword's rarity. While holding the sword, you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Blood Drain (Rare+)
entries: When you hit a creature with the sword, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage.

entries.name: Irresistible Hunger (Very Rare+)
entries: Necrotic damage you deal ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}.

entries.name: Vampiric Charm (Very Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the sword's bonus, no {@status Concentration|XPHB} required) from the sword. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Sword of the Spelldrinker
entries: This sword seems to absorb any light that touches it, making it appear darker than the deepest midnight. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While holding the sword, you treat any magical light or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} within 30 feet of you as if it were nonmagical, and you can breathe normally in any environment.

In addition, this sword has 2 charges and regains {@dice 1d2} expended charges daily at dusk. While holding the sword, you can expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} from it. When cast in this way, the target automatically fails its saving throw if the triggering spell is level 5 or lower, and it automatically succeeds if the spell is level 6 or higher. If you successfully interrupt a spell in this way, you can choose to absorb it into the sword instead of allowing it to dissipate. The absorbed spell must have a casting time of an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. The sword can have only one absorbed spell at a time.

While holding the sword, you can release its absorbed spell. Doing so requires you to take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} (as determined by the spell's normal casting time), and it uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell.
The interrupted spell remains absorbed by the sword for 8 hours or until it's released. Absorbing a new spell replaces the one stored within the sword.

name: Sync Ring
entries: When you attune to this ring, choose a blank book you are touching. Thereafter, whenever you write something using the hand that wears the ring, a copy of your writing magically appears in the chosen book. Magical writing, such as a spell copied from a {@item Spell Scroll|XPHB} or a glyph inscribed for the {@spell Glyph of Warding|XPHB} spell, is transcribed literally but is nonmagical.
If no blank pages are left in the book or the book is on a different plane of existence than you for more than 24 hours, your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the ring ends.

name: Talisman of the Phoenix
entries: This talisman has {@dice 1d4} charges. When you fail a death saving throw while the talisman is on your person, you can choose to expend a charge to succeed instead. Once all of the talisman's charges have been used, it burns up in a flash, leaving behind a pile of ashes. It then reforms with {@dice 1d4} charges somewhere else on the same plane.

name: Talisman of Tormach
entries: The dreadful talisman is crafted from the skull at the center of a gore elemental. When you kill a creature with a melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} while you wear the talisman, you gain 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} for 1 minute.

While you have any of these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, your melee weapon attacks and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage on a hit.

name: Talking Wand
entries: While you are holding this wand, your voice and other sounds you produce are three times as loud as normal. House Phiarlan makes use of a similar device, the Thunderous Amulet, that leaves the wearer's hands free.

name: Talon Gloves
entries: These leather gloves are outfitted with the talons of fallen beasts and stitched together with the arcane stitching of apothecary creations. The gloves are then empowered by elemental magic, reinforced with bone, and powered by an animus.

While wearing these gloves, you gain {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage on a hit.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating Talon Gloves requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Elemental Fluid

items.name: [Hair]
entries: Stitches

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Skin

items.name: [Natural Weapons]
entries: Claws

name: Talon Tincture
entries: When you apply this light tincture to your talons, claws, or other appendages, you gain advantage on Dexterity ability checks and saving throws for 24 hours.

name: Talons of the Squall
entries: Awarded to those who pass the test of endurance administered by priests of {@deity Altus|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting}, these leg-bracers seem to crackle with faint energy. While you wear them, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have resistance to lightning damage.
You have advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to resist being moved by strong winds.

You do not suffer disadvantage on ranged attack rolls or {@skill Perception} checks while in strong winds or under conditions of heavy rain or snowfall. If you can fly, you can fly at a normal speed under such conditions.

name: Talyard the Great's Wand of Power
entries: This normal-looking spruce stick is actually the wand of a famous drunkard. A drunken creature that sees the stick perceives it as a magnificent, colorful wand that radiates with an awesome power.

This wand has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dusk. While you're {@condition drunk|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} and are holding the wand, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (+3 spellcasting ability modifier) from it: {@spell Heroism|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB} (2 charges), or {@spell Thaumaturgy|XPHB} (0 charges).

name: Tarrasque Plate
entries: This impenetrable armor is made from refined fragments of a tarrasque's armored hide and retains some of its original properties. You have resistance to damage from spells and a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor. In addition, whenever you're targeted by a {@spell magic missile} spell, a line spell, or a spell that requires a ranged attack roll, roll a {@dice d6}. On a 6, you are unaffected by the spell, and the effect is reflected back at the caster as though it originated from you, turning the caster into the target.

name: Tarrobe (legendary)
entries: Fossilised bones and oilcloth, a lipid-rich mesh of viscous crude oil and lipophilic fibres, forms the basis of this magical robe. In the same way the oil refracts light in rainbow hues, the cloth has a natural resistance to magic, occasionally sending spells ricocheting back at the caster.
While you wear the robe you can speak and understand Terran.

entries.name: Oily Barrage
entries: While you wear this robe, you can cast a variety of oil-based spells. This robe has {@b 12 charges} and regains {@dice 1d8 + 4} charges daily at dawn. You can expend charges to cast the following spells (save {@dc 15}, {@hit +7} to hit). Some spells are changed to be oil-based.

items: {@spell Grease} (1 charge)
Create or destroy oil (2 charges; as {@spell create or destroy water}, but oil instead of water)
{@spell Mireball|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} (3 charges; instead of mud, thick, rancid fat and oil are conjured)
{@spell bone cage|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} (5 charges)
{@spell conjure elemental} (tar elemental only, see page 589) (5 charges)

entries.name: Spell Reflection
entries: While you wear this robe, any time you are targeted by a {@spell magic missile} spell, a line spell, or a spell that requires a ranged attack roll, roll a {@dice d8}. On a 1-6, you are affected as normal. On a 7 or 8, you are unaffected, and the effect is reflected back at the caster as though it originated from you, turning the caster into the target.

name: Tarrobe (rare)
entries: Fossilised bones and oilcloth, a lipid-rich mesh of viscous crude oil and lipophilic fibres, forms the basis of this magical robe. In the same way the oil refracts light in rainbow hues, the cloth has a natural resistance to magic, occasionally sending spells ricocheting back at the caster.

entries.name: Oily Barrage
entries: While you wear this robe, you can cast a variety of oil-based spells. This robe has {@b 7 charges} and regains {@dice 1d6 + 1} charges daily at dawn. You can expend charges to cast the following spells (save {@dc 15}, {@hit +7} to hit). Some spells are changed to be oil-based.

items: {@spell Grease} (1 charge)
Create or destroy oil (2 charges; as {@spell create or destroy water}, but oil instead of water)
{@spell Mireball|HelianasGuidetoMonsterHunting} (3 charges; instead of mud, thick, rancid fat and oil are conjured)

entries.name: Spell Reflection
entries: While you wear this robe, any time you are targeted by a {@spell magic missile} spell, a line spell, or a spell that requires a ranged attack roll, roll a {@dice d8}. On a 1-7, you are affected as normal. On an 8, you are unaffected, and the effect is reflected back at the caster as though it originated from you, turning the caster into the target.

name: Tavern Seed
entries: A tavern seed must be used outdoors, and when thrown, it creates a small, snug tavern of stone and wood, roughly 40 feet by 20 feet, with a lower public floor and an upper floor devoted to the staff bedchambers, storage, and a single room for rent. The entire building takes on an outward style of architecture, materials, roofing, and appearance as suits the region where it stands. It has a staff of three: a cook, a bartender, and a servant, of a type typical of the region (so humans in a human realm, shadow fey in the Shadow Realm, goblins in the wastelands, and so on).

Using a tavern seed in an existing settlement creates a snug tavern as normal, magically shifting two buildings to either side slightly to make room. The new structure is certainly notable and surprising to residents of the place.
A tavern seed combined with a road seed always includes a set of warm, secure stables as well as the tavern building itself.

entries.name: Illusion Seeds
entries: Illusion seeds are wondrous items first created in the Shadow Realm and reliant on a supply of shadow matter to power their effects—each such seed generates an illusion and those illusions can take quite powerful forms. While illusion seeds are fairly permanent in the Shadow Realm, where there is shadow matter to empower and sustain the illusions, they are notably less permanent anywhere else. In the mortal world and on other planes, the effects of illusion seeds last for {@dice 2d12} hours and then crumble away in a small burst of glittering light and shadows.

To use an illusion seed, its owner merely needs to throw it 5 feet or more from themselves (to avoid being caught in the magical effect). Once expended, their effects are permanent (in the Shadow Realm), though they can be unraveled using {@spell dispel magic} (DC 13).

name: Tea
entries: High-quality tea leaves, dried and ready to brew.

name: Tea Weird
entries: This Tiny, sentient fragment of a charmed water elemental has an endless desire to create tea. When given a leaf or other potential tea ingredient, its watery form gurgles happily as it begins to steep it, magically heating the water surrounding the ingredient to its ideal brewing temperature. It only picks up materials it chooses to and can control whether or not it's wet to the touch. The tea weird can inhabit up to 1 gallon of water, or as little as 1 ounce. Any water controlled by the tea weird is magical for the duration.

The tea weird is considered a magical object and is not a creature. It has a speed of 5 feet and can hover up to 5 feet off the ground. It has AC 10, 10 hit points, and has resistance to all damage. The tea weird regains all its hit points if given at least 1 ounce of water. Drinking the entire tea weird is harmless to you, but destroys the item.

entries.name: Sentience
entries: The tea weird is a sentient chaotic good item with an Intelligence of 3, a Wisdom of 8, and a Charisma of 6. It has hearing and {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 60 feet. It can't speak or read, but understands {@language Primordial||Aquan} and {@language Common}.

entries.name: Personality
entries: The tea weird is dedicated to making tea. It will happily collect moisture, steep it with fresh ingredients, and then separate itself from the freshly brewed tea by pouring it into a cup or similar vessel. It avoids combat at all costs and enjoys resting in cups, kettles, or the pockets of friendly creatures.

name: Tear of Gaia
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can crush this small, green gem underfoot to activate its magic. When you do, plants in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you instantaneously become healthy and full. Fruit and vegetable-bearing plants in the area grow their produce, which become ripe over the course of 1 hour. If there are no plants within range or you crush the gem against an inorganic material, fertile topsoil 1 inch deep spreads across the area. Healthy green grass immediately grows from the new soil.

name: Tectonic Gauntlets
entries: This magical set of stone gauntlets imbues your fists with the power of the Elemental Plane of Earth. While wearing the gauntlets, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} with your fists deal {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage instead of the usual Bludgeoning damage (unless it's already higher), and they deal double damage to objects and structures. In addition, these gauntlets have 15 charges and regain {@dice 1d10 + 5} expended charges daily at dawn. When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} using your fists, you can expend up to 5 charges to extend your fist's reach by 5 feet for each expended charge.

entries.name: Powerglove
entries: When you hit a target with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend up to 3 charges to deal an extra {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage for each charge spent. If you spend any charges in this way, the target must also succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be pushed 5 feet away from you.

entries.name: Geomancy
entries: You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from them: {@spell Earthquake|XPHB} (8 charges), {@spell Move Earth|XPHB} (6 charges), {@spell Shatter|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Spike Growth|XPHB} (2 charges, with stone projections), or {@spell Wall of Stone|XPHB} (5 charges).

entries.name: Tectonic Plate Armor
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can cause rocks to envelop and protect your body. For 1 hour, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved, and you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity checks and Dexterity saving throws. You can end this property early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. While enveloped in this way, you can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone using a {@variantrule Burrow Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet. While doing so, you don't disturb the material you move through. If you end this property while burrowed in this way, you're shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take {@damage 1d10} Force damage. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Curse
entries: These gauntlets are cursed. Your mind and body become sluggish once you attune to the gauntlets. The gauntlets become one with your flesh and prevent you from removing them. Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 5 feet, and your Intelligence score is reduced by 4 (to a minimum of 7) while cursed. The curse remains even if the attunement ends but can be undone by any effect that removes a curse such as a {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} or {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell, allowing you to remove the gauntlets and end the curse on you.

entries.name: Random Properties
entries: The gauntlets have the following random properties:

items: 1 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Beneficial Properties|XDMG|minor beneficial} property
1 {@table Artifact Properties; Minor Detrimental Properties|XDMG|minor detrimental} property

entries.name: Destroying the Gauntlets
entries: The gauntlets can only be destroyed in the depths of the crystalline mines of Durhun on the Elemental Plane of Earth where they were first created.

name: Telescoping Bladelance
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turn to extend or retract this mechanical weapon by twisting its handle. The weapon is a normal {@item Lance|XPHB} while it's extended. If the {@item Lance|XPHB} is retracted, the end of the weapon rests inside the wider, bladed base, and it is treated as a {@item Greatsword|XPHB} instead. This {@item Greatsword|XPHB} deals {@damage 1d10} Slashing damage on a hit instead of {@dice 2d6}.

While using the weapon as a {@item Greatsword|XPHB}, you can choose to extend it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} immediately after hitting a target with an attack. If you do so and the target is a Large or smaller creature, it's pushed 5 feet away from you.

name: Telltale Heart
entries: This cherry-sized bloodstone heart is the beating center of a poppet. While the stone is on your person, when you gain the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, you can make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw. On a success, you end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

Also, when you make an Intelligence ability check while holding the stone, you can listen to it, gaining unusual insight or access to esoteric lore. If you do so, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on that Intelligence check. The Telltale Heart can't be used this way again until the next dawn.

name: Telltale Heart
entries: This cherry-sized bloodstone heart is the beating center of a poppet. While on your person, you have advantage on saving throws against becoming {@condition frightened}. If an effect causes you to be {@condition frightened} without a saving throw, you receive a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw to avoid the condition.

Also, when you make an Intelligence ability check while holding the stone, you can listen to it, gaining unusual insight or access to esoteric lore. If you do so, you gain advantage on that Intelligence check. The telltale heart can't be used this way again until you finish a long rest.

name: Tempest Griffon Bracers
entries: While wearing these oiled bracers lined with magic griffon feathers, your speed increases by 5 feet.

In addition, you can use an action to speak the bracers' command word to vanish into a plume of sparks and feathers. Choose up to 3 different creatures that you can see within 60 feet of you. Make a melee weapon attack against each target, briefly appearing next to each one before making the attack. A target takes an extra {@damage 2d8} lightning damage on a hit, or half as much lightning damage on a miss. You can then teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of one of the targets or return to your original space, reappearing in a flourish of electricity, feathers, and wind. Once this property of the bracers has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Tempest Griffon Feather Cape
entries: While wearing this cape, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning damage, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws against spells and other effects that deal Lightning damage.

While wearing the cape, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and use a command word to transform into a bolt of lightning. When you do, choose an unoccupied space that you can see within 120 feet of you. You immediately travel in your lightning form to the chosen space without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, filling a 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} in your path. Other creatures in the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} or within 5 feet of either your old or new location must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 3d10} Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Tentacle Whip
entries: This whip is made from the tentacles and guts of aberrant creatures, stitched to the webbed membranes of winged beasts and fused to the bark of a plant creature. Once the animus is placed, the tentacles begin to writhe and wriggle and the whip can latch and drag creatures along the ground with uncanny strength.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic whip, which has a reach of 20 feet.
Once per turn when you hit a Large or smaller creature with an attack using this weapon, you can pull it 10 feet towards you.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Tentacle Whip requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Any Animus

items.name: [Hair]
entries: Stitches

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Bark

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Webbed Membrane

items.name: [Natural Weapons]
entries: Tentacles from an Aberration

name: Tethervine Quiver
entries: This seemingly overgrown Quiver keeps a large plant magically concealed inside it, and it can hold up to 20 Arrows or Bolts. When you draw an Arrow or Bolt from the Quiver, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and use a command word to magically connect the end of the ammunition to the plant inside the Quiver. The plant is a ropelike vine that flies effortless behind its connected piece of ammunition when fired. It becomes taut and climbable if the ammunition hits an object or surface, able to hold up to 250 pounds before bursting.

While wearing the Quiver, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically retract the vine and its connected ammunition up to 60 feet back into the Quiver. If the connected ammunition hit an object that weighs less than 25 pounds, that object is also pulled back toward the Quiver when the vine is retracted in this way.

If you hit a creature with a piece of ammunition that was connected to the vine, the vine magically disconnects itself from the ammunition and falls. You can disconnect the vine from its connected ammunition by taking a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to repeat the command word or sever the vine from the Quiver.

The vine grows up to 120 feet long, and a connected piece of ammunition can't be fired longer than the vine's current length. If any portion of the vine is severed, it regrows up to 30 feet of length daily at dawn. A severed portion of vine becomes a mundane length of Rope.

name: Thalamus Thread
entries: This pale gray thread is made from the remains of a powerful mystic's brain. The overdeveloped organ creates a congealed fiber that, once spun, can be used as a functional bowstring. It's always oily to the touch and leaves a faint residue on your fingers when pulled. Ranged attacks made with a weapon strung with this thread are considered magical.

When you hit a creature with a ranged attack using a bow or crossbow that was strung with this thread, you can speak the thread's command word as part of the attack to charge the arrow or bolt with psychic power. When you do, the target of the attack takes an extra {@damage 1d8} psychic damage and must make a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is {@condition stunned} until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature is not {@condition stunned}. A construct or undead creature automatically succeeds on the saving throw. This property of the thread can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: The Bag
entries: This weathered old satchel has three tarnished silver buckles that hold it shut. There are faint bloodstains on the inside of the flap, and the bag occasionally ripples as if something inside is moving. The bag functions as a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG} and has the following additional properties.

entries.name: Inhabitant
entries: A {@creature Lurker in the Dark|CrookedMoon24} lives in the bag's extradimensional space. If reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the lurker vanishes and reappears in the bag at the next midnight. The lurker only dies if it is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} by a creature holding a toy or stuffed animal once owned by a child. If the lurker is killed, the bag loses its magic, and anything in it appears in unoccupied spaces closest to the bag.

entries.name: The Bag's Claw
entries: While holding the bag, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to have the lurker in the dark lash out with its claw at a creature within 5 feet of you. Make a melee attack roll with a +7 bonus. On a hit, the claw deals {@damage 1d10 + 4} Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape DC 14) from the claw, and it has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the grapple ends. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Lurker's Curse
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a 1, the lurker slipped out of the bag during the rest and caused mayhem in a nearby area, such as attacking people, causing livestock to sicken, or spoiling provisions.

name: The Closing Argument
entries: This golden archangel's feather exudes gravitas. The feather can be used as a quill that never runs out of bloodred ink.

While you hold the quill, you have advantage on ability checks made to create and interpret contracts, deeds, and other official documentation, and you have advantage on ability checks made to conduct a legal dispute or negotiation.

Additionally, when a creature (including you) uses The Closing Argument to sign a contract or other legal document, they can't willingly break the terms of the contract while the document exists. This effect can't control the actions of any creature who didn't sign the contract, nor can it empower a signatory to perform impossible actions. When this quill is used to sign a legal document, it supplies ink for 5 minutes (allowing more than one creature to sign), then the ink ceases to flow and no creature can use it to sign a document until a month has passed.

You say it's "just a signature." My good sir, what you believe is a mere scribble is actually your very soul on these pages. This ink is your blood. It is your bond. Try as you might, it will not break. Your choice has already been made. Not even dishonor can reverse it.

name: The Grave Blade

entries.name: Fabled Magic Items
entries: Fabled magic items are distinct as a rarity. A fabled item grows in power alongside the character who wields it. Rules for fabled items are summarized here, and a few fabled magic items can be found in this chapter.
A fabled magic item begins as a Common magic item. The item grants a minor, useful trait to its owner that doesn't require {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to use.

To access any higher-level trait, a PC must attune to it using standard {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} rules. Once attuned, a PC can use the fabled item's more powerful properties as they increase in level. If a PC higher than 1st level attunes to a fabled item, its level-dependent properties, up to the character's current level, are immediately available.

At the GM's discretion, an item's more powerful properties might become available only after the character completes a particular quest or event related to the item's story rather than immediately upon reaching each property's required level.
If a PC chooses not to attune to a fabled item, it remains a common magic item, granting only its minor property, regardless of the character's level.
Unless otherwise noted, properties granted by a fabled item are in effect as long at the character is wearing, carrying, or touching the item.
The pommel of this sword hums a wordless song that can be heard within a {@b 5-foot} radius when Undead are within {@b 60 feet} of it.
As your level increases, you gain the following additional properties while wielding or holding this weapon if you are attuned to it:

entries.name: 5th Level
entries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead. If the damage came from a creature, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against it for 1 minute. Once used, the sword can't be used in this way again until the next dawn.

entries.name: 9th Level
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this sword. In addition, the sword deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage on a hit.

entries.name: 13th Level
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls (instead of +1) with this sword. In addition, when the sword deals damage to a living creature, the target must succeed on a {@dc 15} Charisma saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: 17th Level
entries: You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls (instead of +2) with this sword. If you make a successful attack roll against a creature that has 50 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or fewer, you can compel it to die. Once used, the sword can't be used in this way again until the next dawn.

name: The Griffon's Saddlebag
entries: These leather bags have the stylized face of a griffon on their front and appear across the multiverse in strange locations. One may be found in the belly of a dragon, while another in the limbs of a great tree. Regardless of where it's found, a Griffon's Saddlebag is typically discovered by an adventurer with a destiny.

The saddlebags are made by a great, six-armed griffon on the Astral Plane named Criir. Believed by some to be a demigod of pocket dimensions and craftsmen everywhere, Criir is a patron of artificers and creators across the multiverse.

The griffon creates magic items in its great forge using materials collected from various planes of existence to add to their collection. While no one knows exactly how to contact Criir, the astral griffon has a knack for knowing what items are needed by whom.

entries.name: Superior Holding
entries: This 1-foot-wide bag always weighs 3 pounds, regardless of what's inside it. It functions as a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG} that can only be pierced by another Artifact. Placing a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG}, {@item Heward's Handy Haversack|XDMG} , {@item Portable Hole|XDMG}, or similar item inside the extradimensional space created by the saddlebag, or vice versa, destroys the other extradimensional item but leaves the saddlebag unharmed. Any item stored within the other extradimensional space is magically moved to the space within the saddlebag instead. If doing so overloads the bag, random contents from either space are scattered in the Astral Plane until the bag isn't overloaded.

entries.name: Magic Courier
entries: At the GM's discretion, the saddlebag's beak opens up to reveal a letter. The magical script can be read by any creature with an Intelligence of 4 or higher. The note is a delivery request or similar task that includes the name of an item as well as either specific or vague descriptions of a person or place. At the bottom of the letter is a price listed in coins or other form of payment as well as a date or time depending on the task's urgency.

If the saddlebag is brought to the described person or place within the allotted time, it dispenses the magic item into the hand of the appropriate recipient. If the payment isn't received by the bag within 1 hour of dispensing the magic item, the item vanishes and is lost. After receiving the payment for an item in this way, the bag's beak reopens to dispense a reward for the courier.

entries.name: Sell Magic Items
entries: The saddlebag has a connection to Criir's forge on the Astral Plane. Depending on the magic item, you can sell a magic item to the saddlebag for half the cost of its base price.

entries.name: Spells
entries: The saddlebag has 8 charges and regains {@dice 1d6 + 2} expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the saddlebag, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it: {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} (1 charge), {@spell Identify|XPHB} (1 charge), or {@spell Legend Lore|XPHB} (5 charges).

entries.name: Additional Spells
entries: At the GM's discretion, such as after reaching certain milestones or completing Magic Courier quests, the saddlebag may offer one or more of the following additional spells that can be cast from it: {@spell Blink|XPHB} (3 charges), {@spell Dimension Door|XPHB} (4 charges), Divination (4 charges), {@spell Etherealness|XPHB} (7 charges), {@spell Fly|XPHB} (3 charges), {@spell Mordenkainen's Magnificent Mansion|XPHB} (7 charges), {@spell Plane Shift|XPHB} (7 charges), or {@spell Leomund's Secret Chest|XPHB} (4 charges).

entries.name: Sentience
entries: The saddlebag is a sentient Chaotic Neutral item with an Intelligence of 13, a Wisdom of 15, and a Charisma of 16. It has hearing and normal vision with a range of 60 feet.

The bag knows Common. When in the presence of only creatures it trusts, the bag can speak audibly, its beak moving as it speaks. Otherwise, the bag communicates telepathically with its wearer. The bag can also speak and communicate with griffons.

entries.name: Personality
entries: The bag's purpose is to carry, collect, and deliver magic items. Different bags have different personalities, but they are for the most part largely pleasant to talk to. Their voices are birdlike and are filled with occasional coos and squawks, and their stitched eyes widen, squint, and move expressively.

If the wearer or its allies fail to fulfill the bag's Magic Courier quests, it may stop offering its magic to them. If it does, their items may be lost or inaccessible within the bag or potentially spat out. While the bag provides the names of item recipients and delivery locations, it doesn't know any more information than what was provided to it by the astral griffon. Regardless, it does its best to help its wearer and allies find the specified person or location on the letter.

entries.name: Destroying the Griffon's Saddlebag
entries: While there is no way to permanently destroy the saddlebag, piercing it with an Artifact returns it to its place of origin for repair before it's returned to the multiverse in a new location. Placing a Griffon's Saddlebag inside the extradimensional space created by another Griffon's Saddlebag returns both items to their place of origin and sends all the items stored within them to Criir's forge on the Astral Plane.

entries: The saddlebag is a sentient chaotic neutral bag with an Intelligence of 13, a Wisdom of 15, and a Charisma of 16. It has hearing and normal vision out to a range of 60 feet.

Regardless, it does its best to help its wearer and allies find the specified person or location on the letter.
