Placing a {@i Griffon's Saddlebag} inside the extradimensional space created by another {@i Griffon's Saddlebag} returns both items to their place of origin and sends all the items stored within them to the griffon's forge on the Astral Plane.

name: The King in Yellow
reqAttune: by a DC 15 Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB} check)
entries: A thin, leather-bound volume, The King in Yellow contains a dreamlike play that compels a reader to obsess over the text. They read the play again and again, slowly coming to believe that the disconnected scenes and strange vistas it describes are real.

entries.name: Language:
entries: {@language Common|XPHB}.

entries.name: Attunement Check:
entries: Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) DC 15. Unlike other tomes, you are compelled to make this check when inspecting The King in Yellow. If you succeed, you attune to the book. To end your {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to the King in Yellow, you must meet Hastur.

entries.name: Benefits:
entries: While attuned to The King in Yellow, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks.
You gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) checks as long as your lie involves characters, scenes, and locations drawn from The King in Yellow.

You can cast {@spell Contact Deity|CthulhuTorchlight}. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest. When you cast that spell using this item, you always contact Hastur.

Each time you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1 you can cast {@spell Call Deity|CthulhuTorchlight} to summon Hastur. You lose access to this benefit if you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} without using it. If you do not use the spell, you gain a level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} that cannot be removed while you are attuned to this item.

entries.name: Drawbacks:
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}), Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}), and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks, as images of Carcosa dance in your mind, distracting you from the increasing unreal world around you.

entries.name: Insight-Lost Carcosa (+20):
entries: You must find lost Carcosa and gaze upon forgotten Lake Hali. There, in that dreadful realm, you will finally find peace. No matter the cost, you must find the path there. You see omens and signs of Carcosa in the strangest places. The depths of ancient dungeons. The entrails of a slain enemy. Every sign points you back to Carcosa, again and again.

entries.name: Lore:
entries: The King in Yellow allows you to automatically succeed all checks made to learn about Hastur and elements associated with it.

name: The Luminous Codex
entries: The Luminous Codex is a spellbook that contains all the spells that an {@creature archmage} has, plus the following: {@spell fireball}, {@spell sunbeam}, {@spell sunburst}, {@spell plane shift}, {@spell demiplane}, and {@spell imprisonment}.
While you are attuned to it, you gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Radiant Illumination
entries: You know the {@spell light} cantrip, and you can cast the {@spell daylight} spell at will.

entries.name: Radiant Blast
entries: You can change the damage type of any spell you cast to radiant damage. Once you use this property, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Radiant Resilience
entries: You are immune to radiant damage, and you disregard any penalties you would normally suffer from being in sunlight.

name: The Rose Basket
entries: This silver {@item Rapier|XPHB} has a rose adorning its crossguard and pommel and has thorns lining its hilt. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. If you make an attack with the weapon against a Fey or a creature that is shape-shifted, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Radiant damage on a hit.

entries.name: Field of Roses
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can use a command word and touch the {@item Rapier|XPHB}'s point to the ground at your feet. When you do, silver rosebushes sprout from the ground in a 25-foot square centered on your location. The area becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} until the rosebushes disappear. When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes {@damage 2d4} Piercing damage for every 5 feet it travels. While holding the {@item Rapier|XPHB}, this {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} doesn't cost you extra movement, and you don't take damage from moving into or within the area. The rosebushes disappear after 1 minute or when you dismiss them as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: The Shield of Sacred Flame
entries: This shield has 3 charges, which you regain each day at dawn. When a spellcaster within 60 feet of you targets you with a spell or includes you in the area of a spell, you may expend a charge from the shield to cast {@spell counterspell} as a reaction.

entries.name: Relics of Saint Vitruvio
entries: These holy relics of the Sacred Flame were wielded by Saint Vitruvio and are kept in several religious sites throughout Drakkenheim. The Knights of the Silver Order and the Followers of the Falling Fire now seek these relics. Not only do both factions revere Saint Vitruvio, both wish to use these relics to help advance their goals in Drakkenheim.

A character attuned to three Relics of Saint Vitruvio may cast the {@spell heal} spell three times per day, after which they must finish a long rest before they may do so again. In addition, that character gains the ability to attune to two additional magic items so long as those magic items are both Relics of Saint Vitruvio.

name: The Thorn of Kren
entries: A pitch black thorn that thrums with eldritch power. When you touch the thorn, you must succeed on a {@dc 18} Wisdom saving throw or become automatically attuned to the thorn. If becoming attuned to this item causes you to go over your maximum number of attuned items, the GM chooses one of your currently attuned items to instantly unattune in order to make room for the thorn. Handling the thorn with gloves or wrapping it up in a blanket or cloth protects against this effect.

entries.name: Hunter Senses
entries: While attuned to this item, your senses become heightened and your body becomes more suited for hunting and killing. You have advantage on all Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks.

entries.name: Bite
entries: Your teeth sharpen and become vicious, granting you a bite attack. Your bite is a natural weapon you can use to make unarmed strikes against creatures within 5 feet of you. On a hit, your bite deals {@damage 1d8} piercing damage, and you can use your Strength or Dexterity modifier for its attack and damage rolls. You can use your bonus action on each of your turns to make a bite attack.

entries.name: Vicious Nature
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls you make with unarmed strikes and natural melee weapons while attuned to the thorn. This bonus does not stack with bonuses provided by other magic items.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This item has been cursed by the Amaranthine {@deity Kren|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting} and turns otherwise docile creatures into violent predators. Attuning to this item extends this curse to you. As long as you are cursed, you are driven by an insatiable hunger. You gain the following flaw: "My hunger is never satiated. I must feast on the flesh of beasts at every opportunity."

For each hour you go without eating fresh meat from a beast, you must succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or fall into an overpowering bloodlust. While in this frenzy, you have disadvantage on all ability checks that don't relate to the hunt for fresh meat. In combat with a beast, you have advantage on all attacks, but all attacks made against you also have advantage. Every hour that you stave off the frenzy adds +1 to the save DC to resist it. After you give in to the frenzy and feed, the DC resets back down to 13.

entries.name: Destroying the Thorn
entries: The destruction of the thorn requires a complex ritual to which only ancient orders like the Tenders have access. This strenuous ritual involves placing the thorn at the heart of an Evertree and allowing the tree's natural magics to purify the artifact. Beyond the ritual, only the magic of a {@spell wish} spell can destroy the thorn of {@deity Kren|Amaranthine|HumblewoodCampaignSetting}.

name: Thomas's Dimensional Trousers
entries: This flashy set of pants has four pockets that each lead to a special, extradimensional space. Each pocket is six inches wide at the mouth and can hold up to 20 pounds of material, not exceeding a volume of 2 cubic feet. The pants always weigh 1 pound, regardless of their contents.

Placing an object in one of the pants' pockets follows the normal rules for interacting with objects. Retrieving an item from the pants requires an action as your hand rummages around inside for a few moments before finding the item it's looking for.

If the pants are overloaded, pierced, or torn, they rupture and tear, scattering their contents in a 300-foot radius around you. Casting the {@spell mending} spell on the pants daily for 30 days restores the pants' connection to the extradimensional spaces. If one or more pockets are turned inside out, their contents spill forth, unharmed, but the pocket must be put right before it can be used again. Breathing creatures inside the pocket can survive up to a number of minutes equal to 10 divided by the number of creatures (minimum 1 minute), after which time they begin to suffocate.

Placing the pants inside an extradimensional space created by a bag of holding, portable hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.

name: Thought Talker Orbs
entries: This magical spying device, designed by gnome engineers on behalf of the Ebon Syndicate, is composed of two crystal orbs. The Emitter Orb is marble-sized, making it easy to slip into your target's purse or pocket. The Receiver Orb is fist-sized.

You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and touch the two orbs together to activate them for 7 days. Once activated, the Emitter Orb begins capturing thoughts within a 5-foot {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on it. A creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw. On a success, that creature is immune to the effect for 24 hours. On a failed save, the holder of the Received Orb becomes immediately aware of that creature's surface thoughts for 1 minute, even if it leaves the area.

name: Three-Faced Coin
entries: This gold piece appears to be a normal coin, with the crown of Galifar on one side and the Octogram of the Sovereign Host on the other. However, when flipped, it will land with one of three different symbols showing, each corresponding to one of the patrons of the Three Faces of Coin: Kol Korran, Onatar, and Kol Turrant (the Keeper). When you flip the coin, you can will the coin to land displaying a face of your choice. Once this property is used, you cannot do so again until the next dawn.

While this item doesn't require a command word or {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, the ability must be consciously triggered; if you've never used a Three-faced coin before, you must spend a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} studying it to learn how to activate it. After being flipped, the coin returns to its usual two faces when a creature next touches it.

name: Thricecall Mirror
entries: This ornate hand mirror, made of carved iron and adorned with images of grasping hands, can be used to contact other planes. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can speak the true name of an extraplanar being, such as a Fey, Fiend, or Celestial, into the mirror three times. This summons the named creature in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the mirror.

A creature summoned this way retains its free will, and there is no guarantee it views you as an ally. It cannot leave this plane for 1 minute, after which time it automatically returns to its home plane unless it has the means to travel between planes on its own, in which case it can choose to stay.

name: Throwing Scarab
entries: Bred by the daelkyr Valaara, this bizarre symbiont burrows into the palm of its host, secreting razor-sharp chitin blades that can also be used as throwing weapons. When you attune to the scarab, it fuses with one of your hands, visible only as an iridescent, chitinous growth on your palm.

For every attack you make as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can extrude a shard of razor-sharp chitin from the symbiont into your empty hand, using it for the attack. The shard counts as a magical Simple Melee weapon with which you are proficient. It has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse}, {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light}, and {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} properties with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. On a hit, it deals {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage and {@damage 1d4} Acid damage. The shard dissolves as soon as it hits or misses its target.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

name: Thunder Coach
reqAttune: by a creature with the mark of passage
entries: The Thunder Coach is the workhorse of Orien's overland shipping, sometimes referred to as "galleons of the road." A product of the Twelve, it incorporated members of Kundarak, Cannith, and Orien in the design. A typical coach is a 10-foot-wide, 40-foot-long, 15-foot-high (including the wheels) vessel of wood and steel. When pulled by a large team (typically eight tribex), a coach can maintain a speed of up to five miles per hour. However, if someone with the Mark of Passage attunes to the coach and sits in the driver's seat, the full magic of the Thunder Coach comes into play. Under such conditions, four strong beasts can pull the coach at a steady pace of ten miles an hour. If it is moving along an Orien trade road, the effect is further amplified, allowing a top speed of 15 miles per hour. This requires the driver to remain seated and to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}, as if casting a spell. However, beyond these limitations, they are capable of conversation and other actions.

The forward fifteen feet of the coach holds a small cabin for up to three crew members. The crew of a coach typically includes one marked driver and two crew members who serve as both guards and cargo haulers. One of these haulers is usually a Vadalis- trained (though unmarked) handler who cares for the beasts. The top of the coach has positions at the front and back where archers or wandslingers can be stationed with {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

A typical Thunder Coach has two cargo chambers; one magical and one mundane. The back gate of a Thunder Coach opens to grant access to an extradimensional space that functions in the same way as a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG}. When closed, the gate is typically sealed with an Arcane Lock linked to a password known to the driver. The mouth of the extradimensional space is 10-feet-wide by 10-feet-high. The size of the extradimensional space varies based on the model of the coach; the standard is 20-feet-wide, 15-feet-high, and 50-feet-deep. The system maintaining the extradimensional space takes up the final five feet of the coach.

Objects that produce extradimensional spaces (such as {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG|Bags of Holding}, {@item Portable Hole|XDMG|Portable Holes}, or House Cannith's Crates of Containing) cannot cross the threshold of the rear compartment. For this reason, and to allow the transport of living creatures, the Thunder Coach also has a standard cargo compartment accessed from the side of the vehicle; this space is 10-feet-wide, 10-feet- high, and 20-feet-long.

name: Thunderbelch
entries: Upon ingesting this fiercely fizzing potion, roll a {@dice d4} to determine the number of rounds before you let forth a thunderous belch of epic proportions. On your turn that round, you must use your action to release the belch. Each creature other than you within 10 feet of you must make a DC 14 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 3d8} thunder damage and is {@condition deafened} until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't {@condition deafened}.
{@font {@style 19|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Thunderous Flail
entries: This {@item Flail|XPHB} has 3 charges and regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn. As long as the {@item Flail|XPHB} has at least 1 charge, you deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Lightning damage to the first target you hit with it on each of your turns.

While holding the weapon, you can expend 1 charge to cast the {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB} spell (save DC 15) from the ball of the {@item Flail|XPHB}. Alternatively, if you make a melee attack using the {@item Flail|XPHB}, you can immediately expend 1 charge to cast {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} in the direction of the attack's target.

The ball of the {@item Flail|XPHB} is attached to its chain with a powerful magnetic connection that can be released at will. The {@item Flail|XPHB} can be used to make special ranged attacks by releasing the ball mid-swing. You're proficient with these attacks, which have a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet, use your Strength modifier for their attack rolls and damage rolls, and deal {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage on a hit. While the ball is within 60 feet of you, you can magically pull it up to 20 feet toward you as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. It bounces harmlessly off of creatures and other objects in its path. The ball magically reattaches itself to the chain when it enters your space.

While the ball is detached, you can still use the {@item Flail|XPHB} to cast {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB}. When you do, the spell originates from the ball, affecting creatures in a 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on the ball instead of the spell having its normal area of effect.

name: Thuranni Cloak
reqAttune: by a Creature with the {@feat Mark of Shadow|EFA}

name: Thurimbar Rod
entries: This rod is a magical {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} developed by the gnomes of Zilargo. While holding the rod, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to produce auditory illusions that unerringly replicate the sound of any instrument with which you're proficient, with an effect similar to the {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} spell, with the sound emanating from the rod. To determine the quality of the performance, make a Charisma check with the {@item Musical Instrument|XPHB} you're replicating. If you are proficient with the Thurimbar Rod, you can produce unearthly music unlike any natural instrument.

name: Thwackstaff
entries: This festive {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} is decorated with ribbons and other glittering elements. It is perfectly balanced and seems to be made to perform with. This magic {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} property. In addition, you have a +1 bonus to Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks you make in order to put on an entertaining performance using the {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}.

entries.name: Punishing Parry
entries: This {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}, you can expend 1 charge as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature you can see hits you with a melee attack. When you do, roll {@dice 1d6}. You gain a bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equal to the number rolled against that attack, potentially turning the hit into a miss. If the attack misses you as a result of this bonus to AC, you can immediately make one attack with the {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} against the attacking creature as part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. On a hit, the attack deals extra damage equal to the number rolled on the {@dice d6}.

name: Tide Turner
entries: This magical brass timepiece has a pearl from the Lunar Sea at its top and tells you the phase of the moon, time between dawn and dusk, and time between high and low tides while on the Material Plane. Other planes may cause the device's various dials to behave differently. For example, on the Elemental Plane of Water, the tide's dial may spin chaotically, whereas the daytime dial may only move based on your location while on the home plane of fey creatures.

name: Timber
entries: This magical axe is imbued with a destructive force that builds with each consecutive strike. You have a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon equal to the number of charges it currently has. The {@item Handaxe|XPHB} gains 1 charge each time you hit a target with it, up to a maximum of 3 charges. When Timber gains its third charge, the built-up energy immediately explodes; it loses all charges, and the target takes an extra {@damage 3d6} Force damage, or {@damage 6d6} Force damage if it's made of wood. When this happens, if the target is no more than one size larger than you, you can choose to push it up to 10 feet away from you.
Timber's charges last for up to 1 minute. It loses all charges if you miss with an attack using it, make an attack against a different target, or make an attack using a different weapon.

name: Time Dilation Medallion
entries: The inner workings of this clockwork device are formed from gears forged from magical constructs gathered around a focusing lens, held together carefully by the needles of magical creatures. The animus used harnesses the energy of The Algorithm, a being of order and consequence, whose control over time and space ripples from the strange clockworks of the medallion.
This medallion has 3 charges. It crumbles to dust when you expend the final charge.

You can expend 1 charge from the medallion to take an extra action on your turn. Each time you do, you can roll {@dice 1d6}. On a 1, at the end of your turn, you become unstuck in time and space as the medallion casts the {@spell Maze|XPHB} spell on you. On a 6, the medallion regains {@dice 1d3} charges.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating the Time Dilation medallion requires a Legendary Workshop and the following Legendary Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Animus from The Algorithm*

items.name: [Hide]
entries: Plates from a Construct

items.name: [Natural Weapon]
entries: Any Needles

items.name: [Organ]
entries: Eye from a Construct
{@i * At the Game Master's discretion, the animus could be any other Legendary Construct instead.}

name: Timepiercer
entries: This item appears to be a sword hilt that has a small hole on either end of it. The hilt is made of clear quartz and contains an hourglass with sand inside it. Despite the holes on the hilt, the sand never seems to flow out of the hourglass. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and use a command word to cause it to magically form a thin blade of sand. The hourglass spills sand from the bottom of the hilt that circulates up and around to form the blade and guard of a {@item Rapier|XPHB} before returning to the hourglass again through the hole at the top. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and repeat the command word to cause all the sand to return to the hourglass. While the {@item Rapier|XPHB} is formed, you gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While holding the hilt, you can cast either the Haste or {@spell Slow|XPHB} spell (save DC 16) from it. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws you make to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on a spell cast in this way. While {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating} on such a spell, the sands in the hourglass move quickly if you cast {@spell Haste|XPHB} or more slowly if you cast {@spell Slow|XPHB}. Once the hilt has been used to cast one of these spells, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

name: Timeshifter's Mantle
entries: If a Large or smaller creature hits you with a melee attack while you're wearing this cloak, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cause time to briefly warp around you. After taking the damage from the attack, you can immediately move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, and the attacker's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Tincture of Mourning
entries: When you drink this potion, you weep with inexpressible sorrow for 1 hour. During that time, you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition, but your continued wailing prevents you from being silent. If you are {@condition Charmed|XPHB} when you drink the potion, the condition is suppressed for the duration. This glass bottle is topped with a small crypt angel carved from stone. The fluid within has the taste and consistency of tears and the colors of a rain cloud.

entries.name: Heightened Potency
entries: Creatures within 10 feet of you that are {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you also gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

name: Tinkertop Boltblaster 1000
entries: This strange contraption of gears, wires, and lacquered wood has a handle with a metal grip and crank. Its stock bears a flamboyant maker's mark that reads: "Made in Hupperdook," a city in {@book Wildemount|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn|3|Wildemount}. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this weapon, you can immediately make another attack with this weapon after resolving the critical hit. When you roll a 1 on an attack roll made with this weapon, you must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity {@quickref saving throws|PHB|2|1|saving throw} or take {@damage 1d6} piercing damage as some of its gears and wires spring loose.

name: Tiny Bubbles
entries: Drinking this pink, bitter-tasting potion, causes hundreds of small, iridescent bubbles to emerge from your nose and mouth and fill a 20-foot cube that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the bubbles are left untouched, they float in place, remaining there for 1 hour. When a creature enters a space occupied by the bubbles for the first time on a turn, it must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a cacophony of popping erupts as the bubbles burst, dealing {@damage 1d6} thunder damage to all creatures inside the cube. The sound of the bubbles popping can be heard from a mile away.
{@font {@style 23|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Tiny Telekinesis
entries: When you drink this potion, you feel a slight pressure behind your eyes as though something is pushing on the inside of your skull trying to get out. For the next minute, you gain the ability to move an inanimate object within 60 feet of you with your mind. The object can be no larger than 5 inches in diameter and weigh no more than 1 pound, and it can't be worn or carried. Moving an object in this way requires an action. You can move the object up to 30 feet in any direction, and you can't move it more than 60 feet away from you.
{@font {@style 10|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Tinytar
entries: With the sentient tar of a tar elemental and a dose of enchantment magic, one can craft this friendly and amenable little helper. When applied to anything you can hold, the tinytar ensures you don't accidentally drop it.

entries.name: Grippy
entries: This small, magical phial contains an animate and excitable tar. When applied to the handle of a weapon, shield or other held item, the first creature to hold that item can't be disarmed of the item against its will. The creature can still sheathe or drop the item if it desires; the tinytar is very intuitive. As an action, you can hold the magical phial to the tinytar causing it to shlink back inside.

name: Tireless Rower
entries: Appearing to be merely a copper statue of a seated dwarf, this duergar marvel is actually a magic and clockwork automaton. When the command word is spoken, the device duplicates itself until there are enough dwarves to row the entire ship. A single tireless rower can replace the rowing crew of a longship for {@b 8 hours}. It needs to recharge for 8 hours before it can be used again.

name: Titan Cricket Greaves
entries: These unusual leg braces are crafted from the legs of a giant cricket. While wearing the braces, your long jump is up to 25 feet and your high jump is up to 15 feet, unless it's already higher, with or without a running start. Further, your walking speed increases by 5 feet.

In addition, you can use an action to rub your legs together while wearing the braces to create the signature sound of one or many crickets. The sound can be as quiet as a whisper or as loud as a scream.

name: Titan's Tooth Claymore
entries: This massive two-handed blade is made from the lost or harvested tooth of a tarrasque. You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. If it hits an object, the hit is automatically a critical hit. In addition, if you roll a 20 on an attack roll using this weapon, the target takes an extra {@damage 2d6} slashing damage.

name: Titancall Dagger
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a creature with this Dagger, you can summon a {@creature Frost Giant|XMM} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. When you do, specify a target for the giant's ire.

The giant appears in an unoccupied space you choose within {@b 120 feet} of yourself and is convinced that the target has wronged them. While summoned, the giant is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you and your allies.

The giant remains for {@b 1 hour} or until it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, at which time it vanishes. After a giant is summoned, the dagger can't be used again in this way until the next dawn.

entries.name: Awakened
entries: When the Titanstone Knuckles reach an awakened state, they gain the following properties:

items: Your Strength score becomes 24.

You can use an action to cast the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell from the gauntlets on yourself (enlarge only), with a duration of 10 minutes. This property of the gauntlets can't be used again until you finish a {@quickref resting|PHB|2|0|long rest}.

name: Titanstone Knuckles (Dormant)
entries: Carved from the heartstone of a slain earth primordial, these gauntlets bestow immeasurable might to their wearer. In recent times, they were wielded by the legendary barbarian {@creature Grog Strongjaw|TalDoreiCampaignSettingReborn}, who continues to use them as he seeks worthy challengers across Tal'Dorei and Exandria.

entries.name: Dormant
entries: While the Titanstone Knuckles are in a dormant state, your Strength score becomes 22 while you wear these gauntlets. Additionally, your weapon attacks deal double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Exalted
entries: When the Titanstone Knuckles reach an exalted state, they gain the following properties:

items: Your Strength score becomes 26.
While you are under the effect of the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell cast by the gauntlets, you have resistance to cold, fire, lightning, and thunder damage.

name: Toadstone
entries: This small jade carving of a frog dangles from a simple cord of leather to be worn as a necklace. While you wear it, you gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hold your breath for up to 1 hour. In addition, you can cast the {@spell Jump|XPHB} spell using the necklace, targeting only yourself. Once the necklace has been used to cast this spell, it can't do so again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This necklace is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you're targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic. Removing the necklace fails to end the curse on you. While you're cursed, your skin is perpetually slightly wet and clammy, and you have only an appetite for insects and other grubs instead of the foods you would normally enjoy eating.

name: Toadstool Toddy
entries: This carbonated liquid, a potent distillation of faerie magic, is bright fuchsia and tastes of autumn rain. A Humanoid who drinks a Toadstool Toddy has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Fire and Cold damage for 1 hour.

name: Tome of Advanced Fighting Styles
entries: This book's magically charged pages are filled with detailed descriptions and illustrations that teach unique styles of combat. If you spend 48 hours over a period of 6 days or fewer studying the book's contents and practicing its guidelines, you gain one of the following Advanced Fighting Styles:

entries.name: Advanced Simplicity
entries: Your attacks made with simple weapons score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

entries.name: Crushing Blows
entries: When you score a critical hit using a melee weapon that has the heavy property, the target takes extra bludgeoning damage equal to 5 + the ability score modifier you used for your attack and damage rolls.

entries.name: Net Mastery
entries: When you throw a net, its normal and long range is doubled. In addition, the first time that a creature attempts to escape from a net that you threw, the escape DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice), unless it's already higher.

entries.name: Quick Shot
entries: You gain a special reach with ranged weapons called a firing reach that's a number of feet equal to 5 + your normal reach. While you are wielding a ranged weapon, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they move out of your firing reach.

entries.name: Readied Bulwark
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to AC against opportunity attacks while holding a shield.

entries.name: Versatile Expert
entries: When you hit with an attack using a weapon that has the versatile property, you can use the two-handed damage die even if you're only wielding the weapon with one hand.

You can't take an Advanced Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again. Once the book has been used to grant an Advanced Fighting Style, it loses its magic, but regains it in a century.

name: Tome of Dreams
entries: This beautifully embossed book is full of gripping short stories. You can read a story from the book in 10 minutes. The underlying nature of each story is unclear, leaving your subconscious mind to slowly process and unpack its deeper meanings over the course of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

The next time you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} after reading a story from the book, roll {@dice 1d20}. On a roll of 10 or lower, you take {@damage 2d4} Psychic damage as your mind is plagued with intense terrors from the story you read. On a roll of 11 or higher, you gain {@dice 2d4} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} as your mind is filled with joy and courage instead. If you start a story but don't finish reading it, nothing happens the next time you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Tome of Living Memories (rare)
entries: The pages of this book are littered with the shifting memories of all the aboleth broodmother's eyes have seen. This deluge of information includes historical occurrences, the gods, and all things arcane, in addition to several spells. Unfortunately, the script is a shifting mire of letters that only the most astute can decipher.

entries.name: Knowledge from Beyond
entries: Over the course of a minute, you can attempt to discern information from the broodmother's memories. Make a {@dc 10} Intelligence check. On a success, you gain proficiency in{@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, and {@skill Religion} for the next 10 minutes. On a failure, you take psychic damage equal to your level.

entries.name: Shrouded Spells
entries: In a similar manner, you can spend 10 minutes attempting to cast one of the following spells, requiring no material components and without expending a spell slot. At the end of the 10 minutes, make an Intelligence check. The DC equals 10 plus the spell's level. On a success, you cast the spell. On a failure, you don't cast the spell and you take psychic damage equal to twice the spell's level. When you cast spells from the Shrouded Spells property using this tome, it is the disembodied voice of Slkvol the broodmother that answers.

items: {@spell Identify} (1st level)
{@spell Augury} (2nd level)
{@spell Clairvoyance} (3rd level)
{@spell Divination} (4th level)
{@spell Legend Lore} (5th level)

entries.name: Optional Attunement
entries: A wizard can attune to this item, which becomes augmented with the Knowing Tome property for the duration.

entries.name: OA: Knowing Tome
entries: You can use this tome as a spellbook and an arcane focus. While you use it as your spellbook, you can prepare 1 additional wizard spell and you know the {@spell guidance} cantrip, which is a wizard spell for you.

entries: You can use this tome as a spellbook and an arcane focus. While you use it as your spellbook, you may cast the following spells as if you had them prepared: {@spell comprehend languages} and {@spell detect thoughts}.

{@spell Find the Path} (6th level)

entries.name: OA: Knowing Tome
entries: You can use this tome as a spellbook and an arcane focus. While you use it as your spellbook, you can prepare 2 additional wizard spells and you know the {@spell guidance} cantrip, which is a wizard spell for you.

name: Tome of Lost Knowledge
entries: This gold-trimmed book's cover is embossed with a portrait of {@creature Ogden Fellweaver|GriffonsSaddlebag2} (see appendix L), a legendary wizard infamous for his ill-gotten knowledge. If you can attune to this item, you can use it as a spellbook and an arcane focus. If your attunement to the book ends, anything written in the book disappears.

entries.name: Absorb Knowledge
entries: Immediately after a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell of 1st level or higher, you can use your reaction to make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the spell is magically added to the book in your own notation. You must be holding the book to use this property. If the added spell is a wizard spell and of a level for which you have spell slots, you can prepare this spell just like your other spells. If the spell is not a wizard spell, its notation is garbled and impossible to use. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until a number of days equal to the spell's level have passed.

entries.name: Shift Knowledge
entries: While using this book as your spellbook, you can replace up to 3 spells from your prepared list of spells when you finish a short rest. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Unknown Knowledge
entries: While holding the book, you can use an action to channel its hidden knowledge. When you do, you gain proficiency in one skill or tool of your choice until the next dawn. If you're already proficient in the chosen skill or tool, your proficiency bonus is instead doubled for any ability check you make using that skill or tool. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This book is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the book, keeping it within reach at all times. In addition, you are compelled to use this book as your spellbook. Each time you prepare a spell from another spellbook, you take psychic damage equal to the spell's level.

name: Tome of the Ethereal
entries: Lighter than it rightly should be, this book is always cold to the touch and blurs when seen in periphery. While holding the tome, you can see into the Ethereal Plane out to a range of 120 feet.

In addition, the tome has 3 charges, and it regains all expended charges daily at dusk. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you targets you with a power, a spell, or an attack while you aren't on the Ethereal Plane, you can use your reaction to expend 1 charge and choose one of the following effects:

items: You enter the Ethereal Plane, then return to the plane and the space you left at the start of your next turn.

entries: If that space is occupied, you return to the nearest unoccupied space of your choice.

items: You teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

name: Tongueworm
entries: This coil of muscle terminates in a sharp barb. When you attune to it, this daelkyr-bred worm attaches to your throat and nestles under your tongue. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} with the worm, using your choice of Strength or Dexterity for the attack. On a hit, you deal Piercing damage equal to {@dice 1d4} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice), instead of the normal damage of an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. In addition, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Symbiotic Nature
entries: Once you attune to this symbiote, you can't remove it unless you are targeted by a {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell or similar magic.

name: Tooth of the Jinxed Leviathan (Legendary)
entries: This tooth is razor sharp and can be wielded as a Dagger. Its "hilt" is wrapped in alligator hide, and the flat of its blade flickers with magenta hex magic in carved glyphs.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon determined by its rarity. While holding the tooth, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your spells, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Jinx of Dire Fortune (Rare+)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can force one creature you can see within 60 feet of you to make a Charisma saving throw (DC = 16 + the tooth's bonus). On a failed save, the target is jinxed for 1 minute. While jinxed, when the target makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} and rolls an even number on the {@dice d20}, it must reroll the {@dice d20} and take the new roll. On a successful save, you must make the same saving throw, becoming jinxed for 1 minute on a failure. This property can't be used again while another creature is jinxed by it.

entries.name: Exposed Weak Spot (Very Rare+)
entries: When you make an attack roll with the tooth, you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}.

entries.name: Steal Unluck (Very Rare+)
entries: When an enemy you can see within 60 feet of you makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to negate their {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until a creature you can see makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} and rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20}, or until the next dusk.

entries.name: Strange Fortunes (Legendary)
entries: Each time you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} with the tooth against an enemy, the tooth gains a cumulative +3 bonus to damage rolls. This bonus is in addition to the bonus based on the tooth's rarity. When you roll a 1 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll with the tooth, you take Force damage equal to the accumulated bonus. This property's damage bonus returns to +0 when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

On a successful save, you must make the same saving throw, becoming jinxed for 1 minute on a failure. This property can't be used again while another creature is jinxed by it.
