Once this property is used, it can't be used again until a creature you can see makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} and rolls a 1 on the {@dice d20}, or until the next dusk.

name: Torchbearer's Reach
entries: When held, a magical flame appears at the top of this weapon's handle. The flame sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet. You can snap the handle down as if cracking a {@item whip|XPHB} (no action required) to cause the flame to extend into a 10-foot-long coil of fire, which you can use as a {@item Whip|XPHB}. This weapon has the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property and deals Fire damage on a hit instead of Slashing. The flame doesn't hurt you while you hold the {@item Whip|XPHB}. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can snuff the fire out with your hand or blow it out to extinguish it.
The {@item Whip|XPHB}'s flame is intangible and can't be used to bind a creature or retrieve objects from afar, but can be used to light other fires.

name: Tordalfr's Rebuttal

entries.name: Fabled Magic Items
entries: Fabled magic items are distinct as a rarity. A fabled item grows in power alongside the character who wields it. Rules for fabled items are summarized here, and a few fabled magic items can be found in this chapter.
A fabled magic item begins as a Common magic item. The item grants a minor, useful trait to its owner that doesn't require {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to use.

To access any higher-level trait, a PC must attune to it using standard {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} rules. Once attuned, a PC can use the fabled item's more powerful properties as they increase in level. If a PC higher than 1st level attunes to a fabled item, its level-dependent properties, up to the character's current level, are immediately available.

At the GM's discretion, an item's more powerful properties might become available only after the character completes a particular quest or event related to the item's story rather than immediately upon reaching each property's required level.
If a PC chooses not to attune to a fabled item, it remains a common magic item, granting only its minor property, regardless of the character's level.
Unless otherwise noted, properties granted by a fabled item are in effect as long at the character is wearing, carrying, or touching the item.
When you hit with a ranged weapon attack using this Snaerispear, you may push the target up to {@b 10 feet} directly away from you.
As your level increases, you gain the following benefits while wielding or holding this weapon if you are attuned to it:

entries.name: 5th Level
entries: Immediately after hitting or missing an enemy, this javelin reappears to your hand.

entries.name: 9th Level
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon. In addition, when thrown, the javelin is wreathed in electricity, dealing an extra {@damage 1d6} points of Lightning damage to any target it hits.

entries.name: 13th Level
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon instead of +1. In addition, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to charge your next attack with the weapon with electricity. The next time you hit with this javelin before the end of your turn, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: 17th Level
entries: You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon, instead of +2. In addition, when you hit with this weapon, you can call down a bolt of lightning from the heavens to strike the target. This bolt deals {@damage 8d8} Lightning damage to the target and all creatures within {@b 15 feet} of it. Creatures within the blast radius are pushed {@b 15 feet} away from the target. Once used, this ability can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Torrdok's Magnificent Forgery
entries: This large, gilded mirror is 5 feet tall, 3 feet across, and weighs 20 pounds. While the mirror is against a wall or similar vertical surface, you can speak its first command word using an action to magically fasten the mirror to the wall. You can unfasten the mirror by speaking the command word again using another action.

While the mirror is fastened to a wall, its reflective surface becomes oily and moves ever so slightly. If the fastened mirror is facing a room that's no larger than 40 feet on a side for 24 hours, the reflection stiffens and becomes a beautiful painting of the room's reflection. The painting remains until the mirror is removed from the wall. While the painting remains, a creature can use an action to touch its surface and speak the mirror's second command word to be magically transported to a special demiplane identical to the room the mirror is facing, including any of its furniture and decorations. Doing so again from within the demiplane transports you back to the nearest unoccupied space to the mirror in the original room. Any furniture or decoration created by the demiplane can't be removed from it, and if a piece of furniture or decoration was magical in the original room, the copy of it is not. Further, any doors or windows found in the original room don't appear in the demiplane's version.

Anything brought into the demiplane is shunted back to the original room when the mirror is removed from the wall. While the painting remains, it is indistinguishable from a regular painting. A successful DC 15 Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check can reveal the true nature of the painting, but not what command words are required to use it.

name: Torrent Taiaha
entries: A mote of swirling, magic water circles the top of this {@item wooden staff|XPHB}, which can be wielded as a magic {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}. The staff can also be used to make special melee attacks by extending and lashing out with the water. You're proficient with these attacks, which have a reach of 10 feet, can use your Wisdom modifier for their attack rolls and damage rolls instead of Strength, and deal {@damage 1d4} Bludgeoning damage on a hit. After the attack, the water shrinks back to the staff. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, regardless of whether you attack with the weapon itself or use its special melee attack.

While holding the staff, you can stand on and move across any liquid surface as if it were solid ground. If you end your turn on a liquid in this way, you sink into it as normal until you stand on solid ground again. In addition, while holding the staff, you can cast the {@spell Control Water|XPHB} spell ("flood" or "part water" only) from it. The spell ends early if you are no longer holding the staff. Once the staff is used to cast this spell, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Torture Tools
entries: This satchel contains various small implements that can bludgeon, cut, and pierce in ways designed to maximize pain. Meant to extract the truth, many use these tools with far more nefarious intentions.
Proficiency with these tools grants the following benefits:

entries.name: Exhaustion
entries: Using these tools for 1 hour on a {@condition Restrained} creature causes it to gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, after which you must make a Dexterity (Torture Tools) check. The DC is equal to 20 minus the creature's Constitution modifier. On a failure, the creature takes 10 points of your choice of Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage.

entries.name: Intimidation
entries: When you make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check against a creature you have previously used these tools on, you gain a bonus to the roll equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

name: Tote of Tricky Treat Sugarbombs
entries: This canvas bag holds {@dice 5d8 + 10} clove and pumpkin candies inside. A small illusory face appears over the sewn-on pumpkin at night. Each candy has a minor magical effect that lasts for 1 minute unless otherwise specified. Some effects are pleasant, whereas others are mischievous. You can eat a piece of candy as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action. When you do, roll on the table below to determine the candy's effect.

rows: The candy seems to have spoiled, forcing you to succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or spend your action on your next turn retching and reeling.
Your face appears to melt, revealing the skull beneath it. The effect is harmless and illusory.
Any food you eat or water you drink taste like ash or blood, respectively.
Other creatures' eyes appear to be hollowed out and blackened to you.
Your ears turn a different, vibrant color at the start of each of your turns.
Your hair falls out and regrows over the next minute.
Your laughter becomes maniacal, and you have trouble stopping once you've started.
You hear a fly near your ear, but you can neither see it nor swat it away.
Your skin turns orange, and light spills forth from your eyes and mouth, shedding {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 10 feet.
Confetti bursts from the top of your head, and small children can be heard laughing.
You sprout tiny, flightless bat wings.
You know the location of the nearest pumpkin within 1 mile.
Nearby crows and ravens land on your shoulders or outstretched arm.
A friendly, floppy wizard hat appears on your head. After 1 minute, it disappears in a cloud of stars.
Any alcohol in your stomach or that you drink becomes nonalcoholic.

Your voice becomes smooth and golden, allowing you to add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to Charisma ({@skill Performance}) checks made to sing. If you already have proficiency in this skill, you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it instead.
Any food you eat or water you drink tastes delicious and reminds you of your favorite pastimes.
You gain {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, its range increases by 30 feet.
You can magically sense if a creature is possessed, and you can see creatures that have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition.

name: Tower Shield
entries: This large shield provides more protection than a typical shield. While wielding a Tower Shield, you gain +3 to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB}. If you use an action to set the Tower Shield, you have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover} until the start of your next turn. Additionally, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0 and cannot be increased during that time.
To wield a Tower Shield, you must have a Strength of at least 15 and your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet while wielding the shield.

name: Toy Riverboat
entries: This tiny, brightly painted boat is made in exacting detail, with smokestacks and a paddlewheel that turns, but it looks like a child's plaything. Studying it reveals a miniscule but unearthly passenger within the boat's cabin. The riverboat grants the following properties.

entries.name: Passengers
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you and up to twelve other willing, Medium or smaller creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself shrink to Tiny size and appear aboard the riverboat, along with up to 300 pounds of gear per passenger. The boat moves over water or other liquids at 3 miles per hour and doesn't require wind. You can travel this way for up to 12 hours a day. A passenger that leaves the boat returns to its normal size.

entries.name: Unearthly Passenger
entries: You can release the riverboat onto water to cast {@spell Arcane Eye|XPHB} with it. The riverboat is the spell's sensor and only moves on water, but you can otherwise move it as normal for the spell.

entries.name: Haunting Curse
entries: When a creature leaves the riverboat, it must make a DC 0 Charisma saving throw, becoming cursed on a failed save. While cursed in this way, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom and Charisma ability checks and on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. After you make this saving throw, the save DC increases by 2. This increase can't happen again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

name: Traitor's Gauntlet
entries: This pair of gloves is matched with one dark metal gauntlet, which once belonged to a traitorous knight who was burned for his treason. While wearing these gloves and gauntlet, your unarmed strikes with your hands are turned into magic weapons that deal {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage.

In addition, you can use a bonus action to speak the gauntlet's command word while holding a nonmagical melee weapon in the hand that's wearing it. When you do, the weapon becomes magical while you hold it in that hand. The weapon ceases to be magical if you throw, drop, or stow it. While the weapon is magical in this way, it's wreathed in dark flames that cause any target hit by it to take necrotic damage, instead of the weapon's normal damage, as well as an extra {@damage 1d8} fire damage.
While unworn, the gauntlet can be magically altered to fit over either hand by speaking its other command word as an action.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This gauntlet is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the gauntlet, keeping it within reach at all times, and you can't remove the gloves. In addition, while you're cursed, you gain the following flaw: "Everyone has an ulterior motive, so I can only count on myself." While you have this flaw, you have disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) and Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks made to interact with friendly creatures, and you can't take the Help action.

name: Trampling Crossbow
entries: This heavy crossbow carries with it the force of a raging bull. When you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this magic weapon, the bolt transforms into a spectral stampede immediately after it hits the target. When it does, the target and up to 2 other targets of your choice that you can see within 15 feet of it must make a DC 13 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage, and if it is Large or smaller, it's pushed 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, a target takes half as much bludgeoning damage and isn't pushed. This bludgeoning damage is doubled against objects and structures.

name: Trapper's Teeth
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with these Steel Jaws.

The teeth have 4 charges. When you hit with an attack using them, you can expend 1 charge to leave a set of spectral teeth clamped around the target. The target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make a DC 13 Strength saving throw, ending the effect on a success. The teeth regain all expended charges at dawn.

name: Travel Wok
entries: Unlike other frying pans, this enchanted wok both imbues its food with healing properties and heats up to strike a burning blow against its enemies. The wok is considered a +1 frying pan, which deals an extra {@damage 1d4} fire damage on a hit.

Not only can the wok cook food without the need for a fire, creatures that eat food prepared in the wok within an hour of it being cooked gain {@dice 1d6} temporary hit points. Temporary hit points gained by the wok's food last for 1 hour. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Special
entries: When wielding a frying pan, you can use your bonus action to add a +1 bonus to your AC until the end of your next turn. You can't gain this benefit while wielding a shield.

name: Traveler's Guide
entries: These handy books contain detailed information on a single large city or notable destination chosen by the GM. Most of these guides were written by Jonall, though some were written by other notable explorers. A traveler's guide allows you to add your proficiency bonus to any Intelligence checks you make related to the destination it details.

name: Traveler's Lantern
entries: This compact hooded lantern features a large metal ring on its top, allowing it to be affixed to a belt, sash, or similar article of clothing while still providing light. The lantern sheds {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} in a 15-foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 15 feet. Once lit, it burns for 6 hours on a flask (1 pint) of oil. As an action, you can lower the hood, reducing the light to {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} in a 5-foot radius.

name: Treant Arrow
entries: This arrow is carved from the boughs of a living {@creature treant|FleeMortals}.

When a creature takes damage from the arrow, they are {@condition restrained} by vines that sprout from the shaft. A creature can make a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check as an action, freeing themself or another creature {@condition restrained} by the arrow within their reach on a success.
Once a treant arrow restrains a creature or if the treant used to make the arrow dies, it becomes a mundane arrow.

name: Treasure Rat
entries: When you open the door to this white-furred, red-eyed rat's cage, they point their nose in the direction of the nearest magic item, if any, within 30 feet of them that isn't being worn or carried by another creature. They continue pointing their nose at that item for 1 minute or until you shut the cage door. After pointing at a magic item, the rat refuses to do so again until they consume a piece of cheese worth at least 10 gp.

name: Tremor Spike
entries: This industrial, hollow rod is 3 feet long and weighs 15 pounds. The rod has a tapered spike on one end and an open, tower-like chimney on the other. Three hinged legs unfold from the sides of the rod, allowing it to stand upright with its spiked end pointed downward. Standing or collapsing the rod in this way requires an action.

The unfolded legs magically fasten the rod to the ground while it's standing, but a creature can use its action to try to push it over with a successful DC 20 Strength check. Once the rod is no longer standing, it magically deactivates and collapses itself again.

As a bonus action, you can press a button on the standing rod to cause its mechanisms to churn and whir, repeatedly sending its spike into the ground below it. Pressing the button again deactivates the rod. The spike sends out loud, drum-like shockwaves every 6 seconds. The waves are audible out to 300 feet, or 1200 feet if a creature has {@sense tremorsense|MM}. If a creature has {@sense tremorsense|MM}, its range is halved while it's within 300 feet of the active rod. A creature can't perceive anything within 30 feet of the active rod using its {@sense tremorsense|MM}, but is aware that the disrupting shockwaves originate from that location.

name: Trickster's Boots
entries: These boots are usually shaped with a bright leather: red, orange, or purple. While wearing these boots, you can leave the tracks of any other creature in the snow, as you choose, including animal, monster, or even dragon tracks. You can also leave tracks resembling footgear you have seen or worn in the past. Attempts to follow these tracks are made normally.

name: Trident of Henchantment
entries: A jasper effigy of a chicken's head rests at the top of this {@item trident|XPHB}, and an egg-shaped amethyst is fixed to its base. It is a strange weapon, but is highly coveted by farmers and livestock owners.

This magic weapon has 4 charges, and regains {@dice 1d4} expended charges at dawn. When you use the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with this weapon, you can immediately expend 1 of its charges to cast the {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} spell (save {@dc 15}) and transform your target into a hen (AC 10, HP 1, {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} 30 ft) for 1 hour. If you expend the weapon's last charge, roll {@dice 1d4}. On a 1, yolk explodes out of the egg-shaped gem at the base of the {@item trident|XPHB} and the weapon loses its enchantment.

name: Trident of the Dryad
entries: This magical wooden {@item Trident|XPHB} has 4 charges and regains {@dice 1d3 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. While you're holding the {@item Trident|XPHB} and are within 5 feet of a Large or bigger tree, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to magically teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a second Large or bigger tree that is within 60 feet of the previous tree.

entries.name: Tree Form
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to plant the bottom of this {@item Trident|XPHB} in fertile ground and use a command word to transform it into a healthy tree. The tree is 60 feet tall and has a 5-foot-diameter trunk, and its canopy extends out in a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} around the tree. While you're within 5 feet of the tree, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to magically teleport to another point on its trunk or within its branches.

The tree appears ordinary but radiates a faint aura of Transmutation magic that can be discerned with the {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} spell. While touching the tree, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action and repeat the command word to return the {@item Trident|XPHB} to its normal form. Any creature in the tree falls when the tree reverts to a {@item Trident|XPHB}. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Trident of the Hydra
entries: This oddly shaped {@item Trident|XPHB} is made of hammered mithral and has a strangely short handle, but it is well-balanced for single-handed combat. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which lacks the {@itemProperty V|XPHB|Versatile} property.

When you make an attack by throwing the {@item Trident|XPHB}, the forked end of the weapon magically splits apart to form three separate spears, allowing you to make three ranged attack rolls with it instead of one. These spears each deal {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage on a hit instead of the {@item Trident|XPHB}'s normal damage; you don't add your ability modifier to their damage unless that modifier is negative. After the attack, the {@item Trident|XPHB} regrows its missing prongs from one of the separated spears, and the other two spears dissolve.

name: Trollblood Potion
entries: This potion is a bubbling, sickly, green-brown viscous soup that has the consistency of mucus. What appears to be the rotting eye of a troll floats in the potion. It smells acrid and nauseating and tastes even worse than it looks.
When you drink this potion, for the next minute, you regain 5 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of your turn. The effects of this potion end early if you take Fire or Acid damage.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Trollblood Potion requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Fey Animus

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Monster Blood from a Troll

items.name: [Organ]
entries: Eyes from a Troll

name: Trollgut Rope
entries: This 'rope' is made from treated troll entrails. Typically, it is found in a 50-ft length that weighs 6 pounds and can hold up to 3,000 pounds.

If Trollgut Rope is cut, you can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to press two ends together, causing them to merge together into a single length of rope. This only works with pieces of Trollgut Rope from the same original coil. If the Trollgut Rope takes Fire or Acid damage, it no longer regenerates and becomes nonmagical.

name: Trollkin Unguent
entries: One vial of this oil can cover one Medium or smaller creature, along with the equipment it's wearing and carrying (one additional vial is required for each size category above Medium). Applying the oil takes {@b 10 minutes}. The affected creature then has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage for {@b 1 hour}.

If the creature takes Fire damage, it becomes wreathed in ghostly green flames that shed {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a {@b 15-foot} radius. While ablaze, the creature's melee weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage. After {@b 10 minutes}, the flames die out and the oil's effects expire.
This oil is transparent with a rainbow sheen.

name: Tub of Churning and Fermentation
entries: This squat, wooden and ceramic tub has a screw-on lid that fits snuggly around its base. The tub can hold up to 2 gallons of liquid or 1 cubic foot of material within it. You can leave a liquid or other perishable in the tub and secure the lid before saying the name of the end product you'd like the contents to turn into. If you say the name of a possible result, the tub clicks lightly before locking its lid shut.

After 10 minutes, the tub gives a second, louder click as the lid unlocks. The contents of the tub will have been stirred, processed, or otherwise fermented in such a way to generate the named end product. Adding extra ingredients into the tub can impact the end product's flavor.
Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Tunnel Vision
entries: Drinking this potion causes you to hyperfixate on your strikes but potentially opens you to counterattacks. The effects of this potion last for 1 minute. For the duration, the first time you hit a target with a weapon attack on each of your turns, it deals an extra {@damage 1d12} damage of the same type. Until the potion's effects end, you also take a -2 penalty to AC.
{@font {@style 36|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Turtle Brooch
entries: This gold and amber brooch resembles a turtle that's been flipped on its back. While you're wearing it, standing up from being {@condition prone} costs 5 feet less of your movement (to a minimum of 5 feet).

name: Turtle Dove Dagger
entries: From the tip of its thick steel blade to the base of its golden handle, each knife shimmers with a buzz of illusory energy.

While wielding a pair of Turtle Dove Daggers, you can create an illusory copy of yourself as an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} twice per long rest. The illusion lasts for 1 minute, or until you take damage. The illusion appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 ft of you. You can take an {@action Attack|XPHB} or {@action Magic|XPHB} action on your turn to attack or cast a spell as if you were in the illusion's space, but you must use your own senses. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can move the illusion up to 30 ft to a space you can see, but it must remain within 120 ft of you. Additionally, when both you and your illusion are within 5 ft of a creature that can see the illusion, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature.

name: Twin Telepathy
entries: This potion must be shared with another creature, each of them ingesting half of the potion. When consumed, the potion allows the imbibers to communicate telepathically across any distance. The effects of this potion last for 24 hours.
{@font {@style 44|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Twin Vision
entries: This potion must be shared with another creature, each of them ingesting half of the potion. When the second half of the potion is consumed, the first creature gains the ability to see through the eyes of the second creature, gaining the benefits of any special senses that creature has. While seeing in this way, the first creature is blind with regard to its own senses. Either creature can use its action to stop shared vision or reactivate it. This ability lasts for 8 hours, and it can't be used if the creatures are more than 1 mile apart.
{@font {@style 31|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Tyr's Blade
entries: This magic weapon deals an extra {@damage 2d6} damage to any creature it hits. This extra damage is of the same type as the weapon's normal damage.

name: Tyr's Crushing Might
entries: This iron bowsprit is forged in the shape of the one-handed god Tyr in the moments after he lost his hand to the Fenris wolf. His wounded arm is hugged tight to his body, his sword thrust forward in the other, and a mighty cry upon his lips. While equipped with this item, a ship can take the Ram action for double the normal damage, and it takes no damage to itself from Ramming.

name: Tyrannosaurus Rax
entries: This bone-carved axe can channel the might of a rampaging tyrannosaurus rex. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While holding the axe, you can use a bonus action to rampage. While rampaging, you can move through the space of any creature of your size or smaller. When you move through a creature's space in this way while rampaging, your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks from that creature for the rest of the turn. Once on each of your turns while rampaging, you can force a creature whose space you move through in this way to make a DC 15 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice). On a failed save, that creature takes {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage and is knocked {@condition prone}. In addition, while you're rampaging, your weapon attacks with this weapon score a critical hit against objects, structures, and {@condition prone} creatures on a roll of 19 or 20.

Your rampage lasts for up to 1 minute. It ends early if you don't move through a hostile creature's space on your turn or if you drop to 0 hit points. This property of the axe can be used twice and regains all expended uses daily at dawn.

name: Ulmyr's Eye (Adept)
entries: Ulmyr's Eye appears to be a crystal ball filled with ever-shifting smoke. Peering into the orb reveals hazy visions, many of which are disturbing.

entries.name: Aspirant
entries: At this tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following benefits:

items: You know the {@spell Guidance|XPHB} cantrip and can cast it even if you don't have the Spellcasting class feature.

The orb has 12 charges. You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save {@dc 18}) from it: {@spell Augury|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Clairvoyance|XPHB} (3 charges), {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Divination|XPHB} (4 charges), or {@spell Scrying|XPHB} (5 charges). The orb regains {@dice 2d4 + 4} expended charges at dawn.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Your fears of the future diminish your attention in the present. While attuned to Ulmyr's Eye, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Adept
entries: At the Adept tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following additional benefits:

items: While holding the orb, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on a roll when a creature you can see within 60 feet makes {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}. The triggering creature rerolls and uses the new result. You can use this property a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
While holding the orb, you can expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of your prepared spells without expending a spell slot. The number of charges expended is equal to the spell's level.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Ulmyr's Eye fills your dreams and meditations with nightmarish visions, making it difficult for you to rest. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you must succeed a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or gain only the benefits of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} instead.

name: Ulmyr's Eye (Aspirant)
entries: Ulmyr's Eye appears to be a crystal ball filled with ever-shifting smoke. Peering into the orb reveals hazy visions, many of which are disturbing.

entries.name: Aspirant
entries: At this tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following benefits:

items: You know the {@spell Guidance|XPHB} cantrip and can cast it even if you don't have the Spellcasting class feature.

The orb has 12 charges. You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save {@dc 18}) from it: {@spell Augury|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Clairvoyance|XPHB} (3 charges), {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Divination|XPHB} (4 charges), or {@spell Scrying|XPHB} (5 charges). The orb regains {@dice 2d4 + 4} expended charges at dawn.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Your fears of the future diminish your attention in the present. While attuned to Ulmyr's Eye, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks.

name: Ulmyr's Eye (Master)
entries: Ulmyr's Eye appears to be a crystal ball filled with ever-shifting smoke. Peering into the orb reveals hazy visions, many of which are disturbing.

entries.name: Aspirant
entries: At this tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following benefits:

items: You know the {@spell Guidance|XPHB} cantrip and can cast it even if you don't have the Spellcasting class feature.

The orb has 12 charges. You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save {@dc 18}) from it: {@spell Augury|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Clairvoyance|XPHB} (3 charges), {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (2 charges), {@spell Divination|XPHB} (4 charges), or {@spell Scrying|XPHB} (5 charges). The orb regains {@dice 2d4 + 4} expended charges at dawn.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Your fears of the future diminish your attention in the present. While attuned to Ulmyr's Eye, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Adept
entries: At the Adept tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following additional benefits:

items: While holding the orb, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on a roll when a creature you can see within 60 feet makes {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}. The triggering creature rerolls and uses the new result. You can use this property a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
While holding the orb, you can expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of your prepared spells without expending a spell slot. The number of charges expended is equal to the spell's level.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: Ulmyr's Eye fills your dreams and meditations with nightmarish visions, making it difficult for you to rest. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you must succeed a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or gain only the benefits of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} instead.

entries.name: Master
entries: While at the Master tier of {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}, you have the following additional benefit:

items: While holding the orb, you can cast the {@spell Foresight|XPHB} spell from it, requiring no Material component. When you cast the spell in this way, its duration is reduced to 1 hour. Once you have done so, you can't cast the spell from the orb again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries: You also gain the following curse:

items: You are so filled with dread that you suffer frightful visions difficult to discern from reality. When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, the orb casts {@spell Phantasmal Killer|XPHB} on you (save {@dc 14}). This effect can also be triggered by moments of extreme emotional or physical distress, at the GM's discretion.

name: Umber Painted Stone
entries: {#itemEntry Painted Stone|TalesFromTheShadows}

For 1 minute, you can use your reaction to fling a magical spike at a target you can see within 60 feet. The spike automatically hits its target, causing an amount of force damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

name: Umbrella of Shielding
entries: This silk umbrella is reinforced with iron, making it as durable as it is heavy. It is considered a +1 shield. While wielding the umbrella and targeted by a ranged weapon attack, you can use your reaction to gain a +5 bonus to your AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.

entries.name: Special
entries: Whenever you take falling damage while wielding an umbrella, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by a number equal to twice your proficiency bonus.

name: Umbril Opal Necklace
entries: This stunning necklace is crafted from finely wrought silver and sparkling black opals. When attuned to this necklace, your Charisma score increases by 2. Additionally, you have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed}.

name: Umi's Powerful Undertow
entries: This potent elixir allows the drinker to enhance their aquatic spells with the ocean's wrath. For the next hour, when you cast a spell that produces or manipulates water in some capacity, the spell is cast as if using a spell slot of one level higher. Additionally, spells that use water to deal damage to a creature or object deal an extra {@damage 2d12} bludgeoning damage.

Alternatively, you can throw the potion into an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you, breaking the glass and summoning three {@creature water elemental||water elementals} in the nearest unoccupied spaces. These creatures are under your control until destroyed.
{@font {@style 58|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Uncanny Focus
entries: For 1 minute after imbibing this purplish liquid, you have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain {@status concentration} on spells. In addition, becoming {@condition incapacitated} doesn't cause you to lose {@status concentration} on a spell.
{@font {@style 46|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Underworld Asphodel Regalia
entries: This set of royal finery was worn by a noble necromancer with a unique appreciation for the quality of life that extends beyond death. Asphodel blossoms, representing life beyond the tomb, ornament this enchanted outfit. The lush flowers in its laurel crown are nestled among long-dead leaves.

While wearing the regalia, you can cast the {@spell animate dead} spell from it over the course of 1 minute. You can use this property a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier, and you regain all expended uses daily at dusk. When you create an undead using a necromancy spell, the creature's hit point maximum is increased by an amount equal to five times your spellcasting ability modifier. In addition, when you cast a spell that deals necrotic damage, you can add your spellcasting ability modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

entries.name: Chthonic Command
entries: As an action, you can issue a command of either dismissal or obedience to an undead creature within 60 feet of you. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature immune to features that turn undead automatically succeeds on the saving throw. On a failed save, you can impose one of the following effects on that creature for 1 minute:

items: The creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move into a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the {@action Dash} action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If it has nowhere it can move, the creature can use the {@action Dodge} action. This effect ends early if that creature takes any damage.

The creature is {@condition charmed} by you. While the creature is {@condition charmed}, you have a telepathic link with it as long as the two of you are on the same plane of existence. You can use this telepathic link to issue commands to the creature while you are conscious (no action required), which it does its best to obey. You can specify a simple and general course of action, such as "Attack that creature," "Run over there," or "Fetch that object." If the creature completes the order and doesn't receive further direction from you, it defends and preserves itself to the best of its ability. Each time the creature takes damage, it makes a new Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. If the saving throw succeeds, the effect ends.

entries: You can use this property a number of times equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. You regain all expended uses daily at dusk.

entries.name: Ruler of the Dead
entries: You are always under the effects of the {@spell sanctuary} spell. This version of the spell only affects undead. If you make an attack or cast a spell that affects an undead creature, that creature is immune to this spell's effects for 24 hours.

name: Unerring Dowsing Rod
entries: This gnarled willow root is worn and smooth. The wood is dark from long centuries spent absorbing the living darkness of the Shadow Realm.

When you hold this rod in both hands by its short, forked branches, you feel it gently tugging you toward the closest source of fresh water. If the closest source of fresh water is located underground, the dowsing rod directs you to a spot above the source and then dips its tip down toward the ground. When you use this dowsing rod on the Material Plane, it directs you to bodies of water, such as creeks and ponds. When you use it in the Shadow Realm, where fresh water is much more difficult to find, it directs you to bodies of water, but it might also direct you toward homes with freshwater barrels or to creatures with containers of fresh water on them.

name: Unified Might
entries: When consumed, this potion produces a burning sensation that fills your body, leaving you with newfound intellectual and physical strength. For the next hour, two ability scores of your choice increase to 25.
{@font {@style 57|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Unknown Elixir
entries: This bizarre blend of flavors reminds you of freshly cut grass, petroleum jelly, and honey. When consumed, it sits in your stomach like a rock and slowly swells in power. You gain the ability to cast one random spell of 6th level or lower, without expending a spell slot. This spell uses a save DC of 17 and a spell attack bonus of +9. The effects of this potion last until the spell is cast. This doesn't count against the number of potions you can have affecting your body at once.
{@font {@style 49|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Unraveling Cloak
entries: When you take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to remove the button from the hood of this cloak, the cloak's fabric unravels behind you wherever you go, leaving a continuous thread. Other creatures can see the thread only if they take the {@action Search|XPHB} action to look for it and succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check.

The cloak ceases to unravel after 100 miles or if you take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to rebutton the cloak. If you teleport while the cloak is unraveling, any unraveled thread is immediately destroyed.

name: Unsigned Infernal Contract
entries: The archdevil who created Shadowkeep for Count Rhodar von Glauer wrote up another contract on human skin that Rhodar hasn't signed. The contract is written in Infernal.

When you sign this contract using your blood as ink, you lose all levels in your current classes and have the option of gaining levels equal to your character level in any combination of the illrigger, paladin, and warlock classes.

Additionally, you can reassign your six ability scores. You are bound by the contract until the archdevil dies or the contract is broken by a {@spell wish} spell. The contract can only be signed by one creature.

name: Unstable Crumbler
entries: While holding this weapon, your attacks and spells deal double damage to structures, and Fire damage you take is reduced by an amount equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, this weapon is a roaring {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} with smoke coming out of its mouth. In its Transformed state, the handle extends, turning the weapon into a highly unstable and destructive {@item Maul|XPHB}. As part of this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can do the following:

items: When you transform the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} into a {@item Maul|XPHB}, you can shoot at your feet, even if the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} isn't loaded, using the deflagration to propel yourself and jump up to 30 feet in any direction. This jump doesn't cost you any movement.

When you transform the {@item Maul|XPHB} into a {@item Cannon|SGEHPP}, you can reload the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} and retain its unstable force. If you reload it in this way, the next time you hit with a ranged attack with the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} on your turn, you are pushed back 30 feet in a straight line.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: The Unstable Crumbler heats up {@item Cannonball|SGEHPP|Cannonballs}, transforming them into infernal ammunition. Whenever you roll a 15 or higher on the {@dice d20} when making a ranged attack roll with this weapon, the {@item Cannonball|SGEHPP} becomes overheated and explodes on impact. When the {@item Cannonball|SGEHPP} explodes in this way, it is considered an {@item Explosive Cannonball|SGEHPP}.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: Whenever you roll an 18 or higher on the {@dice d20} when making an attack roll with this weapon, the {@item Maul|XPHB}'s head detonates, causing an effect that acts as the {@spell Fireball} spell (save {@dc 15}) centered on the target. If you succeed on this saving throw, you take no damage.

name: Uorik the Conqueror's Juice Cup
entries: This brass cup changes the flavor of any water it's holding. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can whisper the name of a fruit into the cup. If the cup is filled with water, the water's color and flavors magically change to resemble that kind of fruit juice. Saying the name of another fruit changes the water's color and flavors again. Regardless of its color and flavors, the water is still only water. Shouting into the cup causes the juice to effervesce and bubble. If the water is {@condition poisoned}, the drink tastes foul and badly fermented.

name: Ups-A-Daisy
entries: When poured over a creature or object, this creamy elixir instantly awakens the target, as if by the {@spell Awaken} spell. The awakened creature remains {@condition charmed} by you for 1 year, instead of 30 days.
{@font {@style 54|large}|SneakerProMedium}

name: Urnblade
entries: This item appears to be a small cremation urn. While grasping the urn, you can use a bonus action to speak its first command word and cause its lid to unseal. When you do, a curved blade of dark smoke pours from the mouth of the urn. Speaking the command word again reseals the urn and causes the blade to disappear. If you are proficient with shortswords or longswords, you are proficient with the urnblade.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals necrotic damage instead of slashing damage.

entries.name: Shadow Ally
entries: While holding the urn, you can use an action to speak its second command word to animate your body's shadow, transforming it into an undead creature. When you do, your body's shadow detaches from you and becomes a {@creature shadow} in an unoccupied space that you can see within 10 feet of you.

On your turn, you can mentally command the shadow if you aren't {@condition incapacitated}. You decide what action the shadow takes and where it moves during its next turn, or you can issue it a general command, such as to attack your enemies or guard a location. The GM has the shadow's statistics. This shadow doesn't cause a new one to appear when a non-evil humanoid dies from its attacks.

The urnblade's bonus to attack and damage rolls becomes +2 while the summoned shadow exists. In addition, if you are the target of an attack and are within 5 feet of the shadow, you can use your reaction to command your shadow to become the target of the attack instead.

The shadow disappears when it drops to 0 hit points, when it's farther than 120 feet from you, or when you use an action to dismiss it. When it disappears, your cast shadow returns. If the shadow drops to 0 hit points, there is a cumulative {@chance 5} chance that the urn turns to dust and is destroyed.

name: Uror's Shears
entries: Legends tell of the three Norns, entities of power who weave the threads of fate and destiny. Of the trio, Uror appears as a crone. She crafted these shears to cut the threads of mortals when they die.

This pair of scissors seems forged from crude iron, rough and pitted—but they are impossibly sharp. They first appear in {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1} and return in {@adventure Among the Norns|SagasAdventure|3} and {@adventure Storming the Den of Fenris|NorthlandsSagas|10}.

entries.name: Fated Edge
entries: While wielding the shears, you can use an Action to cut through any single object, regardless of the material or nature of the object. A single action allows you to cut through {@b 5 feet} of material, and you can use your Action on subsequent rounds to continue cutting. On your turn, you can change the direction of your cuts, as long as the shears continue to touch the object and don't stop cutting. The GM has the final determination as to what counts as a single object.

If used on a living creature, the shears are a magic weapon that grants a +1 bonus to attack. On a hit, the shears deal 1 Force damage. A creature that takes damage from the shears must make a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the thread of the creature's fate is cut, and it vanishes forever; on a success, it takes {@damage 10d10} Force damage.

entries.name: One Use Only
entries: When you successfully hit a living creature or have cut through one object (or cut though a number of {@b 5-foot} squares equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}), the shears immediately vanish. Stories suggest the shears return to the hands of the Norns, but this remains unconfirmed.

name: Uul'kur (Dream Key)
entries: This iron token is inlaid with a sliver of a Siberys dragonshard. Most are worn as brooches, but others take the form of coins or keys. While an Uul'kur is a Common magic item, the secret of their creation is known only to the chot'uul monks of the Heirs of Dhakaan, and they are largely unknown in the Five Nations.

When you sleep with an Uul'kur on your person, you remain fully lucid when you dream, and when you wake, you clearly remember everything that transpired. If you understand the workings of the Uul'kur, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to bind it to your dreams until the next dawn. While bound, any creature who sleeps with this token on its person shares your dream instead of creating its own, provided you are asleep at the same time.

name: Vadalis Band

items: {@note Requires the {@feat Mark of Handling|EFA}}

additionalEntries: {@note Duplicated from {@item Ring of Animal Influence|XDMG}}

name: Vain Virtuoso's Violin
entries: This finely crafted instrument is inlaid with intricate pearl designs. When you give another creature a Bardic Inspiration die using this violin, you also gain one yourself, which is a d4.

entries.name: Curse
entries: This violin is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. When a creature that you can see (including yourself) fails an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw after adding the bonus from your Bardic Inspiration to the total of the roll, you take psychic damage equal to the number rolled on the Bardic Inspiration die as you lose faith in your own abilities. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

name: Vampire Blood Potion
entries: This potion is a crimson-red bubbling brew that tastes distinctly of copper. When you drink this potion, you gain the following benefits for the next minute:

items: You gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength, Dexterity, and Charisma attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

If damage reduces you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + half the damage taken, unless the damage is Radiant or from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. On a success, you drop to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead, and the effects of this potion end.
The effects of this potion end early if you take Radiant damage or enter sunlight.

entries.name: Crafting
entries: Creating a Vampire Blood Potion requires a Very Rare Workshop and the following Very Rare Components:

items.name: [Animus]
entries: Undead Animus

items.name: [Dust]
entries: Undead Dust from any Vampire

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Ectoplasm

items.name: [Fluid]
entries: Monster Blood from a Vampire

name: Vancian Helm
entries: This helmet is made from the reclaimed and partially disenchanted remains of a shield guardian, no longer bound to an amulet. You gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} while you wear the helm.

entries.name: Spell Storing
entries: Any creature can cast a spell of level 1 through 4 into the helm by touching the helm as the spell is cast. The spell has no effect other than to be stored in the helm. The helm can only hold one spell at a time.

While wearing this helm, you can cast the spell stored in it. The spell uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell. The stored spell is lost when it is cast from the helm or a new spell is stored.

If you are wearing the helm when a level 5+ spell is cast into it, the spell is lost with no effect, the spell slot used to cast it (if any) is expended, and you take {@damage 2d6} Psychic damage. Your eyes glow with a brilliant color of your choice when you wear the helm while a spell is stored within it.

name: Vanisher Hat
entries: This plain hat appears to be a rough burlap tam. A creature that can see through illusions sees the hat as a golden, bejeweled coronet. While wearing this hat, you can use an action to speak its command word to become invisible and gain a flying speed of 40 feet for up to 1 minute. Anything you are wearing or carrying is invisible with you. You remain invisible and capable of flying until you repeat the command word as an action or until you attack or cast a spell. Once used, the hat can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Veil of the Weeping Widow (Legendary)
entries: This mourning veil is imbued with alien power. The Weeping Widow wore the veil to hide her permanently tear-stained face, and rumors circulate that the widow used it to hide the otherworldly corruption writhing within her eyes.
While wearing the veil, you gain a +3 bonus to Wisdom checks and Wisdom saving throws determined by the veil's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Psychic Fortitude (Rare+)
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

entries.name: Sense Grief (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the veil's bonus) from the veil.

entries.name: Psychic Shock (Very Rare+)
entries: When a creature forces you to make a saving throw against Psychic damage, or to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to deal {@damage 2d8} Psychic damage to it.

entries.name: Thought Worm (Very Rare+)
entries: You can use the veil to cast {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the veil's bonus). When a creature fails its saving throw against the spell, you can implant a parasitic spawn of the White Worm in the target's brain. While you're on the same plane, you know the distance and direction to the target, and you can cast Divination and Enchantment spells on it as if it were in range and in sight. A Greater Restoration or {@spell Heal|XPHB} spell kills the parasite and ends this effect. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

entries.name: Psychic Storm (Legendary)
entries: You can take one extra {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} during a round, which you can only use to activate the Psychic Shock property.

entries.name: Veiled Countenance (Legendary)
entries: When you are the target of a Divination spell, the caster must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the caster takes {@damage 6d8} Psychic damage and has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the caster's turns, it repeats the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

name: Veil of the Weeping Widow (Rare)
entries: This mourning veil is imbued with alien power. The Weeping Widow wore the veil to hide her permanently tear-stained face, and rumors circulate that the widow used it to hide the otherworldly corruption writhing within her eyes.
While wearing the veil, you gain a +1 bonus to Wisdom checks and Wisdom saving throws determined by the veil's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Psychic Fortitude (Rare+)
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

entries.name: Sense Grief (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the veil's bonus) from the veil.

name: Veil of the Weeping Widow (Very Rare)
entries: This mourning veil is imbued with alien power. The Weeping Widow wore the veil to hide her permanently tear-stained face, and rumors circulate that the widow used it to hide the otherworldly corruption writhing within her eyes.
While wearing the veil, you gain a +2 bonus to Wisdom checks and Wisdom saving throws determined by the veil's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Psychic Fortitude (Rare+)
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

entries.name: Sense Grief (Rare+)
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the veil's bonus) from the veil.

entries.name: Psychic Shock (Very Rare+)
entries: When a creature forces you to make a saving throw against Psychic damage, or to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to deal {@damage 2d8} Psychic damage to it.

entries.name: Thought Worm (Very Rare+)
entries: You can use the veil to cast {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB} (save DC = 16 + the veil's bonus). When a creature fails its saving throw against the spell, you can implant a parasitic spawn of the White Worm in the target's brain. While you're on the same plane, you know the distance and direction to the target, and you can cast Divination and Enchantment spells on it as if it were in range and in sight. A Greater Restoration or {@spell Heal|XPHB} spell kills the parasite and ends this effect. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

name: Ventilation Unit D-20
entries: A magically-refilling reservoir of ooze is contained within this icosahedral helmet. Two chemicals are distilled from the ooze, piped through the tubes, and mixed together into an oxygen analogue, allowing its wearer to breathe in otherwise impossible conditions.

entries.name: Breathe Easy
entries: While wearing this helmet, you can breathe normally in any environment, and you have advantage on saving throws made against harmful gases and vapours that you inhale (such as the {@spell stinking cloud} effect, inhaled poisons, and the breath weapons of some dragons, but not contact toxins like {@spell cloudkill}).

entries.name: Biomantic Overload
entries: While wearing this helmet, you can use a bonus action to ingest the chemicals in it before they are combined into a gas, causing your body to go into a mutated state of enhanced adaptability for {@b 1 minute}. During this time, immediately after you take damage from any source, you gain resistance to that damage type. This resistance lasts until you take damage of another type (at which point you gain resistance to that new damage type) or until the effect ends. If you take damage of multiple types simultaneously, the damage type to which you become resistant is determined randomly (GM's discretion). Once this property of the helmet has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Vigilus
entries: This {@item Hand Crossbow|XPHB} has a small spring-loaded case attached to its side, which can hold six {@item Bolt|XPHB|Bolts} and automatically loads the next {@item Bolt|XPHB} into the crossbow whenever it's fired. While the case has {@item Bolt|XPHB|Bolts} in it, you ignore the crossbow's {@itemProperty LD|XPHB|Loading} property. A creature can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to reload the case with more {@item Bolt|XPHB|Bolts}.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can unfold the crossbow's three collapsible legs and plant it firmly on the ground in your space to become a Tiny defensive turret. While you're within 30 feet of the crossbow, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to magically command it to attack a target you can see within 30 feet of it as if you were holding it. The crossbow uses your ability modifier for its attack rolls and damage rolls. When commanded to attack, it magically draws itself and loads the next {@item Bolt|XPHB} in its case, if any.

The first time a creature with the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition (excluding you) enters a space within 30 feet of the deployed crossbow, the crossbow emits a small chirping sound audible out to 100 feet. The deployed crossbow is an object with AC 12, HP 30, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage. If it's reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it falls over and can't be deployed again or used in this way for 1 minute. You can retrieve the deployed crossbow as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while you're in its space.

name: Vilesmog Bomb
entries: This smoky concoction is a favorite of poisoners and assassins. You can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to throw this vial up to 30 feet away from you, at which point it breaks and releases a dark vapor that fills a 15-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on it for 2 rounds. A creature that enters the area or starts its turn there loses any {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage and has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Poison damage. This effect lasts for 1 minute.

name: Violet King's Promise
reqAttune: by a bard, cleric, paladin, or ranger
entries: This elegant brass rapier was originally wielded by a beloved king, whose empathy and care for his subjects lives on within the blade. When you hit with an attack using this magic sword, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} fire damage. In addition, you can use this rapier as a spellcasting focus.

The rapier has 7 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. While holding it, a number of gems inside the guard equal to the weapon's remaining charges glow red. When you expend a charge from the rapier, it releases a plume of dark smoke from one of the gems.

If an attacker makes a spell attack against you or a target within 5 feet of you while you're holding the rapier, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. If the attack misses and was a spell of 1st level or higher, the rapier regains 1 expended charge.
While holding the rapier, you can expend 1 or more of its charges to give one of three decrees that affect the flow of magic and battle:

entries.name: "Clemency"
entries: When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a single creature, you can use your reaction to expend 2 charges to cause a different creature within 10 feet of the original target to regain {@dice 1d8} hit points per spell level. When you do, each creature has advantage on the next ability check or saving throw it makes before the end of its next turn.

entries.name: "Condemn"
entries: When you cast a spell that deals damage to a single creature, you can use your reaction to expend 2 charges to cause that target as well as a different creature within 10 feet of it to make a Dexterity saving throw using your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 3d8} fire damage and has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much fire damage and makes its next attack roll as normal.

entries.name: "Overrule"
entries: After you roll dice to restore hit points to a single creature or roll damage for a spell attack or attack using this weapon, you can expend up to 2 charges (no action required) to change the result of those dice. For each charge you spend, you can use the highest number possible for two of those dice instead of the numbers you rolled.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: The Violet King's promise makes its wielder empathic and reluctant to resort to violence. While attuned to the weapon, you gain the following flaw: "I am slow to resort to violence, even if it's at the cost of my own safety." In addition, if you are attuned to the weapon for 24 consecutive hours, your soft-heartedness causes you to lose your ferocity and battle-readiness. You have disadvantage on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) checks and take a –5 penalty to initiative rolls. These effects can be removed with a {@spell greater restoration} spell, but not while you are attuned to the weapon.

name: Violet Painted Stone
entries: {#itemEntry Painted Stone|TalesFromTheShadows}
For 1 minute, you and one willing creature you can see within 30 feet become immune to the {@condition frightened} and {@condition charmed} conditions.

name: Viper Khopesh
entries: This curved blade was carved from a large viper's fang. When you hit with an attack using this magic sword, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} poison damage. In addition, when you roll a 20 on an attack roll made with this weapon against a Large or smaller creature, that creature must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d6} poison damage and is {@condition poisoned} until the start of your next turn. The {@condition poisoned} creature is {@condition incapacitated}. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much poison damage and isn't {@condition poisoned}.

name: Visage of Delight and Disaster
reqAttune: by a Creature with a Charisma of 17+
entries: The expression of this mask subtly changes to reflect your expression and mouth's movement behind the mask. While wearing the mask, you gain two Bardic Inspiration dice, which are d10s (these dice are added to any Bardic Inspiration dice you have from another source). These dice are used in the same way and grant the same benefits as the level 1 Bard class feature, but they carry with them additional benefits based on the mood of your performance, as described below. You regain all expended Bardic Inspiration dice when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Delight
entries: When you confer one of these Bardic Inspiration dice on a creature with a joyful or uplifting performance, that creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. In addition, when that creature uses the Bardic Inspiration die, it gains an amount of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice the number rolled on the die.

entries.name: Disaster
entries: When you confer one of these Bardic Inspiration dice on a creature with a grim or haunting performance, that creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. In addition, when that creature hits a target with an attack roll using a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, it can expend the Bardic Inspiration die, rolling the die and dealing extra Psychic damage to the target equal to twice the number rolled.

name: Visage of the Old Ways (Legendary)
entries: This wood-carved mask has a haunted expression and makes the wearer's eyes look like empty shadows. Rabbit ears protrude over the head. While you wear the mask, you hear the whispers of an ancient forest archfey deep within your mind.
While wearing the mask, you gain a +6 bonus to your damage rolls when you deal Fire damage determined by the mask's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Cultic Mask (Rare+)
entries: You can't be targeted by Divination spells or perceived through scrying sensors. Ability checks made to discern your identity have a minimum DC of 25.

entries.name: Fire Within (Rare+)
entries: While you are burning, your weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 2d4} Fire damage. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to begin or stop burning.

entries.name: Strange Sight (Rare+)
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet, and you can see normally through areas obscured by smoke.

entries.name: Mastery of Flame (Very Rare+)
entries: Fire damage you deal ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sacrificial Flame (Very Rare+)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can cause a creature you can see with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} that is within 30 feet of you to burst into flame. Its body burns to ash over the next minute, and when a creature {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} to you starts its turn in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the body, it takes {@damage 2d8} Fire damage. The flame is extinguished if the target regains any {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Harvest Offering (Legendary)
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend up to 5 {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} to regain a spell slot of a level equal to the number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} spent. Alternatively, you can touch a creature that is willing or that has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition and force them to expend any number of these {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} in your place. This property can be used twice, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

name: Visage of the Old Ways (Rare)
entries: This wood-carved mask has a haunted expression and makes the wearer's eyes look like empty shadows. Rabbit ears protrude over the head. While you wear the mask, you hear the whispers of an ancient forest archfey deep within your mind.
While wearing the mask, you gain a +2 bonus to your damage rolls when you deal Fire damage determined by the mask's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Cultic Mask (Rare+)
entries: You can't be targeted by Divination spells or perceived through scrying sensors. Ability checks made to discern your identity have a minimum DC of 25.

entries.name: Fire Within (Rare+)
entries: While you are burning, your weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 2d4} Fire damage. You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to begin or stop burning.

entries.name: Strange Sight (Rare+)
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet, and you can see normally through areas obscured by smoke.

name: Visage of the Old Ways (Very Rare)
entries: This wood-carved mask has a haunted expression and makes the wearer's eyes look like empty shadows. Rabbit ears protrude over the head. While you wear the mask, you hear the whispers of an ancient forest archfey deep within your mind.
While wearing the mask, you gain a +4 bonus to your damage rolls when you deal Fire damage determined by the mask's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

entries.name: Cultic Mask (Rare+)
entries: You can't be targeted by Divination spells or perceived through scrying sensors. Ability checks made to discern your identity have a minimum DC of 25.

entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet, and you can see normally through areas obscured by smoke.

entries: Fire damage you deal ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}.
